To this end, we automatically fine-tune the LLM to improve its compliance with ontologically-defined conversation characteristics. Our results show that training the LLM from formally defined concepts effectively enhances alignment with the requested characteristics. Hence, this work demonstrates how ontology-guided conversation control can be achieved while taking into account multiple, concurrent conversation aspects that are formally and transparently defined.

Artificial Intelligence.title: An Empirical Study of Issues in GPU Kernel Libraries for LLM Systems
Artificial Intelligence.summary:
Behind the expanding use of large language models (LLMs) across application domains lies a growing dependence on specialized GPU kernel libraries. These libraries underpin the correctness and efficiency of training and inference across diverse GPU platforms, implementing attention, GEMM, quantization, and low-precision operators while managing tensor shapes, memory layouts, code generation, and hardware-specific dispatch. Problems at this layer can silently corrupt outputs, hang GPUs, prevent compilation, introduce deployment incompatibilities, or degrade performance, thereby reducing developer productivity and wasting expensive GPU resources.
  We present the first comprehensive empirical study of issues in GPU kernel libraries for LLM systems. We manually analyzed 300 high-quality GitHub issue reports, their discussions, and available fixes from seven representative libraries: FlashInfer, FlashAttention, Triton, CUTLASS, DeepGEMM, xFormers, and bitsandbytes. The analysis characterizes symptoms, root causes, fixes, and testing and debugging practices. Our main findings are: (1) 60.33% of the sampled issues originate in the Compiler and Build System or Runtime Environment dimensions, so validation must cover the deployment and execution stack, not just kernel code. (2) Kernel specialization imposes implicit correctness constraints on tensor shapes, metadata layouts, memory aliasing, and hardware resources. Violations can produce incorrect outputs or launch failures even for supported operations, highlighting the need for explicit contract validation and boundary-case testing. (3) Current testing and debugging practices are often insufficient for identifying low-precision numerical problems and hardware-specific execution failures. We outline research opportunities and tooling directions to support future LLM GPU kernel development.

Signal Processing.title: On PMU Adequacy for Wideband Dynamics Tracking Beyond Attenuation Assumptions
Signal Processing.summary: Recent work highlights the inadequacy of standard synchrophasors in capturing high-frequency grid dynamics, including data center oscillations, primarily due to filtering and windowing attenuation during phasor estimation. This letter shows how synchrophasor ambient data spectrum itself contains information on attenuation, which provides a way to identify critically impacted measurements and potentially estimate and undo the effect. Results are shown for synthetic data as well as actual synchrophasor estimates from digital fault recorders (DFRs) within the Dominion Energy system.

Signal Processing.title: Link-Level Performance Comparison of 5G Beamforming: Reciprocity-Based SVD vs. Codebook-Based Precoding
Signal Processing.summary: Downlink (DL) precoding in mid-band MIMO relies on uplink (UL) sounding reference signals (SRS) with reciprocity-based singular value decomposition (SVD) or channel state information reference signals (CSI-RS) with codebook-based precoding matrix indicator (PMI) feedback. Although SVD precoding offers unquantized beamforming, it depends on a channel estimate from SRS transmitted at the limited user equipment (UE) power, whereas Type-I PMI is quantized but derived from a high-power CSI-RS based channel estimate. In this paper, we compare SRS-SVD and CSIRS-PMI for single-user MIMO through an end-to-end, 3GPP-compliant link-level simulation at 3.75 GHz with 100 MHz bandwidth, using a 192 antenna element gNB mapped into 32 ports, the 3GPP Release 19 UE antenna model, and ray-traced (RT) channels in Manhattan and Chicago. We show that neither scheme is uniformly superior: CSIRS-PMI serves weak and shadowed users better and reduces outage, whereas SRS-SVD achieves higher spectral efficiency (SE) and enables more multi-layer transmission for users with strong channels. The results on the Clustered Delay Line (CDL)-C statistical channel also confirm this crossover. We further show that by utilizing a simple logistic regression based on the received power of the standard CSI reference signal (CSI-RSRP) and the channel quality indicator (CQI), the gNB can select the optimal transmission scheme with around 90% accuracy, achieving an SE that closely approaches an ideal per-user selection.
Signal Processing.comment: 7 pages, 8 figures. Submitted to IEEE ICC 2027

Signal Processing.title: Payload-Blind Bistatic Delay-Doppler Sensing with Phase-Injected Chirps in CE-OFDM
Signal Processing.summary: Constant-envelope orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (CE-OFDM) preserves a unit-magnitude sample envelope, but its Hermitian-symmetric structure makes dedicated sensing pilots costly, and additive pilots disrupt this envelope. We show that injecting a known chirp, here a Zadoff-Chu (ZC) sequence, into the CE-OFDM phase enables payload-blind bistatic delay-Doppler sensing without dedicated sensing frames or an explicit pilot power split: the residual carrier, given by the ensemble mean under the adopted payload model, becomes an implicit superimposed pilot for a receive-only node. A Doppler-aligned receiver integrates this reference coherently across frames while the payload residual averages down. In contrast, phase-domain injected training (PIT) frame averaging, designed for quasi-static channel estimation, loses about 32 dB for the simulated target with 16 averaged frames. Closed-form approximations characterize the payload-induced floor, known-cell detection probability and direct-path tolerance. In the noise-limited simulations, the receiver incurs a 2.8 dB detection gap relative to a payload-aware matched filter without interference cancellation and matches a dedicated-pilot benchmark of equal reference energy without its 53% frame overhead.

Signal Processing.title: A Phase-Balanced Differential Rydberg-Atom Quantum Receiver for Weak GNSS Signal Detection
Signal Processing.summary: This paper proposes a phase-balanced differential Rydberg atomic quantum receiver (DRAQR) for weak-signal recovery, using local-oscillator phase control to reinforce differential signal responses and a shared squeezed-reservoir model to correlate inter-cell quantum projection noise (QPN) and photon shot noise (PSN). An analytical model incorporating QPN, PSN, intrinsic thermal noise (ITN), and inter-cell correlations quantifies signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) gain, outage-constrained minimum detectable power, and bit-error rate (BER) for square $M$-QAM. For the evaluated settings, SNR gain reaches approximately $10$~dB as PSN correlation approaches unity, with BER decreasing as correlation increases. Under Rician fading, at a $0$-dB threshold SNR and maximum outage probability of $0.1$, the minimum detectable power decreases from $-146.95$~dBm at $K=1.155$ to $-159.98$~dBm at $K=2.4$. Analytical results are validated against Monte-Carlo simulations over $150{,}000$ data runs per point for receiver-performance plots.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 10 figures, submitted to IEEE ICC 2027 (in review)

Signal Processing.title: Beyond Feasibility: Efficient and Robust On-Device Localization with UWB Concurrent Transmissions
Signal Processing.summary: Concurrent transmissions (CTX) enable an ultra-wideband (UWB) tag to range to, or self-localize from, multiple nodes with a single frame reception, significantly improving update rate and energy efficiency compared to traditional approaches. Prior work demonstrated the concept feasibility via prototypes whose real-world applicability is however hindered by many limitations, notably including their inability to directly execute on UWB tags and to cope with interfering UWB signals. We address these limitations in two ways. First, we redesign the core CTX techniques to enable a fast and efficient execution on resource-constrained MCUs without sacrificing accuracy. Second, we leverage the new features in the IEEE 802.15.4z standard to achieve robustness to interference from other UWB devices and enable tags to dynamically select which anchors to use, two crucial and unexplored capabilities in CTX-based systems. We quantitatively evaluate our approach experimentally in two real-world testbeds with different characteristics. We first analyze our new techniques individually, offering an in-depth discussion of design choices and performance trade-offs. Then, we embed all our techniques into a CTX-based system enabling a tag to self-localize entirely on-device, unlocking gains up to 44% in runtime and 85% in energy efficiency compared to traditional approaches.
Signal Processing.comment: Submitted to the IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing

Signal Processing.title: Multi-Mode Pinching-Antenna-Based OFDM Systems: A Robust Design Perspective
Signal Processing.summary: A robust transmission framework is proposed for a multi-mode pinching-antenna (MPA)-based orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) system under both channel state information (CSI) errors and PA positioning errors. A physical model is first developed based on the multi-mode coupled-mode equations (CMEs), which characterizes the frequency-dependent guided-mode propagation and the coupling among guided modes and PAs over the OFDM band. Based on this model, a worst-case sum-rate maximization problem is formulated to jointly optimize the baseband beamformer and the intended PA positions under CSI and PA positioning errors, subject to user quality-of-service (QoS) and transmit-power constraints. To solve the resulting non convex problem, the worst-case CSI is exactly obtained for any given PA positions by solving trust-region subproblems, while the PA positioning errors are handled by grid-based and second-order approximation-based scenario constructions. Then, an alternating optimization (AO) algorithm is developed, where the baseband beamformer and the intended PA positions are updated via the weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE) method and successive convex approximation (SCA), respectively. Both subproblems are solved efficiently by exploiting the Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) conditions. Numerical results show that the proposed robust design outperforms the non-robust and conventional robust benchmarks with the same multi-mode architecture in terms of both worst-case sum rate and QoS satisfaction. They also demonstrate that the proposed robust design satisfies the QoS requirements of all users more reliably than the baselines that consider either CSI errors or PA positioning errors.
Signal Processing.comment: 13 pages, 8 figures

Signal Processing.title: Expert Spindles in the Wild: Enriched Supervision for a Dense Detector
Signal Processing.summary: Sleep spindles are a hallmark of healthy NREM sleep whose frequency, amplitude, density, duration and topography vary with brain maturation, age and disease. Their manual annotation is impractical and variable between scorers, yet the public references used to train automatic detectors cover these characteristics only partially: stage N2 only, a single central derivation, or short pre-selected segments. Measuring duration and density requires dense detectors that learn event boundaries from annotated onsets and offsets, and therefore inherit the protocol under which those boundaries were scored. We introduce Expert Spindles in the Wild (ESW), a stage-agnostic expert spindle annotation set covering 19 complete MASS-SS2 recordings ($\approx$150 h of continuous EEG, 29,819 events). A sleep neurophysiologist annotated the recordings using the full EEG montage, blinded to sleep-stage labels and prior spindle annotations. On the 15 nights shared with historical scorers, ESW recovers 92.7% of E1 and 73.7% of E2 events, while recovering 81.6% of the MODA expert-consensus events on the common excerpts. Despite stage-blind annotation, 99.0% of ESW events occur in N2/N3. Used to train a fixed dense detector on a frozen SleepFM encoder, ESW reaches an event-level $F_1$ of 0.680 on 166 unseen MODA subjects, compared with 0.635 for E2 ($ΔF_1$ = +0.045, paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.024, 0.065]). ESW is thus useful supervision for cross-dataset detection, and closer annotation-level agreement with the MODA consensus did not translate into better transfer performance in this experiment. The annotations are released under the MASS data-use terms (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23894975).
Signal Processing.comment: 5 pages, 1 figure, 2 tables. Submitted to IEEE ISBI 2027 (under review)

Signal Processing.title: Robust Model Order Selection via Dithered Differential Step-Down Thresholding
Signal Processing.summary: We propose a dithered differential step-down thresholding (DSDT) algorithm for robust model order selection in stationary noise. Evaluating only exceedance counts over a decreasing threshold grid, the proposed algorithm stops when detecting noise extrema value clustering. We prove that deterministic threshold grids are inconsistent under lowered floor detection thresholds due to threshold grid misalignment error. We bound this error using randomized grid dithering. For arbitrary deterministic shifts, any joint noise distribution, and data-dependent thresholds, we obtain non-asymptotic bounds on the estimation risk and family-wise error rate, establishing DSDT as a universal false alarm suppressor for any single-threshold algorithm. When the scale sequence tends to zero or extremes cluster along the search grid, DSDT achieves asymptotic exact order recovery of separated deterministic components exceeding the noise maximum plus the grid step, even below the minimax threshold or without a detection threshold. Using multiple independent dithers reduces error bounds. We provide convergence and consistency analysis for an arbitrary number of dithers. This analysis establishes asymptotic bounds under extreme value laws and non-asymptotic bounds under nondecreasing hazard rates. The results extend to unseparated deterministic shifts, random shifts, unknown noise scales, and multi-dimensional search grids. We show that DSDT is robust to data quantization.
Signal Processing.comment: major rev3

Signal Processing.title: Sparse Array-Inspired Frame Structure Design for 5G NR ISAC
Signal Processing.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has emerged as a promising paradigm for future wireless networks. However, the extensive occupation of time-frequency resources for sensing limits the communication capacity. To address the resource conflict, this paper proposes a novel sparse sensing frame structure aligned with the 5G new radio (5G NR) resource grid at the slot and physical resource block (PRB) levels through a predefined sensing-pattern block. Specifically, inspired by the design of two-dimensional (2D) sparse antenna arrays, we map the sparse spatial geometries onto the time-frequency resource grid. By leveraging the hole-free property of the difference coarray, we eliminate the range-velocity ambiguity and cast the sensing signals into a reconstructed higher-order tensor representation. For efficient parameter estimation, we propose a novel binary-tree-based tensor train decomposition (BT-TTD) algorithm that extracts lower-dimensional tensor train cores (TT-cores) and executes a Vandermonde-prior-guided rectified alternating least squares (RecALS) algorithm. Simulation results validate that the proposed scheme achieves competitive estimation accuracy with reduced complexity. Furthermore, we investigate the topological properties of various sparse patterns, revealing the inherent trade-off among sensing accuracy, resource occupancy, and computational complexity.
Signal Processing.comment: 16 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables

Signal Processing.title: A Hybrid Digital/Analog Polyphase Filtering Approach for High-Speed RF-DACs
Signal Processing.summary: This paper proposes a hybrid polyphase interpolation for RF-DACs that removes the need for full-rate digital commutation by using passive combining on the RF-DAC itself. A P-branch polyphase FIR filter is factored into M streams, each formed by a (P/M)-way digital commutator at fRF/M and driving a dedicated RF-DAC slice, giving either partial digital (1<M<P) or fully analog (M=P) recombination. We show that the slice array acts as a single full-rate DAC with an M-times longer zero-order hold, derive yield laws for slice gain, timing and unit-capacitor mismatch, and find that with retiming the binding requirement is sub-picosecond matching of the fRF clock arrival, so the best choice is the smallest M that closes digital timing. Two 28-nm digital macros, designed for a 12.8GSps output rate and verified by post-layout simulation, illustrate a 4-phase variant that closes timing up to 14.4GSps with its digital logic at fRF/4 and an 8-phase variant that closes timing up to 16GSps with its digital logic at fRF/8. The analog recombination is evaluated with a behavioral model of the slice array. The architectures target wideband software defined radio (SDR) platforms, including cognitive radio, electronic warfare, and satellite communications.
Signal Processing.comment: 11 pages, 5 figures, 5 tables

Signal Processing.title: Scalable BLE Channel Sounding Localization with Ranging-Assisted PDoA
Signal Processing.summary: Bluetooth Channel Sounding (CS) enables accurate phase-based ranging, but multi-anchor localization requires sequential ranging exchanges that limit scalability and increase measurement latency. This paper proposes Ranging-Assisted Phase Difference of Arrival (RA-PDoA), a scalable BLE localization architecture combining one active anchor performing a standard two-way CS exchange with multiple passive receive-only anchors observing the same transmissions. A channel-recovery framework is derived that enables passive anchors to reconstruct a channel response suitable for super-resolution delay estimation, allowing multipath-robust ranging without participating in a two-way exchange. Coarse arrival-time information is further used to bound the position estimate and reject inconsistent range solutions. A comprehensive evaluation characterizes the impact of multipath propagation, body shadowing, synchronization requirements, oscillator impairments, anchor placement, and deployment inaccuracies, thereby quantifying the practical infrastructure requirements for scalable BLE localization. Simulation results in modeled indoor environments show that RA-PDoA reduces the 90th-percentile localization error from 175.3 cm to 95.5 cm under body shadowing while maintaining an airtime requirement independent of the number of anchors. The results demonstrate that a single active ranging link enables scalable and multipath-robust BLE Channel Sounding localization.
Signal Processing.comment: 14 pages, 5 figures, 7 tables, Appendix, For reproducibility code available at https://gitlab.ilabt.imec.be/iwine/ra-pdoa-simulator

Signal Processing.title: Pinching Antenna Systems (PASS) for Air-Ground Integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC)
Signal Processing.summary: This paper proposes a multi-user single-target air-ground integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, in which a ground pinching-antenna system (PASS) transmits communication and sensing signals and an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) receives the target echo. The communication and sensing beamforming vectors, pinching antenna positions, and UAV position are jointly optimized to minimize the weighted Cramér-Rao bound (CRB). A penalty dual decomposition (PDD) algorithm is developed for the resulting nonconvex problem. The auxiliary variable and beamforming subproblems admit globally optimal solutions in semi-closed form, while the positions of the pinching antennas and the UAV are updated by successive convex approximation (SCA). Under mild conditions, every accumulation point of the sequence generated by our proposed algorithm is a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) point of the reformulated problem. Numerical results show that the proposed PASS-UAV design achieves a lower weighted CRB than conventional multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) and PASS benchmarks.
Signal Processing.comment: 5 pages, 6 figures

Signal Processing.title: Beyond the Pseudo-Inverse: GIM Precoding for Per-Antenna Power Minimisation in MU-MIMO
Signal Processing.summary: We study linear precoder design for multi-user MIMO downlink under per-antenna power constraints (PAPC), which arise naturally when each antenna port has its own power amplifier. While the Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse is the unique optimal generalized inverse for zero-forcing precoding under a total power constraint [1], we prove this optimality does not extend to the MMSE/RZF case under PAPC. Any precoder in the Generalized Inverse Matrix (GIM) family shares the same effective channel and per-user SINRs as the pseudo-inverse baseline, while its null-space component reshapes the per-antenna power profile. This separation principle enables minimising peak per-antenna power at fixed SINR targets with zero SINR penalty. We characterise the convex peak-power problem over this family and its active-set optimality, establish MRT and ZF asymptotic limits, and provide a convergent first-order subgradient algorithm. Simulations with 8-64 antennas confirm gains of 1.9-3.7 dB over pseudo-inverse RZF, with GIM-MMSE eliminating essentially all PAPC violations up to 20% per-antenna budget imbalance. The framework applies directly to fully-digital massive MIMO. Cell-free and hybrid analog-digital arrays are promising extensions.

Signal Processing.title: DNN-Driven Proactive UAV Trajectory and Beam Steering for Blockage-Resilient Communications
Signal Processing.summary: This paper proposes Autonomous UAV Communication (AutUAVCom), a proactive communication system that jointly adapts the flight trajectory and RF beam steering to minimize UAV energy consumption while satisfying secrecy and reliability requirements for rescue teams operating in dynamic, cluttered, and GPS-denied environments. Unlike existing modelbased proactive approaches, AutUAVCom employs a deep neural network-based Tracking and Prediction (T&P) module that combines onboard sensing with spatiotemporal and body-orientation information to track users, localize blocking objects, and predict future trajectories and potential beam blockages. Building on the T&P module, we formulate a constrained optimization problem and develop a two-step iterative numerical approach. Monte Carlo simulations show that, relative to a reactive system, AutUAVCom achieves 10% and 19% gains in energy efficiency and channel secrecy, respectively, while reducing the outage probability by 85%, under a mean blockage arrival interval of 120 seconds and a mean blockage duration of 20 seconds.

Signal Processing.title: A Tutorial on Practical QKD Post-Processing Algorithms Using a GUI-Based Simulation Framework
Signal Processing.summary: Recent experimental demonstrations of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) have attracted significant attention for their ability to establish information-theoretically secure encryption keys for next-generation communication systems. As practical deployment accelerates, the realization of compact, scalable, and high-throughput discrete-variable (DV) QKD systems has become increasingly important. While advances in photonic integration are enabling low-size, low-weight, and low-power QKD hardware, the security and performance of these systems rely heavily on efficient post-processing techniques to generate identical, secure keys. This tutorial presents a comprehensive algorithm-level review of practical post-processing techniques for DV-QKD, with particular emphasis on information reconciliation methods based on Cascade, Winnow, low-density parity-check (LDPC), and polar codes. We also analyze the theoretical asymptotic and finite-size secret key rates (SKRs) of DV-QKD and benchmark these bounds against the practical SKRs achieved using actual post-processing algorithms. Furthermore, we present a server-client model to implement the entire QKD post-processing pipeline. The performance is evaluated in terms of QBER and SKR across various system parameters, considering the complete post-processing pipeline, including sifting, information reconciliation, privacy amplification, and authentication. This tutorial also presents a graphical user interface (GUI) for the QKD post-processing methods, enabling researchers, industry practitioners, and academic users to visualize and analyze the impact of different post-processing techniques and system parameters, such as QBER, on the SKR performance of DV-QKD systems.
Signal Processing.comment: Submitted to IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society

Signal Processing.title: Evaluation of a Multi-Link Machine Learning Approach for Rainfall Detection Using Satellite Microwave Links
Signal Processing.summary: The impacts of climate change have increased the need for reliable real-time rainfall monitoring systems. This study investigates rainfall detection using a network of opportunistic sensors based on satellite microwave links (SMLs) combined with machine learning (ML) classifiers. Two models, a random forest (RF) and a convolutional neural network (CNN), were trained on aggregated SML data, including information from neighboring links. The results demonstrate that leveraging information from multiple links substantially enhances the detection of both wet and dry periods compared to single-link approaches. Moreover, the RF model consistently provides a more stable and reliable trade-off than CNN, improving rainfall detection and reducing misclassifications overall, with particularly strong performance during harsh weather conditions. The study spanned up to 32 rainy days between 2021 and 2024.

Signal Processing.title: AirFM-DDA: Air-Interface Foundation Model in the Delay-Doppler-Angle Domain for AI-Native 6G
Signal Processing.summary: The success of large foundation models is catalyzing a new paradigm for AI-native 6G network design: wireless foundation models for physical-layer design. However, existing models often operate on channel state information (CSI) in the spatial-temporal-frequency (STF) domain, where multipath components are superimposed and structurally entangled. This hinders the learning of a universal channel representation. Their reliance on global attention also incurs prohibitive overhead. In this paper, we propose AirFM-DDA, an Air-interface Foundation Model in the Delay-Doppler-Angle (DDA) domain. AirFM-DDA reparameterizes CSI into the DDA domain to resolve multipath components along physically meaningful axes and employs window-based attention with frame-structure-aware positional encoding. Extensive experiments demonstrate transferability across scenarios, tasks, datasets, and antenna configurations. For channel prediction and estimation, AirFM-DDA generalizes zero-shot to unseen cities, achieving average normalized mean-square error (NMSE) gains of 4.9-8.5 dB over the strongest baselines. With only 10% labeled data, it achieves average gains of 12.0 percentage points in Top-1 accuracy for beam prediction and 3.4 percentage points in F1 score for line-of-sight (LoS) identification. It further transfers across simulated datasets and adapts to measured data and different antenna arrays. Compared with global attention, window-based attention reduces training and inference costs by nearly an order of magnitude.
Signal Processing.comment: 18 pages

Signal Processing.title: Quantum-Enhanced Classical Communications for DPMZM-based NG-PON2 Systems
Signal Processing.summary: This paper presents a framework for integrating quantum detection techniques into a Dual-Parallel Mach-Zehnder Modulator (DPMZM)-based Next Generation Passive Optical Network 2 (NG-PON2) communication system. We present a system model for the DPMZM-based NG-PON2 quantum communication system and characterize its signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), demonstrating its superiority over conventional MZM-based systems. We analyze the performance of various quantum modulation techniques, including binary phase-shift keying, quadrature phase-shift keying, and M-ary quadrature amplitude modulation. A comprehensive analytical framework is developed to evaluate the SNR, BER, and mutual information for both classical and quantum detection schemes within the DPMZM-based NG-PON2 quantum communication system. Our simulation results show that quantum detection significantly outperforms classical detection, and the DPMZM architecture further enhances the performance over the baseline MZM architecture by improving the effective modulation efficiency and receiver sensitivity.

Signal Processing.title: DeepRT-Cal: Learning to Calibrate Ray-Traced Twin Channel Statistics with Low-Fidelity Environmental Geometry
Signal Processing.summary: Sixth-generation (6G) wireless systems increasingly rely on digital twin channels (DTCs) to represent and interact with physical radio environments. Ray tracing (RT) is naturally suited to DTC construction because it provides deterministic and physically interpretable channel predictions. However, high-fidelity three-dimensional environment models are expensive to obtain, whereas geometric inaccuracies in low-fidelity models can alter the detected multipath components (MPCs) and consequently distort received-power and delay-domain twin channel statistics. Building on the DeepRT ray-tracing framework, this paper proposes DeepRT-Cal, a geometry-aware cross-fidelity calibration framework that predicts high-fidelity twin channel statistics from low-fidelity geometry and RT features.The network encodes global link descriptors, masked low-fidelity MPC tokens, propagation-corridor geometry, and link-centered environmental objects. During training, detailed geometry is introduced as privileged information with structured masking, while deployment requires only low-fidelity geometry and low-fidelity RT information. A link-conditioned cross-attention module retrieves the environmental context relevant to each Tx--Rx link. The prediction heads estimate high-fidelity twin channel statistics, including total received power, RMS delay spread, mean excess delay, and a normalized power-weighted power-delay profile (PDP). Outdoor evaluation shows that, in an non-line of sight (NLoS) region, the method reduces power MAE from 16.80 to 3.88 dB and RMS delay-spread MAE from 304.89 to 98.19 ns. In a LoS-dominated region, power prediction improves, while RMS delay-spread accuracy remains comparable to direct RT.
Signal Processing.comment: 15 pages, 14 figures, 3 tables

Signal Processing.title: Capacity of Multi-Layer Manhattan-Grid UAV Corridors Served by Terrestrial 5G NR Networks
Signal Processing.summary: Advanced air mobility (AAM) is expected to organize unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) traffic into corridors at multiple altitudes. In this paper, we study the downlink (DL) and uplink (UL) capacity of a multi-layer Manhattan-grid corridor mesh served by a terrestrial fifth-generation (5G) new radio (NR) macro network. The corridor spacing and the numbers of layers, UAVs, and base stations are configurable. We combine the 3GPP aerial channel and antenna models, correlated UAV mobility, and frequency-selective fading with an NR physical-layer abstraction that includes channel aging and link adaptation. Results show that UAVs above 90 m experience a DL signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) about 17 dB below that of ground users, and that a dense macro network with $10^\circ$ downtilt leaves 17-29% of corridor positions without DL service under full-buffer load, regardless of corridor spacing. On a common layout, the carrier frequency (700 MHz, 3.5 GHz, or 7.2 GHz) changes the UAV SINR by less than 0.5 dB, since the corridor links are strongly interference-limited. The UL is the bottleneck: at 85% satisfaction, a 20 MHz carrier supports only about 3.4-4.1 UAVs/km$^2$ with 4 Mb/s of UL video per UAV.
Signal Processing.comment: Under Review

Signal Processing.title: FoundaRF: A Physics-Informed Foundation Model Framework for Radio-Frequency Passive Components
Signal Processing.summary: Designing RF/mmWave passive components is a time-consuming process that relies heavily on expert knowledge and iterative EM simulations. Although recent ML surrogate models have shown great promise in accelerating passive design, they remain task-specific and lack generalization. This paper presents FoundaRF, a foundation model framework that unifies passive layout modeling across diverse layout structures and technologies. It combines a self-supervised encoder with adaptive layout processing and physics-aware decoders to enable few-shot transfer. Experiments across four semiconductor technologies show strong generalization to unseen structures, outperforming baselines with up to a 3.3x reduction in prediction error, reducing labeled-data requirements by up to fourfold, and substantially shortening design turnaround. FoundaRF establishes a scalable and data-efficient solution for RF/mmWave passive design automation.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted for publication in the proceedings of the 2026 IEEE/ACM International Conference on Computer-Aided Design (ICCAD 2026)

Signal Processing.title: Learning Latent Fields in Multiobject Tracking
Signal Processing.summary: Multiobject tracking using measurements from arrays of wireless sensors is a key task in applications ranging from autonomous navigation to public safety. Many existing methods compress raw complex-valued signals into detections or intensity maps during preprocessing, thereby discarding potentially relevant information about the objects and the propagation environment. We propose a Bayesian framework for multiobject tracking that relates object states to raw complex-valued signals via a physics-based superpositional model. The model combines a physics-based array manifold, such as radar steering vectors or the replica vectors of matched-field processing, with a latent field. This latent field is a family of context-dependent signal-power distributions that captures the effects of the objects and the propagation environment and is shared across objects and time. It is parameterized by a conditional normalizing flow, which is trained during runtime without labeled data by maximizing an evidence lower bound (ELBO) derived from the Bayesian model. Learning and inference are thus coupled in a sequential framework. We evaluate the method in simulation and in real-world radio and acoustic experiments, with spatial scales ranging from meters to kilometers, and show that it outperforms detection-based methods.
Signal Processing.comment: Minor wording changes to the abstract; technical content unchanged

Signal Processing.title: GeoJeV: Unified Spatial Probability for Training-Free Efficient Evidence Acquisition in Ultra-High-Resolution Remote Sensing
Signal Processing.summary: Ultra-high-resolution (UHR) remote sensing imagery provides rich spatial details but poses challenges for accurate and efficient multimodal understanding. Existing evidence acquisition methods selectively explore relevant image regions, yet largely rely on generative multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for intermediate search control. However, reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) primarily aligns these models with human-preferred responses rather than explicitly optimizing region-level relevance judgments, while repeated autoregressive decoding introduces additional computational overhead. To address these limitations, we propose GeoJeV, a training-free method that formulates evidence acquisition as spatial probability-driven decision making. At each evaluated region, a frozen JeV model produces a probability distribution over candidate regions. Specifically, Region Rank prioritizes candidate regions, Sparse Branch adaptively determines branching width through sparse probability support, and Depth Gate controls refinement depth based on branch sparsity and distribution concentration. By coordinating search priority, branching width, and refinement depth through a shared distribution, GeoJeV reduces reliance on RLHF-aligned generation and eliminates intermediate decoding. Experiments on LRS-GRO, MME-RealWorld-RS, and LRS-VQA achieve accuracies of 60.59%, 52.79%, and 34.32%, respectively. Across the three benchmarks, GeoJeV improves the average accuracy of Qwen3-VL-8B by +5.32pp with only 1.12 additional seconds per question, while achieving a 7.8-fold inference speedup over the recent method.

Signal Processing.title: Stochastic High-Resolution Parameter-Based Channel Modeling for Sub-Terahertz Outdoor Device-to-Device Propagation at 145 GHz
Signal Processing.summary: Since device-to-device (D2D) systems operating in the sub-THz regime are of interest for a variety of 6G applications, modeling their propagation channels is therefore essential. This paper presents high-resolution parameter estimation (HRPE) of specular multipath components (MPCs) as well as diffuse multipath components (DMCs) from an extensive measurement campaign. The extracted MPCs and DMCs are then clustered, and statistical models for both intra- and inter-cluster statistics are established. Among other insights, we find a large number (typically 10-50) of clusters; both the powers and densities of MPCs within each cluster show significant variations. DMC occurs both when associated with discrete MPCs and standalone. The paper provides a complete model that can generate double-directional impulse responses, and a MATLAB program implementing it is made available. Extensive verifications of "derived" (not directly modeled) parameters are provided as well.
Signal Processing.comment: Currently under submitted and under revision in the IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications

Signal Processing.title: Sparse Network Inference under Imperfect Detection and its Application to Ecological Networks
Signal Processing.summary: Recovering latent structure from count data has received considerable attention in network inference, particularly when one seeks both cross-group interactions and within-group similarity patterns in bipartite networks, which are widely used in ecology research. Such networks are often sparse and prone to imperfect detection. Existing models mainly focus on interaction recovery, while the induced similarity graphs are much less studied. Moreover, existing models for under-counted data place sparsity, if at all, on the detection model rather than on these graphs. To address these issues, we propose a nonnegative low-rank factorization framework that jointly estimates detection probabilities and promotes sparse within- and cross-group graphs through $\ell_{1/2}$ regularization. For the resulting nonconvex, nonsmooth problem, we develop an ADMM-based algorithm with adaptive penalization, and establish asymptotic feasibility and KKT stationarity of cluster points under stated assumptions. We also give sufficient conditions for exact recovery of within- and cross-group graphs. On synthetic data with up to 20% missing entries, the method recovers the graphs and detection probabilities with competitive accuracy. Across three ecological datasets, it matches the baseline held-out predictions while estimating detection probabilities and within- and cross-group graphs.
Signal Processing.comment: 16 pages, 2 figures

Signal Processing.title: An Ultra-Low-Noise Tunable TIA in 45nm Silicon Photonics for Electro-Optical Ultrasound Data Acquisition
Signal Processing.summary: This paper presents the design and experimental characterization of a 32-channel, WDM-compatible electronic-photonic receiver array fabricated in the GlobalFoundries 45nm monolithic silicon photonics process. Optimized for miniaturized, millimeter-scale electro-optical ultrasound data acquisition probes for broadband photo-acoustic imaging (PAI), the chip utilizes integrated micro-ring resonator (MRR) demultiplexers and photodiode (PD) arrays to decode multi-wavelength acoustic signals outside the body. This work focuses specifically on the comprehensive characterization of the receiver front-end, evaluating both the optical WDM filter bank and the transimpedance amplifier (TIA) performance. Monolithic co-integration minimizes critical photodiode-to-TIA interface parasitics. The TIA incorporates a DC-offset cancellation loop that compensates for photodiode-induced offset currents while providing tunable low-frequency cutoff control over a range of 30 kHz to 1.5 MHz. This tunability enables effective suppression of flicker noise and improves overall signal integrity. The front-end achieves the peak transimpedance gain of 144 dB$Ω$ while maintaining an ultra-low input-referred noise current density of $1\text{ pA}/\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$, demonstrating a highly scalable architecture for high-sensitivity intravascular and endobronchial imaging.

Signal Processing.title: Energy-Aware Vertically Layered Pinching-Antenna System Design with Probabilistic LoS Availability
Signal Processing.summary: This paper investigates a vertically layered pinching antenna (PA) system, in which dielectric waveguides deployed at different heights provide additional vertical spatial degrees of freedom for line-of-sight (LoS)-favorable PA placement. We consider a practical energy model that captures in-waveguide attenuation, base station-to-feed-point optical-fiber loss, and PA repositioning energy, along with a statistical LoS-availability model that depends on elevation and distance. We then jointly optimize the transmit beamforming, PA positions, time allocation, and transmission rates to maximize the expected successfully delivered frame-effective sum rate under per-user outage and quality-of-service constraints. To avoid enumerating the exponentially many LoS states, we derive a certified conditional-moment outage envelope for outage-guaranteed rate selection and a differentiable safe approximation of the chance constraints to facilitate tractable optimization. Building on these results, a block coordinate descent algorithm with a penalty-aided majorization-minimization procedure attains a high-quality suboptimal solution. Simulation results confirm the gains of vertical layering and reveal a fundamental energy-LoS tradeoff: LoS-favorable PA placement generally enhances both performance and reliability, although it incurs higher attenuation, path loss, and energy costs.

Signal Processing.title: Sensing-Based Communication: A Non-Orthogonal Passive Reflection Framework for ISAC
Signal Processing.summary: While integrating uplink without disrupting the primary downlink remains a critical challenge for existing reflective communication systems, this paper proposes a non-orthogonal passive integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) mechanism termed Sensing-based Communication. Originating from and validated within an optical retro-reflective system, this mechanism possesses an underlying wave-agnostic architecture with the potential to be generalized across other physical modalities. It leverages incident downlink signals for parasitic modulation via passive tags. By relying solely on fundamental on-off keying (OOK) reflection, the tag unifies the reflective sensing channel and the uplink communication channel, and simultaneously achieves both sensing and duplex communication. Consequently, our approach introduces uplink capability without sacrificing the downlink data rate or consuming additional spectrum resources. At the receiver, we design a joint decoding architecture combining cross-correlation computation and successive interference cancelation (SIC) to fully exploit the degrees of freedom in broadband signals for multi-user interference suppression. We derive closed-form expressions for the interference and bit error rate (BER) assuming zero-mean Gaussian signals. Using an experimental testbed, we validate the pivotal theoretical finding, the scaling relationship of SINR with signal bandwidth and cross-correlation time--where linear regression yields a strong goodness-of-fit with $R^2 = 0.9688$. Furthermore, evaluations under noise-like orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) waveforms exhibit high consistency between theoretical derivations and simulation data ($R^2 = 0.9372$, mean absolute percentage error, $\text{MAPE} = 14\%$), confirming the model's accuracy and waveform generalizability.

Signal Processing.title: Two-Timescale Receive Combining for Fronthaul-Constrained Uplink XL-MIMO with Visibility Regions
Signal Processing.summary: Extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) arrays are hard to deploy in virtualized radio access networks, because the fronthaul data rate grows with the number of antennas when the radio unit forwards every antenna sample. We propose a two-timescale receiver that allocates the per-user combining ranks under the fronthaul stream budget from the channel statistics. The radio unit applies the long-timescale transform, after which the distributed unit applies a minimum mean-squared-error receiver in the reduced dimension. For disjoint visibility regions, we prove that the reduced-dimension receiver decouples across users. We characterize the sum-rate loss to second order and show that the greedy allocation, which we call saturating capture, minimizes its leading term. In simulations, the allocation gains over a uniform-rank baseline, matches a budget-trimmed threshold rule at a small number of users and exceeds it as the array and the user count grow. The gain grows with the heterogeneity of the per-user eigenvalue profiles and vanishes for identical profiles. Under out-of-cell interference offset by at least half a window width, the gain survives with clean covariances, which window-restricted estimation keeps for disjoint windows.
Signal Processing.comment: The manuscript was submitted to IEEE, and is currently under review

Signal Processing.title: Bayes-Optimal Quantum Computational Sensing via Convex Spectral Design
Signal Processing.summary: Quantum computational sensing performs task-specific inference directly through coherent sensing dynamics, avoiding an intermediate estimation step. Existing designs, however, typically optimize quantum control parameters through nonconvex programs whose performance can depend strongly on initialization. This contribution formulates binary phase classification directly in terms of the sensor's measurement response. For a fixed query budget, generalized quantum signal processing (GQSP) restricts this response to a bounded trigonometric polynomial, while the Bayes classification error is linear in the response. These properties yield an exact finite-dimensional semidefinite program for the globally Bayes-optimal sensor response. Fejér--Riesz factorization and GQSP synthesis then recover a physically realizable control sequence. The same formulation extends naturally to sample-based design and additive phase uncertainty. Numerical tests show improved accuracy and optimization reliability over direct control-angle training; noise-aware redesign also lowers error under phase uncertainty.

Signal Processing.title: Real-Time Trans-Oceanic Fiber Sensing via Convergence of Long-Reach OFDR, High-Speed Optical Networking, and RDMA-Capable Edge-GPUs
Signal Processing.summary: We demonstrate real-time network-integrated bi-directional fiber sensing over a 4400-km subsea cable. Streaming and fusing two OFDR instruments via RDMA over a live transoceanic 130Gbaud coherent link and GPU edge-compute enabling parallel capture of multiple spatial resolutions from ~10m to ~100m.
Signal Processing.comment: 3 pages, 2 figures

Systems and Control.title: Geometric Pairwise Classification of Affine Constraints over Ellipsoidal Regions
Systems and Control.summary: This paper presents a deterministic geometric procedure for analysing affine constraints over fixed ellipsoidal regions, motivated by chance-constrained set approximation. Analytical tests classify inequalities as always violated, never violated, or cutting. Pairwise tests determine whether two inequalities can be strictly violated at a common point, yielding a compatibility matrix. The tests follow from quadratic optimisation and the Karush--Kuhn--Tucker conditions, with explicit treatment of tangencies, parallel normals, and degenerate inequalities. The formulation applies in arbitrary finite dimensions and provides geometric information for subsequent bounds on simultaneous sampled violations and safe-region approximation.

Systems and Control.title: A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for the Minimal Input/Output Node Cardinality Disturbance Decoupling Problem over Networks via Output Feedback
Systems and Control.summary: For networked systems, we propose a polynomial-time algorithm for solving the minimal input/output node cardinality disturbance decoupling problem via output feedback. The algorithm computes an optimal solution, namely, a pair of minimum-cardinality sets of control input and measurement output nodes that achieve disturbance decoupling, by solving a min-cut/max-flow problem on an extended network.
Systems and Control.comment: MATLAB functions implementing the results presented in this article are available in the GitLab repository: https://gitlab.liu.se/lucle71/node-based-ddp or in Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23476722

Systems and Control.title: Beyond Benchmarks: Continuous Edge Inference for Traffic Sign Recognition on Embedded Vehicular Hardware
Systems and Control.summary: Traffic sign recognition (TSR) systems deployed on embedded vehicular hardware face deployment effects that image-based benchmark evaluation does not capture, including frame-to-frame prediction instability in streaming video and load-dependent throughput under sustained operation. We present Edge-TSR, a continuous edge inference system for TSR on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano that combines sparse detection, multi-object tracking, region-level fine-grained classification, and a lightweight track-aware temporal stabilization mechanism adding only 0.07~ms per sampled frame. Evaluating on the source videos of the INTSD benchmark, we find that the state-of-the-art TSR models lose 20-30 percentage points of mAP@50 when moving from image-based to streaming evaluation. Edge-TSR achieves the best streaming classification performance among all evaluated baselines, and temporal stabilization improves accuracy by 10.58 percentage points over per-frame inference. We characterize latency, throughput, and thermal behavior across sampling intervals and four driving conditions, showing that throughput is load-proportional (20 ms per classified region) and that every-frame inference is limited by throughput rather than thermal throttling. A 55-minute, 26 km vehicular deployment demonstrates sustained online operation at 16.18 FPS within safe thermal limits without cloud offload. We also release the annotated 50,732-frame streaming evaluation dataset and full implementation.

Systems and Control.title: A Comprehensive Comparison of Reinforcement Learning Algorithms in Autonomous Driving
Systems and Control.summary: This paper presents a comprehensive comparison of four representative Reinforcement Learning (RL) methods in autonomous vehicle (AV) decision-making, including Fitted Value Iteration (FVI), Rollout Classification Policy Iteration (RCPI), Deep Q-Network (DQN), and a discrete-action adaptation of Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (D-DDPG). The four methods are applied to the same AV decision-making problem at an unsignalized intersection and are compared in terms of optimality, safety, training stability, and training and decision cost. Observations suggest that RCPI provides the closest estimation to the exact solution and has the most stable training curve; however, it is data-intensive and requires the largest volume of data. D-DDPG is the most data-efficient one, but at the price of the training stability. Based on the observations, we provide suggestions for the algorithm selection for AV decision making.

Systems and Control.title: Can sunlight replace LEDs in vertical farms? A critical assessment of optical-fiber daylighting strategies
Systems and Control.summary: Vertical farming is a promising approach for increasing food production in controlled environments while reducing land use, water consumption, and dependence on external climatic conditions. However, its large electricity demand, mainly driven by artificial lighting, still limits its energetic and economic sustainability. This study evaluates the techno-economic potential of an optical-fiber daylighting system designed to transport concentrated sunlight directly to the crop growing zones of a vertical farm. A validated transient vertical farm model was coupled with Tonatiuh ray-tracing simulations to assess a single-axis solar-tracked Fresnel concentration system. Five optical fiber typologies and three daylighting strategies were compared in terms of crop production, specific electrical energy consumption, and light cost, and benchmarked against light-pipe and rooftop photovoltaic solutions. The optical-fiber system achieved an annual useful-PAR delivery efficiency of 19-27%, depending on fiber typology. By distributing daylight across all rack shelves and limiting heat gains through a UV-IR filter, it reduced electricity consumption by 35-89%, compared with 12% for the light-pipe configuration. The daylight-only strategy achieved the lowest SEEC, equal to 1.81 kWh kg^-1, but caused a 52% crop productivity reduction. Hybrid LED-optical-fiber strategies avoided this penalty and achieved electricity savings of about 50%, with a minimum SEEC of 3.16 kWh kg^-1. However, current optical fiber costs make the system economically unattractive, requiring an estimated capital cost reduction of about 90% to become competitive. Rooftop photovoltaics covered 22% of annual electricity demand and achieved an 11-12-year payback, making PV the most economically viable rooftop solar option under current market conditions.

Systems and Control.title: Generalized H matrix stability for power systems
Systems and Control.summary: The small-signal stability of a power system model with arbitrary loads is investigated, with a focus on locally constant power loads in lossless networks. A central element of the proposed analysis is the matrix H, which represents the partial derivatives of generator powers with respect to their relative angles. The local stability of any equilibrium point is determined by the properties of H if the loads consume locally constant power. Specifically, an equilibrium point is asymptotically stable if H is positive definite and unstable if H is full-rank and not positive definite, while several quantitative relationships between the eigenvalues of H and the system Jacobian matrix are also established. The main contribution is that loads are allowed to be arbitrarily located within the transmission network, thereby generalizing the existing H matrix stability criterion which is valid only if loads are located at the same buses as the generators. The advantage of the proposed criterion is demonstrated through case studies involving systems with up to 2869 buses. Accurate stability assessments are maintained, where alternative methods, such as the NRPS model, are found to be overly conservative. Additionally, a computational acceleration by a factor of 340 relative to Jacobian-based methods is achieved.

Systems and Control.title: Autonomous Whole-body Loco-manipulation Using a Snake Robot
Systems and Control.summary: Snake robots can leverage their hyper-redundant morphology for both locomotion and manipulation through distributed body contact but whole-body loco-manipulation is particularly challenging since the entire body serves simultaneously as propulsive mechanism and manipulation tool Prior work on wheeled legged and snake robot platforms has decoupled these functions through dedicated appendages body segmentation or grippers We present closed-loop loco-manipulation with our snake robot COBRA without this distinction such that any part of the body may make contact We develop a contact-implicit dynamic model unifying robot-ground robot-object and object-ground interactions within a Moreau-Jean time-stepping framework and formulate a trajectory optimization over the full-order dynamics guided by a geometric planner and nominal proportional controller to autonomously push an object to a goal location during sidewinding We validate the planner and controller on hardware across varied configurations and present simulation results for a simplified trajectory optimization that resolves robot-object and object-ground contacts

Systems and Control.title: A Cross-Domain TARA-to-NAC Rule Mapping Methodology: From Automotive OEM Networks to Energy Storage Systems
Systems and Control.summary: Threat analysis and risk assessment under ISO/SAE 21434 ends with cybersecurity goals, but existing methods give little structured guidance for turning those goals into enforceable network access control rules. Compliance standards such as IEC 62443, ISO/SAE 21434, and ISO/IEC 27001 are usually applied as parallel efforts rather than as one enforcement architecture. This paper presents a six-step methodology that maps cybersecurity goals from a threat analysis and risk assessment to network access control rules, each placed at a named enforcement point and traceable to the threat records behind it. It also presents a unified compliance framework that treats IEC 62443 and ISO/IEC 27001 as a fixed substrate and domain-specific regulation as an interchangeable overlay. The methodology is applied to an automotive original equipment manufacturer plant network, addressing multi-tier supplier authorization and legacy operational technology devices, and then to utility-scale battery energy storage, where North American Electric Reliability Corporation Critical Infrastructure Protection standards and ISO/IEC 27019 replace the automotive-specific standard while the substrate stays constant. In the automotive example, 37 threat entries and 24 cybersecurity goals yield 23 rules covering 11 of the 13 in-scope goals; the energy example yields six rules. Three derived rules have no equivalent in the cited standards. Both examples are desk-based: the methodology is applied to them, not tested on them. The result is a reusable pattern for translating risk assessment into enforcement across critical infrastructure sectors, with empirical validation left as future work.

Systems and Control.title: A Realistic Discrete Event Simulation model for Ambulance Location and Deployment within a regional Emergency Medical Service
Systems and Control.summary: The objective of Emergency Medical Services (EMSs) is to promptly respond to calls from citizens for first aid, providing pre-hospital care and, if necessary, to transfer patients to an appropriate Emergency Department (ED) by ambulance. The efficiency of such a system strongly depends on the deployment of ambulance home bases, i.e., locations where ambulances and their crews are strategically positioned, ready to respond to emergency calls. This paper presents a general Discrete Event Simulation (DES) model designed to capture the stochastic behaviour and workflow of regional ambulance emergency systems. The proposed model incorporates and integrates information collected from different sources, reproducing very accurately the operation of the ambulance system, thus allowing a more comprehensive and realistic analysis. To show the applicability and reliability of the proposed general model, a case study provided by the Azienda Regionale Emergenza Sanitaria - ARES 118 (an Italian Regional Emergency Medical Services Authority - ARES~118}) is presented. It concerns a territory within the Lazio region of Italy, including a medium-size city along with sparsely populated areas. The reported results about scenario analyses highlight how the model we propose can be fruitfully used by the managers to improve effectiveness and quickness of the entire regional EMS system.

Systems and Control.title: Dynamic Centrality Measures for Water Distribution Network Hydraulics
Systems and Control.summary: Water distribution networks (WDNs) are susceptible to various failures, including but not limited to human errors, cyber-attacks, and network modifications, necessitating the vulnerability analysis of WDNs. Graph-theoretic centrality measures---as a main class of centrality measures---aim to rank the network components solely based on their influence (i.e., criticality) on the WDN topology in the case of input changes, while overlooking the WDN dynamics. To overcome such a limitation, this paper uses a control-theoretic centrality measure to identify the network's most and least influential pipes in WDNs, by simultaneously incorporating the dynamics and topology of the WDN. First, given a WDN modeled by nonlinear differential-algebraic equations (NDAEs) consisting of transient flow dynamics as differential equation (DE) and conservation of water mass as algebraic equation (AE) and considering the pipe flow rates as states of the state-space (SS) representation, we extract a linearized system modeled by linear ordinary differential equations (LODEs) around the equilibrium (i.e., steady) flow rate vector. Second, treating pipe flow rates as SS nodes (states), we introduce a node centrality-based measure, namely \textit{vulnerability vector (VV)}, to rank the network pipes based on their influence on the dynamics and topology of the WDN in the case of input changes. In particular, the network's most and least influential pipes can be identified through such a centrality-based approach. This enables water engineers to understand the WDN's vulnerability better and effectively prioritize the maintenance and operational efforts on the most influential pipes within the WDN.

Systems and Control.title: Adaptive PD-like Fault Tolerant Controller for a Class of Nonlinear Systems
Systems and Control.summary: The article presents a nonlinear adaptive control strategy for a class of feedback-linearizable systems subject to process faults and disturbance. The controller is derived through Lyapunov analysis and incorporates an adaptive proportional gain within a PD-like structure, preserving simplicity while providing nonlinear adaptive behavior. A residual-based gating mechanism activates the adaptation only when the tracking error exceeds a prescribed threshold, preventing unnecessary gain updates during nominal operation and improving robustness to noise. The proposed design yields uniform global ultimate boundedness of the closed-loop signals, with explicit expressions for the steady-state tracking bound. Practical tuning guidelines for the adaptive parameters and Lyapunov matrix selection are provided to ensure consistent gating behavior. Simulations on a precision positioning system illustrate effective compensation of process faults, rapid gain escalation during degraded conditions, and smooth reversion to nominal performance, demonstrating that the method enhances fault tolerance while retaining the structural simplicity of PD control.

Systems and Control.title: Nonlinear Fault Tolerant Control of Wind Turbine Pitch Systems: A Comparative Study
Systems and Control.summary: Electro-hydraulic pitch systems account for about one fifth of wind-turbine failures, motivating the development of resilient control strategies for fault mitigation. The study considers a large set of robust nonlinear control designs of different feedback principles and architectures, and assesses their fault-tolerant capabilities in comparison to each other and against the industrial standard, i.e. the Proportional-Integral (PI) controller. The implementation and tuning of each scheme is based on a high-fidelity simulator to ensure nominal performance, whereas each controller is deployed unchanged on an experimental apparatus that includes a full-scale electro-hydraulic pitch system. The comparative evaluation of the considered fault-tolerant solutions is carried out through several tests that cover nominal operation and twenty-five representative fault scenarios, including sensor, process, and actuator faults. The analysis highlights the trade-off between performance preservation under faults and increased actuator chattering. The experimental results show that introducing a dynamic input-reconstruction module into the design of the nonlinear controllers significantly reduces actuator chatter without compromising their fault-tolerant properties.

Systems and Control.title: LACART: Lookahead-Augmented Collision Avoidance and Reference Tracking Strategies for Safety-Critical Robots
Systems and Control.summary: Autonomous racing provides a demanding testbed for collision avoidance under tight geometric and computational constraints. Building on a recent conference contribution and a master's dissertation, LACART combines lookahead-based control barrier functions (CBFs), a relaxed control Lyapunov function (CLF), and quadratic programming (QP) to modify nominal vehicle commands for obstacle avoidance and reference tracking. The method handles circular obstacles and track boundaries in a common optimisation layer. Comparative simulation results against Huang \emph{et al.} \cite{r9} show similar full-track paths and lower median computation times: 0.31 versus 0.33 ms per step and 0.023 versus 0.025 ms per QP solve. The dissertation further demonstrates a 1:43-scale vehicle with camera-based estimation and wireless actuation at a reported 25 Hz control rate. We identify the conditions linking lookahead-point clearance to body clearance, illustrate hardware limitations, and propose a recorded demonstration of safety intervention and recovery. The contribution targets ground-robot collision avoidance and real-time safety monitoring.

Systems and Control.title: A Novel Algorithm to Simulate Conductance-based Neuronal Networks
Systems and Control.summary: Conductance-based models are central to neurophysiology and neuromorphic engineering, yet their simulation scales poorly to large networks. We study and analyze an iterative solver that operates in signal space. Each iteration reduces to $N$ decoupled scalar linear time-varying differential equations, one per neuron, which are solved in parallel and in closed form. The solver admits two complementary interpretations: a variable metric forward-backward splitting method, rooted in operator theory, and a waveform relaxation quasi-Newton method, rooted in circuit simulation. We prove uniform and superlinear convergence, with a bound that reflects the conductance structure of the dynamics. The algorithm is illustrated on the classical Hodgkin--Huxley neuron and on networks of up to 5000 neurons.

Systems and Control.title: Beyond Feasibility: Efficient and Robust On-Device Localization with UWB Concurrent Transmissions
Systems and Control.summary: Concurrent transmissions (CTX) enable an ultra-wideband (UWB) tag to range to, or self-localize from, multiple nodes with a single frame reception, significantly improving update rate and energy efficiency compared to traditional approaches. Prior work demonstrated the concept feasibility via prototypes whose real-world applicability is however hindered by many limitations, notably including their inability to directly execute on UWB tags and to cope with interfering UWB signals. We address these limitations in two ways. First, we redesign the core CTX techniques to enable a fast and efficient execution on resource-constrained MCUs without sacrificing accuracy. Second, we leverage the new features in the IEEE 802.15.4z standard to achieve robustness to interference from other UWB devices and enable tags to dynamically select which anchors to use, two crucial and unexplored capabilities in CTX-based systems. We quantitatively evaluate our approach experimentally in two real-world testbeds with different characteristics. We first analyze our new techniques individually, offering an in-depth discussion of design choices and performance trade-offs. Then, we embed all our techniques into a CTX-based system enabling a tag to self-localize entirely on-device, unlocking gains up to 44% in runtime and 85% in energy efficiency compared to traditional approaches.
Systems and Control.comment: Submitted to the IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing

Systems and Control.title: Data-driven representation of continuous-time linear time-invariant behaviors via Hankel integral operators
Systems and Control.summary: We present a data-driven representation of the finite-horizon behavior of deterministic controllable continuous-time LTI systems. We first introduce a notion of persistency of excitation for continuous-time signals that does not require the signal to be differentiable. We then show that, when the input is persistently exciting in this sense, the closure of the range of a Hankel integral operator built from a single input-output trajectory equals the behavior of the system over a finite time horizon. This result provides a nonparametric representation of system trajectories directly in terms of measured data, without requiring an explicit parametric model of the system.

Systems and Control.title: Characterization of the Frequency-Current Curve of First-Order High-Pass Neurons
Systems and Control.summary: A spiking model, called the High-Pass (HP) model, has recently been proposed as a minimal excitable primitive. This model is composed of a static activation function, usually a sigmoid, in positive feedback with a high-pass filter. The HP model enters a tonic spiking regime whenever its input lies in the high-gain zone of the sigmoid, where the sigmoid's slope exceeds 1. In neuroscience, the frequency-current (FI) curve is the standard way of characterizing the tonic spiking regime of a neuron. So far, the FI curve of the HP model has been characterized analytically only for specific sigmoids, and has otherwise been computed through simulation. These simulations are computationally heavy, since simulating neurons requires solving a stiff system of differential equations. This paper bridges this gap by analytically characterizing the FI curve of the HP model with a first-order high-pass filter, for a broad class of sigmoid functions. The FI curve of the first-order HP model can be computed by solving two input-independent equations and evaluating two input-dependent integrals, with no need to simulate the model itself. A spiking primitive is said to be Type I (resp. Type II) if tonic spiking starts at a zero (resp. non-zero) frequency. This paper also shows that, for the HP model, the type depends solely on the local shape of the sigmoid at the outer edges of its high-gain zone. A sharp corner, where the derivative approaches a value strictly smaller than 1 from the outside, yields a Type I primitive. A locally twice differentiable corner, with a bounded second derivative and a derivative approaching 1 at the edge, yields a Type II primitive.

Systems and Control.title: RADAR Perception for Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance onboard small-scale Quadrotor UAVs
Systems and Control.summary: Fast dynamic obstacle avoidance (DOA) on uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) demands not only low-latency control and actuation but also reliable, long-range perception to detect obstacles and estimate their motion in time to maneuver. We present, to the best of our knowledge, the first mmWave RADAR-based perception-and-control system for fast onboard DOA. We derive and analyze latency and spatial bounds that relate sensing range, relative speed, and control delay, yielding sufficient conditions for successful avoidance. We further extend prior latency analyses to include the decision latency of the tracker and trigger to evaluate them per trial. Our computationally efficient system combines a lightweight interacting multiple models (IMM) tracker with a control-barrier functions (CBF) controller that directly outputs evasive accelerations. In 300 throw experiments spanning three object sizes and varying visibility (light and dark), it achieves mean position errors of at most 0.15 m, 0.93m, and 0.87m in the x, y, and z directions, with a similar spread in 90 experiments in smoke. An onboard implementation on a Raspberry Pi 4B demonstrates real-time feasibility with an end-to-end processing latency of approximately 14ms per RADAR frame and a system latency of 75ms from first detection to the avoidance command. The UAV successfully avoided obstacles in all 20 tethered indoor flights and all 39 untethered outdoor avoidance maneuvers across three ball sizes, during both hover and forward flights at up to 5m/s with measured closing speeds up to 14.6m/s.
Systems and Control.comment: Preprint. This work has been submitted for possible publication and is currently under review

Systems and Control.title: Data-Driven Continuous-Time LQR: Linking Reinforcement Learning and Behavioral System Theory
Systems and Control.summary: Behavioral system theory and reinforcement learning (RL) have independently developed data-driven approaches to the continuous-time LQR problem, yet their respective methods have largely evolved in separation. We connect these two adjacent lines of work by studying their data-driven parameterizations, namely a closed-loop (CL) parameterization from behavioral system theory and an integral RL (IRL) parameterization. The CL parameterization characterizes the closed-loop system via a matrix that satisfies equality constraints. While this parameterization has been extensively studied for discrete-time systems, we adapt key results to the continuous-time setting and develop a policy iteration (PI) scheme, derive an algebraic Riccati equation, and introduce an alternative convex program. The IRL parameterization utilizes off-policy data to perform policy evaluation, which is used for PI or value iteration. Within the IRL framework, we derive a policy gradient flow and propose convex programs for the LQR problem. Finally, we provide a unified treatment of these parameterizations that enables a systematic understanding of existing approaches, and clarifies their structural relationships.

Systems and Control.title: Safety Blind Spot in Remote Driving: Considerations for Risk Assessment of Connection Loss Fallback Strategies
Systems and Control.summary: As part of the overall goal of driverless road vehicles, remote driving is a major emerging field of research of its own. Current remote driving concepts for public road traffic often establish a fallback strategy of immediate braking to a standstill in the event of a connection loss. This may seem like the most logical option when human control of the vehicle is lost. However, our simulation results from hundreds of scenarios based on naturalistic traffic scenes indicate high collision rates for any immediate substantial deceleration to a standstill in urban settings. We show that such a fallback strategy can result in a SOTIF-relevant hazard, raising the question whether this design decision is acceptable. Therefore, from a safety perspective, we call this problem a safety blind spot, as safety analyses in this regard seem to be very rare. In this article, we first present a simulation on a naturalistic dataset that shows a high probability of collision in the described case. Second, we discuss the severity of the resulting potential rear-end collisions and provide an even more severe example by including a large commercial vehicle in the potential collision.
Systems and Control.comment: This work has been submitted for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

Systems and Control.title: An Inspection Game for Monitor Design Against GNSS Timing Attacks in Synchronous Islanding
Systems and Control.summary: Phasor measurement units (PMUs) take their time from GNSS, so a spoofer that slowly drags a receiver clock rotates the reported phase without touching the power waveform. The threat is acute in synchronous islanding, where a controller keeps an islanded generator in phase with the grid, using one PMU on each side of an open breaker, so that the two can be reconnected at any moment: a differential clock bias of about $0.56$\,ms can make the controller hold the generator $10^\circ$ out of phase while it reports perfect synchronism. We cast the defense as a zero-sum inspection game. The defender, as inspector, chooses its timing monitors and audits the clocks periodically; the attacker, as inspectee, drags the two clocks to an unsafe bias by the next audit; the payoff is the evidence, the Kullback--Leibler divergence between the probability laws of the defender's record under attack and under normal operation. Our central result is that the evidence equals the cost of the cheapest innocent explanation of the attacked record. This single identity predicts which monitors work, turns the attacker's best response into a strictly convex quadratic program, and turns the defender's design into a convex program with a saddle point. Pairing explanations, which bound the evidence from above, with test statistics, which bound it from below, certifies audit periods in which every successful attack leaves at least a threshold of evidence. On a 50\,Hz island, these evidence-based periods, at the matched-test threshold, are up to 8.4 times as long as those of a rule that checks each monitor separately, and the case study favors placing the better oscillator on the utility side of the breaker.

Systems and Control.title: An Optimal Power-Flow Grouping Topology for Single-Isolation-Stage Multi-Output Solid-State Transformers
Systems and Control.summary: Electric-vehicle dc fast-charging stations and data centers require multiple high-power dc outputs with independently varying demands. Conventional multi-output solid-state transformers typically establish a common dc bus and use downstream dc/dc converters for port-level regulation and, where required, galvanic isolation. A single-isolation-stage solid-state transformer can eliminate this additional high-power interface stage by directly forming multiple isolated outputs from its submodule dc/dc stages. However, because one submodule is generally insufficient for an individual output port, multiple submodules must be connected in parallel, while inter-submodule balancing circuits redistribute power under unbalanced loading. The submodule grouping therefore determines the internal balancing-power paths. Sequential grouping can create long transfer paths and accumulated balancing power, increasing current stress and losses. This paper proposes an optimal power-flow grouping topology that interleaves submodules assigned to different output ports, thereby localizing power redistribution and reducing the power processed by the balancing circuits. Analytical models quantify the required balancing power and its reduction relative to sequential grouping. A coordinated submodule-bypass strategy is also developed, and the remaining output-power capability under different fault scenarios is evaluated. A six-submodule prototype validates the proposed topology.
