Under the same highly unbalanced operating conditions, the proposed topology reduces the maximum submodule dc-link voltage difference by 63\% and the peak balancing current by 14.5%, while improving the measured efficiency by approximately 5.6% at rated power. Stable post-fault operation is also experimentally demonstrated.
Systems and Control.comment: 13 pages, 19 figures. Submitted to IEEE for possible publication

Systems and Control.title: DC-Link Voltage Regulation in a Single-Isolation-Stage Multioutput Solid-State Transformer for Wide-Range DC Outputs
Systems and Control.summary: Single-isolation-stage solid-state transformers with balancing circuits eliminate an additional downstream dc--dc conversion stage. However, the remaining isolated converters must directly accommodate a wide output-voltage range. This paper investigates variable dc-link voltage operation of a single-isolation-stage multioutput SST to ease this requirement. Coordinated cascaded H-bridge modulation and embedded four-switch balancing circuits support intentionally unequal submodule dc-link voltages, allowing the isolated-converter input voltages to be adjusted according to the output requirements. The achievable voltage range is determined by relating the required balancing power to the BC transfer capability within the available CHB switching windows, subject to modulation and peak and rms current limits. The analysis quantifies the range extension provided by BC operation beyond modulation alone. For a single-phase-shift dual-active-bridge converter, input-voltage following within this range reduces the calculated peak current and extends the ideal zero-voltage-switching region compared with fixed input. Experiments on a six-submodule SST prototype demonstrate unequal dc-link voltage operation and inter-submodule power exchange. Experiments result on DAB demonstrate reduced current stress and improved efficiency with voltage following.
Systems and Control.comment: Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics (TPEL) for possible publication

Systems and Control.title: Reconciling European Electricity Data with Diffusion Priors Learned from Observations Alone
Systems and Control.summary: The ENTSO-E Transparency Platform publishes generation, load, and cross-border power flows for European bidding zones. The values carry undocumented errors and violate energy conservation, and data reconciliation consists in correcting them to satisfy that balance. In this work, we formulate data reconciliation as Bayesian inference. Classical methods implicitly take a uniform prior, which we replace with a diffusion model estimated from the observations alone by empirical-Bayes expectation-maximization. The resulting posterior is sampled with a guided process whose projection step makes every sample satisfy the balance exactly. On synthetic systems of six to thirty-five bidding zones, built from ENTSO-E resource-adequacy data, the diffusion prior gives the most accurate reconciliation, increasingly so as the system grows. Its credible intervals are calibrated or conservative, and it remains the most accurate under a misspecified noise covariance. Finally, when the generation of entire zones goes unreported, the classical methods fail while the learned prior recovers it from cross-zone structure.

Systems and Control.title: Voltage Sensitivity-Based Fair Allocation of Operating Envelopes in Distribution Networks
Systems and Control.summary: Operating envelopes (OEs) define the admissible active and reactive power injections of distributed energy resources while respecting distribution network limits. In unbalanced low-voltage feeders, OEs based only on voltage magnitude and thermal limits may overestimate available flexibility because they neglect power quality requirements. This paper develops a three-phase unbalanced AC optimal power flow framework to compute coupled active and reactive power OEs while enforcing limits on the voltage unbalance factor (VUF). It also proposes a fairness mechanism based on voltage sensitivities to allocate available flexibility among multiple photovoltaic (PV) units. The proposed mechanism is compared with lexicographic max--min fairness as a benchmark for equitable resource allocation. Case studies on unbalanced test feeders evaluate how VUF constraints change the feasible operating region of PV units. The results show how VUF constraints affect feasible flexibility and demonstrate that the proposed voltage sensitivity-based mechanism is nearly six times faster than lexicographic max-min fairness.

Systems and Control.title: Probabilistic Sequential Safety for Stochastic Dynamical Systems
Systems and Control.summary: In this letter, we investigate a notion of probabilistic safety for a stochastic dynamical system. Standard safety notions are based on the idea that an unsafe region of the state-space must be avoided at each instant. In contrast, we study a sequential safety notion which is based on avoiding a tuple of target regions of the state-space. The proposed safety notion is inspired by many practical systems, ranging from modeling jailbreak attacks in large language models (LLMs) to predicting hazardous chemical reactions. In solving the sequential safety problem, we solve a sequential reachability problem for a stochastic dynamical system.

Systems and Control.title: Controlled Excitation for Identification of Nonlinear Systems with Saturated Outputs
Systems and Control.summary: We consider nonlinear systems whose measured output is the product of an unknown matrix and a known saturation function of the unmeasured state. Generating excitation that allows the matrix to be recovered from the output is challenging when the dynamics are largely unknown. We exploit saturation to construct this excitation. Under a geometric accessibility condition, we derive explicit open-loop controls that drive the state into regions where the saturation takes prescribed values. For componentwise saturations, this condition holds generically with as few as two independent control directions. The controls require no state measurement and only partial knowledge of the dynamics, with no information on the structure of its nonlinear part. The resulting regressor is known in advance, and the unknown matrix is recovered exactly by a closed-form regression. Under stronger structural assumptions and with sufficiently many independent outputs, an output feedback tracks prescribed reference trajectories within the unsaturated region to arbitrary accuracy and permits exact state recovery. Suitably chosen references then also enable exact identification of linearly parameterized (nonlinear) dynamics. We analyze robustness to measurement noise and illustrate the method numerically in the presence of both measurement and dynamical noise.

Systems and Control.title: Real-Time Nonlinear Mixed-Integer Model Predictive Control With Horizon-Tail Relaxations
Systems and Control.summary: Model predictive control (MPC) of nonlinear systems with discrete decisions leads to mixed-integer nonlinear programs (MINLPs) whose combinatorial complexity often prevents real-time deployment. In this paper, we propose a decomposition-based MPC method that reorders and reduces computations to shorten the delay between receiving a state measurement and applying the control input. Before the measurement arrives, we solve a continuous relaxation of the MINLP at a predicted state and construct a mixed-integer quadratic program (MIQP). Once the measured state is available, we solve the MIQP that reconstructs the discrete controls and simultaneously performs one sequential quadratic programming step toward the corresponding nonlinear solution. To reduce the combinatorial complexity in the horizon length, we either fix the integer controls or relax their integrality over the prediction horizon tail, while retaining an integer-feasible first control input. We derive error bounds relating the nonlinear objective values obtained with the horizon-tail approximations to the optimal value of the original mixed-integer problem. In a data center cooling example, the proposed method reduces mean feedback computation time by 94% relative to a state-of-the-art MINLP method with a total closed-loop cost difference of less than 1%.

Systems and Control.title: Circuit Theory-Informed AI for Condition Monitoring in Power Electronics
Systems and Control.summary: Artificial intelligence for power electronics is evolving toward a deeper comprehension of system intrinsic behaviors and dynamics. As a novel integration of neural computation and electric circuits, spike-based neuromorphic computing offers promising potential in high energy efficiency and adaptability for data-driven applications. Building on the latency-coding principles, this article proposes a framework for data-light condition monitoring that relies solely on three-phase AC current measurements. The AC current signals are encoded as membrane potentials of RC-based spiking neurons, which are inherently compatible with spiking neural networks that can effectively facilitate the estimation of device parameters. Case studies are presented to validate the performances, while constraints and further optimizations are also evaluated and discussed, and future extensions of the methodology are provided.
Systems and Control.comment: The manuscript has been accepted for publication in the Proceedings of 2026 IEEE Design Methodologies Conference (DMC 2026)

Systems and Control.title: An Enhanced Submodule for Modular Multilevel Converters With DC Fault-Clearing Capability
Systems and Control.summary: Modular multilevel converter (MMC) has been successfully applied in various power electronic systems owing to its high efficiency, scalability, and superior output performance. Although the half-bridge submodule (HBSM) is widely used in MMCs for its structural simplicity, it is incapable of handling direct-current (DC) short-circuit faults. The diode-clamp submodule (DCSM) addresses this limitation by providing DC fault ride-through capability. However, because its two identical capacitors are connected in series, the equivalent capacitance is halved. To overcome this drawback, an enhanced SM is proposed in this paper. For the same energy storage capacity, the proposed SM reduces the total required capacitance by 75% compared with the DCSM. In addition, the proposed SM requires one fewer diode than the DCSM, thereby lowering the overall MMC capital cost. The topology and the operating modes of the proposed SM are described in detail, and its functionality is experimentally validated. The results demonstrate that the proposed SM can suppress DC fault currents and restore normal operation without additional external protection devices.

Systems and Control.title: Safe Circumnavigation on Heterogeneous Orbits: A Range-Only HOCBF-QP Framework for Nonholonomic Multi-Agent Systems
Systems and Control.summary: Circumnavigating a stationary target with a team of robots requires each robot to hold its own standoff distance, to stay evenly spaced from its neighbours, and to avoid collisions with the target and with each other at every instant. The task becomes arduous when the robots are assigned different orbital radii, as their sensors or roles may demand. This paper presents a safety-critical control framework for this problem. Each robot commands both its acceleration and its turn-rate, measures only its distance to the target, and exchanges information only with its two ring neighbours. The design has three features. First, a structural property of the model lets one control law serve every robot regardless of its assigned radius. Second, the acceleration drives each radius exactly to its target, while the turn-rate balances the formation with the neighbours. Third, a higher-order control-barrier-function quadratic program enforces target, geofence, and inter-robot safety on both inputs at once; it leaves the nominal controller untouched away from the constraints and stays valid while the unmeasured range rate is still being estimated. Simulations confirm these guarantees. In a comparison, the closest existing multi-orbit design, even with full state information, violates both the target standoff and the inter-robot margin, whereas the proposed controller does not.

Systems and Control.title: Fair Selection of Generalized Nash Equilibria: A Comparability Perspective
Systems and Control.summary: Generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) problems model self-interested agents coupled through their costs and shared constraints, and arise throughout control applications that allocate a scarce common resource. Such problems typically admit a continuum of equilibria, so any implementation must \emph{select} one. This selection is not neutral: it decides how the cost of the shared constraint is distributed among the agents, a decision often expected to be fair. The variational GNE (v-GNE), which charges all agents a uniform shadow price, is the conventional choice and is frequently advocated as fair. Through the lens of \emph{comparability} from social choice theory, we show that the GNE set itself requires no inter-agent comparability of costs, whereas the v-GNE implicitly assumes cardinal unit comparability, one of the stronger notions. We then introduce the fair GNE (f-GNE), which selects an equilibrium by explicitly optimizing a fairness metric matched to the comparability at hand, and give constructive routes to compute it for single-constraint and linear-quadratic games. An electric-vehicle charging game serves as a running example throughout this self-contained tutorial.
Systems and Control.comment: Book chapter, 25 pages, 4 figures. To appear in Socio-Inspired and Socially Aware Control for Complex Systems, Springer

Systems and Control.title: Supporting Data Center Grid Integration via Co-Optimized Battery Energy Storage Sizing and Capacity Allocation
Systems and Control.summary: Interconnecting large data centers can be delayed by grid requirements on demand flexibility, ramping limits, and ride-through performance. This paper proposes an optimization-based framework to size a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) that accelerates data center grid integration by providing BESS capacity required to meet selected flexibility and grid-support requirements. The model co-optimizes BESS power rating and energy capacity while allocating capability across three services: (i) demand response over a specified duration, (ii) mitigation of high-magnitude, high-frequency load fluctuations through reserved active power with zero net state-of-charge change, and (iii) voltage support via reactive power capability at the point of common coupling. Minute-level operational scheduling enforces state-of-charge feasibility and load ramp constraints, and incorporates a controllable queue of delay-insensitive computing tasks to enhance flexibility. A case study using a real data center load profile demonstrates the proposed method and quantifies the BESS power-energy requirements and operational trade-offs needed to satisfy the multi-service constraints, providing practical guidance for interconnection planning and deployment.

Systems and Control.title: Grid-Oriented Probabilistic Load Forecasting for AI Data Centers
Systems and Control.summary: Probabilistic load forecasts for AI data centers need to represent both uncertainty under changing workloads and temporal dependence to support grid operations. This paper develops an open, grid-oriented benchmark using measured GPU power from a 448-GPU AI cluster. Forecasts are evaluated through four stages: probabilistic prediction, online uncertainty calibration, temporal scenario generation, and horizon-wide reserve sizing. Following a change in cluster utilization, a quantile LightGBM forecast achieves only 63.4% coverage for a nominal 90% interval, while online regime-conditioned calibration increases coverage to 87.3%. Even with well-calibrated marginal forecasts, independent sampling produces unrealistic ramp distributions and excessive reserve procurement. Reconstructing temporal dependence from historical forecast errors reduces the discrepancy in ramp statistics and lowers realized reserve cost by 7.4-10.6% across three forecasting tasks. These findings show that marginal forecast quality alone is insufficient for operational decisions and motivate joint evaluation of calibration, temporal structure, and decision outcomes.

Systems and Control.title: Defense Filters for Robust Learning of Partially Observed Dynamical Systems
Systems and Control.summary: Robust estimation of unknown system dynamics from partial observations under attack is a core challenge in learning for control, increasingly critical in multi-agent networks subject to adversarial data poisoning. Existing methods either require highly restrictive assumptions on the adversary or yield weak error bounds. In this paper, we consider identifying partially observed linear dynamical systems subject to adversarial attacks with an attack probability $p < 0.5$ at each time. We propose a defense-filtering framework leveraging knowledge of the observation matrix to construct a defense filter satisfying full column rank and subspace separability conditions, which enables the evaluation of a single-attack scenario against observed data. Using this framework, we analyze the constrained $\ell_2$-norm estimator and establish finite-sample error bounds for recovering the Markov parameter matrix up to a linear transformation. This is the first approach to provide provable system identification guarantees via a defense filter for partially observed systems subject to harsh environments where the attack probability approaches $0.5$.

Systems and Control.title: A Measure-Theoretic Formulation of Behavioral Systems
Systems and Control.summary: Ensemble control specifies probability laws on admissible trajectories, including their temporal dependence. Starting from an arbitrary closed behavior, we organize its laws into a framework that connects standard probability-measure geometry, occupation-measure control, and data-driven trajectory parametrization. Classical convexity and extreme-point properties describe the feasible laws, while classical Bellman duality governs additive control objectives. On compact state and input spaces, full-path constrained duality for continuous trajectory functions gives primal attainment and zero gap whenever feasible. For controllable linear time-invariant systems, the noise-free Fundamental Lemma yields an equivalent law-level Hankel factorization, with a canonical pseudoinverse lift. The factorization transfers trajectory-law constraints exactly to coefficient space and connects them to covariance control. Explicit noisy-Hankel bounds quantify subspace approximation for second-moment-bounded laws under known rank and Gaussian output measurement noise. Numerical studies include a nonlinear reset problem whose nonadjacent correlation constraint requires temporal memory, covariance-constrained optimization, and noisy-data policy evaluation. Known transition kernels provide a further structural perspective through history-conditional consistency.

Systems and Control.title: Extending Grid Foundation Models for Phasor-Domain Dynamic Simulation
Systems and Control.summary: Grid Foundation Models (GridFMs) are emerging as a powerful framework for learning and transferring knowledge across power grids and grid analysis tasks. This work extends GridFMs from steady-state analysis to dynamic simulation. We present DynGridFM, which uses component-wise tokenization and a structured latent operator to learn shared dynamic representations across heterogeneous grids and enable transfer to unseen systems. Pretrained on nine grids, DynGridFM is adapted to a held-out 48-machine grid, where fine-tuning on 64 trajectories achieves accuracy comparable to training from scratch on 128. On a single GPU, it achieves 924x to 1232x speedup over numerical simulators on one CPU core.

Systems and Control.title: An Ultra-Low-Noise Tunable TIA in 45nm Silicon Photonics for Electro-Optical Ultrasound Data Acquisition
Systems and Control.summary: This paper presents the design and experimental characterization of a 32-channel, WDM-compatible electronic-photonic receiver array fabricated in the GlobalFoundries 45nm monolithic silicon photonics process. Optimized for miniaturized, millimeter-scale electro-optical ultrasound data acquisition probes for broadband photo-acoustic imaging (PAI), the chip utilizes integrated micro-ring resonator (MRR) demultiplexers and photodiode (PD) arrays to decode multi-wavelength acoustic signals outside the body. This work focuses specifically on the comprehensive characterization of the receiver front-end, evaluating both the optical WDM filter bank and the transimpedance amplifier (TIA) performance. Monolithic co-integration minimizes critical photodiode-to-TIA interface parasitics. The TIA incorporates a DC-offset cancellation loop that compensates for photodiode-induced offset currents while providing tunable low-frequency cutoff control over a range of 30 kHz to 1.5 MHz. This tunability enables effective suppression of flicker noise and improves overall signal integrity. The front-end achieves the peak transimpedance gain of 144 dB$Ω$ while maintaining an ultra-low input-referred noise current density of $1\text{ pA}/\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$, demonstrating a highly scalable architecture for high-sensitivity intravascular and endobronchial imaging.

Systems and Control.title: Sensing-Based Communication: A Non-Orthogonal Passive Reflection Framework for ISAC
Systems and Control.summary: While integrating uplink without disrupting the primary downlink remains a critical challenge for existing reflective communication systems, this paper proposes a non-orthogonal passive integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) mechanism termed Sensing-based Communication. Originating from and validated within an optical retro-reflective system, this mechanism possesses an underlying wave-agnostic architecture with the potential to be generalized across other physical modalities. It leverages incident downlink signals for parasitic modulation via passive tags. By relying solely on fundamental on-off keying (OOK) reflection, the tag unifies the reflective sensing channel and the uplink communication channel, and simultaneously achieves both sensing and duplex communication. Consequently, our approach introduces uplink capability without sacrificing the downlink data rate or consuming additional spectrum resources. At the receiver, we design a joint decoding architecture combining cross-correlation computation and successive interference cancelation (SIC) to fully exploit the degrees of freedom in broadband signals for multi-user interference suppression. We derive closed-form expressions for the interference and bit error rate (BER) assuming zero-mean Gaussian signals. Using an experimental testbed, we validate the pivotal theoretical finding, the scaling relationship of SINR with signal bandwidth and cross-correlation time--where linear regression yields a strong goodness-of-fit with $R^2 = 0.9688$. Furthermore, evaluations under noise-like orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) waveforms exhibit high consistency between theoretical derivations and simulation data ($R^2 = 0.9372$, mean absolute percentage error, $\text{MAPE} = 14\%$), confirming the model's accuracy and waveform generalizability.

Information Theory.title: How far does a hash-only sender go? A pre-registered map of sender memory versus bits for short text messages
Information Theory.summary: Can a sender that only computes hashes, with a language model only at the receiver, transmit short human text more cheaply than a classical sender trained on the same domain? We answer with one pre-registered run on 1,000 English user utterances from Taskmaster-1. The primary endpoint is the cost per message to deliver 100% of the messages (hash bits, plus a 2-byte negative acknowledgement and the raw text when the first attempt fails), paired against an in-domain PPM order-1 sender. The hash-only sender delivered 857 of 1,000 messages on the first attempt and cost 192.8 bits per message, 18.4 bits more than PPM order 1 (95% bootstrap interval 10.9 to 26.3); by the pre-registered rule it spends more and is not equivalent within one byte. As secondary results we map measured sender memory against bits. The hash-only sender (8,190 B on a host build, keyed BLAKE2b tag included, as in every method) was the cheapest point in bits from 8,190 B up to, but excluding, PPM order 1 at 24,844 B, 45 to 46 bits below smaz2 and Unishox2; from PPM order 1 upwards, in-domain senders spend fewer bits, except order 2 pruned to 16 KiB. In airtime it loses to PPM order 1 on all five links priced, to Unishox2 on four, and to raw text with a tag on two, because each failure costs an acknowledgement frame and a fallback frame. A wider receiver search recovers half of the failures and makes the cost 7.7 bits lower than PPM order 1, at about three minutes of receiver time per failure, and still loses in airtime on four of five links. We report the measurement as a delimitation, with every deviation of the run.
Information Theory.comment: 10 pages, 1 figure, 2 tables. Code, data and per-message results: https://github.com/msamoilenko/hash-sender-llm-receiver

Information Theory.title: Asymptotic Analysis of Data Deduplication Under a Constant Edit Model
Information Theory.summary: Data deduplication has become increasingly important in large-scale storage systems, driven by the rapid growth of digital data. By identifying and removing repeats in the data stream, deduplication saves storage space more efficiently than traditional compression methods. In this paper, we study the performance of variable-length deduplication and multi-chunk deduplication algorithms from an information-theoretic perspective, focusing on data streams where repeats are approximate rather than exact. We consider two probabilistic source models in which source strings consist of repeated blocks that are modified by either a constant number of substitution edits or burst-insertion edits per block, the latter capturing the localized edit patterns commonly observed in real-world data. For both models, we show that variable-length deduplication achieves asymptotically arbitrarily large compression ratios, and that multi-chunk deduplication achieves compression within a constant factor of the source entropy under mild conditions.

Information Theory.title: An Efficient Synchronization Scheme for Distributed Bandits
Information Theory.summary: We study the problem of synchronizing two players in a \emph{distributed multi-armed bandit} setting. The probability of \emph{synchronization error} is analyzed by recasting synchronization as a \emph{communication problem}. Using a well-designed random coding ensemble, we derive error exponents for the maximum-likelihood decoder. We then introduce a \emph{universal decoder} that achieves the same error exponents as the optimal decoder. Finally, applying these results to distributed multi-armed bandits, we show an upper bound on the regret of our synchronization scheme.
Information Theory.comment: Accepted at IEEE ISIT2026. 3 Figures, 6 pages. Theorem 7 redrawn

Information Theory.title: Quasipolynomial-Time Planning for Decodable POMDPs
Information Theory.summary: We study planning for finite-horizon partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) with finite state, action, and observation spaces. Both exact and approximate planning are known to be computationally hard in this setting, so prior work has explored natural assumptions that make planning easier. Recent work [Golowich et al., 2022] gave quasipolynomial-time approximate planning algorithms for observable POMDPs. These are POMDPs whose observation channels satisfy an $\ell_1$-observability condition, but notably, no assumptions are required on the transition dynamics. In a similar vein, for every fixed $ρ>0$, we give quasipolynomial-time approximate planning algorithms for $ρ$-decodable POMDPs. We show that decodability is implied by both $\ell_1$- and $\ell_2$-observability and is strictly weaker than observability. Moreover, we show that the optimal decodability constant can be computed in polynomial time, whereas computing the optimal $\ell_1$-observability constant is NP-hard in the worst case. We also show that the fast filter-forgetting guarantee underlying the approach of [Golowich et al., 2022] does not extend directly from $\ell_1$-observability to constant $\ell_2$-observability. Thus, decodability is an easy-to-check, unifying assumption under which quasipolynomial-time approximate planning for POMDPs is possible.

Information Theory.title: Instance-Optimal Estimation with Multiple LLM Judges on a Budget
Information Theory.summary: Evaluating large language models increasingly relies on LLM-as-a-judge protocols, but such evaluations remain costly: different judges have different prices and reliabilities, and the difficulty of each prompt-response pair can vary substantially. This raises a basic allocation question: under a fixed budget, how should one distribute evaluation queries across heterogeneous judges and instances to obtain the most accurate score estimates? We formalize this question as budgeted heteroskedastic multi-judge estimation under independent, unbiased score observations. Given $K$ prompt-response pairs and $J$ judges with known costs but unknown query-judge variances, our goal is to estimate the bounded score vector while minimizing an $\ell_p$-error. Our first contribution is to analyze the inverse-variance weighted estimator (IVWE) and to derive the oracle allocation that minimizes its leading error bound. Since this allocation depends on the unknown variances, we then address the unknown-variance setting by proposing EST-IVWE, an adaptive algorithm that constructs and uses optimistic variance estimates to stabilize the empirical allocation. We prove that EST-IVWE matches the oracle IVWE rate up to lower-order terms in the budget. Our second and central theoretical contribution is a local minimax lower bound matching the leading allocation-dependent rate, establishing asymptotic instance-optimality up to logarithmic factors. An Assouad-type construction based on local, variance-preserving perturbations yields this bound both in expectation and with constant probability. A complementary Fano-type change-of-measure argument captures the logarithmic dependence on the confidence level with a different (suboptimal) allocation geometry. Finally, we numerically validate our approach on synthetic data and resampled HelpSteer2 evaluations, demonstrating improvements over naïve uniform allocation.
Information Theory.comment: 55 pages, 4 figures; the first two authors contributed equally

Information Theory.title: The Gaussian Multiuser Channel Capacity Region
Information Theory.summary: This work characterizes a Gaussian multiuser-channel capacity-region using receiver-subset message atoms, Gaussian single-user equivalents, and successive decoding. A memoryless multiuser-channel model specifies both the channel conditional distribution and the independent-use input distribution. For all linear Gaussian channels, independent Gaussian user signaling and receiver-local worst-case-noise/MMSE-GDFE transformations provide a single-user-equivalent basis for the complete capacity-region construction. Each user distributes its input autocorrelation among a finite set of receiver-subset atoms, whose rate sums satisfy the applicable receiver constraints. Minimum-energy and weighted-rate-sum designs optimize these allocations, while fixed-allocation linear programs determine feasible atomic rates and synchronized time-shared successive-decoding implementations. The resulting framework includes Gaussian multiple-access, broadcast, and interference channels, with numerical examples illustrating their rate regions and receiver designs.
Information Theory.comment: 20 pages, 4 figures. Revised Gaussian specialization of the original preprint. Invited submission to IEEE Transactions on Communications

Information Theory.title: Capacity of Generic Symmetric Distributed Linear Computation: The Geometry of Relations
Information Theory.summary: In distributed linear computation, $K$ users observe linear functions of common finite-field data and send separate messages to a server that wants another linear function. We characterize the generic capacity $C$, the minimum total number of field symbols sent per computed instance, when all observations and the demand have dimension $ν$, the data have dimension $μ$, and the coefficients of these linear functions are drawn independently and uniformly from the field and stay fixed during coding, with the field size growing through arbitrary prime powers. For fixed $K$, $C/ν$ depends only on $τ=μ/ν$: the curve has finitely many linear pieces for at most three users, infinitely many pieces approaching one value of $τ$ for four users, and a rational part between two sequences of linear pieces for five or more users. The geometry of the relation space, formed by the linear relations among the observations and the demand, determines three things: the shape of the curve, which relations the coding scheme aligns, and the entropy inequalities used in the converse. Generically, the user subspaces of this space are either balanced, where the capacity lies on a single rational curve, or split into two balanced components, a sparse and a dense one, which produces the linear pieces. Achievability uses asymptotic set alignment, in which monomial precoders confine the combined observation differences to a small set. The converse uses the same geometry to lower-bound the sum of the users' remaining observation entropies in terms of the remaining data entropy.

Information Theory.title: From Formulation to Articulation: Considerations for AI-Assisted Research in Information Theory
Information Theory.summary: Recent advances in artificial intelligence have contributed to several information-theoretic results through genuinely different modes: a language model may suggest a proof, participate in an extended mathematical dialogue, coordinate computation, or operate as one component of a search harness. Treating all of these as "AI-discovered mathematics" obscures distinctions that matter for scientific reliability, attribution, and reproducibility. This article examines a set of recent cases through a four-stage pipeline: how the problem was formulated; how AI participated in finding a solution; how the resulting analytical and computational claims were verified; and how machine-generated outputs were translated into mathematical exposition for human understanding. Based on these cases, we recommend that research publications (1) disclose the nature and extent of AI assistance at each stage, (2) report verification of analytical reasoning separately from certification of numerical computations, and (3) place more emphasis on articulating the underlying ideas, techniques, and interpretations.

Information Theory.title: Orders between channels and implications for partial information decomposition
Information Theory.summary: The partial information decomposition (PID) framework is concerned with decomposing the information that a set of random variables has with respect to a target variable into three types of components: redundant, synergistic, and unique. Classical information theory alone does not provide a unique way to decompose information in this manner and additional assumptions have to be made. Recently, Kolchinsky proposed a new general axiomatic approach to obtain measures of redundant information, based on choosing a preorder relation between information sources (equivalently, a preorder between communication channels). In this paper, we exploit this approach to introduce three new measures of redundant information (and the resulting decompositions) based on well-known preorders between channels, thus contributing to the enrichment of the PID landscape. We relate the new decompositions to existing ones, study some of their properties, and provide examples illustrating their novelty. As a side result, we prove that any preorder that satisfies Kolchinsky's axioms yields a decomposition that meets the axioms originally introduced by Williams and Beer when they first propose the PID.

Information Theory.title: Symmetry Breaking over Multiway Channels
Information Theory.summary: Identical users running the same algorithm must often break their symmetry and agree on distinct roles, as in leader election, naming, and resource allocation. We study anonymous symmetry breaking over a discrete memoryless multiway channel invariant under permutations of its $J$ users: each user observes only a private output and must choose a number in $\{1,\dots,J\}$, and the symmetry is broken if the $J$ numbers are distinct. Using a Rényi change of measure, we derive a finite-blocklength converse on the error probability of every symmetric causal protocol, including adaptive and randomized ones. For achievability, block coding with random names reduces the problem to all-source multicast, for which we derive a Gallager random-coding exponent for every fixed $J$, and a cut-set bound that limits the exponent of the probability that two names coincide or are decoded wrongly. Interactive role controllers instead let the users contend for identifiers directly: we give their exact error probability, an achievable exponent given by a spectral radius when some outputs certify a role, and a floor for finite-state controllers when every output has positive probability, and we introduce generalized musical chairs. On a noisy bandit channel motivated by multiplayer multi-armed bandits, with noiseless collisions and arms of a common mean below one, interactive schemes provably exceed the limit of name decoding, and numerical estimates suggest the same with noisy collisions. For two users, noiseless collisions, one informative arm and a silent arm, the optimal error probability is determined up to a factor of two.

Information Theory.title: Finite Fields: Root Sets, Frobenius, and Algebraic Structure
Information Theory.summary: This monograph develops finite field theory through root sets, Frobenius orbits, trace duality, and cyclic modules, with applications to polynomial constructions and algebraic coding theory. Root-set descent and linearized polynomials connect field extensions, normal bases, invariant subspaces, and linear recurrences. Cyclotomic cosets link additive symmetries and local phase data with polynomial composition, factorization, and compatible lifting. Low-degree subfield representations and relative traces lead to root-block recovery, while return maps on root fibers organize constructions of irreducible polynomials. Coding applications include duality, distance bounds, Fourier support, and syndrome decoding. Character sums yield trace-norm distributions, the primitive normal basis theorem, and recurrences for extension-field sums and curve point counts. The final chapter constructs finite fields as residue fields of unramified p-adic extensions and relates Teichmuller representatives and Hensel lifting to cyclotomic orbits, periodic digit expansions, Witt carries, coefficient valuations, and Newton slopes. The emphasis throughout is on explicit proofs and reusable connections between field structure, orbit structure, and linear dependence.

Information Theory.title: A Two-Term Ziv-Zakai Bound for Multitarget DoA Estimation in MIMO Radar
Information Theory.summary: Multitarget direction of arrival (DoA) estimation is challenging when fluctuating targets are closely spaced: local Cramér--Rao bounds (CRBs) miss global errors, while direct vector Ziv--Zakai bound (ZZB) evaluation is computationally demanding. For colocated multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar with Swerling-II fluctuations and an ordered angular prior, we derive a rigorous two-term Bayesian mean squared error lower bound. A finite separation contribution addresses nonlocal discrimination, while a correction based on the prior averaged Fisher information matrix (FIM) retains target coupling and virtual array geometry. We show that the prior averaged pointwise CRB diverges under unrestricted target spacing when the FIM is nonsingular almost everywhere, although the proposed bound remains finite. Once the averaged FIM is obtained, evaluation avoids displacement optimization and multidimensional binary error integration. The bound supports analysis of snapshot diversity, target spacing, and transmit and receive allocation. Numerical comparison with the vector ZZB shows close agreement at low SNR but greater conservatism at high SNR, quantifying the tradeoff in tightness.

Information Theory.title: Universal Decoding for Gaussian MIMO-ISI: Spherical Ensembles and Symmetric Neighborhoods
Information Theory.summary: We construct a universal decoder for cyclic Gaussian multiple-input multiple-output channels with intersymbol interference and unknown channel taps and spatial noise covariance. Codewords are drawn independently and uniformly from a sphere of fixed total energy. Under stated bounds on frequency variation, the decoder attains the ensemble-average error exponent of informed maximum-likelihood decoding for fixed channels and channels with growing memory. We approximate the frequency response by a constant matrix within each frequency block. For this auxiliary channel, every matched log-likelihood is affine in a common sufficient statistic. At fixed received output, we compute the statistic density of an independent competitor. The decoder selects the candidate with the smallest statistic density, equivalently minimizing a weighted sum of residual log-determinants. The density and its support volume give an upper bound on the universal competitor probability. Affinity ensures that at least half of a suitable symmetric neighborhood of the transmitted statistic has matched likelihood no smaller than that of the transmitted word. Integrating a density lower bound over this half gives the matched competitor bound. These bounds establish equality of error exponents, which a Gaussian channel comparison transfers to the original channel. The same decoder attains the matched exponent for independent frequency blocks with prescribed energies satisfying the stated conditions. For energies proportional to block length, an additional gain condition ensures that this exponent is at least that of the total-energy spherical ensemble.

Information Theory.title: Anchored Iterative Decoding of Reed-Solomon Product Codes for High-Rate Magnetic Tape Storage
Information Theory.summary: We present a decoding algorithm for a Reed--Solomon product code targeted at the demanding reliability requirements of modern magnetic tape storage. For a code $RS(256, 224)\times RS(175, 173)$ in a BSC we achieve post-decoding bit error rate (BER) of $10^{-20}$ at $\approx 5.3\times 10^{-3}$ raw BER while maintaining the common requirement to detect and correct 4 out of 32 dead tracks. We resolve two common problems of miscorrections and stall patterns that arise under such a high raw BER via simplified versions of anchor decoding and binary image analysis. The highest efficiency is achieved by performing an unlimited iterative decoder, which performs decoding iterations until no changes are made. We give an empirical analysis of the average number of iterations: below the raw BER of $5\times 10^{-3}$, four half-iterations are performed on average while improving substantially over a decoder that always performs 4 half-iterations. We provide a CPU implementation achieving 100-200 megabytes/s single-core throughput on a regular laptop and a design of a potential hybrid FPGA-CPU implementation of our decoder.

Information Theory.title: Enhanced Informed Dynamic BP Decoding Scheduling Strategies for 5G NR LDPC Codes
Information Theory.summary: We present an enhanced informed dynamic scheduling (IDS) strategy to avoid propagations of unreliable messages in the residual belief-propagation (RBP) algorithm for decoding low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. To reduce the resource needed for updating the degree-one variable nodes (VNs) in an RBP-based algorithm for decoding 5G New Radio (NR) LDPC codes, we further introduce a process consisting of several simple procedures for managing the resource consumption. Simulation results demonstrate that our RBP algorithm based on the Proposed IDS strategy outperforms existing RBP-based algorithms at the early decoding iterations. By using our degree-one VN resource managing approach, the performance of both the proposed and the existing decoders is significantly improved in decoding the 5G NR codes.
Information Theory.comment: 7 pages, 5 figures, 2022 IEEE 96th Vehicular Technology Conference

Information Theory.title: On derandomizing the line-point low-degree test
Information Theory.summary:
We investigate the derandomized version of the classical line-point low-degree test in the high-error regime in the bivariate setting and reveal some unexpected behavior. The classical line-point low-degree test takes an $m$-variate function $f$ over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, queries it along a random line and accepts if the restriction of the function to this line is a low-degree polynomial.
  The high-error version of (the analysis of) this test asserts that if $f$ has at least $ε$ expected local agreement with a degree-$k$ univariate polynomial on a random line, then in fact $f$ is non-trivially close to some degree-$k$ $m$-variate polynomial even as $ε$ approaches $0$ (provided $q$ is sufficiently large compared to $k$ and $1/ε$). The derandomized version of the problem asks if the same holds when the line is not chosen uniformly over all possible lines but rather from a small set.In this paper we explore the bivariate case ($m=2$). We show, somewhat surprisingly, that there exists a function $f\colon \mathbb{F}_q^2 \to \mathbb{F}_q$ and a set of lines $\mathcal{L}$ in $\mathbb{F}_q^2$ of size nearly $q^{3/2}$ such that on every line in $\mathcal{L}$, $f$ has agreement $\approx 1/2$ on average with some univariate polynomial of degree $k=\sqrt{q}/2$ and yet $f$ is $1 - O(q^{-1/2})$ far from every polynomial of degree $O(k)$. On the positive side, we show that once the field size $q$ is at least $k^2/(ε)^{O(1)}$ such examples disappear and we can get sets of lines of size $O(q/ε^{O(1)})$ on which the low-degree test has a high-error analysis.
  On the way to our positive result, we show a new high-degree version of the classical two-direction Polishchuk--Spielman divisibility lemma.

Information Theory.title: AirFM-DDA: Air-Interface Foundation Model in the Delay-Doppler-Angle Domain for AI-Native 6G
Information Theory.summary: The success of large foundation models is catalyzing a new paradigm for AI-native 6G network design: wireless foundation models for physical-layer design. However, existing models often operate on channel state information (CSI) in the spatial-temporal-frequency (STF) domain, where multipath components are superimposed and structurally entangled. This hinders the learning of a universal channel representation. Their reliance on global attention also incurs prohibitive overhead. In this paper, we propose AirFM-DDA, an Air-interface Foundation Model in the Delay-Doppler-Angle (DDA) domain. AirFM-DDA reparameterizes CSI into the DDA domain to resolve multipath components along physically meaningful axes and employs window-based attention with frame-structure-aware positional encoding. Extensive experiments demonstrate transferability across scenarios, tasks, datasets, and antenna configurations. For channel prediction and estimation, AirFM-DDA generalizes zero-shot to unseen cities, achieving average normalized mean-square error (NMSE) gains of 4.9-8.5 dB over the strongest baselines. With only 10% labeled data, it achieves average gains of 12.0 percentage points in Top-1 accuracy for beam prediction and 3.4 percentage points in F1 score for line-of-sight (LoS) identification. It further transfers across simulated datasets and adapts to measured data and different antenna arrays. Compared with global attention, window-based attention reduces training and inference costs by nearly an order of magnitude.

Information Theory.title: Graphical Analysis of Lifted Product Code Constructions
Information Theory.summary: Lifted product codes are an important family of quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes, as they were the first QLDPC code family shown to be asymptotically good. Understanding the structure of their parity-check matrices $H_{\mathsf{X}}$ and $H_{\mathsf{Z}}$, as well as the associated Tanner graphs, is essential for analyzing their decoding behavior and error-floor performance. In this work, we show that the Tanner graphs of $H_{\mathsf{X}}$ and $H_{\mathsf{Z}}$ are indeed isomorphic, and investigate their graph-theoretical structure. We establish conditions ensuring the connectivity of these graphs and provide bounds on their minimal absorbing sets, providing new insight into the combinatorial structures influencing decoding performance.

Information Theory.title: Stabilizing Vector Approximate Message Passing with Circuit-Designed Lag-Lead Damping
Information Theory.summary: Vector approximate message passing (VAMP) often fails to converge on ill-conditioned matrices, and its damping factor is tuned either manually or adaptively. Using the fact that VAMP iterations are the discretization of an electric circuit, we show that the denoiser and the likelihood act as nonlinear resistors, the Onsager correction is a mirror resistor and damping is a lag filter. This circuit gives a closed-form loop gain whose spectrum can predict when VAMP fails. Because a lag filter cannot isolate the oscillating modes, we add a lead capacitor whose design often results in a negative capacitance. Across a wide range of condition numbers, our proposed damping strategy achieves a higher convergence rate than adaptive damping and Anderson acceleration at a lower mean iteration cost. On ill-conditioned multipath channels, across ranks and sparsity levels, it also converges more reliably than existing damping baselines.

Information Theory.title: The Schur products of some nonbinary narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes
Information Theory.summary: In recent years, the Schur products of linear codes have been extensively studied due to their favorable applications in cryptography. In this paper, we aim to study the parameters of the Schur products of some nonbinary narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes. Let $\mathcal{C}_1$ and $\mathcal{C}_2$ be two narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes with designed distances $δ_{1}$ and $δ_{2}$, respectively, where $2\le δ_{1},δ_{2}\le n$. Let $\mathcal{C}_1\star\mathcal{C}_2$ be the Schur product of $\mathcal{C}_1$ and $\mathcal{C}_2$. We present some necessary and sufficient conditions for $\mathcal{C}_1\star\mathcal{C}_2\ne\mathbb{F}_q^n$ by applying some constraints to $δ_{1}$ and $δ_{2}$. Furthermore, we determine the dimensions of these products and lower bounds on their minimum distance. Several linear codes with best known parameters are found.

Information Theory.title: A Novel Two-Parameter Penalty: Relaxation Degree Analysis and Sparse Signal Recovery
Information Theory.summary: In this article, we introduce a nonconvex two-parameter penalty function $P_{a,p}$, parameterized by $a\in(0,\infty)$ and $p\in(0,1]$, and the relaxation degree RD$_P$ for a separable nonconvex penalty function $P$. Based on $P_{a,p}$, we further propose the $P_{a,p}$ minimization framework for sparse signal recovery. This framework generalizes the TL1 minimization model established by S. Zhang and J. Xin (corresponding to the special case $p=1$) and provides a unified family of nonconvex penalty functions for sparse signal recovery. Using the sparse convex-combination technique, we establish both exact and stable sparse signal recovery under the restricted isometry property (RIP). To efficiently solve the resulting nonconvex optimization problem, we apply a modified iteratively re-weighted least squares method and the difference of convex functions algorithm (DCA) to develop the IRLSTLp algorithm for unconstrained $P_{a,p}$ minimization and prove some convergence results. Finally, numerical experiments compare recovery and runtime against single- and double-loop baselines, examine sensitivity to $(a,p)$, and assess the empirical correlation between RD$_{P_{a,p}}$ and recovery within the proposed family.

Information Theory.title: Sensing-Based Communication: A Non-Orthogonal Passive Reflection Framework for ISAC
Information Theory.summary: While integrating uplink without disrupting the primary downlink remains a critical challenge for existing reflective communication systems, this paper proposes a non-orthogonal passive integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) mechanism termed Sensing-based Communication. Originating from and validated within an optical retro-reflective system, this mechanism possesses an underlying wave-agnostic architecture with the potential to be generalized across other physical modalities. It leverages incident downlink signals for parasitic modulation via passive tags. By relying solely on fundamental on-off keying (OOK) reflection, the tag unifies the reflective sensing channel and the uplink communication channel, and simultaneously achieves both sensing and duplex communication. Consequently, our approach introduces uplink capability without sacrificing the downlink data rate or consuming additional spectrum resources. At the receiver, we design a joint decoding architecture combining cross-correlation computation and successive interference cancelation (SIC) to fully exploit the degrees of freedom in broadband signals for multi-user interference suppression. We derive closed-form expressions for the interference and bit error rate (BER) assuming zero-mean Gaussian signals. Using an experimental testbed, we validate the pivotal theoretical finding, the scaling relationship of SINR with signal bandwidth and cross-correlation time--where linear regression yields a strong goodness-of-fit with $R^2 = 0.9688$. Furthermore, evaluations under noise-like orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) waveforms exhibit high consistency between theoretical derivations and simulation data ($R^2 = 0.9372$, mean absolute percentage error, $\text{MAPE} = 14\%$), confirming the model's accuracy and waveform generalizability.

Information Theory.title: A Time-Frequency Framework for GKP Codes
Information Theory.summary: We develop a time--frequency framework for lattice GKP codes in which ideal codewords are realized in the modulation space $M^\infty$ and identified, through a vector-valued Zak transform, with a finite logical fibre over the continuous syndrome torus. Multi-window Gabor analysis then represents the logical vector by a finite block of adjoint-lattice coefficients. We prove that the normalized block map is an isometry, obtain an explicit recovering projection, and derive stable logical reconstruction. We further construct normalizable GKP approximants as lattice-envelope Gabor multipliers and establish weak-$*$ convergence and asymptotically isometric encoding. Finally, we recover displacement syndromes from phase relations between translated coefficient blocks and quantify their stability under additive perturbations.

Information Theory.title: Mobility Information Capacity of Multi-Robot Systems: Safety-Aware Maneuver Design
Information Theory.summary: Multiple robots operating in shared workspaces must adjust their speed, direction, and trajectories to coordinate with one another and respond to changing tasks and disturbances. The available maneuver freedom depends on the dynamics, uncertainty, and safety margins, even for a fixed fleet size and workspace. However, robot count, workspace occupancy, and task throughput do not quantify how much the fleet can vary its motion or how reliably these variations can be observed. We develop a mobility information capacity (MIC) framework that jointly characterizes these two aspects. Mobility information is defined as the mutual information between a joint maneuver sequence and its noisy trajectory observation, and MIC maximizes this quantity under maneuver-resource constraints. For a linear Gaussian maneuver-to-observation model with feedback dynamics, we characterize the finite-horizon information benchmark and derive its stationary long-horizon spectral limit, accounting for heterogeneous mobility gains, colored uncertainty, and temporally coupled maneuver costs. We further map workspace-boundary, inter-robot separation, and actuator chance constraints into coupled maneuver-covariance restrictions and derive conditions under which covariance optimization reduces to resource allocation across mobility modes. Finite joint maneuver codebooks are then constructed through individual risk screening and noise-whitened trajectory separation, with bounds linking sequence recovery error and achieved information to the capacity benchmarks. An aerial-robot simulation study evaluates spectral convergence, safety-aware allocation, finite-codebook identification, and fleet-size scaling. The resulting framework complements occupancy and task-throughput measures by quantifying the maximum observable maneuver freedom supported by a mobility system.

Information Theory.title: Testing CCZ-equivalence to permutations via projections of Walsh zero spaces, with applications to APN functions
Information Theory.summary: Whether almost perfect nonlinear (APN) permutations exist in even dimension $n\ge 8$ is a long-standing open question, the big APN problem. The only example known in even dimension, on six bits, was found from a quadratic APN function that is not itself a permutation, by Carlet--Charpin--Zinoviev (CCZ) equivalence. It is therefore natural to test APN functions for CCZ-equivalence to a permutation. This amounts to finding two complementary $n$-dimensional subspaces among the zeros of the Walsh transform, which lie in $\mathbb{F}_2^{2n}$. A known necessary condition only uses their projections to $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ and cannot decide every case. We give an exact test for functions whose Walsh supports are affine, including all quadratic functions. It reconstructs the subspaces from their projections, through searches for subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ and for constrained bilinear maps. On the benchmarked functions in dimension twelve, it lists them $39$ to $55$ times faster than the generic search of the commonly used sboxU library. We then study the functions $x^3+a^{-1}\mathrm{Tr}(a^3x^9)$, which Göloğlu and Pavlů proved not to be CCZ-equivalent to permutations when $4$ divides $n$. With their result, our computations show that this holds for every even $n\le 24$. In dimension $18$ the necessary condition is satisfied, and the new test decides the case. We conjecture this for every even dimension. We also compile $25$ classes of quadratic APN functions in dimension ten from published instances, with equivalence certificates. No function in these classes or in their switching closure is CCZ-equivalent to a permutation. All code and data are public.

Information Theory.title: On the Monotonicity of Information Measures
Information Theory.summary: We study the monotonicity of information measures, functions that assign a value to each statistical experiment, with respect to the Blackwell and Lehmann orders. We show that such monotonicity can be characterized by local, first-order conditions. Under natural invariance properties, a measure is Blackwell monotone if and only if it decreases in the direction of signal replacements, and Lehmann monotone if and only if it decreases in the direction of reverse signal replacements, which replace signals with higher ones only in low states or with lower ones only in high states. We translate both conditions into the space of posterior beliefs and apply them to likelihood-separable and posterior-separable measures, showing in particular that the entropy cost is Lehmann monotone. Among posterior-separable measures, we further identify a Lehmann monotone subclass, posterior-mean-ratio measures, that characterizes the Lehmann order.

Probability.title: Global Two-Sided Estimates for Time-Fractional Diffusion Kernels on Hyperbolic Space
Probability.summary: We study time-fractional diffusion on real hyperbolic space $\mathbb H^n$, $n\ge2$, with Caputo order $0<α<1$. We establish global two-sided pointwise estimates for the homogeneous fundamental kernel $Z_{\mathbb H}(t,r)$ and the inhomogeneous (Duhamel) kernel $Y_{\mathbb H}(t,r)$, uniformly over all $t>0$ and positive geodesic distances $r$. By combining inverse-stable subordination with global bounds for the hyperbolic heat kernel, we distinguish a short-time local regime, a large-time interior region, and an exterior region governed by a saddle-point problem with parameter $r/t$. Both kernels have the same exterior exponential rate, while their amplitudes are related by an explicit saddle-point factor. The estimates are uniformly comparable on the interfaces between regimes, recover the Euclidean time-fractional singularities at small scales, and identify the influence of hyperbolic geometry on large-scale decay. The kernel $Z_{\mathbb H}$ also describes the one-time marginal density of hyperbolic Brownian motion under an independent inverse stable clock. This representation yields a radial limit law, moment and quantile asymptotics, and a change in the mean square displacement from order $t^α$ at small times to order $t^{2α}$ at large times.

Probability.title: Rough Heston model as the scaling limit of bivariate cumulative heavy-tailed INAR processes: Weak-error bounds and option pricing
Probability.summary: We study nearly unstable bivariate cumulative heavy-tailed INAR($\infty$) processes and show that, under a one-factor parameterization and a suitable scaling, they converge to the rough Heston model. This yields a discrete-time microstructural route to the joint price-variance dynamics and gives explicit formulas linking the INAR asymmetry parameters to the leverage correlation and diffusion scale of the limiting volatility process. For pricing, we reduce the exact finite-$τ$ Fourier--Laplace transform recursion to a quadratic discrete Volterra equation and compare it with the rough Heston fractional Riccati equation. Under a transform-strip condition for the continuous model and bounded-Riccati regularity, every fixed bounded frequency window admits a uniform transform-error bound of order $τ^{-α}+τ^{-(1-α)}$. The finite-$τ$ transform is entire, and a uniform exponential-moment estimate then removes the Fourier cutoff and yields convergence of the exact, untruncated call prices. We also develop an FFT-accelerated CDQ simulator with $\mathcal O(τ\log^2τ)$ complexity per path and use it to price European and path-dependent options, benchmark the Markovian case $α=1$, and analyze the model-implied volatility surface.

Probability.title: Mixing times for the stochastic $p$-Laplace equation
Probability.summary: We review quantitative results on the convergence to equilibrium of the stochastic $p$-Laplace equation, $p>1$, on a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with additive, possibly degenerate Wiener noise. From these results we derive upper bounds on $\varepsilon$-mixing times in different distances, depending on the initial data. We show that the Wasserstein distance to equilibrium is non-increasing in time and that, for $p>\frac{2d}{d+2}$, the invariant measure has moments of all orders. For $1<p<2$ with $p>\frac{2d}{d+2}$ and possibly degenerate noise, the $\varepsilon$-mixing times in every Wasserstein distance $\mathcal{W}_r$, $r\ge1$, are $O(\varepsilon^{-δ})$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow 0$ for every $δ>0$. Two tables collect the convergence rates and the mixing-time bounds.

Probability.title: Spectral Rigidity of Stochastic Operators with Heavy Tailed Perturbations
Probability.summary: In this paper, we provide a new set of tools for establishing the number rigidity of point processes which are particularly well suited for the spectral processes of stochastic operators. These tools allow one to prove the number rigidity of a wide class of stochastic operators that had been previously inaccessible to the standard methods in the area, such as the variance of linear statistics, which require being able to precisely analyze correlations between individual points. We propose an alternative mechanism which uses a pathwise comparison between the growth rate of the unperturbed eigenvalues and the cumulative random noise which allows one to convert the probabilistic problem into a more tractable perturbation theory problem. This new approach allows us to prove the rigidity of previously inaccessible operators including those with heavy tailed perturbations or complex correlation structures. As a demonstration, we use these tools to prove the number rigidity of new classes of stochastic Schrödinger and Sturm-Liouville Operators which are resistant to analysis using the standard rigidity toolkit.

Probability.title: Kernel Metrics and Learning for Borel MDPs: Identifiability and Adaptive Control
Probability.summary: We consider a Markov decision process with standard Borel spaces and an unknown transition kernel under the average cost criterion. We do not impose any parametrization on the set of possible kernels. To facilitate our analysis, we first develop implication relations between several topologies on kernels defined by pointwise, continuous, or uniform weak convergence; we then review robustness properties on the space of kernels, and finally we establish compactness conditions on the space of kernels. Building on this regularity analysis, we then present two data-driven identifiability results; the first one being Bayesian and the second one empirical. Our conditions for the Bayesian setting are significantly more relaxed compared with prior work which considered either finite or parametric models, though we do not obtain a rate of convergence. Our analysis is asymptotic and builds on measurability in terms of the tail $σ$-field of the available information. Identifiability results are then used to design near-optimal adaptive control policies which alternate between periods of exploration, where the controller acts according to a policy which is conducive to the identification of the true kernel, and periods of exploitation where the controller's information on the kernel is utilized. We will establish that such policies are near optimal. In summary, our contribution is with regard to the general standard Borel setup where there is no apriori parametric representation.

Probability.title: The Localization Scale of the Block Anderson Model in One Dimension at Arbitrary Coupling and Volume
Probability.summary: We study the one-dimensional block Anderson model with independent $W\times W$ Gaussian unitary ensemble potentials and deterministic nearest-neighbor hopping, with hopping-to-disorder ratio $g$. The system consists of $L$ blocks, with total dimension $N=WL$. As $W\to\infty$, we identify the bulk localization length, up to an arbitrarily small power of $W$, with $\min\{N,\max\{W,W^2g^2\}\}$, uniformly for deterministic couplings $g\ge0$ and cycle lengths $L\ge3$. For every fixed $D>0$ and all sufficiently large $W$, the expected fraction of eigenvectors in the selected energy interval satisfying these bounds is at least $1-W^{-D}$. In polynomial volume the bounds hold simultaneously for all eigenvectors in that interval with probability at least $1-W^{-D}$. The localization length is the number of coordinates in the shortest cyclic interval containing at least half of an eigenvector's mass.
Probability.comment: 189 pages, 4 figures. Lean formalization repository: https://github.com/JYin80/Lean-LSBA1d

Probability.title: Malliavin structure for conditionally independent random variables
Probability.summary:
We consider a countable family of random variables which are conditionally
  independent given a latent random variable $Z$. Given $Z$, the random variables are independent. Hence the Malliavin
  calculus for independent random variables applies for each value of $Z$. We show that these constructions fit
  together. We obtain the chaos decomposition, the domains of the Malliavin
  operators, the Mehler formula and the carré du champ operator, with
  conditional expectations given $Z$ in place of ordinary expectations. For normal
  approximation, conditioning on $Z$ and the infinite de Jong theorem of
  Döbler give mixed normal approximations of degenerate U-statistics, in
  Wasserstein and Kolmogorov distances. Working under the unconditional
  probability, we obtain a de Jong type bound for U-statistics whose kernels
  are products. In both cases, the fluctuations of the conditional variance
  appear as an additional term, which cannot be removed. As an application, we
  consider subhypergraph counts in a random $3$-uniform hypergraph built on a
  latent random graph. For the count centred at its conditional mean, we
  obtain an explicit rate in Wasserstein distance. It reduces to the known
  rate for the Erdős--Rényi hypergraph when the latent graph is
  complete. The count centred at its mean is a pattern count in a non-uniform
  hypergraph with independent edges, which gives a necessary and sufficient
  condition for its asymptotic normality.
Probability.comment: New version: the Malliavin structure follows Döbler (arXiv:2609.15725); errors of v1 corrected; complete proof of the rate for the conditionally centred count

Probability.title: Limit laws for the friendship paradox in random geometric graphs
Probability.summary: The friendship paradox says that, on average, the neighbours of a vertex have more neighbours than the vertex itself. We study the size of this effect, the average over all vertices of the mean degree of the neighbours minus the degree of the vertex, in the random geometric graph on the torus with the maximum-norm distance. We determine its limit law in every regime of the connection radius and quantify the approximation by non-asymptotic error bounds in the Kolmogorov distance or the total variation distance. We also give its exact mean for every $n$ and every radius below one half. For a fixed radius the limit is not Gaussian but a weighted sum of centred exponential variables; when the radius shrinks and the expected degree grows, the statistic is asymptotically Gaussian, with a Berry--Esseen bound; for bounded expected degree it is Gaussian at the classical rate; and when the expected degree tends to zero it is asymptotically Gaussian, Poisson or identically zero, depending on how fast the radius shrinks. When the expected degree is large, the proofs rest on the vanishing of the first Hoeffding projection, which makes a degenerate $U$-statistic of pairs of points the source of the fluctuations; it is analysed by Fourier series for a fixed radius and by Stein's method of exchangeable pairs for a shrinking radius. For bounded expected degree we use normal approximation for local functionals, and for vanishing expected degree the Chen--Stein method.

Probability.title: Percolation on grandparent graphs of Bienaymé trees
Probability.summary: We consider Bernoulli bond percolation on the grandparent graph of a Bienaymé tree, obtained by adding to the tree an edge between every vertex and its grandparent. We show that the critical parameter $p_c$ is the unique solution of an explicit equation involving the generating function of the offspring distribution, and we study how $p_c$ depends on this distribution beyond its mean $m$. When $m\geq 1.569$, the offspring distribution concentrated on the (one or two) integers closest to $m$ is the unique maximiser of $p_c$ among all offspring distributions with mean $m$, and its critical parameter is $\frac1{m^2}-\frac1{m^3}+O\left(\frac1{m^4}\right)$ as $m\to\infty$; more generally, for two distributions that are comparable in the convex order, $p_c$ is larger for the smaller of the two distributions under the condition that its support bounded some explicit $N(m)$ of order $m^4$. These restrictions cannot be removed: the convex order alone does not determine the order of the critical parameters, even among distributions with support bounded by $O(m^4)$, and the extremal property fails for $m$ close to $1$. Finally, for every $m>1$, the critical parameter $p_c$ can be arbitrarily close to $0$ for general offspring distributions with mean $m$. If we only consider offspring distributions that do not charge $0$, so that the obtained tree is almost surely infinite, this remains true if and only if $m\geq 2$.

Probability.title: Harper's beyond square-root conjecture for random matrices
Probability.summary: For a Haar unitary matrix $U_N$ of size $N$, we prove that the first absolute moment of $\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{Sym}^k U_N)$ tends to zero as $\min(N,k)\to\infty$. This settles the random matrix version of Harper's beyond square-root conjecture formulated by Wang and Xu, with no restriction on $k/N$. The proof is elementary and self-contained, combining exact weighted trace moments with a Gaussian change of measure. It also connects the result to the critical chaos model studied by Soundararajan and Zaman, also known as holomorphic multiplicative chaos.

Probability.title: Strong Convergence for Zig-Zag Products and Typical Spectra of Irregular Graphs
Probability.summary:
We investigate the following: do existence bounds obtained by interlacing methods describe the spectra of typical random graphs? Depending on the model, we provide both positive and negative answers.
  We establish a Friedman-type theorem for zig-zag products of random regular graphs $G$ with a fixed vertex-transitive gadget $H$, where $G$ is sampled from independent permutations or matchings. We prove that the new spectrum converges in Hausdorff distance to that of the zig-zag product of the infinite regular tree with $H$. In particular, the new spectral radius converges to the sharp threshold established by Cohen, Cohen, and Maor. We establish the spectral limit using strong convergence and, drawing on quantitative estimates of Chen, Garza-Vargas, Tropp, and van Handel, obtain an $O(1/n)$ upper-tail bound in the permutation model.
  For the irregular configuration model, we show that the interlacing bound of Cohen and Maor, asymptotically $2\sqrt{μ-1}/μ$ for limiting average degree $μ$, is atypical: for uniformly bounded degree sequences with a nonconstant limiting degree law of minimum $δ\ge 2$, a random graph exceeds the interlacing bound by a positive constant with high probability. This gap is explained by the limiting spectral distribution, whose support edge is $2\sqrt{δ-1}/δ$. Strikingly, unlike the familiar behavior of random regular graphs, our experiments reveal second eigenvalues that remain far below this limiting edge even for the largest graphs tested. For $δ\ge3$, we propose that the scarcity of minimum-degree trees explains this behavior; estimates for their size suggest spectral witnesses within $O\left((\log\log n)^{-2}\right)$ of the limiting edge, which is consistent with our numerical observations.

Probability.title: Extreme-value asymptotics for smallest enclosing balls of spherically symmetric samples
Probability.summary: Let $R_n$ denote the radius of the smallest ball containing an i.i.d.\ sample of spherically symmetric random vectors in $\mathbb R^d$, and let $D_n$ be the sample diameter. While the asymptotic behaviour of $D_n$ is well understood, much less is known about $R_n$. Starting from a classical result of Daniels for planar Gaussian samples, we develop a point-process approach to the asymptotic behaviour of $R_n$ in the three classical extreme-value regimes. We obtain limit theorems in the Gumbel, Fr'echet and Weibull cases, with the limiting laws described by geometric functionals of Poisson point processes. In dimension two, the Gumbel limit can be identified explicitly and is universal within the corresponding max-domain of attraction. We also study the asymptotic relationship between $R_n$ and $D_n$ and the supporting configurations of the smallest enclosing ball.

Probability.title: Circular flows and bisections of random regular graphs
Probability.summary: For every fixed odd $d\ge5$, we prove that the circular flow number of a uniformly random simple $d$-regular graph is asymptotically almost surely less than $2+4/(d-1)-\varepsilon_d$ for an explicit constant $\varepsilon_d>0$. At degree five the upper bound is $3-1/24006$. At degree seven it is $21/8$, answering a question of Li and Li. For every fixed $p\ge1$, we also obtain a strongly connected Jaeger orientation at degree $4p+1$, with outdegrees in $\{p,3p+1\}$. At large degrees we count dense bisections together with sets that violate their cut inequalities. This gives flow intervals of length $O(d^{-2})$ above the maximum-bisection lower bound of Li and Li. The finite-degree estimates, together with the large-degree transfer, also prove the conjecture of Greenhill, Isaev and Lewis that the threshold for orientations with outdegrees in $\{p,d-p\}$ exceeds the corresponding bisection threshold by at most one.
Probability.comment: 55 pages, Conjecture 7.1 in version 1 (positive gaps for circular flow number of random 5- and 7-regular graphs)is now proved, and Conjecture 7.1 is replaced with a new conjecture

Probability.title: Fourier Positivity and Sharp Poincaré Inequalities on Graphs
Probability.summary:
We prove sharp dimension-free $L^1$-Poincaré inequalities on Hamming cubes, a sharp quadratic $L^1$-Poincaré inequality on product Poisson spaces, and a sharp pseudo-Poincaré inequality on finite abelian Cayley graphs. These inequalities use a generalization of the Beckmann boundary introduced by Ivanisvili, Xie, and Zhang. In particular, we prove that the optimal dimension-free constant in the classical $L^1$-Poincaré inequality on the Hamming cube is $\sqrt{π/2}$, answering a question of Ivanisvili et al.
  Semigroup duality and explicit Malliavin weights reduce these estimates to integrals of first absolute moments of centered Bernoulli and Poisson sums. The key ingredient is a Fourier positivity principle, which shows that replacing the coefficients by their absolute values can only increase these integrals. For the underlying Bernoulli functional at subquadratic exponents, we also characterize the maximizers and determine their exact phase transitions.

Probability.title: Free energy Wasserstein gradient flow and their particle counterparts: toy model, (degenerate) PL inequalities and exit times
Probability.summary:
In finite dimension, the long-time and metastable behavior of a gradient flow perturbated by a small Brownian noise is well understood. A similar situation arises when a Wasserstein gradient flow over a space of probability measure is approximated by a system of mean-field interacting particles, but classical results do not apply in these infinite-dimensional settings. We are concerned with the situation where the objective function of the optimization problem contains an entropic penalization, so that the particle system is a Langevin diffusion process.
