  The work has two parts: the first and main one is devoted to the general study of a very simple class of models, for which the infinite-dimensional behavior is fully characterized by an autonomous diffusion process at fixed finite dimension. On the one hand, we prove the equivalence between fast convergence for the mean-field gradient flow and for the particle system in terms of functional inequalities (log-Sobolev, Polyak-Łojasiewicz, Talagrand and variants thereof) including the degenerate polynomial case occurring at phase transitions, and on the other hand we characterise the metastable behavior in terms of transition time between local minimiser -- establishing an Eyring-Kramers formula -- and of exit time from unstable critical points.
  In a second part, motivated by and building on the systematic study of the toy models, we consider the continuous Curie-Weiss model in a symmetric double-well potential, exactly at the critical temperature. We show that, although the $N$-particle Gibbs measure does not satisfy a uniform-in-$N$ standard log-Sobolev inequality (the optimal constant growing like $\sqrt{N}$), it does satisfy a more general Łojasiewicz inequality uniformly in $N$, inducing uniform polynomial long-time convergence rates, propagation of chaos at stationarity and uniformly in time, and creation of chaos.

Probability.title: Equi-dependence implying independence
Probability.summary: It is shown that, if an event $A$ has the same conditional probability in each trial in an infinite sequence of Bernoulli trials, then $A$ is independent of each trial. More general results are actually established.
Probability.comment: Version 1: 5 pages. To appear in The American Mathematical Monthly. Version 2: Added a counterexample due to Qiyuan Gu. Version 3: Minor style improvements in the appendix. Version 4: Added a counterexample due to ChatGPT. Minor improvements in presentation

Probability.title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part 4: variance under a general distribution
Probability.summary: We study the variance of the reference-centered discrete total variation $d_{\mathbf p}=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}|X_{j+1}-X_j-N(p_{j+1}-p_j)|$ of $X\sim\mathrm{Mult}(N;\mathbf p)$ for fixed $n\ge3$ and fixed $\mathbf p$ with all $p_i>0$, as $N\to\infty$. We prove $\mathrm{Var}(d_{\mathbf p})=N\,v(\mathbf p)+O(1)$, where $v(\mathbf p)$, the variance of the sum of absolute values of the limiting Gaussian edge vector, is expressed through the exact multinomial edge variances and correlations and Nabeya's covariance formula for folded bivariate normal variables. Unlike in the uniform case, non-adjacent edge pairs generally contribute to $v(\mathbf p)$. The $O(1)$ remainder is controlled by a lattice Edgeworth expansion and Poisson summation; it oscillates with the lattice phases $\{N(p_{j+1}-p_j)\}$, and for $n=3,4$, where a pair of edges exhausts the bins, the summation runs over a sublattice coset. The formula reduces to the known uniform result (the classical Hoel--Kamat variance), gives a closed form when the reference law is a symmetric comb, and has a shape-independent large-bin limit for positive $C^1$ profiles. For the statistic $d_{\mathbf r}$ centered at a reference law $\mathbf r\ne\mathbf p$ the absolute values linearize: when every edge is mismatched the variance is that of a linear form in the counts up to an exponentially small error, and in mixed (triangular-array) regimes it is given to $o(N)$ by bivariate folded-normal covariances. The two-bin formulas are recorded from the companion preprints, and exact finite-$N$ reductions for $n\le4$ are used for validation.

Probability.title: Singular Vortex in the Large Deviation of Empirical Current for Symmetric Simple Exclusion Process
Probability.summary: We prove a large deviation estimate for singular current observables of the two-dimensional symmetric simple exclusion process. In particular, the observable has a non-standard large deviation scaling $N^2(\log N)^{-1}$ due to the presence of singular vortices, whereby trajectories rotating near the origin point yield an enhanced contribution to the current observable. The proof combines the heuristics of Bodineau-Derrida-Lebowitz 2008, the averaging method of Jara-Menezes 2018, and novel cancellation and multi-scale renormalization arguments developed by this paper.

Probability.title: The probability that a branching random walk does not hit a point
Probability.summary: We study the probability that a branching random walk in ${\bf Z}^d$ driven by a Galton-Watson tree conditioned to have $n$ vertices does not hit a fixed point. For $d\in\{1,2,3\}$ this probability behaves like $n^{-α/4}$ in logarithmic scale, where $α=4$ when $d=1$, $α=2\sqrt{2}$ when $d=2$, and $α=(\sqrt{17}-1)/2$ when $d=3$.

Probability.title: The small ball problem for the Brownian sheet: sharp bounds via entropy numbers in $L_\infty$
Probability.summary: We settle the uniform small deviation conjecture for the Brownian sheet in every dimension $d\ge2$, namely, that the logarithmic exponent is $2d-1$. Our proof proceeds through sharp entropy and Kolmogorov estimates for the associated anchored mixed Sobolev embedding in the uniform norm. Their connection to small deviations is known from the Kuelbs--Li theorem. To establish the entropy estimates, the key is a probabilistic small ball inequality for smooth tensor product atoms whose exceptional set has Gaussian measure exponentially small in the number of atoms. Its proof combines a count of dyadic rectangles with tools from probability, in particular Ehrhard's Gaussian Brunn--Minkowski inequality. This also yields sharp entropy and Kolmogorov number estimates for embeddings of periodic mixed Sobolev, Besov and Nikol'skii classes with smoothness $r>1/2$ in $L_\infty$. Finally, we extend our results to fractional and integrated Brownian sheets.

Probability.title: Backward--forward interacting systems with probability-valued strategies and common noise
Probability.summary: We study a system of interacting agents in which a backward stochastic equation is coupled to the forward evolution of a probability-valued strategy distribution. The agents interact through their empirical state--strategy law and are exposed to a common Brownian noise. Under Lipschitz, mass-conservation, and positivity assumptions, we establish well-posedness of the finite-agent system on a sufficiently short time interval. We then identify its large-population limit as a conditional mean-field backward--forward system and prove conditional propagation of chaos. When agent characteristics take finitely many values, we obtain order $N^{-1}$ bounds for the expected squared particle--copy error and the expected squared Wasserstein distance of order one between the empirical law and the conditional limiting law. An adaptive-strategy model with replicator dynamics illustrates the theory, accompanied by a numerical comparison of the two errors.

Probability.title: Sharp universality thresholds for random profinite groups
Probability.summary: We determine sharp universality thresholds for quotients of the free profinite group $\widehat F_n$ on $n$ generators by $n+u$ independent random relations, where $u$ is a fixed nonnegative integer. For products of mutually independent uniformly coset-balanced factors, convergence to the Liu--Wood measure $μ_u$ holds when the minimum number of factors grows faster than $\log n$, which is a uniformly sharp condition. For random words of fixed length $\ell_n$, convergence holds exactly when $\ell_n$ is eventually odd and $\ell_n-\log n\to\infty$. We also prove universality for randomly ordered products of independent integer powers under the balance condition $nα_{n,p}/\log n\to\infty$ at each fixed prime, recovering finite-prime cokernel laws by abelianization.

Probability.title: Non-asymptotic First- and Second-Order Tail Brackets for the Kostlan-Shub-Smale Field and Spherical k-Spin Complexity
Probability.summary: For the Kostlan-Shub-Smale field $X$ of degree $k\ge3$ on the sphere $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, we prove the two-sided bound $(1-\varepsilon(u))\,δ_{*}(u)\le\mathbb{P}\{\sup X>u\}\leδ_{*}(u)$ at every finite $(k,d)$, where $δ_{*}(u)$ is the expected number of critical points above $u$, halved when $k$ is even, and $\varepsilon(u)$ is explicit for $ρu\ge\min\{d-1,\frac32\sqrt{2(d-1)}\}$. The gap is therefore at most of order $e^{-(1+ρ^{2})u^{2}/2}$ with $ρ^{2}=k/(2(k-1))$. We also give $δ_{*}$ itself in closed form, as a finite sum of Hermite polynomials, together with a two-term envelope that is asymptotically sharp and a single-monomial relaxation of the form $Cu^{d-2}e^{-u^{2}/2}$. As an application we bracket the annealed complexity of the spherical $k$-spin Hamiltonian at every finite $(k,d)$: the upper bound holds at every energy, a lower bound of the same form at every energy above $9/4$ times the spectral edge $\sqrt{2(d-1)}/ρ$, above twice the edge when $d\ge10$, and is consistent with the Auffinger-Ben Arous-Černý complexity function as $d\to\infty$.

Probability.title: Fluctuations of heat kernels and exit times on random graphs and application to the critical long-range percolation
Probability.summary: Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a graph equipped with random conductance. We give sufficient conditions for the Markov chain on $\mathcal{G}$ to exhibit large scale fluctuations in its on-diagonal heat kernel and in exit times. The conditions also imply non-tightness of the height process w.r.t. the quenched measure, while it is tight w.r.t. the annealed measure. As an application of the general theory, we prove large scale fluctuations for the simple random walk on $1$-dimensional critical long-range percolation.

Probability.title: Commutation relations for two-sided radial SLE
Probability.summary: We study the commutation relation for 2-radial SLE in the unit disc starting from two distinct boundary points. We follow the framework introduced by Dubédat~[12]. Under an additional requirement of the interchangeability of the two curves, we classify all locally commuting 2-radial SLE$_κ$ for $κ\in (0,8)$: it is either two-sided radial SLE$_κ$ with spiral of constant spiraling rate or chordal SLE$_κ$ weighted by a power of the conformal radius of its complement. Namely, for fixed $κ$ and starting points, we have exactly two one-parameter families of locally commuting 2-radial SLE curves. We also discuss the semiclassical limit of the commutation relation as $κ\to 0$. In particular, we show that the limit for the second family with an appropriately chosen power of the conformal radius is a chord that minimizes a modified chordal Loewner energy, which is unique only when the endpoints are not antipodal.
Probability.comment: 50 pages, 7 figures. Final version. To appear at Science China Mathematics

Probability.title: Truncated Signature Information for Mixed Fractional Brownian Paths
Probability.summary: We study finite expected-signature information for mixed-fBm paths with Hurst indices above $1/4$. Up to level three, the only parameter-dependent expected features are the variance transform $q_θ$ and the time-ordered transform $R_θ$. We prove the scale tradeoff $2K$ level-two scales versus $K$ selected level-two/three scales, together with separation and local inverse bounds.
Probability.comment: There are some mistakes and the theory is not useful in practice

Probability.title: Feynman-Kac Representation and the Asymptotic Speed of the Fisher-KPP Equation with Finite-Activity Jump Noise
Probability.summary:
We study the asymptotic propagation speed of travelling wave solutions to the stochastic Fisher--KPP equation with multiplicative finite-activity pure jump Lévy noise, i.e.\ a compensated Poisson random measure of finite intensity, so that the solution evolves deterministically between successive jumps and jumps multiplicatively at the event times.
  Our main contribution is a stochastic Feynman--Kac representation for the solution, which expresses the random field as the product of the exponential martingale of the jump noise and an expectation over the paths of an independent Brownian motion. The representation converts the nonlinear stochastic partial differential equation into an expectation problem, allowing a direct analysis of the front position.
  Building on this representation, we derive sharp upper and lower bounds for the propagation of the front: for every speed $c>2\sqrt{1+a}$ the solution decays exponentially along the ray $x=ct$, while for every speed $c<2\sqrt{1+a}$ it does not. The two together identify the asymptotic speed in the critical-speed sense: the threshold between exponentially decaying and non-decaying fronts equals $2\sqrt{1+a}$ almost surely, an identity proved without any a priori existence of the limit $R_δ(t)/t$. The complementary bounds $2\sqrt{\underlineγ}\le c\le2\sqrt{\overlineγ}$ also hold, with $\overlineγ,\underlineγ$ explicit in $ε$ and $μ$.
  Under the finite-activity assumption, a stopping-time iteration yields pathwise $L^\infty$ bounds and finite-speed propagation of the level sets of the front, which underlie the existence of a travelling wave profile. The framework extends naturally to multi-species cooperative systems, and numerical simulations illustrate the informativeness of the speed bounds.

Probability.title: Mesoscopic eigenvalue statistics for random regular graphs: a case study
Probability.summary: We study mesoscopic fluctuations of linear eigenvalue statistics for random $d$-regular graphs on $N$ vertices with fixed $d\ge 3$. Revisiting the approach developed by Dumitriu-Johnson-Pal-Paquette (2013) and Johnson (2015), we establish a mesoscopic central limit theorem in the bulk and identify its universal limiting variance. Our result applies to test functions with smooth compactly supported Fourier transforms and to a specific range of spectral scales $(\log N)^{-1}\llη\ll 1$. In particular, this case study allows the mesoscopic scale to tend to zero arbitrarily slowly.

Probability.title: Joint modelling of financial cost and carbon footprint in motor insurance claims: a BINAR(1) decision framework for circular auto parts adoption
Probability.summary: Motor insurance claims management increasingly faces a dual objective: controlling claim costs while reducing greenhouse-gas emissions associated with vehicle repair decisions. This paper proposes a bivariate, discrete-time modelling framework that links the dynamics of financial claims and repair-related carbon footprint inspired by a BINAR(1) dependence structure, allowing for temporal persistence, cross-dependence and a positive/negative correlation between the two dimensions. Using externally sourced emission factors and cost information for replacement parts, we operationalise the carbon footprint of claims under two repair pathways: new parts versus circular-economy reused parts (PIEC). We then conduct scenario analyses in which the acceptance rate of reused parts varies, and we quantify the joint implications for expected monetary outlays and CO 2 -equivalent emissions. Results show that higher PIEC acceptance can simultaneously reduce expected emissions and average claim cost, and the magnitude of the joint benefit depends on the dependence structure and persistence captured by the BINAR(1) process. The proposed framework provides a transparent, reproducible tool for insurers to evaluate repair-policy levers and to align claims operations with decarbonisation targets while retaining an explicit stochastic risk perspective.

Probability.title: Phase transition for conditional covariance matrices estimated by importance sampling, and implications for cross-entropy schemes in high dimension
Probability.summary: Motivated by recent high-dimensional reliability algorithms, we study a random matrix model corresponding to the estimation by importance sampling of $Σ_A$, the covariance matrix of a Gaussian vector conditioned by a rare event $A$. For such models, we show that, in contrast to most random matrix models, the minimal sample size to ensure an accurate estimation of $Σ_A$ needs to grow superlinearly in the dimension. More precisely, if $n$ is the sample size and $d$ the dimension, we show that the estimation of $Σ_A$ is accurate if $n/d \gg L$ and not accurate if $n/d \ll L$ where $L$ is the maximum likelihood ratio. Moreover, we relate the asymptotic behavior of $L$ to $λ_1$, the smallest eigenvalue of the auxiliary covariance matrix, which suggests that $L$ (and thus the minimal sample size) will be larger for small values of $λ_1$. Numerical experiments confirm that this insight carries over to recent cross-entropy algorithms, with the best performing algorithms being also the ones with the largest smallest eigenvalue. Although backed up by our theoretical result, this result is surprising as these algorithms were not designed to act on the spectrum.

Probability.title: A Dirichlet form approach to the potential theory of $m$-subharmonic functions
Probability.summary:
On a bounded open subset of $\mathbb{C}^n$, we study the Dirichlet form induced by an admissible pair $(θ,μ)$, where $μ$ is a positive Radon measure and $$θ=dd^c u_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dd^c u_{m-1}\wedge(dd^c \lvert z\rvert^2)^{n-m}$$ for locally bounded $m$-subharmonic functions $u_1,\dots,u_{m-1}$. We prove that locally bounded $m$-subharmonic functions belong locally to the domains of these Dirichlet forms and are quasi-continuous with respect to the induced capacities. We establish a monotonicity property for Dirichlet forms, which motivates the introduction of $μ$-quasi-monotone convergence of $m$-subharmonic functions. The natural embeddings into these domains are continuous with respect to this convergence. These results yield new proofs of the commutativity and continuity of complex Hessian operators.
  Using this framework, we characterize quasi-continuity with respect to the induced capacity for an arbitrary $m$-subharmonic function in terms of its pole set having zero measure $μ$, or equivalently, zero induced capacity. On bounded strictly $m$-pseudoconvex domains, we prove that the Bedford--Taylor capacity for $m$-subharmonic functions and the capacities induced by the corresponding Dirichlet forms have the same null sets. We further characterize $m$-polar sets in terms of Dirichlet forms and stochastic processes, extending the corresponding characterization of pluripolar sets due to Fukushima and Okada to the $m$-subharmonic setting.

Probability.title: Erratum to: Monotonicity of Ursell functions in the Ising model
Probability.summary: In this note, we correct an error in the proof Theorem 1 of Comm. Math. Phys. 401 (2023), 2459-2482.

Probability.title: Regularity of the Value Function in Discounted Infinite-Time Mean Field Games
Probability.summary: In [18], we introduced discounted infinite-time mean field games. Subsequently, in [19], we studied the connection between infinite-time mean field FBSDEs and elliptic master equations. In this paper, we further investigate the regularity of the representative player's value function $V(x,μ)$. We first establish strong well-posedness and uniqueness in law for an extended class of infinite-time FBSDEs. In the weighted $L_r^2$ framework, we construct directional variations and obtain a bounded continuous representation of the Lions-derivative of $\partial_xV$. Under additional smoothness and quantitative stability assumptions, $L_r^p$ estimates for scalar linear FBSDEs allow us to establish the existence of higher-order derivatives of $\partial_xV$. Consequently, $\partial_xV$ is a classical solution of the elliptic master equation for the value function's derivative.

Probability.title: Group Invariance of Statistical Models and Associated Statistical Manifolds
Probability.summary: We study the group invariance of a parameterized statistical model that is closed under push-forward sample transformations given by a group action. We prove that the group action on the sample space induces an isometric action on the associated statistical manifold. Furthermore, it preserves the Fisher-Rao metric as well as the Amari-Chentsov tensor. Moreover, we establish that this isometric action is compatible with equivariant and sufficient statistics in the spirit of the Hall-Wijsman-Ghosh generalized Stein's theorem. This compatibility leads to a novel reduction of the original group-invariant model, where its Fisher information loss is explicitly quantified via conditional expectation. As an application, we apply this framework to a generalized cardioid distribution in circular data analysis, illustrating how the reduced model facilitates estimation and hypothesis testing for relative parameters.

Probability.title: Measuring and Decomposing Mode Separation via the Canonical Diffusion
Probability.summary: Mode separation, namely how sharply a distribution fragments into barrier-separated clusters, is a fundamental geometric property of densities, difficult to quantify in high dimensions. Modes are often the meaningful alternatives in the data, such as the conformations of a molecule or the distinct semantic types among a generative model's outputs. Mode separation is distinct from dispersion, which is what standard label-free tools capture: differential entropy rises with spread regardless of fragmentation, and PCA orders directions by variance regardless of barriers. Mutual information does capture it, but only given the latent component labels, which are usually unavailable. We measure mode separation through a single stochastic process intrinsic to the density, namely the unique reversible diffusion with $f$ as its stationary distribution and a constant scalar diffusion coefficient. From its autocovariance matrix we extract two readouts. The first, SSA (Sum of Squared Autocorrelations), is a scalar barrier-sensitive measure. The second, DA (Dominant Autocorrelation directions), gives linear projections ordered by metastability rather than variance. Under an isotropic-Gaussian null, we derive the limiting spectrum of the empirical autocovariance in closed form, generalizing the Marchenko--Pastur law. Its upper edge gives a noise floor that separates metastable directions from sampling noise. Both readouts use only samples and a score function, scaling to high dimensions through pretrained score-based generative models via Tweedie's identity. We apply our framework to three settings: (i) synthetic Gaussian mixtures, where SSA tracks mutual information; (ii) SDXL text-to-image generations, where SSA and DA capture structure that entropy and PCA miss; and (iii) molecular dynamics of alanine dipeptide, where DA recovers the known slow backbone dihedrals from static samples alone.

Probability.title: Stochastic optimal transport for the Langevin dynamics and its zero-mass limit
Probability.summary: We introduce a stochastic optimal transport for the Langevin dynamics with positive mass and study its zero--mass limit. The new aspect of this paper is that we only fix the initial and terminal probability distributions of the positions of particles under consideration, but not those of their velocities, with Heisenberg's uncertainty principle in mind. In the zero--mass limit, we show that the minimizers of our stochastic optimal transport is tight if and only if the initial momentum (=(mass)$\times$(velocity)) of a particle converges to zero. We also prove that the limit of minimizers of our stochastic optimal transport is a minimizer of a standard stochastic optimal transport for continuous semimartingales.
Probability.comment: 51 pages, to appear in Ann. Appl. Probably

Probability.title: On the Incompleteness of do-calculus for Universal Identifiability
Probability.summary: We study the problem of causal effect identification from an arbitrary set of observational and/or interventional distributions, which we call Universal Identifiability (uID). The uID problem generalizes existing classical identifiability (ID) and general identifiability (gID) problems, which considered the identification problem from either mere observational distributions or a specific type of interventional distributions. Prior research has established graphical criteria to determine when a causal effect is identifiable in ID and gID problems. Moreover, algorithms that leverage do-calculus and basic probability manipulations have been proposed to compute these effects. Consequently, it has been shown that do-calculus is both sound and complete in these problems. Despite these well-established results, a formal definition of what it means for the do-calculus to be complete does not exist. We propose a rigorous formalization for the completeness of the do-calculus and show that the completeness results in previous work remain valid. However, for more general problems, such as uID, the rules of do-calculus are no longer complete. This is perhaps the reason why the uID problem has remained open thus far.

Probability.title: Empirical approximation of $L_p$ norms for $p\in (2, \infty)$
Probability.summary: For $p>2$ and an $N$-dimensional subspace $X\subset L_\infty(μ)$ satisfying \[ \|f\|_\infty\le (KN)^{1/p}\|f\|_{L_p(μ)} \quad\forall f\in X, \] we show that $m\ge C(p)KN \bigl(\varepsilon^{-p} +\varepsilon^{-2}\log_2(2N)\bigr)$ independent samples $ξ^1,\ldots,ξ^m$ with distribution $μ$ satisfy \[ (1-\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p(μ)}^p \le\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m|f(ξ^j)|^p \le(1+\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p(μ)}^p \quad\forall f\in X \] with probability at least $1-\exp(-c(p)\frac{m\varepsilon^2}{KN})$. This gives the optimal sample-size order $N\log_2 N$ for independent random sampling with fixed $K$, $p$, and $\varepsilon$. This result follows from a more general empirical moment estimate over unit balls of $p$-convex norms.

Probability.title: Line crossing problem for biased monotonic random walks in the plane
Probability.summary: A $β$-biased monotonic random walk in the plane moves from $(x,y)$ to $(x+1,y)$ or $(x,y+1)$ with probabilities $1/(β+1)$ and $β/(β+1)$. We study $Φ_β(α,d)$, the probability that the walk started at the origin ever visits a lattice point strictly above the line $y=αx+d$, and $Ψ_β(α,d)$, the probability that it visits a lattice point \emph{on} the line after leaving the origin. For integer slopes $α=p$ we show $Φ_β(p,d)=ρ^{\lfloor d\rfloor+1}$, where $ρ$ is the smallest positive root of $y^{p+1}-(β+1)y+β=0$, give the Fuss--Catalan series for $ρ$, identify $ρ$ with the extinction probability of a Galton--Watson process, and compute the exact law and mean of the first crossing point. We prove that the return probability is $Ψ_β(p,0)=(p+1)(1-β/((β+1)ρ))$, which equals $(p+1)/(β+1)$ for $β\ge p$. For rational slopes $α=r/s$ we obtain $Φ_β$ in closed form from the $s$ large roots of the kernel $\tfracβ{β+1}z^{r+s}-z^r+\tfrac1{β+1}$, and $Ψ_β$ as a ratio of Green's functions. For arbitrary real $α$ we prove that the walk crosses every line $y=αx+d$ almost surely if and only if $β\geα$, and we establish the two-sided bound $e^{-θ(d+1)}\leΦ_β(α,d)<e^{-θd}$ with an explicit Lundberg exponent $θ$. Finally, $α\mapstoΦ_β(α,0)$ is a pure jump function: it is constant on $[0,β]$, continuous at every irrational point and has a jump at every rational $α>β$.

Differential Geometry.title: Radial reductions of variable exponent Laplacian equations on warped products with compact symmetry
Differential Geometry.summary:
We study nonlinear elliptic equations of variable exponent type, \[ -Δ_{q(x)}u+|u|^{q(x)-2}u=f(x,u), \] on non-compact Riemannian manifolds with symmetry. We consider complete warped products \[ M=\mathcal R\times_φY,\qquad g_φ=dr^2\oplusφ(r)^2g_Y, \] where $\mathcal R$ is a non-compact interval, possibly with boundary, and $Y$ is a compact homogeneous manifold. We establish sufficient conditions on the warping function ensuring a Ricci lower bound, a uniform non-collapsing volume condition, and the orbit-growth hypothesis of the abstract existence theorem proved in \cite{JFA}. We also obtain comparison bounds for the admissible warping functions.
  We analyze the corresponding radial equations for the admissible exponential and linear models $φ(r)=e^{ar}$ and $φ(r)=ar$, with $r\geq r_0>0$. For a constant diffusion exponent $q=k$, we consider explicit decaying profiles $u=φ^{-σ}$, which belong to $L_1^k(M)$ provided $σk>\dim Y$ in the exponential case and $σk>\dim Y+1$ in the linear case. Under additional explicit parameter restrictions, these profiles solve a resonant equation with a positive bounded coefficient, a construction distinct from the superlinear regime of the abstract existence theorem. Finally, we establish logarithmic reductions for constant and variable radial exponents, and justify the passage from radial identities to weak formulations against arbitrary compactly supported interior test functions.

Differential Geometry.title: Neutral Ricci spectra of homogeneous Riemannian four-manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: It is shown that every quadruple of real numbers with two positive and two negative entries is the Ricci spectrum of some left-invariant Riemannian metric on a Lie group of dimension four. Consequently, for eight out of the fifteen possible Ricci signatures of four-dimensional homogeneous Riemannian manifolds, one can determine precisely which spectra in each given signature actually occur. We also describe the Ricci spectra realized by left-invariant metrics on a certain class of 2-step solvable Lie groups of all dimensions $n>2$.

Differential Geometry.title: A generalization of the Gauss Lemma
Differential Geometry.summary: We give a generalization of the Gauss Lemma for normal exponential maps and a covering criterion as a consequence.

Differential Geometry.title: Finite-Scale Folding and Maximal Asymptotic Variance
Differential Geometry.summary: Based on the recent breakthroughs by OpenAI and consequently by Binder-Ivrii-Prause-Smirnov, we develop a finite-scale folding method for the nonlinearity of a schlicht function, based on a signed critical-point count for superharmonic potentials and a quantitative target cutoff. Furthermore, we use a cylindrical root transform to reduce the logarithmic cost of access to the point at infinity. Combined with a Littlewood-Paley formula as well as dilation, the method yields the maximal asymptotic variance bound $Σ_{\max}^2\le1$ for the unrestricted schlicht class of normalized univalent functions.

Differential Geometry.title: Deformation of Associative Submanifolds joining Minimal Surfaces in Hyperbolic Geometry
Differential Geometry.summary: Donaldson and Thomas proposed a Floer-type theory on a Calabi-Yau threefold $M$, generated by the complex curves, and whose boundary operator is given by counting appropriate associative submanifolds in $M\times \mathbb{R}$. We consider a similar setting, in which the Calabi-Yau manifold is replaced by the twistor space $Z$ of an oriented hyperbolic 4-manifold $X$ and the $J$-holomorphic curves in $Z$ project to minimal surfaces in $X$. We give a formula for the virtual dimension of (a subset of) the moduli space of associatives asymptotic to a pair of $J$-holomorphic curves in $Z$, proving it equals the difference of the Morse indices of the corresponding minimal surfaces in $X$.

Differential Geometry.title: The first gap for minimal submanifolds in spheres
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $f:M^n\to\Sn^{n+q}(1)$ be a minimal immersion of a closed connected manifold with $n\ge3$ and $q\ge2$, and let $S$ be the squared length of its second fundamental form. We prove an integral inequality that gives $\max_M S\ge n$ if the immersion is not totally geodesic. If $n\ne4$ or $q=2$, equality $\max_M S=n$ holds if and only if the immersion is a Clifford minimal hypersurface; if $n=4$ and $q\ge3$, equality holds if and only if the immersion is a Clifford minimal hypersurface or the standard minimal embedding of $\mathbb{CP}^2$ in $\Sn^7(1)$. Both classifications are understood up to an ambient isometry, a totally geodesic inclusion, and a finite covering. We construct the integral inequalities using polynomial weights and divergence identities. The required algebraic estimates are proved by sums of squared tensor norms.
Differential Geometry.comment: There are some proof details that need to be carefully checked

Differential Geometry.title: Total Mean Curvature Gaps for Scalar-Flat Hypersurfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that a complete connected scalar-flat Euclidean hypersurface of dimension $n\geq3$ is an affine hyperplane if its normalized mean curvature has sufficiently small $L^n$ norm. We also compute the total mean curvature energy of a classical rotational scalar-flat family to show that finiteness cannot replace smallness in dimensions $n\geq3$.

Differential Geometry.title: No Connectedness Lemma for Alexandrov spaces
Differential Geometry.summary: Since its introduction in 2003, Wilking's Connectedness Lemma has become a powerful tool in the study of manifolds with positive sectional curvature. In recent work of the authors, this has been extended to orbifolds. The purpose of this note is to exhibit counterexamples in the class of Alexandrov spaces for the Connectedness Lemma in both its ordinary and dual formulation. This answers a 2007 question of Wilking.

Differential Geometry.title: Topological Rigidity of Contractible 3-Manifolds and Handlebody Interiors under Nonnegative Scalar Curvature
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that a contractible $3$-manifold admitting a complete Riemannian metric of nonnegative scalar curvature is diffeomorphic to $\R^3$. We also prove that, if the interior of a compact handlebody of genus $γ$ admits such a metric, then $γ\leq1$. This answers two open questions posed by Wang and Gromov, respectively.

Differential Geometry.title: Natural potentials for TT tensors, divergence-free symmetric tensors and linearised relativistic initial data
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $N$ be a natural tensor which vanishes at a metric $g\_0$. By diffeomorphism invariance, $DN(g\_0)^*$ takes values in divergence-free symmetric $2$-tensors, and in TT tensors if moreover $DN(g\_0)$ kills conformal directions. Such operators are local potentials, which we call machines: they produce smooth compactly supported tensors with the required property and, on closed manifolds, all of them up to a finite-dimensional space when their symbol is injective. On Einstein manifolds of every dimension, the linearised Bach tensor gives the operator $P$ of an earlier paper, which factorises on TT tensors into the massless and partially massless spin-$2$ operators; we also construct machines on Bach-flat, conformally flat and Ricci-parallel metrics. Replacing the diffeomorphisms of $M$ by those of the vacuum development, we obtain potentials, with a Fredholm property, for the linearised Einstein constraint equations on arbitrary spacelike hypersurfaces of Minkowski, de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetimes.

Differential Geometry.title: Higher Holonomy for Higher Lie Algebroid Connections on Graded Vector Bundles
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove the existence of a Riemann--Hilbert $A_\infty$-functor from the curved dg-category of $\mathscr{A}$-connections on graded vector bundles, where $\mathscr{A}$ is a higher Lie algebroid, to the curved dg-category of $Π_\infty(\mathscr{A})$-connections on graded vector bundles, where $Π_\infty(\mathscr{A})$ is the homotopy groupoid of $\mathscr{A}$. When restricted to the sub dg-categories of flat objects, it induces an $A_\infty$-functor from the dg-category of representations up to homotopy of $\mathscr{A}$ to the dg-category of representations up to homotopy of $Π_\infty(\mathscr{A})$, which recovers the one from arXiv:1011.4693 and arXiv:0908.2843 when $\mathscr{A}$ is a Lie algebroid. The key ingredient for defining such functors is a non-abelian Stokes's theorem for endomorphism-valued differential forms. Furthermore, for a graded vector bundle $E$, we introduce the notion of its higher general linear groupoid in such a way that $G$-connections on $E$, for a higher Lie groupoid $G$, become smooth functors from $G$ to the higher general linear groupoid of $E$. We combine this with the Riemann--Hilbert functor to define higher parallel transport functors for $\mathscr{A}$-connections. Finally, we use these functors to define the higher holonomy groups of $\mathscr{A}$-connections and endow them with the structure of augmented simplicial Lie groups.

Differential Geometry.title: A splitting theorem for Einstein manifolds with symmetries
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that every negative-Einstein manifold with cocompact symmetries splits isometrically as a Riemannian product $H \times K$ with $H$ homogeneous and $K$ compact. This confirms a conjecture due to Böhm and Lafuente. As a consequence, we obtain a new proof of the 1975 Alekseevskii conjecture.

Differential Geometry.title: Schwarzian Residue of the Samuelson Obstruction in Tangent Lagrangian 2-Webs
Differential Geometry.summary:
The Samuelson condition, a classical area-ratio condition for planar Lagrangian $2$-webs, is equivalent in local web coordinates $(u,v)$ to $\partial_u\partial_v\log|J_F(u,v)|=0$, where $F$ is the inverse web-coordinate map and $J_F$ is its Jacobian. For the tangent-line family $L_t: y=tx+h(t)$, with $h$ smooth on an open interval, let $Ψ(u,v)$, for $u
eq v$, be the intersection map of $L_u$ and $L_v$, write $J_Ψ$ for its Jacobian, and set $S_h(u,v) := \partial_u\partial_v\log|J_Ψ(u,v)|$ where $J_Ψ(u,v)
eq0$. Near each diagonal point $(t_0,t_0)$ with $h''(t_0)
eq0$, the obstruction admits the decomposition $S_h(u,v) =  rac{1}{(v-u)^2} + R_h(u,v)$, where $R_h$ extends smoothly across the diagonal near $(t_0,t_0)$. The universal pole yields $S_h(u,v)>0$ off the diagonal in a sufficiently small neighborhood of $(t_0,t_0)$, so the tangent web does not satisfy the Samuelson condition there. We call $R_h(t,t)$ the Schwarzian residue and show that $R_h(t,t) =  rac{1}{2}\{σ,t\} = -κ_{\mathrm{aff}}(σ) \left( rac{dσ}{dt}ight)^2$. Here $σ$ is the equi-affine arclength parameter of the envelope $γ(t)=(-h'(t),h(t)-t h'(t))$, and $\{σ,t\}$ denotes the Schwarzian derivative of $σ$ with respect to $t$. The equi-affine curvature $κ_{\mathrm{aff}}$ is defined by $γ_{σσσ}+κ_{\mathrm{aff}}γ_σ=0$. We also derive the transformation law of the residue under reparametrization of the tangent-line family.
Differential Geometry.comment: Revised text and discussion of previous work

Differential Geometry.title: Transformation theorem and monotonicity of the numbers of almost Euclidean factors of geodesic balls
Differential Geometry.summary:
In \cite{HH}, H. Huang-X.Huang introduced the generalized Reifenberg condition which describes the non-increasing property of numbers of almost Euclidean factors of geodesic balls and gave a transformation theorem under this condition. In this note, we study how almost Euclidean factors of concentric geodesic balls interact with harmonic splitting maps under a lower Ricci curvature bound and prove a dimension gap for harmonic functions of almost linear growth and then derive a transformation theorem under a non-decreasing property compared with the non-increasing property above.
  We also construct complete manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature whose balls are uniformly almost $1$-Euclidean at every scale, but for which no single harmonic function can be transformed into a splitting function at all smaller scales which give a negative answer to the existence question for all-scale splitting functions in \cite{HH}.
Differential Geometry.comment: Drop the results about fundamental groups for giving no new examples than Huang's results {Finite generation of fundamental groups for manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature whose universal cover is almost k-polar at infinite}. Fix some errors in the old version

Differential Geometry.title: A Poincare-Einstein Liouville Theorem and the Yamabe Invariant of Lens Spaces
Differential Geometry.summary:
Schoen conjectured that the Yamabe invariant of every lens space is achieved by the round metric. A proof of this conjecture is presented for all lens spaces, together with rigidity: equality is only achieved for the round class. The key step is to show that every $\mathbb Z_p$-invariant Yamabe-positive conformal class on $S^3$ admits a $\mathbb Z_p$-equivariant Poincaré-Einstein filling. The distance function from a fixed point of the filling then gives an invariant test function with Yamabe quotient at most $σ(S^3)$, which descends to the lens space.
  The proof of the main theorem was generated by AI (ChatGPT Astra, September 2026); this is mainly a learning note of the AI generated proof.

Differential Geometry.title: Projective Rigidity of $U(k)$-Radial Ricci-Flat Kähler Metrics
Differential Geometry.summary: We study Kähler immersions of Ricci-flat metrics into finite- or infinite-dimensional complex projective space. Let $L^{\otimes k}\simeq K_X$ over a real-analytic Kähler manifold $X$. Let $φ$ be a base potential and $s$ the canonical squared fibre norm on $L^{\oplus k}$. Consider Ricci-flat potentials $φ+h(s)$ near the zero section, with $h$ independent of the base point. We prove that local projective inducibility forces the base to be Ricci-flat and the metric to split locally as $X\times\mathbb C^k$. In that case projective inducibility is equivalent to that of the base. The proof combines Calabi's criterion, positivity of the homogeneous fibre-degree blocks, and the singularities of the radial profile. A related obstruction along holomorphic curves excludes every positive multiple of the Taub--NUT metric and Calabi's hyperkähler metrics on $T^{*1,0}\mathbb{CP}^n$. Applications also include the resolved conifold, canonical-bundle metrics in non-Einstein classes, and Cifarelli's rank-two Type-2 metric.
Differential Geometry.comment: v2: expanded into a paper on projective rigidity of Ricci-flat Kahler metrics, with a new title; the v1 theorem is now Theorem 5.1, proved along a holomorphic curve. 17 pages, no figures

Differential Geometry.title: An improved isodiametric inequality for convex surfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: Alexandrov conjectured that every closed convex surface of area $A$ and intrinsic diameter $D$ satisfies $A/D^2\leqπ/2$. Using an averaging argument over the curvature measure, we prove that every closed convex surface satisfies $A/D^2\leq2π/3$, improving the best previously known bound.

Differential Geometry.title: Differentiation of tepui groupoids and the holonomy groupoid of singular foliations
Differential Geometry.summary: Tepui groupoids are a generalization of Lie groupoids which allow the arrow space to be singular, as is the case for holonomy groupoids of singular foliations. We construct a Lie differentiation functor for a large class of tepui groupoids. When restricted to effective and source-connected tepui groupoids, this differentiation recovers the correspondence between holonomy groupoids and their underlying singular foliations.

Differential Geometry.title: Left-Invariant Kernels of the Hodge-de Rham Operator on Three-Dimensional Lorentzian Lie Groups
Differential Geometry.summary: We determine the kernel of the Hodge--de Rham operator on left-invariant differential forms for the seven customary families of three-dimensional Lorentzian metric Lie algebras. Every parameter stratum is treated, including zero structure constants, singular bracket matrices, and null modular directions. If $θ(X)=\mathrm{tr}\,\mathrm{ad}_X$ is the modular character, the full kernel is the direct sum of constants, the space $K=\mathrm{Ann}([\mathfrak{g},\mathfrak{g}])\capθ^\perp$, its Hodge dual, and the volume forms. We give explicit real bases in all seven families and compute the exterior differential and geometric codifferential on every basis form. The non-unimodular calculation remains valid without the customary extra normalization conditions, and hence also covers metric representatives omitted by those conditions. The resulting dimensions are $2,4,6$, or $8$; the two middle-degree dimensions agree. Explicit examples distinguish the kernel of the first-order operator from the kernel of its square. All assertions concern smooth left-invariant forms, with no square-integrability condition.

Differential Geometry.title: The Whitney Extension Problem in Carnot groups
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a Carnot group, let $E \subset \mathbb{G}$ be compact, and suppose we are given a function $f: E \to \mathbb{R}$. The $C^1_H$ {\em Whitney Extension Problem} asks the following: what must be true about $f$ to guarantee that there exists a smooth, horizontal function $F \in C^1_H(\mathbb{G})$ extending $f$, i.e., there is some $F:\mathbb{G} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $F|_E = f|_E$ and $XF$ is continuous for every horizontal left invariant vector field $X$? We adapt the method of G. Glaeser and C. Fefferman to answer this question in this non-commutative setting. Moreover, we provide an alternative solution to the $C^1$ Whitney Extension Problem for horizontal curves in the Heisenberg group.

Differential Geometry.title: Foliated and compactly supported isotopies of tubular neighborhoods
Differential Geometry.summary:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a foliation with a "singular" submanifold $Σ$ on a smooth manifold $A$ and $p:E \to Σ$ be a tubular neighborhood of $Σ$ in $A$. Under certain "scalability" assumptions on $\mathcal{F}$ near $Σ$, we prove that every leaf preserving diffeomorphism $h$ of $A$ is isotopic via a leaf preserving isotopy to a diffeomorphism which coincides with some vector bundle morphism of $E$ near $Σ$. This result is simultaneously a foliated, compactly supported and parametrized variant of a well known statement that every diffeomorphism $h$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ fixing the origin is isotopic to the linear isomorphism induced by its Jacobi matrix at $0$. Particular cases of such a "linearization theorem" allowed recently to compute homotopy types of leaf preserving diffeomorphism groups of polar Morse-Bott foliations on lens spaces and the twisted bundle $S^2\tilde{\times}S^1$.
  In general, that "linearization theorem" can be used to reduce the study of the homotopy type of the group of leaf preserving diffeomorphisms of $\mathcal{F}$ to an investigation of the following three groups (being independent in a certain sense): (a) diffeomorphism group of $Σ$, (b) the group of leaf preserving vector bundle isomorphisms of $E$, and (c) the group of leaf preserving diffeomorphisms of $A$ supported in $A\setminus Σ$, i.e. out of the "singularity" $Σ$.

Differential Geometry.title: On the index of two-dimensional elliptic end-periodic operators
Differential Geometry.summary: This paper investigates the index problem for elliptic end-periodic differential operators on a two-dimensional manifold with a cylindrical end. We define the topological index as the sum of the contribution of the interior symbol, expressed by an Atiyah--Singer type integral, and the contribution of the limit operator, expressed in terms of the Melrose type eta-invariant and a correction term that depends on the lower order terms of the limit operator. We prove the homotopy invariance of the topological index, which allows us to reduce the original problem to the study of operators of a simpler form by employing $K$-theoretic methods.

Differential Geometry.title: On deformations of foliated complex analytic structures IV-1: Obstructed and unobstructed foliated deformations
Differential Geometry.summary: We study obstructions of deformations of foliated complex analytic structures. We describe obstructions in terms of Cech resolutions. From foliated complex analytic families in Part I and unfolded complex analytic families in Part III, we deduce the integrability conditions. We identify infinitesimal deformations and obstructions in terms of Dolbeault resolutions or Dolbeault type bicomplexes from the integrability conditions. Then we describe the correspondences of infinitesimal deformations and obstructions between Cech resolutions, and Dolbeault resolutions or Dolbeault type bicomplexes.

Geometric Topology.title: Pure mapping class group fixed points in $\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$
Geometric Topology.summary:
We classify all the fixed points for the action of the pure mapping class group on $\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$ character varieties of surface groups. Up to trivial peripheral monodromies, we prove that the irreducible fixed points are either pair of pants representations, or restrictions of reduced Burau representations to a once-punctured torus and restrictions of reduced Gassner representations to a 4-punctured sphere. On the other hand, we prove that the only non-trivial reducible fixed points appear in genus 0 where they map all but at most three peripheral loops in the centralizer of the image, and in genus 1 where they are valued in the quaternion group $H_8$.
  As consequences, we deduce (i) that an irreducible representation in genus 0 with at least four non-trivial peripheral monodromies is rigid if and only if it is a fixed point, and (ii) a partial classification of irreducible representations of pure braid groups into $\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$.

Geometric Topology.title: A homotopical consequence of branched covers
Geometric Topology.summary: We prove that the profinite completion of a pseudomanifold is the Artin-Mazur's etale homotopy type construction on its branched covers, which was implicitly conjectured by Sullivan in his MIT note (page 272) around 1970. This is a consequence of the existence of enough $K(π,1)$ open dense subspaces in a pseudomanifold.

Geometric Topology.title: On the functoriality of the space of equivariant smooth $h$-cobordisms
Geometric Topology.summary: We construct an $(\infty,1)$-functor that takes each smooth $G$-manifold with corners $M$ to the space of equivariant smooth $h$-cobordisms ${\mathcal H}_{\mathrm{Diff}}(M)$. We also give a stable analogue ${\mathcal H}^{\mathcal U}_{\mathrm{Diff}}(M)$ where the manifolds are stabilized with respect to representation discs. The functor structure is subtle to construct, and relies on several new ideas. In the non-equivariant case $G=e$, our $(\infty,1)$-functor agrees with previous constructions of the smooth $h$-cobordism space as a functor to the homotopy category.
Geometric Topology.comment: 95 pages. Final version, to appear in Transactions of the AMS

Geometric Topology.title: The splitting of the stable space of equivariant $h$-cobordisms
Geometric Topology.summary: We prove that the space of equivariant $h$-cobordisms on a smooth $G$-manifold $M$ has a tom Dieck style splitting, after stabilization. As an intermediate step, we introduce a space of isovariant $h$-cobordisms on $M$ and prove that this space also has a splitting, even before stabilizing. This completes the proof of the equivariant version of Waldhausen's stable parametrized $h$-cobordism theorem. Along the way, we establish several foundational results on equivariant smooth manifolds with corners.

Geometric Topology.title: Contact Surgery Numbers of the 3-torus
Geometric Topology.summary: We study contact surgery numbers for contact structures on the 3-torus. We show that all contact structures obtained via contact surgery along a Legendrian Borromean ring are overtwisted, and that this construction yields infinitely many pairwise non-contactomorphic contact structures on $\mathbb{T}^3$. We prove an obstruction on the maximal Thurston-Bennequin invariant of 3-component links to produce $\mathbb{T}^3$ by Dehn surgery. We also compare Legendrian surgery presentations of the Stein-fillable contact structure on $\mathbb{T}^3$. In this setting, we exhibit a non-destabilizable Legendrian knot with no graded normal ruling whose associated Stein filling has nonzero full symplectic homology.
Geometric Topology.comment: 22 Pages, 3 figures, 1 Table. Comments are welcome

Geometric Topology.title: HOMFLY homology for oriented tangles
Geometric Topology.summary: We introduce an extension of Khovanov and Rozansky's categorification of the HOMFLY polynomial to arbitrary oriented tangles. Unlike previous such extensions, ours is invariant under the full suite of oriented Reidemeister moves, including the "misoriented" Reidemeister IIb. For oriented links $\mathcal{L}$, our construction recovers Khovanov and Rozansky's construction while removing the preliminary step of presenting $\mathcal{L}$ as a braid closure.
Geometric Topology.comment: 52 pages, many figures. Comments and suggestions welcome!

Geometric Topology.title: Cable Knot Counterexamples to the All-Knot Volume Conjecture
Geometric Topology.summary: Let $E$ be the figure-eight knot and let $V$ be the hyperbolic volume of its exterior. We study the reduced colored Jones polynomial at $q=e^{2πi/N}$ for the $(p,w)$-cable of the connected sum of $d\ge 2$ copies of $E$, where $w\ge 2$ and $p,w$ are coprime. The normalized logarithmic growth rate converges to the JSJ volume $dV$ along colors coprime to $2w$, and its upper limit along colors sharing a divisor with $w$ is at most $V$. Thus the $(1,2)$-cable of $E\#E$ violates the full-sequence volume limit for knots. The $(1,3)$-cable of the same companion shows that convergence can fail even along all odd colors. The separation comes from the multiples of $N$ in the exact cabling sum and a uniform first-derivative estimate for the other companion colors.

Geometric Topology.title: Zariski dense hyperbolic 3-manifold groups in $\mathrm{SL}(4,\mathbb{Z})$
Geometric Topology.summary: We show that $\mathrm{SL}(4,\mathbb{Z})$ contains an infinite family of Zariski-dense subgroups isomorphic to the fundamental group of a fixed closed hyperbolic $3$-manifold, which are pairwise noncommensurable up to conjugacy.

Geometric Topology.title: Holed cone structures on 3-manifolds
Geometric Topology.summary: We introduce holed cone structures on 3-manifolds to generalize cone structures. In the same way as a cone structure, a holed cone structure induces the holonomy representation. We consider the deformation space consisting of the holed cone structures on a 3-manifold whose holonomy representations are irreducible. This deformation space for positive cone angles is a covering space on a reasonable subspace of the character variety.
Geometric Topology.comment: 27 pages, 4 figures, to appear in Osaka J. Math

Geometric Topology.title: Relationship between quandle shadow cocycle invariants and Vassiliev invariants
Geometric Topology.summary: As one of the problems in his list [20], T. Ohtsuki proposed to study relations between quandle cocycle invariants and quantum invariants. The aim of this paper is to answer one of those questions. We prove that the coefficient of the finite perturbative expansion of the quandle shadow cocycle invariant defined by $(\Z /p\Z)$-Laurent polynomial quandle is Vassiliev invariant for any braids.

Geometric Topology.title: Liftable braid factorizations from line arrangements: Hironaka's relations and a Zariski pair
Geometric Topology.summary: We realize Hironaka's generalized lantern relations by lifting positive braid factorizations. For a nonpencil real line arrangement with no parallel lines, we construct a family of branched coverings on the regular fibers of a blown-up pencil of spheres. The motion of the branch points gives a factorization of a power of the full twist into least liftable powers of half-twists. The Artal-Carmona-Cogolludo-Marco Zariski pair gives two such factorizations of the same braid for a single simple branched covering of the disk. Their lifts are Hurwitz inequivalent even up to simultaneous conjugation by page homeomorphisms. The corresponding Milnor fibers fill the same planar contact three-manifold and have the same incidence matrix. They are homeomorphic and lie in distinct strong symplectic deformation classes.

Geometric Topology.title: Semifree actions and representation varieties
Geometric Topology.summary: A group action on a topological space induces an action on the space's representation variety. We determine the fixed point sets of this latter action for semifree group actions on surfaces and circle bundles over surfaces. We also discuss implications for mapping tori of periodic maps.

Geometric Topology.title: Embedding Calculus, Goodwillie Calculus and Link Invariants
Geometric Topology.summary: We study Goodwillie-Weiss embedding calculus through its relationship with Goodwillie's functor calculus. Specifically, building on a result of Tillmann and Weiss, we construct a functorial complement for \(T_{n}\)-embeddings that takes values in Heuts's categorical \(n\)-excisive approximation of pointed spaces. We also establish an analogue of Stallings' theorem for lower central series in the context of \(T_{n}\)-embeddings of \(P \times I\) into \(D^{d}\) for any compact manifold \(P\). As an application, we show that the embedding tower of string links detects Milnor invariants.
Geometric Topology.comment: Withdrawn due to errors in the proof of Theorem B. Weaker versions of the results are available in the author's thesis.

Geometric Topology.title: Foliated and compactly supported isotopies of tubular neighborhoods
Geometric Topology.summary:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a foliation with a "singular" submanifold $Σ$ on a smooth manifold $A$ and $p:E \to Σ$ be a tubular neighborhood of $Σ$ in $A$. Under certain "scalability" assumptions on $\mathcal{F}$ near $Σ$, we prove that every leaf preserving diffeomorphism $h$ of $A$ is isotopic via a leaf preserving isotopy to a diffeomorphism which coincides with some vector bundle morphism of $E$ near $Σ$. This result is simultaneously a foliated, compactly supported and parametrized variant of a well known statement that every diffeomorphism $h$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ fixing the origin is isotopic to the linear isomorphism induced by its Jacobi matrix at $0$. Particular cases of such a "linearization theorem" allowed recently to compute homotopy types of leaf preserving diffeomorphism groups of polar Morse-Bott foliations on lens spaces and the twisted bundle $S^2\tilde{\times}S^1$.
  In general, that "linearization theorem" can be used to reduce the study of the homotopy type of the group of leaf preserving diffeomorphisms of $\mathcal{F}$ to an investigation of the following three groups (being independent in a certain sense): (a) diffeomorphism group of $Σ$, (b) the group of leaf preserving vector bundle isomorphisms of $E$, and (c) the group of leaf preserving diffeomorphisms of $A$ supported in $A\setminus Σ$, i.e. out of the "singularity" $Σ$.

Geometric Topology.title: Simply connected quotients of fake quadrics
Geometric Topology.summary: Fake quadrics are minimal complex surfaces of general type with $b_1=0$ and $e=4$. The paper gives a short introduction to their arithmetic construction, aimed at low-dimensional topologists, and studies their holomorphic and antiholomorphic quotients and their fundamental groups. The running example in the paper comes from a quaternion algebra over a totally real cubic field. The lattice is generated by three explicit pairs of matrices. A holomorphic involution gives (after resolving the singularities) a simply connected minimal complex surface of general type with $p_g=0$ and $K^2=4$, a smooth $4$-manifold homeomorphic but non-diffeomorphic to $CP^2$ blown up $5$ times. An antiholomorphic involution gives a smooth four-manifold homeomorphic to $S^4$, with a knotted torus as branch locus.

Optimization and Control.title: On the (non-)closedness of the set of ReLU networks
Optimization and Control.summary: We prove that the set $\mathcal{N}_N$ of ReLU networks with one hidden layer and at most $N\in\mathbb N$ neurons is weakly closed in $W^{1,p}(Ω)$, for a bounded connected open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$. Consequently, every coercive, weakly lower semicontinuous energy on this space attains its minimum over $\mathcal{N}_N$. This covers the Deep Ritz method with convex integrands, Sobolev training and Lipschitz learning. Moreover, as the weight decay parameter tends to zero, minimizers of the regularized problem converge, up to subsequences, to minimizers with minimal parameter norm. We also prove that the set of ReLU networks with two hidden layers of bounded widths is not closed in $W^{1,p}(Ω)$ or in $C(\overlineΩ)$. This disproves a conjecture of Petersen, Raslan and Voigtlaender.

Optimization and Control.title: Geometric Pairwise Classification of Affine Constraints over Ellipsoidal Regions
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper presents a deterministic geometric procedure for analysing affine constraints over fixed ellipsoidal regions, motivated by chance-constrained set approximation. Analytical tests classify inequalities as always violated, never violated, or cutting. Pairwise tests determine whether two inequalities can be strictly violated at a common point, yielding a compatibility matrix. The tests follow from quadratic optimisation and the Karush--Kuhn--Tucker conditions, with explicit treatment of tangencies, parallel normals, and degenerate inequalities. The formulation applies in arbitrary finite dimensions and provides geometric information for subsequent bounds on simultaneous sampled violations and safe-region approximation.

Optimization and Control.title: Differentiable Nonlinear Model Predictive Control
Optimization and Control.summary: The efficient computation of parametric solution sensitivities is a key challenge in the integration of learning-enhanced methods with nonlinear model predictive control, as their availability is crucial for many learning algorithms. This paper discusses the computation of solution sensitivities of general nonlinear programs using the implicit function theorem and smoothed optimality conditions treated in interior-point methods (IPM). We introduce sequential barrier quadratic programming (SBQP), which generalizes SQP with an IPM quadratic programming (QP) solver by allowing the barrier parameter to approach a prescribed nonnegative target value, recovering classical SQP when this target is zero. Previous works are limited to convex or unconstrained formulations, or lack an implementation for efficient sensitivity evaluation. The publication is accompanied by an efficient open-source implementation within the `acados` framework, providing both forward and adjoint sensitivities for general optimal control problems, achieving speedups exceeding 3x over the state-of-the-art solvers `mpc.pytorch` and `cvxpygen`.

Optimization and Control.title: A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for the Minimal Input/Output Node Cardinality Disturbance Decoupling Problem over Networks via Output Feedback
Optimization and Control.summary: For networked systems, we propose a polynomial-time algorithm for solving the minimal input/output node cardinality disturbance decoupling problem via output feedback. The algorithm computes an optimal solution, namely, a pair of minimum-cardinality sets of control input and measurement output nodes that achieve disturbance decoupling, by solving a min-cut/max-flow problem on an extended network.
Optimization and Control.comment: MATLAB functions implementing the results presented in this article are available in the GitLab repository: https://gitlab.liu.se/lucle71/node-based-ddp or in Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23476722

Optimization and Control.title: Instantaneous control for stabilization of interacting particle systems: convergence rates and dominant frequencies
Optimization and Control.summary: We study a class of Cucker-Smale-type systems with a binary interaction potential subject to an external control input. We apply an instantaneous rolling horizon control (IRHC) feedback to address two different control problems: full set-point stabilization of a spatial configuration with zero velocity and stabilization of the center of mass at a desired position with zero mean velocity using a single external agent. The IRHC feedback has been shown to preserve the port-Hamiltonian structure of the corresponding open-loop systems. We analyze how the control parameters and the time discretization affect convergence rates and oscillation frequencies and compare the IRHC feedback with the corresponding IDA-PBC feedback obtained by omitting an additional correction term. For the reduced center of mass dynamics, we derive explicit predictions for continuous- and discrete-time spectral decay rates and oscillation frequencies and verify these predictions numerically. For the full nonlinear particle system, the controller comparison is done by numerical experiments.

Optimization and Control.title: Kernel Metrics and Learning for Borel MDPs: Identifiability and Adaptive Control
Optimization and Control.summary: We consider a Markov decision process with standard Borel spaces and an unknown transition kernel under the average cost criterion. We do not impose any parametrization on the set of possible kernels. To facilitate our analysis, we first develop implication relations between several topologies on kernels defined by pointwise, continuous, or uniform weak convergence; we then review robustness properties on the space of kernels, and finally we establish compactness conditions on the space of kernels. Building on this regularity analysis, we then present two data-driven identifiability results; the first one being Bayesian and the second one empirical. Our conditions for the Bayesian setting are significantly more relaxed compared with prior work which considered either finite or parametric models, though we do not obtain a rate of convergence. Our analysis is asymptotic and builds on measurability in terms of the tail $σ$-field of the available information. Identifiability results are then used to design near-optimal adaptive control policies which alternate between periods of exploration, where the controller acts according to a policy which is conducive to the identification of the true kernel, and periods of exploitation where the controller's information on the kernel is utilized. We will establish that such policies are near optimal. In summary, our contribution is with regard to the general standard Borel setup where there is no apriori parametric representation.

Optimization and Control.title: Convergence of optimizers implies eigenvalues filtering at equilibrium
Optimization and Control.summary: Ample empirical evidence in deep neural network training suggests that a variety of optimizers tend to find nearly global optima. In this article, we adopt the reversed perspective that convergence to an arbitrary point is assumed rather than proven, focusing on the consequences of this assumption. From this viewpoint, in line with recent advances on the edge-of-stability phenomenon, we argue that different optimizers effectively act as eigenvalue filters determined by their hyperparameters. Specifically, the standard gradient descent method inherently avoids the sharpest minima, whereas Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) algorithms go even further by actively favoring wider basins. Inspired by these insights, we propose two novel algorithms that exhibit enhanced eigenvalue filtering, effectively promoting wider minima. Our theoretical analysis leverages a generalized Hadamard--Perron stable manifold theorem and applies to general semialgebraic $C^2$ functions, without requiring additional non-degeneracy conditions or global Lipschitz bound assumptions. We support our conclusions with numerical experiments on feed-forward neural networks.

Optimization and Control.title: Quasipolynomial-Time Planning for Decodable POMDPs
Optimization and Control.summary: We study planning for finite-horizon partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) with finite state, action, and observation spaces. Both exact and approximate planning are known to be computationally hard in this setting, so prior work has explored natural assumptions that make planning easier. Recent work [Golowich et al., 2022] gave quasipolynomial-time approximate planning algorithms for observable POMDPs. These are POMDPs whose observation channels satisfy an $\ell_1$-observability condition, but notably, no assumptions are required on the transition dynamics. In a similar vein, for every fixed $ρ>0$, we give quasipolynomial-time approximate planning algorithms for $ρ$-decodable POMDPs. We show that decodability is implied by both $\ell_1$- and $\ell_2$-observability and is strictly weaker than observability. Moreover, we show that the optimal decodability constant can be computed in polynomial time, whereas computing the optimal $\ell_1$-observability constant is NP-hard in the worst case. We also show that the fast filter-forgetting guarantee underlying the approach of [Golowich et al., 2022] does not extend directly from $\ell_1$-observability to constant $\ell_2$-observability. Thus, decodability is an easy-to-check, unifying assumption under which quasipolynomial-time approximate planning for POMDPs is possible.

Optimization and Control.title: Attractivity Implies Lyapunov Stability for Multidimensional Fornasini--Marchesini Systems
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the linear multidimensional Fornasini--Marchesini recurrence with uniformly bounded boundary data prescribed on the open coordinate faces. Attractivity is understood in the sense of Pringsheim convergence, in which all discrete indices tend to infinity. We establish that attractivity alone implies Lyapunov stability, and consequently is equivalent to asymptotic stability, for an arbitrary number of discrete directions. Our proof combines inheritance of attractivity by lower-dimensional subsystems, a Baire-category uniform boundedness argument, and word-sum estimates to control coordinate slabs outside the Pringsheim tail. We use a generalized spectral stability criterion proved in a separate companion preprint, without reproving that criterion here. We also obtain a uniform exponential interior estimate and contrast our boundary/convergence convention with an earlier two-dimensional attractivity theorem.

Optimization and Control.title: Fixed-point acceleration on Neural Wasserstein manifolds
Optimization and Control.summary: We propose a fixed-point acceleration method for optimization over probability measures, applicable to a variety of machine learning problems. We represent probability measures as pushforwards of a reference distribution through a neural network map and equip the parameter space with the induced pullback Wasserstein metric. This geometric structure allows natural gradient descent to be interpreted as a fixed-point iteration on a Riemannian manifold. We accelerate this iteration using Riemannian Anderson mixing method, which exploits historical residuals to capture approximate second-order information without forming Hessians. In the present parametric setting, the manifold is represented by Euclidean coordinates endowed with a point-dependent metric, simplifying retraction and vector transport. We evaluate the method on multimodal sampling, PDE-based inverse problems, aggregation dynamics, Bayesian logistic regression, and generative modeling. Across the tested tasks, Anderson mixing reduces the number of natural-gradient iterations and achieves competitive performance relative to SGD and Adam in terms of both loss-gradient evaluations and wall-clock time. These results suggest that fixed-point acceleration is an efficient tool for improving the computational efficiency of training on parametric Wasserstein methods.

Optimization and Control.title: Row-sparse ah-symmetric reflexive generalized inverses with a few extra rows: local search with approximation guarantees
Optimization and Control.summary: For a rank-$r$ matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, ah-symmetric reflexive generalized inverses $H$ with few nonzero rows give least-squares solutions that are fast to evaluate and use few variables. A known determinant-based local search finds one with exactly $r$ nonzero rows and 2,1-norm within an essentially tight factor $r$ of the minimum at an exact local optimum. We let the nonzero rows of $H$ lie in a set $K$ of $k\ge r$ indices and study how to choose $K$. We bound the loss of this restriction (restricted over unrestricted minimum 2,1-norm) by a simple geometric certificate and establish that a local search maximizing the squared rank-$r$ volume of the corresponding columns of $A$ gives loss at most $\sqrt{k(r+εk)/(k-r+1)}$, where $1+ε$ is the swap tolerance. With $ε=0$ this is $r$ at $k=r$ and less than $\sqrt{2r}$ for $k\ge2r$; with $ε=1/k$ the search runs in polynomial time on rational data. The same support yields an ah-symmetric reflexive generalized inverse with spectral norm within a factor $\sqrt{1+(n-k)(r+εk)/(k-r+1)}$ of that of the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse. The loss guarantees hold for every norm on the rows. In general, our certificate bound is tight up to a factor depending only on $k/r$, and on some instances, for a suitable row norm, so is the loss bound; for the 2,1-norm, however, the certificate can overestimate the loss by a factor $\sqrt r$. The local search is the Fedorov exchange algorithm of 0/1 D-optimal design; this yields a fast implementation and, via the Kiefer-Wolfowitz theorem, supports of at most $r(r+1)/2+1$ rows with certificate at most $\sqrt r$, best possible in general. On instances from earlier work, the observed loss is far below the guarantee, and the method matches two ADMM heuristics when few rows are removed and otherwise gives 2,1-norms up to 27% smaller, one to two orders of magnitude faster.

Optimization and Control.title: Dynamic Centrality Measures for Water Distribution Network Hydraulics
Optimization and Control.summary: Water distribution networks (WDNs) are susceptible to various failures, including but not limited to human errors, cyber-attacks, and network modifications, necessitating the vulnerability analysis of WDNs. Graph-theoretic centrality measures---as a main class of centrality measures---aim to rank the network components solely based on their influence (i.e., criticality) on the WDN topology in the case of input changes, while overlooking the WDN dynamics. To overcome such a limitation, this paper uses a control-theoretic centrality measure to identify the network's most and least influential pipes in WDNs, by simultaneously incorporating the dynamics and topology of the WDN. First, given a WDN modeled by nonlinear differential-algebraic equations (NDAEs) consisting of transient flow dynamics as differential equation (DE) and conservation of water mass as algebraic equation (AE) and considering the pipe flow rates as states of the state-space (SS) representation, we extract a linearized system modeled by linear ordinary differential equations (LODEs) around the equilibrium (i.e., steady) flow rate vector. Second, treating pipe flow rates as SS nodes (states), we introduce a node centrality-based measure, namely \textit{vulnerability vector (VV)}, to rank the network pipes based on their influence on the dynamics and topology of the WDN in the case of input changes. In particular, the network's most and least influential pipes can be identified through such a centrality-based approach. This enables water engineers to understand the WDN's vulnerability better and effectively prioritize the maintenance and operational efforts on the most influential pipes within the WDN.

Optimization and Control.title: A Regular First-Order Calculus for the Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao Geometry
Optimization and Control.summary: We introduce a notion of intrinsic differentiability for functionals on the space of finite nonnegative measures equipped with the Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao (WFR) distance, also known as the Hellinger--Kantorovich (HK) distance. The resulting static first-order calculus accounts simultaneously for spatial transport and mass reweighting. We characterize regular barycentric logarithms through optimal semicouplings and measurable selections at the transport threshold, and prove their tangency at arbitrary finite source measures. The defining expansion extends to non-optimal semicouplings, with remainder of smaller order than the square root of their cost. This yields differentiation formulas for simultaneous transport and reweighting and uniqueness of the gradients. We also give a sufficient criterion in terms of regular flat derivatives. We characterize differentiability of one half the squared WFR distance by a common optimal Monge transport--growth representation with no target mass created from the cone vertex. Equivalently, the regular barycentric logarithm is unique and its norm equals the distance; the gradient is minus this logarithm. Finally, we formulate the corresponding calculus on probability measures. On $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R}^d)$, WFR differentiability implies intrinsic Wasserstein differentiability, with the transport component of the WFR gradient coinciding with the Wasserstein gradient. Whenever a flat derivative exists, one quarter of the reaction component agrees almost everywhere with its centered representative. As a byproduct we obtain a Wasserstein differentiability result for the squared $\mathrm{WFR}$ distance.

Optimization and Control.title: Free energy Wasserstein gradient flow and their particle counterparts: toy model, (degenerate) PL inequalities and exit times
Optimization and Control.summary:
In finite dimension, the long-time and metastable behavior of a gradient flow perturbated by a small Brownian noise is well understood. A similar situation arises when a Wasserstein gradient flow over a space of probability measure is approximated by a system of mean-field interacting particles, but classical results do not apply in these infinite-dimensional settings. We are concerned with the situation where the objective function of the optimization problem contains an entropic penalization, so that the particle system is a Langevin diffusion process.
  The work has two parts: the first and main one is devoted to the general study of a very simple class of models, for which the infinite-dimensional behavior is fully characterized by an autonomous diffusion process at fixed finite dimension. On the one hand, we prove the equivalence between fast convergence for the mean-field gradient flow and for the particle system in terms of functional inequalities (log-Sobolev, Polyak-Łojasiewicz, Talagrand and variants thereof) including the degenerate polynomial case occurring at phase transitions, and on the other hand we characterise the metastable behavior in terms of transition time between local minimiser -- establishing an Eyring-Kramers formula -- and of exit time from unstable critical points.
  In a second part, motivated by and building on the systematic study of the toy models, we consider the continuous Curie-Weiss model in a symmetric double-well potential, exactly at the critical temperature. We show that, although the $N$-particle Gibbs measure does not satisfy a uniform-in-$N$ standard log-Sobolev inequality (the optimal constant growing like $\sqrt{N}$), it does satisfy a more general Łojasiewicz inequality uniformly in $N$, inducing uniform polynomial long-time convergence rates, propagation of chaos at stationarity and uniformly in time, and creation of chaos.

Optimization and Control.title: Implementation-Based Incentive Design for Autonomous Mobility-on-Demand and Transit Systems
