We further establish that the horizontal unit normal belongs to $BV_{\mathrm{loc}}$ and characterize its $W^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ regularity in terms of the vanishing one-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the characteristic set. Finally, we answer an open question by Danielli, Garofalo and Nhieu by constructing a $C^2$ surface with a unique characteristic point whose horizontal mean curvature fails to be locally integrable, thus showing that the additional Hölder regularity cannot, in general, be replaced by $C^2$ regularity.

Differential Geometry.title: A remark on the reach and upper bounds on some extrinsic geometry invariants of submanifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We consider a compact submanifold $M$ of a Riemannian manifold $N$ and we use the second variation formula as a tool to drive some geometric results on reach$(M, N)$ the reach of $M$ in $N$, including some useful relations between the extrinsic geometry of $M$ in $N$ and reach$(M, N)$. Our results generalize some theorems previously proved for the special case where $N$ is Euclidean space.

Differential Geometry.title: Complete self-shrinkers with scalar curvature bounded below
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $X:M^n\to\mathbb R^{n+1}$ be a complete self-shrinker with constant squared norm of the second fundamental form. We prove that up to an orthogonal transformation, the image $X(M^n)$ is a sphere $S^n(\sqrt n)$, or a hyperplane $\mathbb R^n$ or a generalized cylinder $ S^k(\sqrt{k})\times\R^{n-k},\ 1\le k\le n-1$ if scalar curvature $R$ satisfies $R\geq -3/2$, which improves the recent results in \cite{CLW1}.

Differential Geometry.title: On the Structure of Kähler-Ricci Shrinkers
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that every complete Kähler--Ricci shrinker with nonnegative Ricci curvature is holomorphically isometric to $\mathbb{C}^k\times N^{n-k}$ for some $0\le k\le n$, where $\mathbb{C}^k$ is the Gaussian shrinker and $N$ is a compact Kähler--Ricci shrinker with nonnegative Ricci curvature. As a corollary, every complete Kähler--Ricci shrinker with quasi-positive Ricci curvature is compact. We also prove that every singular Kähler--Ricci shrinker on a Fano cone is a Ricci-flat Kähler cone.
Differential Geometry.comment: v2: Added discussion and results on singular Kähler-Ricci shrinkers on Fano cones. Comments are welcome!

Differential Geometry.title: Singular points of envelopes and offsets: a transition from 2D to 3D
Differential Geometry.summary: We recall properties of the offsets of a (plane) kiss curve and their singularities, then we make a transition to 3D, considering the surface obtained by revolution of the kiss curve about one of its axes. When pos?sible, geometric constructions using automated methods are performed. This induces a need to focus on algebraic computations. Networking be?tween different kinds of software is of utmost importance, in order to use their respective strengths (dynamic geometry, dragging points, strong al?gebraic computations, etc.). A core difference between the 2D and 3D situations is that automated commands existing in 2D are not available in 3D. This makes the DGS less relevant in 3D than in 2D. In 3D, most of the work must be performed with the CAS. The singular points of a kiss curve in the plane are tacnodes (cusps) and crunodes (self-intersection). The singularities are not isolated anymore and cuspidal edges appear. In this setting, implicitization is a heavy endeavour and we need another technology, related to AI; we describe this briefly. The 2D activities have been proposed to in-service teachers learning towards an advanced degree.

Differential Geometry.title: Generalized Frobenius manifolds: symmetries and their classification in 2-dimensions
Differential Geometry.summary: A theory of symmetries of generalized Frobenius manifolds is developed. This is used to study the solution space of all generalized Frobenius manifolds that are "above" a specific Frobenius manifold. Since all (semi-simple) Frobenius manifolds in 2-dimensions are known, by constructing all homogeneous Legendre fields associated to these manifolds we classify all 2-dimensional generalized Frobenius manifolds. With this description, the known examples of generalized Frobenius manifolds correspond to distinguished points in this solution space. For Hurwitz-Frobenius manifolds the action of a Legendre transformation on Hurwitz space data, and in particular the primary differential, is given.

Differential Geometry.title: Morse index and bifurcation of Clifford hypersurfaces under Hopf squashing
Differential Geometry.summary: Clifford hypersurfaces are products of two spheres embedded in a round sphere. We call them balanced when their radii are chosen so that the product is minimal in the round metric. We study how their Morse index and nullity change when the ambient metric is deformed along the fibers of a Hopf fibration. This deformation, called \emph{Hopf squashing}, rescales the fiber metric by a parameter $t>0$ while leaving the horizontal metric unchanged. For the complex, quaternionic, and octonionic Hopf fibrations, we determine the index and nullity of balanced Clifford hypersurfaces throughout the fiber-shortening range and show that their Jacobi potential is independent of $t$. In the octonionic case we also determine the first positive Jacobi eigenvalue and its multiplicity. In the octonionic case, at $t=27$, a branch of nonhomogeneous minimal hypersurfaces bifurcates from the balanced Clifford hypersurface; its members have Morse index $1432$ and nullity $15$.

Differential Geometry.title: Combinatorial curvature flows for spherical vertex scalings on infinitely triangulated surfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the combinatorial Yamabe and Calabi flows for spherical vertex scalings on infinitely triangulated surfaces. Under the assumptions of uniformly bounded vertex degree and an $ε$-uniformly nondegenerate initial metric, we establish the short-time existence of smooth solutions to both combinatorial curvature flows. We also establish short-time uniqueness for the combinatorial Yamabe flow. For the combinatorial Calabi flow, we establish short-time uniqueness among solutions that are continuous in time with respect to the $L^\infty(V)$ norm.

Differential Geometry.title: Strongly invariant differential operators on parabolic geometries modelled on $Gr(3,3)$
Differential Geometry.summary: We consider the curved geometries modelled on the homogeneous space $G/P$, where $G=SL(6,\mathbb R)$ acts transitively on the Grassmannian $Gr(3,3)$ of three-dimensional subspaces in $\mathbb R^6$, and $P$ is the corresponding isotropic subgroup. We classify the strongly invariant operators between sections of vector bundles induced on such geometries by irreducible $P$-modules, i.e., those obtained via homomorphisms of semi-holonomic Verma modules.
Differential Geometry.comment: 24 pages, new section and 2 ancillary files with Python code added

Differential Geometry.title: First-order asymptotic expansions for spectral convergence of normalized graph Laplacians constructed from samples on manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: Under i.i.d. uniform sampling from a closed Riemannian manifold embedded in Euclidean space, we derive first-order asymptotic expansions for the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of symmetrically normalized graph Laplacians constructed via Gaussian kernels and provide concentration inequalities for the remainder terms. As a direct consequence, we establish the corresponding weak convergence results. Unlike most related works, our analysis does not impose a multiplicity-one assumption on the eigenvalues, thereby extending the applicability of the framework to general manifolds with potentially nontrivial eigenvalue multiplicities.

Differential Geometry.title: Perturbations of a minimal surface with triple junctions in $\mathbb{R}^2 \times \mathbb{S}^1$
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct stationary perturbations of a specific minimal surface with a circle of triple junctions in $\mathbb{R}^2 \times \mathbb{S}^1$, that satisfy given boundary data.
Differential Geometry.comment: Add 1 figure, include Remark 1.2 and 1.3 right after Theorem 1.1. To appear in CAG

Differential Geometry.title: Warped area-minimizing hypersurface and warped product metric
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth, compact, connected and oriented Riemannian manifold with $3\le n\le 7$ and $H_{n-1}(M;\mathbb{Z})\neq 0$, and let $u>0$ be smooth on $M$. Suppose that \[ -γu^{-1}Δ_g u+\Ricmin_g\ \geq\ (n-1)(n-3)\,u^{-2}|\nabla u|^2, \qquad γ=n-1, \] where $\Ricmin_g$ is the pointwise least Ricci curvature. Since both this hypothesis and the class of warped (weighted) area-minimizers are invariant under $u\mapstoλu$, we normalize $u\equiv1$ on the minimizer. We prove that some non-trivial class in $H_{n-1}(M;\mathbb{Z})$ contains a warped area-minimizing hypersurface $Σ$ on which $u$ is constant, and that $M$ locally splits as a warped product $(-ε,ε)\times_fΣ$, $g=dt^2+f^2(t)g_Σ$, with $f=u^{-1}$ and $\operatorname{Ric}_{g_Σ}\geq (n-2)[(f')^2-ff'']\,g_Σ$. By extending the foliation via Federer--Fleming compactness of the constant-warped-area leaves, this local splitting upgrades to a \emph{global} one: $M$ is covered by $\mathbb{R}\times_fΣ$, its universal cover is $\mathbb{R}\times_f\tildeΣ$ where $\tildeΣ$ is the universal cover of $Σ$, and $f=u^{-1}$ is periodic and bounded above and below, so $M$ fibres over $\mathbb{S}^1$ with fibre a quotient of $Σ$. This spectral bound is saturated with equality by warped product metrics, which is what makes it the natural threshold for warped rather than direct product rigidity. When $u\equiv1$ it reduces to $\Ricmin_g\geq0$ and our conclusion to the classical product splitting.

Differential Geometry.title: A uniqueness theorem for Allen--Cahn global minimizers asymptotic to the Simons cone
Differential Geometry.summary: For every integer $m\ge4$, we prove that the saddle-shaped solution of the Allen--Cahn equation in $\R^{2m}$ constructed by Cabré and Terra \cite{CabreTerra2009} is a global minimizer. Moreover, up to sign, it is the unique global minimizer whose nodal set at infinity is a normal graph over the Simons cone with a height that decays faster than that of the Hardt--Simon leaves.

Differential Geometry.title: A counterexample on the main flatness conjecture for $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundles
Differential Geometry.summary: The main flatness conjecture for $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundles predicts the existence of a unique strongly positive flat compatible Hermitian metric for every $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundle. We use cyclic Higgs bundles to disprove this conjecture for every rank $n \geq 3.$

Differential Geometry.title: Making Poisson σ again - an étude on groupoidal gauging, anomalies, gerbes, and defects
Differential Geometry.summary: The Poisson $σ$-model (PSM) over a closed worldsheet $Σ$ is reinterpreted as a theory of connections on a trivial principaloid bundle $P_0 = Σ\times G \to Σ$ with the symplectic structure groupoid $(G,ω)$ integrating the Poisson target $(M,Π)$, and that of sections of the shadow bundle $F_0 = Σ\times M \to Σ$ - as defined in 2503.09886 [math.DG]. The flat directions of the PSM are explained as linearisations of automorphisms of $P_0$, modelled on maps from $Σ$ into the group of lagrangean bisections of $G$, which induce Poisson automorphisms of $(M,Π)$. The gauge anomaly of the ensuing field theory is derived and demonstrated to vanish for prequantisable $ω$. A general anomaly-cancellation mechanism is proposed, which couples the bare model - rewritten as the holonomy of a connection-dependent trivial gerbe on $F_0$ - to a background gerbe over $M$ endowed with a $G$-equivariant structure. The coupling takes the form of the tensor product of the two gerbes and the extended PSM is defined as the holonomy of the product gerbe. An essential generalisation of the theory is then proposed - to shadows $F$ of principaloid bundles $P$ of arbitrary topology, in keeping with the interpretation of the gauging as descent to the orbistack $M//G$. The generalisation uses local product gerbes depending on local connections over trivialisations of $F$. The $G$-equivariant structure is proven to ensure a 2-stacky descent of the local gerbes to a global one over $F$. Its holonomy is taken as the definition of the generalised PSM. A cohomological discussion of obstructions against the descent is provided. Finally, a reformulation of the generalised PSM as a field theory with a topological gauge-symmetry defect is given, in which the $G$-equivariant structure is employed - alongside the transition cocycle of $P$ - as the datum of the defect.

Differential Geometry.title: Generalized Fermat's principle and Snell's law for cone structures and applications
Differential Geometry.summary: Fermat's principle is fully generalized to the case where a smooth interface separates two cone structures -- Lorentz-Finsler lightcones -- representing wave propagation in a potentially inhomogeneous, anisotropic, time-dependent and discontinuous medium. The interface, wave source and receiver are assumed to be a hypersurface, a submanifold and a curve in the spacetime, respectively, of any causal character. For a trajectory to fulfill Fermat's principle -- i.e., to be a critical point of the arrival time functional -- its direction must change at the interface, obeying a precise condition that generalizes Snell's law of refraction when the wave crosses the interface, or the law of reflection when it remains in a single medium. Both laws are analyzed in detail to establish the conditions ensuring the existence and uniqueness of refracted and reflected trajectories, and to determine whether they actually minimize the arrival time. Applications to Zermelo's navigation problem and the determination of geodesics in discretized spacetimes are also emphasized.
Differential Geometry.comment: Slight reformulation of the Appendix to increase its generality. This version now matches the published version. 51 pages, 11 figures

Differential Geometry.title: Invariant forms compute the Dolbeault cohomology of complex nilmanifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that the inclusion of left-invariant forms into the Dolbeault complex of a compact nilmanifold $M$ endowed with a left-invariant complex structure $J$ induces an isomorphism in cohomology in every bidegree, settling a long-standing conjecture originating from a question of Console-Fino and Cordero-Fernández-Gray-Ugarte. As consequences, we show that small deformations of $J$ are still invariant, as conjectured by Hasegawa, and that Bott-Chern, Aeppli, and Frölicher invariants are computed by invariant forms and are independent of the lattice, settling a conjecture of Angella on Bott-Chern cohomology.
Differential Geometry.comment: 25 pages, no figures. v2: Expanded and clarified proofs and exposition, with explicit polynomial degree bounds and a fuller treatment of deformations; main results unchanged

Differential Geometry.title: Spheres with transitive families of CMC hypersurfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: The goal of this paper is to investigate the following question: what geometric restrictions does the existence of a transitive family of constant mean curvature hyperspheres impose on a Riemannian metric on $\mathbb S^n$? The notion of a transitive family can be made precise through the theory of Zoll families developed by Ambrozio, Marques, and Neves. Within this framework, we partially extend their local rigidity theorem for even conformal factors on $\mathbb S^3$ to every dimension $n\ge4$, assuming each hypersphere in the minimal Zoll family has the area of a round equator. Moreover, we give a partial answer to the following generalized version of a question posed by Bryant: must a metric on $\mathbb S^n$, conformal to the round metric and admitting a Zoll family of hyperspheres with a common nonzero constant mean curvature, have constant sectional curvature? Finally, we investigate inverse problems following ideas of Hangan and prove a rigidity result about metrics for which the canonical geodesic spheres have constant mean curvature.

Differential Geometry.title: The Isoperimetric Flow and Synthetic Scalar Curvature for Causal Variational Principles
Differential Geometry.summary: An isoperimetric flow is introduced in the setting of causal variational principles. Describing the whole space by the support of a minimizing measure, we define an area functional on subsets by a surface layer integral. Mean curvature is defined via the first variation of this area functional. Using the method of minimizing movement, the isoperimetric flow is constructed as a Lipschitz curve of measures with prescribed volume change. As illustrating examples, we introduce and analyze ``smeared variants'' of the mean curvature flow in Euclidean space and on a Riemannian manifold. In these examples, it is shown that our area functional coincides with the usual area up to specified curvature corrections. As an application of our general results, by analyzing the volume and area of small isoperimetric balls, we introduce notions of local dimension and synthetic scalar curvature.

Geometric Topology.title: $G_2'$-Slodowy Slices II: Anosov Representations
Geometric Topology.summary: We find \emph{exotic} connected components of Anosov representations of surface groups in the higher rank group $G=G_2'$ that are neither $ι$-Fuchsian deformations nor higher rank Teichmüller spaces. These representations are found through the non-abelian Hodge correspondence via $G_2'$-Higgs bundles that we call \emph{$α$-bundles} and \emph{$β$-bundles}, which are particular cyclic Higgs bundles in the Slodowy slices of the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triples associated to the simple roots $α$ and $β$ of $\mathfrak{g}_2^{\mathbb{C}}$. We first prove that (most) $β$-bundles that are also Hodge bundles are $P_β$-Anosov and $α$-bundles are $P_α$-Anosov. The strategy employed is new, geometric, and general. For $σ\in \{α, β\}$, we then show the locally homogeneous $(G_2', G_2'/P_σ)$-manifold ${\mathscr{M}}_σ(ρ)$ recently described in arXiv:2510.12757, for the representation $ρ:π_1S\rightarrow G_2'$ associated to a $σ$-bundle, coincides up to finite cover with the corresponding geometric structure for $ρ$ defined via domains of discontinuity by Guichard-Wienhard and Kapovich-Leeb-Porti. Consequently, we find that $π_1({\mathscr{M}}_σ(ρ))$ is an invariant for the connected component of $ρ$ in the space of $P_σ$-Anosov representations. After verifying the folklore result that the $G_2'$-character variety has exactly three connected components, we conclude lower bounds for the number of connected components of $P_σ$-Anosov representations in the two non-Hitchin components, most of which are exotic.
Geometric Topology.comment: 53 pages, 7 figures, 1 table. No AI proof assistance

Geometric Topology.title: Generalized Hopf bifurcations: a homological analysis and obstructions to their existence
Geometric Topology.summary: A generalized Hopf bifurcation takes place when varying a parameter of a (semi)dynamical system causes an attractor $K$ to become a repeller. In doing so, it expels a (parameter-dependent) family of attractors. In this paper we concentrate on two questions: (1) what do the expelled attractors look like?, and (2) can any attractor $K$ undergo a generalized Hopf bifurcation? Regarding (1), we compute the cohomology of the expelled attractors in terms of the cohomology of $K$; in the case of continuous-time dynamics this can be improved to a computation of their Borsuk shape. As for (2), we show that certain compacta cannot undergo generalized Hopf bifurcations and, when the ambient space has dimension $ \leq 3$, give a complete topological characterization of which can.

Geometric Topology.title: Monodromy and vanishing cycles for complete intersection curves
Geometric Topology.summary: We compute the topological monodromy of every family of complete intersection curves. Like in the case of plane curves previously treated by the second-named author, we find the answer is given by the $r$-spin mapping class group associated to the maximal root of the adjoint line bundle. Our main innovation is a suite of tools for studying the monodromy of sections of a tensor product of very ample line bundles in terms of the monodromy of sections of the factors, allowing for an induction on (multi-)degree.
Geometric Topology.comment: Revised version incorporating further referee comments

Geometric Topology.title: On the topology of some linear systems of hyperelliptic curves in Hirzebruch surfaces
Geometric Topology.summary: Following a program suggested by Dolgachev and Libgober in 1981, we study the topology of the locus of smooth sections of linear systems of hyperelliptic curves on Hirzebruch surfaces. Our primary interest is the computation of various flavors of ``enriched monodromy representations''. Within this class of examples, we find that a variety of behaviors occur - in some situations the enriched monodromy faithfully captures the fundamental group, and in others it does not. Our arguments mainly leverage algebro-geometric techniques to compute cohomological obstructions to families of embeddings.

Geometric Topology.title: Khovanov and knot Floer homology of fibered positive links
Geometric Topology.summary: For fibered positive links, we compute the reduced and unreduced Khovanov homology in homological grading two over both $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{F}_2$, and the knot Floer homology in the penultimate Alexander grading. Our Khovanov calculations, combined with the result of Przytycki-Sazdanović, prove that every nontrivial semi-adequate knot has 2-torsion in its unreduced Khovanov homology. This establishes Shumakovitch's conjecture for semi-adequate knots, which include all nontrivial positive knots. The proofs involve induction using the skein exact sequences, with the Hopf link as the base case.
Geometric Topology.comment: v2: Added Khovanov results and changed the title. 36 pages, 11 figures

Geometric Topology.title: Vietoris-Rips complexes of affine Coxeter groups
Geometric Topology.summary: We prove that all affine Coxeter groups admit contractible Vietoris-Rips complexes. More precisely, for any affine Coxeter group $W_a$ with standard generating set $S$, we prove that the Vietoris-Rips complex $\mathcal{VR}_t(W_a;S)$ is contractible for all sufficiently large $t$. We also investigate other finitely generated groups of the form $G=H\rtimes F$ for $F$ finite, and prove that for any finite symmetric generating set $A$ for $H$ such that $A^F=A$, the complexes $\mathcal{VR}_t(G;AF)$ and $\mathcal{VR}_t(H;A)$ are homotopy equivalent for all $t\ge 1$.
Geometric Topology.comment: 19 pages, 3 figures. V2: Submitted version. The results about Coxeter groups are unchanged. The more general results are slightly weaker, following our fixing an error (a certain generating set needed to be invariant under conjugation by a certain finite subgroup)

Geometric Topology.title: No 13-vertex triangulation of the three-torus
Geometric Topology.summary: Kühnel and Lassmann constructed a neighborly triangulation of the three-torus on 15 vertices, and Lutz conjectured that it is vertex-minimal. The standard lower-bound arguments exclude at most twelve vertices but do not decide the 13- and 14-vertex cases. We exclude the 13-vertex case. Our proof uses the Novik--Swartz $g_2$-inequality and a simplicial-complement reduction to a nine-vertex model of the punctured three-torus. By analyzing fundamental groups of small simplicial complexes and applying Alexander duality in a vertex link, we obtain a contradiction from the deficiency of $\Z^3$.

Geometric Topology.title: Anosov representations from cyclic Higgs bundles
Geometric Topology.summary: For every complex simple Lie group G (not of type $E_8$) we construct the minimal Slodowy slice, which is a half-dimensional slice in the character variety of a closed surface group into G, containing the composition of Fuchsian representations with the minimal representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ in G and invariant under the mapping class group action. This slice is defined via cyclic Higgs bundles, and we show that when G is not of type $E_8$, the corresponding representations are Anosov, so in particular discrete and faithful, and dominate some Fuchsian representation. For each of these Higgs bundles, we consider the equivariant harmonic map to the symmetric space, and we show it is an embedding and a quasi-isometric embedding with regard to the induced metric. From the cyclicity of these Higgs bundles we are also able to construct an auxiliary harmonic map to a pseudoriemannian symmetric space $G/G^σ$ which is also an embedding. Our techniques also apply to harmonic Higgs bundles over the unit disk satisfying a certain completeness condition. These techniques also apply to two other families of cyclic Higgs bundles.

Geometric Topology.title: LLM-Assisted Advances in the Ropelength Problem
Geometric Topology.summary: This work summarizes some updates to the ropelength problem, concerning the shortest possible contour length of a unit-thickness knot, that were derived with the assistance of ChatGPT-5.6 Luna. The first of two main results is that the universal lower bound for a knot with crossing number C has been improved from $L\geq1.105C^{3/4}$ to $L\geq2.0996C^{3/4}$, achieved by further separating local and global terms in an optimization integral. The second main result is a bound relating ropelength to stick number (s), such that $L\geqπ(s-1)$. This implies stronger lower bounds for the ropelengths of at least 41 torus knots, and a specific class of pretzel knots. Other results include an improved packing-based lower bound for T(Q,Q) links and an optimized standard parameterization for torus knots. There were many problems for which the LLM was unable to render assistance, for example in reducing the numerical coefficients or scalings of known universal upper bounds.

Geometric Topology.title: Classifiyng metrically conical rational singularities
Geometric Topology.summary:
We will in this article classify which rational complex surface singularities are metrically conical, that is have the bilipschitz type of their inner metric equivalent to that of a cone. This is done using the thick-thin decomposition for the inner geometry of a normal complex surface singularity and properties of rational singularities.
  The result is a family of singularities depending only on their topology which is given as a $3$-parameter family.

Geometric Topology.title: One internal stabilization is enough for resolving self-referential tubes
Geometric Topology.summary: This paper shows that one internal stabilization is enough to resolve all the self-referential tubes on an embedding. As an application, this paper gives a complete isotopy classification for embedded surfaces with a common geometric dual in orientable $S^2$-bundle over a surface, provided that the embedded surfaces have greater genus than the base surface of the bundle.
Geometric Topology.comment: In the new version, we have strengthened the conclusion of the main theorem by extending its applicability from standard internal stabilizations to general internal stabilizations. 15 pages, 5 figures. Comments are welcome!

Geometric Topology.title: Seifert surfaces in the four-ball and composition of binary quadratic forms
Geometric Topology.summary: We use composition of binary quadratic forms to systematically create pairs of Seifert surfaces that are non-isotopic in the four-ball. Our main topological result employs Gauss composition to classify the pairs of binary quadratic forms that arise as the Seifert forms of pairs of disjoint Seifert surfaces of genus one. The main ingredient of the proof is number-theoretic and of independent interest. It establishes a geometric approach to Gauss composition via planes in the space of two-by-two matrices.

Geometric Topology.title: Surface subgroups with prescribed finite quotients
Geometric Topology.summary: We prove that every finite quotient of a finite covolume Kleinian group $G$ can be realized by a surface subgroup. More precisely, given an epimorphism from $G$ onto a finite group $F$, there exists a surface subgroup that maps surjectively onto $F$. As a consequence, the union of the surface subgroups is dense in $G$ with respect to the profinite topology. We also apply this result to obtain more examples of atoroidal surface bundles with signature zero in the construction of Kent--Leininger.

Geometric Topology.title: Genus zero simple knots
Geometric Topology.summary: We classify the simple knots in lens spaces with planar rational Seifert surfaces. As a consequence, we classify the homology classes of all knots in lens spaces that admit planar rational Seifert surfaces.

Geometric Topology.title: A counterexample on the main flatness conjecture for $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundles
Geometric Topology.summary: The main flatness conjecture for $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundles predicts the existence of a unique strongly positive flat compatible Hermitian metric for every $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundle. We use cyclic Higgs bundles to disprove this conjecture for every rank $n \geq 3.$

Geometric Topology.title: Geometric Combinatorics of Polynomials with Rotationally Symmetric Roots
Geometric Topology.summary: In a recent paper by Dougherty and McCammond, the authors introduced a piecewise Euclidean cell structure for the space of monic centered polynomials. This was achieved by studying the relationship between the polynomials and their critical values, using the Lyashko-Looijenga (LL) map, as well as the noncrossing combinatorics of the polynomials. In this paper, we extend their results to the space of polynomials with rotationally symmetric roots by studying an appropriate generalisation of the LL map, which relates the polynomials and their reduced critical values. The combinatorics of the polynomials are noncrossing partitions of type $B_d$. This give us a piecewise Euclidean cell structure built using the order complex of the noncrossing partition of type $B_d$. Along the way, we also give a compactification of this space of polynomials.

Geometric Topology.title: Complete Intersection Semigroups and End Curves on Singularities of Splice Type
Geometric Topology.summary: We prove that any complete intersection numerical semigroup can be realized as the value semigroup of an end curve in a splice quotient singularity. Therefore, providing a converse to the semigroup-theoretic statement of the End Curve Theorem of Neumann and Wahl for integral homology sphere links. Moreover, for a complete-intersection numerical semigroup, we define a family of knots such that the Alexander polynomial of any knot of the family coincides (up to a factor) with the generating series of the semigroup. Let $(X,0)$ be a splice quotient singularity with $\mathbb{Z}HS^3$ link $Σ$ and let $(C,0)$ be a reduced curve-germ embedded in $(X,0)$ defined as the zero locus of the product of end curve functions. We prove, thorugh our topological characterization of complete intersection semigroups, the coincidence between the Alexander polynomial of the knot cut out by $C$ in $Σ$ and the Poincaré series of the embedded curve. Hence providing a generalization of the result due to Campillo, Delgado and Gusein-Zade for plane curve singularities. Furthermore, for any good resolution of $(X,0)$ compatible with the splice quotient analytic structure, we provide an explicit description of the semigroup of integer multiplicities of functions along any divisor of the resolution.

Geometric Topology.title: Real monopole Floer homology and the Alexander polynomial
Geometric Topology.summary: We prove that the Euler characteristic of the framed real monopole Floer homology of the double branched cover of a link is given by the Alexander polynomial evaluated at $\sqrt{-1}$. For knots $K$ with determinant one, this formula shows that Miyazawa's degree invariant of $K$ can be computed in terms of the Alexander polynomial of $K$. The proof involves a new connected-sum formula and oriented skein exact triangles for some new variants of real monopole Floer homology, called the diagonal and cone real monopole Floer homology, which admit mod-two gradings. This is the monopole counterpart of Srivastava's Euler characteristic formula in real Heegaard Floer homology.

Geometric Topology.title: Sliding 2-handles over 3-handles and the barbell diffeomorphism
Geometric Topology.summary: We give three fundamental examples highlighting the relationship between loops of spheres in $\#^k S^2\times S^2$, pseudo-isotopies, and diffeomorphisms of the 4-sphere. First, we describe an explicit pseudo-isotopy and Hatcher-Wagoner family that realizes the barbell diffeomorphism $β$ of the 4-sphere by constructing a finger-Whitney system for the family. From the Hatcher-Wagoner family, we are able to conclude that the example in §7 of ``Pseudo-isotopies of simply connected 4-manifolds'' generates $β$. Next, it is known that the square of $β$ is isotopic to id. We reprove this by building an explicit 2-parameter family of Morse functions that trivializes the Hatcher-Wagoner family for $β^2$. We do this by utilizing exchange points and families of handle slides. In the final example, we show that another Hatcher-Wagoner family, affectionately called the double cross, also generates $β$.

Optimization and Control.title: Configuration-Constrained Tube MPC for Periodic Operation
Optimization and Control.summary: Periodic operation often emerges as the economically optimal mode in industrial processes subject to varying economic or environmental conditions. This paper proposes a robust model predictive control (MPC) framework for uncertain systems described by polytopic linear difference inclusions (LDIs), whose dynamics evolve as convex combinations of finitely many linear control systems subject to additive disturbances. The robust control problem is formulated as a convex optimization program over configuration-constrained polytopic tubes, with the objective of tracking a periodic tube that is optimal for a given economic criterion. Artificial variables embedded in the formulation ensure recursive feasibility and robust constraint satisfaction under changes in the economic criterion, and convergence to the optimal periodic tube when the criterion remains constant. To improve computational efficiency, we introduce a quadratic upper approximation of the periodic cost under a Lipschitz continuity assumption, yielding a Quadratic Program (QP) that preserves the above theoretical guarantees. The approach is demonstrated on an illustrative example and an eight-state ball--plate system.

Optimization and Control.title: Two Communities, One Problem: Branch-and-Bound vs. A* for Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling
Optimization and Control.summary: Branch-and-Bound (B&B) and $A^*$ are popular exact search methods originating from Operations Research and Artificial Intelligence, respectively. Although the two methods share fundamental search principles, their different ways of exploring the search space can lead to substantially different computational performance. We investigate these differences using the Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling Problem (RCPSP) as an exemplary problem setting. We first establish the relationships between mixed-integer linear programming, state-action, and timed Petri-net representations. Since B&B and $A^*$ admit numerous algorithmic enhancements, we focus on relatively basic implementations. This allows us to examine the fundamental differences between the methods rather than compare the performance of state-of-the-art solvers. By using the same lower bound and best-first node selection, we isolate the effects of the search mechanisms, particularly the identification of equivalent states reached through different scheduling decision sequences. Experiments on 480 benchmark RCPSP instances show that graph-based $A^*$ substantially outperforms the B&B variants considered. With additional pruning rules, $A^*$ proves optimality for all 480 instances, compared with 445 for best-first B&B under the same time and memory limits. Depth-first B&B uses less memory and can find feasible solutions even when the search does not finish within the time limit. Stronger linear programming relaxations reduce the search space but introduce considerable computational overhead. Our findings highlight the importance of duplicate-state detection and clarify the computational trade-offs between the search approaches. These insights can help researchers select an appropriate method and identify opportunities to incorporate effective mechanisms from one approach into the other.

Optimization and Control.title: Cotangent-lift inference of stochastic microbial dynamics
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the parameter estimation for the stochastic logistic and Lotka--Volterra diffusions from discrete, irregularly spaced observations corrupted by measurement noise, a setting typical of microbiome time series. For the logistic equation, the growth rate acts as a time change and does not enter the stationary law, so it can be identified only from the temporal structure of the data. We prove that the maximum-likelihood estimator of the Euler scheme, with the observations taken as the states, coincides with the regression of log-increments on abundances used in the literature, and we characterise what this estimator cannot see under measurement noise: for the linearised dynamics, the law of consecutive pairs of observations is invariant along an explicit one-parameter family of relaxation rates and noise levels, and the regression converges to a limit set by the noise. Treating the true abundances as latent, we compute the likelihood with a Gaussian moment filter and show that measurement noise is precisely what couples the filter states across samples. The exact gradient is then the backward recursion of the discrete cotangent lift, whose cost, two to three likelihood evaluations, does not depend on the number of parameters, and we give the covector map of each filter step in closed form. In simulations, the latent estimator recovers the relaxation times, noise levels and interaction strengths that the regression biases, while larger communities require prior information on the interactions. In gut microbiome time series it attributes most of the variability of a dominant genus to measurement noise and estimates its relaxation time at about $64$ hours, with a large standard error.

Optimization and Control.title: Cost controllability and predictive control of input-constrained monotone systems on Hilbert spaces
Optimization and Control.summary: Cost controllability, relating controllability and a performance measure like the stage cost in model predictive control (MPC), is a key tool in the stability and suboptimality analysis of closed-loop systems. We establish cost controllability for maximal monotone control systems subject to input constraints, a class encompassing finite- and infinite-dimensional port-Hamiltonian systems with colocated input and output. To this end, we employ a recently proposed saturated feedback to derive state-dependent bounds on the closed-loop cost. Our main result is that cost controllability holds globally with semiglobal exponential rate. We first establish this result in continuous time and then extend it to sampled-data systems. Whereas a qualitative detectability-like property is sufficient for asymptotic convergence of the controller, cost controllability requires quantitative rates. We provide two verifiable conditions ensuring cost controllability with explicit exponential rates: coercivity of the sum of system operator and output injection, and exponential detectability of the linear part. Moreover, under the coercivity condition, the resulting MPC scheme without terminal conditions renders the equilibrium globally asymptotically stable with semiglobal exponential rate already for prediction horizon two. We illustrate our results by a nonlinear finite-dimensional system, a semilinear heat equation and a nonlinearly damped wave equation.

Optimization and Control.title: Computing Lower Bounds on the Nonnegative Rank via Non-Convex Optimization Solvers
Optimization and Control.summary: The nonnegative rank of a nonnegative matrix $X$ is the smallest number of nonnegative rank-one factors that sum to $X$. Since computing the nonnegative rank is NP-hard, it is common to circumvent this issue by computing lower and upper bounds. In this paper, we propose non-convex formulations and practical implementations for four important lower bounds for the nonnegative rank, namely the fooling set bound (FSB), the rectangle covering bound (RCB), the hyperplane separation bound (HSB), and the self-scaled bound (SSB). In particular, to the best of our knowledge, our algorithm for computing the SSB is the first available in the literature. We compute the SSB for several matrices for which its value had not previously been reported. In some cases, the SSB provides the best known upper bound, while the other three bounds do not. Moreover, on canonical benchmarks, we show that our non-convex approaches are often competitive with existing methods. The paper also provides a consolidated reference for the current state of several classical lower bounds on a large number of benchmark matrices.
Optimization and Control.comment: Added a proof that the hyperplane separation bound equals 2 for the linear Euclidean distance matrices studied here. Improved the lower bound on the nonnegative rank of the slack matrix of the icosidodecahedron from 10 to 11. Clarified how the self-scaled bound recovers the known nonnegative rank of 7 for both M11 and M12

Optimization and Control.title: Smoothed Least-Absolute Conditional Multidimensional Scaling via Iteratively Reweighted Majorization
Optimization and Control.summary: Conditional multidimensional scaling combines latent coordinates with observed covariates to fit pairwise dissimilarities. We develop a smoothed l1 formulation using the shifted Charbonnier loss. We prove residualwise sharpness of the quadratic loss majorizer, monotonicity, compact containment, and stationarity of noncollapsed accumulation points. A uniform additive bound quantifies approximation to exact least-absolute conditional stress. The experiments use paired contamination, separately calibrated loss parameters, combined-configuration recovery, and direct checks of the theorem's inequalities.

Optimization and Control.title: Pareto Front Tracing in Higher Dimensions Using Numerical Integration
Optimization and Control.summary: We propose a numerical integration approach for tracing the Pareto front of unconstrained continuous multi-objective optimization problems. By stating optimality conditions for weighted sum scalarizations, we derive parametric equations for Pareto critical points, parameterized by the weights. Sensitivity analysis with respect to the weights yields a system of partial differential equations (PDEs). We prove local existence and uniqueness of solutions and derive conditions under which a solution extends to the entire weight space and yields Pareto optimal solutions. A tracing strategy for the resulting PDE system is developed that uses numerical integration along individual weight coordinates using Runge--Kutta methods. We provide an error analysis considering inexact initial solutions, perturbations of the right-hand sides, and numerical integration errors. We investigate the accuracy and computational efficiency of the tracing strategy on convex quadratic problems and WFG examples, where the latter demonstrate the applicability to problems with Pareto fronts consisting of convex and non-convex parts. Comparisons with repeated weighted sum scalarizations and a predictor--corrector method illustrate the computational benefits of the proposed strategy.

Optimization and Control.title: A New Computational Model for the Spin-Free Sum-of-Squares Energy Bounds of Electronic Hamiltonian
Optimization and Control.summary: Optimizing spin-free sum-of-squares (SOS) energy bounds for electronic Hamiltonians leads to semidefinite programs whose expanded size grows rapidly with the orbital dimension. We derive an exact reformulation of an established spin-free SOS model as a convex quadratic problem over a single symmetric matrix constrained between zero and the identity. Explicit recovery maps connect feasible quadratic-program iterates to certificates in the original SOS formulation, and identify the Frank--Wolfe gap with the separation between recovered primal and dual objectives. We implement the quadratic action through GPU-accelerated Coulomb contractions and solve the reformulated problem using a cached implementation of fully corrective Frank--Wolfe, referred to here as the dimension-reduced simplicial method (DRSM) that caches operator products and optimizes convex-combination weights in a small corrective quadratic program. Numerical experiments cover 65 FCIDUMP models, molecular geometries, and regular hydrogen rings, including original-coordinate recovery checks on nine instances and comparisons with FISTA and a boundary-point SDP solver. On eight H100 GPUs, a cold-start calculation for C$_{720}$ with 10,080 spatial orbitals reaches a freshly recomputed Frank--Wolfe gap of $8.82\times10^{-9}$ hartree in 5.02 hours. Full-space hydrogen-ring calculations reach 10,000 orbitals, with cyclic reduction providing further computational savings. These results show how exact reformulation, data structure exploitation and reuse of Coulomb actions make optimization of the selected large-scale SOS relaxation practical.
Optimization and Control.comment: 35 pages, 2 figures. Yuming Bao and Yancheng Wu contributed equally to this work and share first authorship

Optimization and Control.title: Policy Optimization in the Linear Quadratic Gaussian Problem: A Frequency Domain Perspective
Optimization and Control.summary: The Linear Quadratic Gaussian (LQG) problem is a classic and widely studied model in optimal control, providing a fundamental framework for designing controllers for linear systems subject to process and observation noises. In recent years, researchers have increasingly focused on directly parameterizing dynamic controllers and optimizing the LQG cost over the resulting parameterized set. However, this parameterization typically gives rise to a highly non-convex optimization landscape for the resulting parameterized LQG problem. To our knowledge, there is currently no general method for certifying the global optimality of candidate controller parameters in this setting. In this work, we address these gaps with the following contributions. First, we derive a necessary and sufficient condition for the global optimality of stationary points in a parameterized LQG problem. This condition reduces the verification of optimality to a test of the controllability and observability for a novel, specially constructed transfer function, yielding a precise and computationally tractable certificate. Furthermore, our condition provides a rigorous explanation for why traditional parameterizations can lead to suboptimal stationary points. Second, we elevate the controller parameter space from conventional finite-dimensional settings to the infinite-dimensional $\mathcal{RH}_\infty$ space and develop a gradient-based algorithm in this setting, for which we provide a theoretical analysis establishing global convergence. Finally, representative numerical experiments validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the practical viability of the proposed approach. Additionally, the appendix section explores a data-driven extension to the model-free setting, where we outline a parameter estimation scheme and demonstrate its practical viability through numerical simulation.
Optimization and Control.comment: This version corrects several typos and notational errors in both the derivations and the statements of theorems

Optimization and Control.title: From Worst-Case to Smoothed Complexity in Continuous Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: Worst-case complexity bounds often fail to reflect the practical performance of optimization algorithms, while average-case complexity heavily relies on the distribution of the input. In this work, we develop a smoothed-analysis framework for classical continuous optimization algorithms by studying their behaviour on random perturbations of arbitrary functions. Our main contribution is to apply methods suited for non-degenerate functions to perturbations of degenerate functions, thereby recovering the faster best-known rates for the non-degenerate class. We derive smoothed complexity guarantees for several standard methods, including (Accelerated) Gradient Descent, Conjugate Gradient, and Newton-type methods, under various settings including nonconvex ones, and show that these bounds can substantially improve upon their worst-case guarantees, bringing them closer to the practical behaviour of the respective methods.

Optimization and Control.title: Feedback Stabilization for Sampled Linear Systems with Control-linear Noise
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper, we consider linear stochastic systems with control-linear noise and periodically sampled measurements. We address the problem of feedback stabilization in the mean-square sense. The main contribution of the paper is to provide a necessary and sufficient condition for feedback stabilization. In particular, we relate feedback stabilizability of the stochastic system to the existence of a fixed point of a Riccati-type algebraic equation and, further, to the existence of a solution to an infinite-horizon optimal control problem.

Optimization and Control.title: Saturation on compact manifolds via Stone-Weierstrass type theorem, and forced nonlinear PDEs
Optimization and Control.summary: We consider polynomial nonlinear PDEs on compact manifolds with finite-dimensional forcing terms. We provide necessary and sufficient conditions under which the forcing, through the nonlinear dynamics, attains a dense subspace on manifolds with and without boundary. Our key argument is Nachbin's theorem, which is an analogue of the well-known Stone-Weierstrass theorem in spaces of differentiable functions. As applications, we prove small-time approximate controllability by additive finite-dimensional controls, topological irreducibility, and almost sure unboundedness of Sobolev norms.

Optimization and Control.title: Large Deviations Principle for Bures-Wasserstein Barycenters
Optimization and Control.summary: We prove the large deviations principle for empirical Bures-Wasserstein barycenters of independent, identically-distributed samples of covariance matrices and covariance operators. As an application, we explore some consequences of our results for the phenomenon of dimension-free concentration of measure for Bures-Wasserstein barycenters. Our theory reveals a novel notion of exponential tilting in the Bures-Wasserstein space, which, in analogy with Cramér's theorem in the Euclidean case, solves the relative entropy projection problem under a constraint on the barycenter. Notably, this method of proof is easy to adapt to other geometric settings of interest; with the same method, we obtain large deviations principles for empirical barycenters in Riemannian manifolds and the univariate Wasserstein space, and we obtain large deviations upper bounds for empirical barycenters in the general multivariate Wasserstein space. In fact, our results are the first known large deviations principles for Fréchet means in any non-linear metric space.

Optimization and Control.title: Regularized Extragradient Methods for Solving Equilibrium Problems on Hadamard Manifolds
Optimization and Control.summary: Employing two distinct types of regularization terms, we propose two regularized extragradient methods for solving equilibrium problems on Hadamard manifolds. The sequences generated by these extragradient algorithms converge to a solution of the equilibrium problem without requiring the Lipschitz continuity of the bifunction and without an upper bound on the regularization parameters. We establish convergence results for both algorithms under a monotonicity condition. When the bifunction is additionally strongly pseudomonotone, we derive global error bounds and establish $R$-linear convergence rates. Finally, we present numerical experiments to demonstrate the effectiveness of our methods.

Optimization and Control.title: On Federated Averaging with Partial Participation under a General Variance Condition
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper, we study the convergence of Federated Averaging (FedAvg) with partial participation under a general variance condition. In each communication round, the server samples $S$ of the $n$ clients uniformly at random without replacement. The stochastic gradients are assumed to satisfy the so-called ABC condition, which allows their variance to grow with the local objective gaps. For smooth nonconvex objectives, we establish a finite-time stationarity bound in terms of the heterogeneity measure $σ_f^\star:=f^\star-\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i^\star$ and the client sampling factor $I_S:=(n-S)/(n-1)$. Here, $f^\star$ and $f_i^\star$ denote the infima of the global average objective and client $i$'s local objective, respectively. The bound exhibits a linear speedup in the number of sampled clients $S$ and recovers the full-participation result when $S=n$. Under diminishing stepsizes, we further prove that the gradient norm converges to zero both in expectation and almost surely. Notably, compared with existing analyses of FedAvg with partial participation, our results require no additional data heterogeneity assumption such as bounded gradient dissimilarity (BGD), and the sampling-induced term in our bound is not amplified by the number of local updates at the leading order. The importance of removing the BGD assumption is illustrated by an example that is smooth and lower bounded but violates BGD, yet is covered by our analysis.

Optimization and Control.title: Fixed-time stabilization of systems with nilpotent matrices in the presence of large unknown delays
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper, we study state-feedback fixed-time stabilization of continuous-time perturbed linear systems with nilpotent matrices in the presence of unknown large constant input/measurement delays with known bounds. By using an additional artificial delay, we design a feedback that for a precisely known linear system with a nilpotent matrix drives the state to zero in fixed time (which is larger than the bound of the unknown delay) and achieves input-to-state stability with a large exponential decay rate in the presence of additive disturbances and small system matrix perturbations and nonlinearities. For perturbed single integrators, fixed-time stabilization is achieved in the case of fast-varying unknown measurement delays with known bounds. The results are extended to discrete-time systems. Numerical simulations illustrate the efficiency of the results.

Optimization and Control.title: A Strategic Freight Market Model for Liner Shipping: Pricing, Entry, and Endogenous Service Choice
Optimization and Control.summary: National freight transport models usually treat prices and service provision as exogenous. This paper models both as outcomes of strategic interaction among operators of scheduled, loop-based freight services. It compares oligopolistic competition, monopoly, Ramsey pricing with service-level or system-wide cost recovery, and welfare-maximising planning. Shippers across multiple segments choose between direct cyclic liner services and an outside option, using logit demand. Operators select from candidate port rotations, vessel classes and speeds, and set origin-destination prices subject to leg capacities. Under competition, each operator offers one service. Equilibrium requires that no operator can profitably enter, exit or replace its service after prices re-equilibrate. The solution method computes global pricing best responses and tests all unilateral service deviations, pruning only those excluded by an analytical profit bound. All regimes use the same demand and cost structure. In a synthetic Baltic-North Sea application, multinomial logit competition sustains more overlapping services and lower prices than monopoly. System-wide Ramsey pricing captures most of the planner's welfare gain without a deficit. Fuel-price and demand shocks affect competitive prices through changes in the service set. When maritime services are close substitutes, entrants avoid overlapping markets and competition can reproduce monopoly outcomes. The results illustrate mechanisms rather than forecast actual markets, showing how market organisation shapes service provision, prices, modal shares and welfare.

Optimization and Control.title: A definition of the background state of the atmosphere using optimal transport
Optimization and Control.summary: The dynamics of atmospheric disturbances are often described in terms of displacements of air parcels relative to their locations in a notional background state. Modified Lagrangian Mean (MLM) states have been proposed by M.E.McIntyre using the Lagrangian conserved variables potential vorticity and potential temperature to label air masses in the instantaneous 3-D atmospheric state, and then rearranging air masses sandwiched between potential vorticity contours in potential temperature layers so that they are zonally symmetric. Methven and Berrisford used conservation of Kelvin's circulation to define the distribution of MLM state mass in zonal angular momentum ($z$) and potential temperature ($θ$) coordinates given 3-D global data. We prove that for any such mass distribution in $(z, θ)$ there exists a mapping to a unique mass distribution in geophysical coordinates (latitude and pressure) which minimises energy and completely defines the MLM state in a single hemisphere. Since the state is an energy minimum, it is suitable for quantification of finite amplitude disturbances and examining atmospheric instability. This state is obtained by solving a free surface problem, which we frame as the minimisation of an optimal transport cost over a class of source measures. The solution consists of a source measure, encoding surface pressure, and an optimal transport map, connecting the distribution of mass in geophysical coordinates to the known distribution of mass in $(z, θ)$. We show that this problem reduces to an optimal transport problem with a known source measure, which has a numerically feasible discretisation, and we present a numerical solution using atmospheric reanalysis data. Additionally, our results hold for a large class of cost functions, and generalise analogous results on free surface variants of the semi-geostrophic equations.

Optimization and Control.title: Davenport Constants of High-Dimensional Integer Sets
Optimization and Control.summary: The Davenport constant of a finite set of integer vectors is the maximum length of an irreducible zero-sum sequence over that set. For nonempty sets closed under negation, it equals the largest $\ell_1$-norm of a Graver basis element of the matrix formed by those vectors. We study extremal and average-case versions in growing dimension, with applications to integer programming. For integer cubes $[-R,R]^d \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ and the sign cube $\{-1,1\}^d$, totally unimodular encodings improve on the upper bounds from direct circuit decomposition, while random perturbations of Hadamard matrices give new lower bounds. A key ingredient is a uniform affine Bernoulli variant of Nguyen and Wood's surjectivity theorem. In every sufficiently large dimension the sign-cube lower bound is $d^{d/2}2^{-d-o(d)}$, and the integer-cube lower bound is $R^d d^{d/2}2^{-o(d)}$ uniformly for polynomially bounded integer radii. For random sign-cube sequences of even length conditioned on summing to zero, we prove a sharp threshold from irreducibility to reducibility at $d\log d/\log 4$, far below the extremal scale. For fixed $p$ and $R$, we determine exact exponential rates for lattice $\ell_p$-balls when $p=1$, $R\geq3$, or $2\leq p<\infty$, $\lfloor R^p\rfloor\geq3$. For each fixed integer $k\geq3$, we determine the exponential rate of the worst-case $\ell_1$-distance from an optimal LP vertex to the nearest integer optimum in standard-form programs with ternary matrices having at most $k$ nonzero entries per column.

Optimization and Control.title: Adaptive Reparametrized Time for Score-Based Diffusion Sampling
Optimization and Control.summary: We study timestep allocation for score-based diffusion sampling, where a learned reverse-time dynamics is discretized on a finite grid. Uniform and hand-crafted schedules are standard choices, but they rely on fixed prescriptions and can therefore be suboptimal. To address this limitation, we propose Adaptive Reparameterized Time (ART), a continuous-time control formulation that learns a time change by treating the speed of the sampling clock as the control, so that a uniform grid on the learned clock induces adaptive timesteps in the original diffusion time. Based on a leading-order Euler error surrogate, ART provides a principled objective for allocating timesteps along the sampling trajectory. To solve this deterministic control problem, we introduce ART-RL, an auxiliary randomized formulation with Gaussian policies that turns schedule learning into a continuous-time reinforcement learning problem. We prove that the randomized ART-RL formulation is equivalent to ART at the optimizer level, in the sense that its optimal Gaussian policy recovers the optimal ART time-warping rate through its mean. We further establish policy evaluation and policy improvement characterizations and derive trajectory-based moment identities that yield implementable actor--critic updates for learning the schedule. Across experiments ranging from controlled low-dimensional settings to image generation, ART-RL can be plugged into existing diffusion samplers by changing only the timestep grid, consistently improving sample quality over strong baseline schedules at matched budgets while leaving the rest of the sampling pipeline unchanged. The learned schedules also exhibit broad generalization, transferring without retraining across sampling budgets, datasets, solvers, pipelines, and representation spaces.
Optimization and Control.comment: 37 pages, 14 figures, 8 tables. Accepted for publication in the Journal of Machine Learning Research (JMLR)

Optimization and Control.title: Numerical investigation of a MST conjecture for random Haar matrices
Optimization and Control.summary: The state-to-state control time of finite-dimensional conservative bilinear quantum systems is bounded by the weight of minimum spanning trees (MST) derived from the drift matrices. For a spectrum scaling as k^3/2 , determining whether the control time vanishes as the dimension d tends to infinity remains an open problem due to the global correlations imposed by the Haar measure. We formulate two conjectures regarding the asymptotic behavior of the MST weight\,: a general decay to zero, and a scaling in 1/sqrt(ln d) derived from an independent Gaussian surrogate model. Numerical investigations up to dimension d = 18101 validate the general decay, confirm that the exact Haar model and the independent surrogate are statistically indistinguishable in mean at all tested dimensions, and extract the thermodynamic limit $α$ = 10/3, which both models approach from below once the scaling variable 1/ ln d is adopted.

Optimization and Control.title: Discrete-Time Stochastic Control Beyond i.i.d. Noise
Optimization and Control.summary: We study discrete-time stochastic control problems where the noise driving the state dynamics is a stationary infinite-order chain rather than an i.i.d. sequence. We formulate the problem as a controlled Markov process by enlarging the state space to include the posterior distribution of the noise given the state-action history. Assuming that the sensitivity of the noise transition kernel to past noise values decays exponentially, we show that the expected total variation distance between the full-history and finite-memory noise filters decays at rate $\sqrt{N}ρ^{\sqrt{N}}$. We use this result to construct finite-memory control models and establish explicit near-optimality bounds for their policies. Finally, under suitable ergodicity conditions, we show that Q-learning converges to the optimal solution of the approximate model, so the same performance bounds apply to the learned policies.

Optimization and Control.title: Decay rates for monotone operator flows in the space of probability measures
Optimization and Control.summary: Motivated by the mean-field dynamics of large populations of interacting agents, we study the long-time behavior of flows driven by monotone demicontinuous operators on the Wasserstein space. For cocoercive operators, we prove that the flow converges to a zero of the operator and that the operator residual and the metric speed decay as $o(t^{-1/2})$, so that the population comes to rest (the agents asymptotically stop moving). We also consider Tikhonov regularized flows of merely monotone demicontinuous operators and show that the operator residual and the metric speed tend to zero, with rate $O(1/t)$ when the Tikhonov parameter is $α/t$ with $α\geq 1$, and that the trajectory converges to the zero of minimal second moment, which is a Dirac mass, so that the agents reach consensus (all agents reach the same point). Finally, we study a discrete analogue for nonexpansive operators and show that the generated sequence converges to the fixed point closest to a reference Dirac mass; this fixed point is again a Dirac mass, so that consensus is also reached under this scheme. The main arguments rely on a specially tailored superposition principle, which represents the flow as a curve in a fixed Hilbert space of random trajectories, where the crucial estimates are derived.

Optimization and Control.title: Vanishing Control Times for Single-Input Bilinear Quantum Systems under Rapid Drift Spectral Growth
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper investigates the asymptotic behavior, as the Hilbert space dimension tends to infinity, of the state-to-state control time of single-input bilinear quantum systems whose control operator is drawn from an isotropic (unitarily invariant) random ensemble. Relying on deterministic graph-theoretic bounds, namely star cuts of the interaction graph for the lower bound and spanning trees for the upper bound, and on integration over the Haar measure, we derive high-probability lower and upper bounds on the control time, expressed in terms of the empirical spectral variance and of the relative concentration of the drift spectrum. Whenever the spectrum grows fast enough (for instance polynomially with an exponent larger than 3/2, geometrically, or super-exponentially), the upper bound vanishes and the control time tends to zero in probability: in these cases, enlarging the Hilbert space constructively speeds up control.

Optimization and Control.title: A Silverman-Meadows-type criterion for the null controllability of time-dependent coupled heat equations with non-diagonalizable diffusion matrices
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper is devoted to a uniform spectral Silverman-Meadows rank condition for the nullcontrollability of coupled systems of heat equations with time-dependent diffusion, coupling and control matrices. The proof relies on an adaptation of the Lebeau-Robbiano strategy combined with uniform finite-dimensional observability estimates associated with each Laplace eigenmode.

Optimization and Control.title: Predictive Neuromorphic Control of a Scanning Mirror System: An Event-Centric Framework
Optimization and Control.summary: Organizing control around events can reduce sensing and actuation demands while directly linking control decisions to the occurrence and timing of desired system behaviors. This paper proposes a novel event-centric model predictive control (MPC) framework that unifies event sensing, event prediction, and event regulation. Events define the feedback information, prediction horizon, and event-timing objectives, placing them at the center of predictive control design. The framework is developed for a scanning mirror system equipped with a baseline neuromorphic controller composed of spiking neurons that supports sparse actuation. The control objective is to achieve prescribed zero-crossing times and a desired scanning range while minimizing the mechanical energy transferred between the actuator and the mirror. A sampling-based algorithm is presented to obtain suboptimal solutions of the event-centric MPC optimization problem without requiring an explicit event-to-event prediction model. By grounding predictive optimization in events, the proposed framework opens a new direction for MPC design and its integration with neuromorphic control.
Optimization and Control.comment: 8 pages, submitted to ECC27, this work is the first, foundational work that proposes Event-Centric Model Predictive Control (EC-MPC), a framework that combines model predictive control and neuromorphic control. Philosophy: predicting events but not trajectories; regulation without calibration

Optimization and Control.title: Sharp Proximity Bounds for Integer Programs with Few Rows
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the proximity between an optimal vertex of a standard form linear program with constraint matrix $A\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n}$ and an optimal integer solution. When $m = 2$, we prove the sharp infinity-norm bound $Δ-1$, where $Δ$ is the largest absolute maximal minor of $A$. When $m = 1$, we express the difference between an optimal LP vertex and an optimal integer solution as a nonnegative combination of certain generators in the kernel of $A$ with a bounded coefficient sum. This implies sharp proximity bounds for all norms when $m=1$. Combining this representation with its known counterpart for Hilbert bases due to Sissokho, we develop techniques that transfer results from $m=1$ to $m=2$. Along the way, for $m=2$, we prove that such a representation exists for an extended Gomory group relaxation and obtain the sharp infinity-norm bound $Δ$ for Graver basis elements. We also present a new short proof of Sissokho's result and lower bounds on the proximity for all $m$ and $Δ$.

Optimization and Control.title: Mixed-integer dual network problems are solvable in strongly polynomial time
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper we show that mixed-integer linear programming is solvable in strongly polynomial time if the constraint matrix is totally unimodular with at most two nonzero entries in every row. This is done by reducing the problem to an instance of minimization of an $L$-convex function.

Optimization and Control.title: Forecast Projection and Decision Regret: Theory and Evidence from Battery Arbitrage
Optimization and Control.summary: Decision-focused learning trains forecasts for the decisions they lead to, but forecasts are often projected onto known bounds before use. We study the resulting mismatch in battery arbitrage. When a battery starts and ends the day at the same charge level, a common shift in prices affects its schedule only through round-trip losses. As a result, decision-focused losses identify the forecast level only weakly. For the SPO+ and perturbed Fenchel-Young losses, we characterize the preferred level by a throughput-matching condition. Projecting forecasts onto a price cap can then remove profitable spreads and increase regret, even as prediction error falls. We give bounds on the change in regret, a dual-threshold condition under which a raw-optimal schedule remains optimal after clipping, and a general version of the mechanism for other problems with a conservation constraint. On 1,158 holdout days of the Indian day-ahead market, an equal-weight average of three statistical forecasts outperforms the five decision-focused variants tested. On 53 later days, with 62% of price blocks at the cap, no variant outperforms the regression or the equal-weight average, although most differences from the average are not significant. The results suggest that forecast post-processing should be treated as part of the predict-then-optimize pipeline.
Optimization and Control.comment: 38 pages, 14 tables, 4 figures. Includes an electronic companion (Sections EC.1 to EC.5)

Optimization and Control.title: Safe and Scalable Minimax Adaptive Control of Positive Systems
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper studies minimax adaptive control of positive linear systems with fixed unknown dynamics and nonnegative disturbances. We reformulate the problem by compressing the historical data into a vector and a positivity-induced consistency set containing the models compatible with the observations. Together with the physical state, these quantities form a sufficient information state and yield an exact reformulation as a standard minimax dynamic game. We allow the admissible input set to adapt to the current consistency set, ensuring positivity for every remaining feasible model. As inconsistent models are eliminated, the input set can expand, allowing less cautious control actions. For finite model sets, we derive an explicit solution to the Bellman inequality and construct a safe and stabilizing certainty-equivalence controller with robustness guarantees. The framework also accommodates structured classes of continuum model uncertainty whose consistency sets admit fixed, finite-dimensional representations, enabling scalable information-state updates.

Optimization and Control.title: Distributionally Robust Indirect-Feedback Stochastic MPC with Gelbrich Ambiguity Sets
Optimization and Control.summary: Stochastic model predictive control uses disturbance statistics to set safety margins. Errors in these statistics can invalidate the safety guarantees. This paper therefore describes the uncertainty in the disturbance mean and covariance by a prescribed Gelbrich ambiguity set. This contains distributions of any shape whose moments are close in the Gelbrich distance to the nominal values, including distributions with unbounded support. For linear time-invariant systems with additive disturbances, we build on the indirect feedback paradigm, propagate this moment uncertainty along the error dynamics, and obtain a closed-form constraint tightening that is computed offline. Robustness enters as a single additive term that grows with the size of the ambiguity set, so the online problem remains a quadratic program. Recursive feasibility and closed-loop satisfaction of conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) constraints hold for every disturbance distribution in the set. We illustrate the method on a linearized planar quadrotor.
Optimization and Control.comment: 6 pages, 2 figures, 1 table. Submitted to the 2027 European Control Conference (ECC)

Optimization and Control.title: Optimization-Based Path Planning for Industrial Manipulators: Experimental Validation in Additive Manufacturing
Optimization and Control.summary: Robotic additive manufacturing requires joint paths that reconcile robot feasibility with process-specific geometry. We develop an offline optimization-based path planner that combines joint-path regularity and self-collision penalties with process costs and constraints, so that a new process enters through its own reference, residuals, and tolerances. Full-path and boundary-coupled chunked optimization handle references of different lengths. Iterative Weight Tuning (IWT) determines the cost weights from the gaps between Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and their targets. In carbon-fiber winding and robotic 3D printing, the planned paths meet the geometric tolerances and all KPI targets, and both paths are executed on a UR10e, without extrusion for printing, with joint-level tracking recorded during execution.
Optimization and Control.comment: Submitted for the review in ECC 2027

Optimization and Control.title: The parental parsimony problem on binary, tree-child phylogenetic networks
Optimization and Control.summary: Phylogenetic reconstruction is one of the major challenges in computational biology. Among existing reconstruction methods for phylogenetic networks, an important subtask emerges in extending a leaf-labelling on a phylogenetic network to determine a most parsimonious tree inside the network. There exist different variants of this subtask depending on the biological model assumptions for which distinct evolutionary phenomena are captured by the network. In this article we assume that next to hybridization or recombination events, also allopolyploidy or incomplete lineage sorting are present. Then, finding the most parsimonious tree inside the network is called the parental parsimony score problem (PPS), a NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem. We provide the first constant-factor approximation for the PPS on arbitrary but fixed leaf labels and a class of networks on which the PPS remains NP-hard, namely binary, semi-simplex, tree-child phylogenetic networks. Furthermore, we introduce a novel exact solution algorithm for the PPS on binary, tree-child phylogenetic networks and analyze its performance on simulated data.

Optimization and Control.title: On the Spectral Estimation of VARMA Processes
Optimization and Control.summary: We consider the problem of estimating the power spectral density of a Vector-valued Autoregressive Moving-Average (VARMA) process. A well-established approach to accomplishing this task consists of formulating a moment problem that selects the spectral density maximizing an entropy-like index while matching certain moments of the underlying process. However, existing methods assume that the moving-average (MA) component is either fixed or scalar, thereby reducing the class of ARMA models over which the optimal spectral density is sought. In this paper, we propose a new moment problem, based on the notion of transportation entropy, for learning the spectral density of a VARMA process without fixing the MA component or restricting it to be scalar.
Optimization and Control.comment: 12 pages, 2 figures with the IEEE Transactions template

Optimization and Control.title: Delay-Certified Readiness Barriers for Overactuated Multirotor Allocation Without Lipschitz Constants
Optimization and Control.summary: Overactuated multirotors can produce the same wrench with many rotor-speed combinations, some of which leave the vehicle unable to change its wrench quickly, e.g., to reject a gust. Readiness barriers keep this ability, the readiness, above a floor, but only in continuous time; with sampled commands and varying speed-controller delays, the available robustness bound covers less than one millisecond. We remove this limit by exploiting the structure of the problem: each rotor responds monotonically and in closed form to its own torque, so the speeds reachable under uncertain switching times lie in a cheaply computed box, and the lowest readiness over that box sits at a corner known in advance.
