Procedures in this third class seek to optimally balance two quantities: the cost of learning about the performance of each alternative and the quality of the alternative ultimately selected on the basis of that learning. Fixed-precision and fixed-budget procedures tend to optimize one of these quantities while constraining the other. We clarify these differences and show why they matter. We then present new frequentist R&S procedures in this third category, including both two-stage procedures and a sequential heuristic, assuming Gaussian observations with either known or unknown variances. We find that EoS is not a question of Bayesian versus frequentist analysis, asymptotic versus finite-sample analysis, finite-stage versus fully sequential procedures, or comparing one mean with a standard versus comparing multiple alternatives. We identify opportunities for further R&S research.

Methodology.title: Bayesian Multinomial Logistic Normal Additive Regression for Microbiome Data Analysis
Methodology.summary:
Longitudinal microbiome studies often seek to separate background temporal variation from nonlinear perturbation-associated dynamics while accounting for the count-compositional nature of sequencing data. We introduce \textit{MultiAddGPs}, a semi-parametric Bayesian multinomial logistic-normal framework that combines linear effects with additive Gaussian process components. We first prove that MultiAddGPs remain within the Marginally Latent Matrix-T Process class (MLTP) and derive the collapsed and uncollapsed representations needed for scalable inference with the Collapse--Uncollapse (CU) sampler. We then develop a back-sampling procedure for efficient posterior inference on the individual additive components. We further develop approximate maximum marginal likelihood and penalized maximum marginal likelihood procedures for hyperparameter estimation in this broader class of models. In simulations, MultiAddGPs provides accurate posterior inference and calibrated uncertainty while scaling more effectively than existing GP-based additive alternatives. Applications to two longitudinal microbiome studies demonstrate how the model separates background temporal variation from intervention-associated dynamics, including travel-associated perturbations in a human gut time series and starvation effects
  in an artificial gut system. Our methods are implemented in the \textit{fido} package on CRAN.

Methodology.title: Regression Modeling for the Bloc Basu Bivariate Exponential Distribution: Marginal and Conditional Means
Methodology.summary: The bivariate absolutely continuous exponential distribution introduced by \citet{block1974continuous} provides a model for dependent lifetimes in reliability and survival analysis. Its marginal means depend jointly and nonlinearly on the rate parameters, which complicates regression modeling and the interpretation of covariate effects on these means. In this paper, we develop two regression approaches based on a region-wise multivariate exponential-family representation. In the full-distribution approach, link functions relate the cumulant derivatives in a fixed reference region to linear predictors. These derivatives do not directly equal the marginal means, which are instead probability-weighted combinations of the regional derivatives. This relationship allows covariate effects on the marginal means to be examined. Likelihood derivatives are obtained through the chain rule, and the regression coefficients are estimated by maximum likelihood. The rate parameter estimates are then recovered through the inverse link functions and an explicit inverse mapping, with the admissible solution selected to ensure positive rates. As an alternative, we propose regression models based on the normalized conditional distribution within each region. In this setting, the cumulant derivatives coincide with the conditional means, allowing covariates to be linked directly to these means. Both approaches are evaluated through a simulation study.

Methodology.title: High-Dimensional Nonsparse Regression under Covariate Shift via Importance-Weighted Partial Least Squares
Methodology.summary: This paper studies high-dimensional nonsparse regression when the data exhibit both strong predictor dependence and covariate shift. Many existing regression methods struggle with highly correlated predictors, while covariate shift can make components learned from source data less effective for target-domain prediction. To address these joint challenges, we develop an importance-weighted partial least squares (IWPLS) method that reweights source observations to reflect the target covariate distribution and extracts response-relevant components for coefficient estimation. The resulting estimator depends on weighted sample covariances, which generally lack the usual Wishart structure even when the target-domain covariates are Gaussian. We therefore combine a perturbation analysis of weighted PLS moments with an influence-function decomposition to establish consistency for the one- and multi-component estimators and asymptotic normality for the one-component estimator. Simulation studies and real-data analyses show that IWPLS outperforms the benchmark methods considered.

Methodology.title: Accuracy of Uniform Inference on Fine Grid Points
Methodology.summary: Uniform confidence bands are widely used to quantify uncertainty about unknown functions in nonparametric inference. Although various methods, including the multiplier bootstrap, have been developed and theoretically justified, practical implementations typically replace the supremum over a continuum by the maximum over a finite evaluation grid. This paper investigates how this discretization affects coverage accuracy and how fine the evaluation grid must be to ensure valid uniform inference. We first illustrate through simulations of a kernel-based nonparametric estimator that coarse grids can substantially reduce uniform coverage. Surprisingly, increasing the sample size can worsen coverage on a fixed coarse grid, even as the remaining approximation error on the grid decreases. We then derive general upper bounds on the coverage probability and coverage error of uniform confidence bands based on finite-grid multiplier-bootstrap critical values, separating discretization error from the remaining approximation errors. In particular, the general coverage error bound identifies the constant in the discretization term explicitly. For local empirical processes arising from kernel smoothing, we establish primitive conditions under which coverage converges to zero even when the number of grid points diverges, and conditions ensuring asymptotically nominal coverage. We further develop two implementable grid selection rules for a user-chosen discretization tolerance. Gaussian Monte Carlo experiments show that the proposed rules select grid sizes close to those required by the Monte Carlo benchmark.

Methodology.title: Knowing When to Intervene: Causal Evaluation of AI Agents
Methodology.summary: Current evaluations of agentic AI systems primarily rely on benchmarks. However, the static nature of benchmarks makes them uninformative about the value of auditing interventions at deployment time. For reliable deployment, we often need to determine within an agent's trajectory whether or not to intervene, e.g., by verifying the agent's current output or steering it toward different behavior, using either human review or more costly models or time-consuming agentic supervision. The value of such interventions is fundamentally a causal inference question, asking whether the causal effect of such an intervention is beneficial for the final outcome. Estimating this causal effect is particularly challenging due to the dynamic nature of the problem: the impact of an intervention depends on the current context and environment, as well as the agent's future behavior. We develop the first methodologically grounded framework for evaluating the causal effects of randomized interventions within agent trajectories. By leveraging a relatively small dataset of agent trajectories collected under randomized interventions such as verification or screening, we can estimate the dynamic causal effect of a rich class of (contextual) intervention policies. The structural parameters that we estimate can also be used to construct safety leaderboards that capture the risk of various agentic actions, which can be used by practitioners for audit prioritization. Applying our methods to tau-bench Retail, ToolSandbox, and ImpossibleBench, we find that intervention effects vary substantially across agent actions and states. More broadly, our work suggests a rich research agenda at the intersection of causal inference and agentic evaluation, which we believe is essential for the reliable and safe deployment of AI agents in the real world.

Methodology.title: Orthographic depth at two scales, with English also matched for lexicon size
Methodology.summary: A reader can struggle to read in only one of their languages, and one proposed reason is how predictably spelling maps to sound. We measure that predictability as conditional entropy, the pronunciation uncertainty left once the spelling is seen, at two grain sizes (unit sizes): the alignment unit, an aligned spelling-sound chunk, and the syllable, bounded in the pronunciation. We analyse word lists in twelve alphabetic orthographies and report five in full, with English pronunciations from a dictionary and the rest from the synthesizer eSpeak-ng, length marks removed. Among the five, English has the most uncertainty and Finnish the least at both grains. Across all twelve, Portuguese and Danish exceed English per alignment unit, and German and Italian order differently by grain and transcription. These orders hold when English is transcribed by eSpeak-ng with u allowed to spell /j/ plus a vowel. Uncertainty per unit has no shared direction as units grow: it falls in Spanish and, less securely, German, is level in Finnish, depends on transcription in Italian and on the word list in English, and rises in Norwegian and Swedish. Summed uncertainty per word falls in all twelve, but that score is handed the pronunciation's boundaries and mixes context with in-sample memorisation, so it is no evidence of what a reader computes. An exact identity states when discarded spelling boundaries could reverse that fall. A uniform 20,000-word English sample holds 35% of the dictionary's syllable spellings and has syllable entropy 0.098 bits lower, so lexicons must be matched in size. In an exploratory check over eleven languages, syllable-scale entropy tracked first-year reading accuracy (rho = -0.74, falling to -0.25 if English is given the lowest entropy instead), without separating the syllable scale from the alignment unit. These estimates describe sampled writing systems, not readers.
Methodology.comment: 38 pages, 5 figures. Spelling-to-sound entropy as a measure of orthographic depth for cross-language reading research; exploratory check against Grade 1 reading accuracy in Section 3.5. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/A9T3C

Methodology.title: Cross-Spectral Analysis of Bivariate Graph Signals
Methodology.summary: With the advancements in technology and monitoring tools, we often encounter multivariate graph signals, which can be seen as the realizations of multivariate graph processes, and revealing the relationship between their constituent quantities is one of the important problems. To address this issue, we propose a cross-spectral analysis tool for bivariate graph signals. The main goal of this study is to extend the scope of spectral analysis of graph signals to multivariate graph signals. In this study, we define joint weak stationarity graph processes and introduce graph cross-spectral density and coherence for multivariate graph processes. We propose several estimators for the cross-spectral density and investigate the theoretical properties of the proposed estimators. Furthermore, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed estimators through numerical experiments, including simulation studies and a real data application. Finally, as an interesting extension, we discuss robust spectral analysis of graph signals in the presence of outliers.

Methodology.title: A Geometric Perspective for Marginal R2: Estimation and Inference in Generalized Linear Mixed Models
Methodology.summary: Generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs) are widely used across scientific disciplines, yet quantifying response variation explained by auxiliary information remains challenging for non-Gaussian outcomes and hierarchical dependence. Existing $R^2$ measures provide useful summaries, but their variance-based constructions are not generally linked to a common geometric interpretation, a fixed-design marginal estimand, and corresponding statistical inference. We propose marginal quasi-$R^2$ through two distinct operations. First, marginalization integrates over latent random effects, retaining their uncertainty in the marginal response moments and specifying the model for explanatory assessment. Second, a Quasi-GLM formulation supplies a local working information metric under which orthogonal projection yields an Pythagorean decomposition of explained and unexplained variation. We define a fixed-design population estimand, establish consistency and asymptotic normality of its estimator, and derive cluster-robust sandwich standard errors and confidence intervals under stated regularity conditions. Simulations assess estimation accuracy and interval coverage across response families and random-effects structures. Two ecological applications illustrate the importance of reporting estimation uncertainty alongside marginal quasi-$R^2$. The method is implemented in the R package quasiR2.

Methodology.title: Lost in the Bins: Treatment Effects with Discretized Covariates
Methodology.summary: Mean independence restrictions are widely used to identify average treatment effects, but the covariates used to formulate these restrictions are often observed or used in coarsened form. This paper shows that mean independence conditional on a finely measured covariate need not hold after the covariate is replaced by a coarsened version. Coarsening can therefore change the identifying content of the comparison rather than only the precision of estimation. I characterize the resulting coarsening bias for the ATT and ATE. For the ATT, the bias is driven by within-cell composition in untreated potential outcomes. For the ATE, an additional treatment effect heterogeneity term appears. I then introduce $c$-mean dependence, a nonparametric relaxation of exact mean independence at the coarsened level, and derive sharp bounds for average treatment effects. The parameter $c$ determines how far comparisons may extend across neighboring values of the coarsened covariate. I propose sample analogue estimators and bootstrap inference procedures for the resulting bound functions. In an application to voluntary military service using data from Angrist (1998), positive effects on early earnings, which primarily reflect military pay, hold even under the weakest form of $c$-mean dependence, whereas the evidence on later effects on civilian earnings is inconclusive once mean independence is relaxed.

Methodology.title: Semiparametric Inference for Marginal Win Odds with Censored Time-to-Event Outcomes
Methodology.summary: Win statistics provide clinically interpretable measures for comparing treatment groups with prioritized composite outcomes, but efficient covariate-adjustment methods for win statistics with right censored time-to-event outcomes remain limited. We develop a semiparametric framework for marginal win probability and win odds with prioritized time-to-event outcomes, including semi-competing risks, while also accommodating scalar survival outcomes as a special case. The estimand compares independent draws from the marginal distributions of the potential outcomes under treatment and control, which preserves a marginal causal interpretation. We derive the efficient influence function under conditional independent censoring, allowing censoring to depend on baseline covariates and predictable event history. The resulting cross-fitted one-step estimator incorporates covariate adjustment and censoring martingale augmentation, allows flexible estimation of nuisance parameters, and attains the semiparametric efficiency bound under suitable conditions on consistency and convergence rate of nuisance parameters. Simulation studies show that the estimator has small bias, accurate standard error estimation and confidence interval coverage, and substantial efficiency gain relative to the inverse-probability-of-censoring weighted (IPCW) estimator. An application to a randomized breast cancer trial comparing tamoxifen combined with radiotherapy against tamoxifen alone demonstrates improved precision, with an approximately 25\% reduction in estimated variance at five years.

Methodology.title: Identification of Rational Inattention-Additive Random Utility Models
Methodology.summary: This paper introduces a novel class of econometric models, called Rational Inattention-Additive Random Utility Models. It is based on the discrete choice rational inattention model of Matvejka and McKay (2015) with additive unobserved heterogeneity incorporated. We show that some of the systematic components of the primitives of the model are nonparametrically identified even if the distributions of unobserved variables and the prior of decision makers are both unknown to the Econometrician. If additional information about the prior is known to the Econometrician, even stronger identification results become available.

Methodology.title: Don't Match the Noise: Distribution Matching under Unknown Measurement Error with an Audit Sample
Methodology.summary: Real-world machine learning systems often operate on imperfect measurements: sensors are noisy, annotations are produced by non-experts, and scientific observations are often indirect. In these settings, classic distribution comparison tools such as maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) can be systematically biased, matching artifacts of the measurement process rather than the underlying mechanisms of interest. We study a practical regime in which noisy observations are abundant, but only a small audited subset contains ground-truth measurements. We propose measurement-error-corrected MMD (MEC-MMD), an audit-based estimator that debiases kernel evaluations without requiring a noise model. MEC-MMD is exactly unbiased for the oracle MMD under simple random auditing, admits an explicit variance decomposition, and is consistent for the population MMD, achieving the standard $O_p(N^{-1/2})$ rate when the audit size scales with the dataset. We demonstrate the utility of distributional matching with MEC-MMD loss for both parameter estimation and unsupervised applications, showing that MEC-MMD consistently outperforms MMD and alternative methods. These results provide a principled foundation for robust distribution comparison, simulation-based inference, and learning in noisy real-world machine learning pipelines.

Methodology.title: Asymptotic Consistency of a Weighted Nadaraya-Watson Estimator Driven by Fractional Brownian Motion at Random Times
Methodology.summary: Nonparametric regression conventionally assumes equispaced observations, a premise often violated by empirical data with irregular sampling and long-memory noise. This study establishes the asymptotic mean square ($L^2$) consistency of a weighted Nadaraya-Watson (wN-W) estimator for stochastic processes sampled at random times and perturbed by fractional Brownian motion (fBm). Leveraging the occupation time formula and Fernique's Theorem, we derive exact parametric restrictions on bandwidth and sampling rates ensuring convergence. We validate these theoretical findings via extensive simulations evaluating the mean squared error under varying noise persistence. Crucially, we explicitly benchmark the performance of the estimator under random sampling times against classical deterministic grids, while assessing the relative efficiency of quartic versus Gaussian kernels. Finally, we introduce an interactive Shiny application to dynamically visualize the admissible parameter space, and we empirically validate our theoretical framework by applying the estimator to the Vostok ice core paleoclimatological dataset. This real-world application demonstrates the practical capacity of the methodology to extract macroscopic trends while robustly avoiding severe overfitting under random sampling times.\

Methodology.title: Martingale posteriors for flexible regression via recursive least squares
Methodology.summary: Predictive Bayes quantifies uncertainty by specifying a sequence of one-step-ahead predictive distributions, inducing a martingale posterior without an explicit prior. Existing parametric constructions rely on stochastic-gradient updates and have seen limited development for flexible regression. We propose a predictive Bayes framework based on recursive least squares, whose martingale posterior has an explicit representation: given future covariates, it is the law of the posterior mean plus a weighted series of independent draws from the standardized predictive distribution. The posterior mean is a penalized least squares estimator, available in closed form and invariant to data ordering, whereas the predictive distribution, for example heavy tailed, is chosen separately without changing the estimator or algorithm. We derive the exact posterior variance under a known design and an asymptotically Gaussian approximation, and obtain the martingale posterior in closed form for Gaussian predictive distributions. Posterior draws are independent by construction, with a known truncation error, and require no Markov chain Monte Carlo. The construction extends to additive, mixed and Gaussian process models. In simulations and an analysis of NHANES triglyceride data, the method attains accuracy comparable to that of a fully Bayesian model with the same response distribution at a fraction of its computational cost.

Methodology.title: Orthogonal Sparse Subgraph Alignment for Structure-Function Coupling in Brain Networks
Methodology.summary: Characterizing the relationship between brain anatomical wiring and functional coordination remains a fundamental challenge in computational neuroscience. This difficulty primarily arises because structure-function coupling in the human brain is spatially heterogeneous, often localized to subnetworks, and inherently difficult to align across disparate representational modalities. We introduce Orthogonal Sparse Subgraph Alignment (OSSA), a principled and interpretable framework designed to identify compact structural cliques that exhibit maximal concordance with functional connectivity (FC) across subjects. Within each FC-derived community, OSSA optimizes an alignment objective over an orthogonal transformation, which absorbs coordinate mismatch between the two connectivity modalities, and a sparse node-selection vector, which identifies the induced structural connectivity (SC) subgraph. Furthermore, for canonical OSSA within a fixed population community, we establish local statistical guarantees under the required assumptions. With high probability, an empirical local maximizer exists in a specified neighborhood of the population target, and every local maximizer in that neighborhood exactly recovers the active support and satisfies a nonasymptotic error bound for the aligned functional projector. Extensive empirical evaluations on simulated data, alongside analyses of the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) baseline and longitudinal cohorts, demonstrate that OSSA successfully recovers aligned structural cliques under latent cross-modal rotations. Ultimately, the proposed methodology significantly improves out-of-sample SC-FC alignment over size-matched baselines and identifies compact structural supports with longitudinal consistency in node selection, while multi-support diagnostics suggest a dominant aligned core within the estimated FC communities.
Methodology.comment: 47 pages, 13 figures. Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. Project page: https://rampageoppa.github.io/projects/ossa/

Methodology.title: Hypothesis testing for estimable parameters with missing data: available cases or complete cases?
Methodology.summary: Whether to base inferences on available-case (AC) or complete-case (CC) estimators is a long-standing practical dilemma when data are missing. This issue has been investigated for point estimation in specific problems, but hypothesis testing has received comparatively little attention. The tools needed to address this problem are developed in a fully nonparametric framework for hypotheses concerning parameters that can be estimated through functions of vectors of $U$-statistics, under a MCAR missingness mechanism. The joint asymptotic normality of the AC estimators is established, permitting availability probabilities to vary with the sample size. The limiting covariance matrix factorizes into the complete-data covariance matrix and a matrix determined solely by the availability pattern, with both components admitting consistent estimators. This fact enables the construction of a Wald-type test statistic. The CC approach arises as a special case. These results allow AC and CC based tests to be compared, although the comparison is problem specific, which limits its practical value. Rather than selecting one approach, a test based on the maximum of the two statistics is also considered, whose critical value can consistently approximated by two bootstrap procedures. In simulations, its power lies between those of the AC and CC approaches.

Methodology.title: The exact region of the Average Rectangular Volume and Spearman's rho, with an application to arachnitude
Methodology.summary: The average rectangular volume ($\ARV$) of a bivariate aggregation function is the average of its volumes over all axis-parallel rectangles of the unit square; for a copula, it is the expected copula volume of the rectangle spanned by two independent uniform points. We determine the exact region of the pairs $(\ARV(C),ρ(C))$, where $C$ ranges over all bivariate copulas and $ρ$ is Spearman's rho. The region is compact, convex and symmetric, and its upper boundary consists of three analytically parametrized arcs. A previously proposed family of shuffles of Min generates one arc, but only on part of its range; the other two arcs are generated by singular copulas whose supports contain hyperbolic branches. The boundary is continuously differentiable away from its left endpoint $\ARV=\frac{11}{120}$, where it has a vertical tangent. The proof uses a folding transformation and explicit Kantorovich potentials for a family of optimal transport problems. Finally, we show that the arachnitude, a rank correlation used in actuarial practice, is an affine transformation of $\ARV$, so that the result also describes the joint region of Spearman's rho and arachnitude.

Methodology.title: Two-sample Behrens-Fisher problems for high-dimensional data: noncentral normal-reference inference
Methodology.summary: We study noncentral normal-reference inference for high-dimensional two-sample Behrens-Fisher problems. Within the Gaussian reference, a shifted null law is accurate if and only if covariance-weighted signal energy is negligible relative to the trace of the squared covariance. We establish the sharp uniform fourth-root error order over unrestricted spectra and a linear bound under spectral spread. A separate spectral-range criterion determines when signal magnitude alone suffices. An augmented spherical reference gives finite-sample calibration for Gaussian samples and asymptotically recovers Gaussian-reference local power under projection fourth-moment bounds and control of diagonal fluctuations, without a dimension-to-sample-size restriction. For unknown Gaussian covariance, explicit trace and hollow-Gram confidence bounds turn the linear approximation bound into a simultaneous, computable certificate over local effect ranges. Eigenspace signal energies describe directional power, while a two-point argument limits estimation of unknown local power. Simulations with 10,000 evaluation replications per configuration examine unequal and noncommuting covariances, severe sample imbalance, non-Gaussian observations and the informativeness of the certificate.

Graphics.title: A Lightweight Differentiable Method for Real-Time Skin Rendering and Digitization
Graphics.summary: Inverse rendering for skin typically relies on offline path tracing to estimate physical properties, which fail to map directly to the approximate shaders utilized in interactive applications, such as game engines. We bridge this gap by directly estimating subsurface scattering parameters tailored for real-time rendering pipelines. We introduce a differentiable Screen-Space Subsurface Scattering (SSSS) framework that enables the joint optimization of spatially varying base textures and scattering distances. To account for local variations in skin thickness, we estimate these parameters across distinct facial regions, generating a blended profile map ready for production runtime engines. Our pipeline utilizes a low-cost, single-light, single-view capture setup designed for accessible and practical appearance acquisition. Optimization is driven by a masked loss function targeting regions where subsurface scattering effects are dominant. We validate our approach on a real-world dataset of $45$ individuals across the Monk Skin Tone Scale, ensuring demographic generalization. Furthermore, we complement this evaluation with synthetic data, a multi-light setup validating our single-light assumption, and a tilted-view configuration confirming angular consistency. Results demonstrate that our method effectively recovers scattering parameters from lightweight inputs, yielding realistic skin appearance directly compatible with standard real-time shaders.
Graphics.comment: 20 pages, 25 figures; includes 6 pages of supplementary material. Accepted to Computers and Graphics

Graphics.title: Linear-size graphs at every strict dismantling level
Graphics.summary: Dismantling reduces a graph to one vertex by successive deletions. At level zero, a vertex is eligible if one of its neighbours is adjacent to all its other neighbours. At level $k\geq1$, its neighbours must induce a graph dismantlable at level $k-1$. A graph has strict level $k$ if it admits a reduction at level $k$ and none at level $k-1$. For every $k\geq1$, we construct a graph of strict level $k$ with $3k+8$ vertices. Each step adds three vertices: the neighbours of one induce the preceding graph, and the other two provide the adjacencies used to rule out other first deletions at the lower level. A second construction gives a graph of order $4k+4$ at strict level $k$. Together the two families give the upper bound $\min\{4k+4,3k+8\}$ on the least order at strict level $k$.

Graphics.title: Exploring Cross-Reality Transitions between Projections and Head-Mounted Displays for Immersive Digital Art
Graphics.summary: Immersive exhibitions increasingly combine large-scale projections with mixed reality (MR) head-mounted displays (HMDs), but how users perceive transitions across these heterogeneous visualization environments remains underexplored. We investigate cross-reality (CR) object- and scene-level transitions in a hybrid immersive art installation spanning projection, augmented reality (AR), and virtual reality (VR). In a within-subjects study (N=24), we compared a calibrated condition with a bundled inconsistency condition introducing noticeable differences in spatial alignment, visual appearance, and cross-device latency. This contrast was used not to establish perceptual thresholds or hardware targets, but as a diagnostic probe to make transition disruptions more perceptible and discussable. The inconsistency condition reduced presence and increased workload. Interviews showed that spatial misalignment disrupted action-outcome predictability, appearance mismatch reduced aesthetic coherence, and latency weakened perceived responsiveness. Effects also varied by asset type: rigid static assets exposed inconsistencies more clearly, animated skeletal assets shifted attention toward motion, and particle effects often masked small discrepancies. These findings clarify how users perceive projection-MR transitions and support asset-aware design strategies for coherent hybrid immersive art. We also release HUICRSync, an open-source Unreal Engine plugin for prototyping projection-MR CR experiences.

Graphics.title: FAME-QP: A GPU-Accelerated Quadratic-Programming Solver for Real-Time Model Predictive Control
Graphics.summary: We present FAME-QP, a GPU-accelerated solver for dense quadratic programs arising in linear model predictive control. FAME-QP combines constraint-dependent operator representations with fused single- and two-kernel iterations replayed through CUDA graphs, automatically selecting the execution configuration through device calibration and problem-specific timing. It probes a cached operator bank to select the initial penalty and updates operators lazily when problem matrices change. Numerical benchmarks and simulated humanoid and quadrotor control experiments demonstrate reduced latency relative to competing GPU solvers while maintaining solution accuracy and control performance.

Graphics.title: Physics-Driven Extraction of Dynamic Fluid Asset from Monocular Video with Generative 3DGS
Graphics.summary: Existing methods for dynamic 3D scene synthesis from video rely on per-frame deformation fields optimized through pixel-level reconstruction losses. While effective for closed systems such as elastic solids, these approaches face challenges with open systems like fluids where material continuously enters and exits the scene, topology changes freely, and no stable point correspondence exists across frames. We propose a simulation-driven alternative that optimizes the parameters of a fluid simulator to reproduce dynamics observed in a single-view video, rather than fitting per-point deformation to pixel values. Our framework leverages generative 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) models to obtain initial fluid geometry including unseen surfaces, estimates a physically grounded velocity field from surface motions with a physics-constraint correction algorithm, and converts it into a divergence-free, grid-based representation. A differentiable Affine Particle-In-Cell (APIC) simulation then optimizes effective simulation parameters, such as viscosity, boundary conditions, and inflow/outflow velocities, to match the observed dynamics. Because the dynamics are governed by forward simulation, the output assets are inherently editable, interactive, and temporally extendable, which reconstruction-based approaches cannot readily provide. Stage-wise ablations confirm that each stage is necessary, and hyperparameter sweeps show the pipeline to be robust without sensitive per-scene tuning. Our method handles various liquid fluids, including inviscid and viscous types, demonstrating the potential for automatically creating simulation-ready 3D fluid assets from readily available internet videos.
Graphics.comment: Accepted to IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics. 21 pages (18 pages + 3 pages supplementary material), 28 figures

Graphics.title: Pygmalion Effect in Vision: Image-to-Clay Translation for Reflective Geometry Reconstruction
Graphics.summary: Understanding reflection remains a long-standing challenge in 3D reconstruction due to the entanglement of appearance and geometry under view-dependent reflections. In this work, we present the Pygmalion Effect in Vision, a novel framework that metaphorically "sculpts" reflective objects into clay-like forms through image-to-clay translation. We then introduce a dual-branch design in which a BRDF-based reflective branch and a clay-guided branch share the same Gaussian geometry but operate through independent rendering paths. The clay-guided branch, supervised by the synthesized clay images, provides reflection-free geometric guidance that complements the photometric supervision of the BRDF branch. Experiments on both synthetic and real datasets show consistent improvements in both geometry and photometric metrics. Beyond technical gains, our framework reveals that seeing by unshining, translating radiance into neutrality, can serve as a powerful inductive bias for reflective object geometry learning.

Graphics.title: Deformable Texture Maps: Compiling Dynamic Microgeometry into Neural Textures
Graphics.summary: Deformable material surfaces, such as cloth, owe their appearance to fine-scale geometries that restructure under deformation. Even when coarse simulation models efficiently recover this microstructure, explicitly instantiating and rendering it remains expensive. We introduce Deformable Texture Maps (DTM), a representation that compiles deformation-driven microgeometry into a continuous and compact neural texture. Our model maps texture coordinates and local deformations to intrinsic maps describing opacity, surface normals, depth, and material identity. This captures the occlusion and visibility changes generated by deformation. At runtime, these maps provide a common texture-space representation of deformation-driven fine-scale structure that can be evaluated directly on coarse deforming surfaces. Since our representation encodes geometric attributes rather than radiance, lighting and material response remain decoupled from the learned model. This allows us to apply relighting, as well as shading and material editing without retraining. We further introduce a persistent texture-space rendering strategy that caches these intrinsic maps and selectively updates them as deformation changes. This effectively decouples neural evaluation from frame rendering and enables their reuse across frames and conventional rendering effects. We demonstrate our approach on yarn-based textiles, where non-linear material stretch and shear induce changes in yarn geometry, spacing and occlusion. We build our model by, first, sweeping tileable yarn patches through deformation space, then, rendering the detailed geometry into a canonical texture-space, and finally, compressing the resulting maps into a single neural representation. Our resulting model can be evaluated directly on arbitrary coarse garment meshes and integrated with conventional shading pipelines, keeping appearance authorable at render time.

Graphics.title: Patch-Based Generalized Neural Texture Upscaling
Graphics.summary: We propose a lightweight neural texture upscaling method. A single generalized MLP is trained on a diverse collection of texture patches and integrated into the texture sampling stage, upscaling low-resolution textures on-the-fly at rendering time. Because the model is generalized rather than overfit to specific content, no per-asset training is required - the same model applies to any existing scene without modifying texture data or the asset pipeline. Storing lower-resolution base textures reduces disk footprint, upscaling at sampling time eliminates the need to store high-resolution textures in VRAM, and sharing a single set of model weights across all textures ensures non-divergent GPU execution. We evaluate our method across multiple texture classes, demonstrating consistent improvement over analytic upscaling methods in perceptual quality.

Signal Processing.title: ARIA: An AI-Powered Radio-Channel Inference and Analysis Pipeline
Signal Processing.summary: Statistical channel models play a key role in the design and standardization of next-generation wireless systems. The models substitute for costly and time-consuming field measurements when fitted distributions accurately reproduce the measured channel impulse responses. Future wireless systems will operate in global spectrum allocations from 1 to 150 GHz. Over the full span, analytically chosen distribution families fitted to scarce measurement data fail to deliver the required accuracy. Generative AI models instead learn each distribution from the radio-propagation data itself, adapt to the measured structure at every frequency, and scale across the entire band. We present ARIA, an AI-powered Radio-channel Inference and Analysis pipeline that learns each channel-parameter distribution from the measurements. The pipeline extracts power-delay profiles and recovers the channel parameters with time-cluster spatial-lobe (TCSL) analysis. Three neural density estimators, namely mixture density networks, neural spline flows (NSF), and denoising diffusion implicit models, learn each parameter's distribution. A composite rank across goodness-of-fit metrics with Friedman-Nemenyi testing identifies the best estimator, and a maximum-likelihood step anchored to the measured samples converts its density into closed-form parametric families. We instantiate ARIA on the NYU WIRELESS 16.95 GHz InH campaign and find that NSF outperforms the other estimators on every metric. We also show that a conditional NSF with feature-wise linear modulation, trained jointly on the 6.75 and 16.95 GHz measurements, improves over single-frequency training. We feed the fitted distributions into the NYUSIM simulator and reproduce the measured omnidirectional RMS delay spread medians within 2 ns, the per-lobe azimuth and zenith spread medians within 1 degree, and the omnidirectional zenith spread medians within 0.5 degrees.
Signal Processing.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication

Signal Processing.title: Thickness-Field-Excited Bimorph Piezoelectric Micromachined Ultrasonic Transducer in Submicrometer Thin-Film Lithium Niobate
Signal Processing.summary: This work presents the first demonstration of a submicrometer-thick thickness-field-excited (TFE) lithium niobate (LN) flexural-mode piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducer (PMUT). A 670-nm-thick bilayer periodically poled piezoelectric film (P3F) 128Y LN is used to demonstrate a suspended membrane with an area of 0.25 mm$^{2}$, achieving a low resonance frequency of 33.4 kHz for airborne transduction. Its electrical measurements reveal an extracted effective electromechanical coupling efficiency ($k_{\mathrm{eff}}^{2}$) of 3% and a moderate static capacitance $C_0$ of 17 pF. Meanwhile, mechanical measurements using a laser Doppler vibrometer (LDV) yield a high quasi-static peak out-of-plane displacement ($ξ_{\mathrm{static}}$) of 145 nm/V and a high corresponding open-circuit sensitivity ($S_{\mathrm{OC}}$) of 1.4 mV/Pa in the audio band. The fabricated device is compared with state-of-the-art (SoA) airborne piezoelectric transducers with sub-100-kHz resonance frequencies, underscoring the potential of the TFE P3F LN transducer platform by simultaneously demonstrating strong actuation capability while featuring high sensitivity.
Signal Processing.comment: 8 pages, 11 figures

Signal Processing.title: PRIMO: GPU-Accelerated Joint Beamforming and RIS Placement Optimization for Outdoor-to-Indoor Coverage at FR1(C) and FR3
Signal Processing.summary: Upper mid-band spectrum is promising for 5G and 6G cellular networks, yet concrete and low-emissivity glass impose over 20 dB of building penetration loss above 2 GHz, degrading outdoor-to-indoor (O2I) coverage. A reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) on a neighboring building bypasses this blockage by focusing energy onto indoor users. This paper introduces PRIMO (Parallel RIS Min-Rate Optimization), a training-free joint optimizer of base-station precoding, RIS phase shifts, and RIS placement, validated by calibrated ray tracing in a MetroTech Commons digital twin (Brooklyn, NY) at 6.75 and 16.95 GHz. At equal physical aperture, half-wavelength spacing packs 6.25 times as many elements per array at FR3 as at FR1(C), so FR1(C) leads at low indoor-user counts while FR3 dominates at higher counts, where the additional spatial degrees of freedom suppress inter-user interference. Above a 1 bps/Hz service floor, PRIMO supports 92% more indoor users at FR3 than at FR1(C), and raises the minimum user rate by up to 90% over a fully converged alternating-optimization baseline while running about 100 times faster.
Signal Processing.comment: 5 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables. Presented at the 2026 Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems, and Computers, Pacific Grove, CA, USA, Oct. 25-28, 2026

Signal Processing.title: Beyond TR 38.811 for 6G NTN Channel Models
Signal Processing.summary: As the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) expands 6G non-terrestrial network (NTN) to S, Ku, and Ka bands for integration with existing terrestrial cellular networks, the necessary satellite channel model for link and network performance evaluation remains tied to TR 38.811, last revised in 2020. We identify issues on multiple fronts: inappropriate parameter specifications based on very limited site-specific environments considered, omission of satellite-induced Doppler spread and directional antenna effects and lack of a transparent channel model generation procedure. To address these limitations, we re-derive the channel parameters using ray tracing (RT) over urban and rural environments based on ITU-R building statistics. Our results show that TR 38.811 substantially overestimates the K-factor at low elevations and predicts a decreasing trend with elevation, which is inconsistent with RT. The Ka-band clutter loss (CL) also exceeds the RT estimates by more than 15 dB in urban cases. It also underestimates rural delay spread (DS) at low elevations and predicts an elevation trend inconsistent with RT. We further quantify the previously neglected satellite-induced Doppler spread. Finally, we demonstrate that the conventional TR 38.811 channel generator significantly underestimates the K-factor in the presence of directional antenna (beamforming), while our modified generator substantially reduces this discrepancy.

Signal Processing.title: STAR: Semantic-Criticality Tiered Allocation of Radio Resources via Zero-Shot Learning
Signal Processing.summary: In remote inference, edge devices transmit high-resolution images over wireless links to a receiver, where an artificial intelligence (AI) model answers task-specific questions about these images to enable reliable decisions. These answers are often determined by a small set of task-causal pixels, such as those of text, whose corruption changes the answer, so these pixels must be delivered with high fidelity. Conventional transmission protects every pixel equally, so it either consumes many resource elements (REs) or corrupts these regions at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). To overcome these limitations, in this paper, a zero-shot, domain-agnostic framework, termed semantic-criticality tiered allocation of resources (STAR), is proposed. In particular, a per-pixel semantic-criticality indicator (SCI) is derived from the attention of a frozen vision-language model, so new tasks and domains are handled by changing only the prompt, without retraining. The resulting task causality-aware resource allocation problem over protection tiers is solved exactly by a threshold rule on the SCI, realized by a coded tier for the task-causal pixels and an uncoded, downsampled base layer for the full image. Simulations over a 5G New Radio link demonstrate that STAR attains a semantic accuracy of at least 0.98 for $E_s/N_0 \geq -4$ dB and, at comparable semantic reliability, reduces the REs of robust coded transmission by 59.5% and 91.5% on factory- and vehicle-monitoring datasets, respectively, the latter without any change to the models. Although a deep joint source-channel coding baseline uses fewer REs at comparable semantic accuracy, it must be retrained with labeled data for every new task or domain.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 9 figures, 1 table. Submitted to IEEE ICC 2027

Signal Processing.title: One-hot Coding-based URA with RFFI-Enabled Message Authentication
Signal Processing.summary: Unsourced random access (URA) has emerged as a promising paradigm for enabling massive connectivity in Internet-of-Things (IoT) networks. However, since URA transmissions do not contain device identifiers, the receiver may not associate decoded messages with their originating devices, introducing a security vulnerability: forged messages may be decoded as legitimate. To address this problem, this paper proposes a one-hot coding (OHC)-based URA framework that enables message authentication while preserving the unsourced transmission principle. Specifically, distinct messages are mapped onto orthogonal channel uses via an OHC-based common codebook and transmitted using on-off keying modulation. The resulting orthogonal channel structure enables radio-frequency fingerprint identification to authenticate received signals by exploiting device-specific hardware impairments, thereby authenticating decoded messages without introducing an additional authentication payload. Analytical expressions for the per-user probability of error and the probability of successful spoofing are derived. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed scheme enables secure URA transmission while maintaining reliable communication performance in ultra-short-payload IoT scenarios.
Signal Processing.comment: 5 pages, 6 figures, submitted to IEEE Journal

Signal Processing.title: Graph Attention-based Decentralized Actor-Critic for Dual-Objective Control of Multi-UAV Networks
Signal Processing.summary: This research focuses on optimizing multi-UAV systems with dual objectives: maximizing service coverage as the primary goal while extending battery lifetime as the secondary objective. We propose a Graph Attention-based Decentralized Actor-Critic (GADC) to optimize the dual objectives. The proposed approach leverages a graph attention network to process UAVs' limited local observation and reduce the dimension of the environment states. Subsequently, an actor-double-critic network is developed to manage dual policies for joint objective optimization. The proposed GADC uses a Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence factor to balance the tradeoff between coverage performance and battery lifetime in the multi-UAV system. We assess the scalability and efficiency of GADC through comprehensive benchmarking against state-of-the-art methods, considering both theory and experimental aspects. Extensive testing in both ideal settings and NVIDIA Sionna's realistic ray tracing environment demonstrates GADC's superior performance.

Signal Processing.title: A unifying view of contrastive learning, importance sampling, and bridge sampling for energy-based models
Signal Processing.summary: In the last decades, energy-based models (EBMs) have become an important class of probabilistic models in which a component of the likelihood is intractable and therefore cannot be evaluated explicitly. Consequently, parameter estimation in EBMs is challenging for conventional inference methods. This work is a review paper that brings together these different methodological contributions within a unified framework, highlighting the connections among noise contrastive estimation (NCE), reverse logistic regression (RLR), Bennett's acceptance-ratio (BAR) method, multiple importance sampling (MIS), and bridge sampling within the context of EBMs. Some of them are equivalent under specific conditions. This unified perspective clarifies relationships among existing methods and enables the development of new estimators, with the potential to improve statistical and computational efficiency. Furthermore, this study helps elucidate the success of NCE in terms of its flexibility and robustness, while also identifying scenarios in which its performance can be further improved. Our aim is to provide a self-contained and accessible treatment, with clear and straightforward derivations, that brings together these contributions within a common framework and makes the main results and their underlying ideas understandable to a broader readership. The contribution is twofold. First, this work serves as a comprehensive tutorial for researchers entering the field, introducing the fundamental concepts and derivations. Second, it offers a thorough review for experienced practitioners. The code used in the numerical experiments is available to support the reproducibility of the results.

Signal Processing.title: Coexistence of Direct-to-Device (D2D) Satellite Systems with 5G/6G Terrestrial Networks: Cross-Border Aggregate Interference Analysis in Saudi Arabia
Signal Processing.summary: Direct-to-device (D2D) satellite systems, particularly those based on 3GPP-compliant non-terrestrial networks (NTN), deliver connectivity to standard mobile phones and IoT devices using terrestrial International Mobile Telecommunications (IMT) spectrum. This raises the risk of harmful cross-border interference into incumbent terrestrial IMT networks, an issue considered under Agenda Item 1.13 of the ITU World Radiocommunication Conference 2027 (WRC-27). This paper presents an ITU-R-compliant assessment of aggregate downlink interference from two hypothetical D2D systems operating in Jordan and Iraq into terrestrial IMT user equipment (UE) in Saudi Arabia, operating in the 698-960 MHz band. Unlike prior studies that evaluate a few test points near a simplified ideal tri-border intersection, we distribute multiple victim UEs along realistic national borders within various strips at a distance of 0-40 km from the borders. We compare two satellite selection strategies: highest-elevation and random strategies. The CDF of the interference-to-noise ratio (I/N) together with the intra-system and inter-system aggregation factors are analyzed. Results show that the protection criterion is exceeded up to 88% of the time, requiring up to 27 dB of additional isolation, so coexistence is infeasible without interference mitigation. In general, random selection produces higher interference because low-elevation beams place victims closer to boresight. Two mitigation techniques are then evaluated. A border isolation zone of one cell diameter yields only a moderate improvement under both strategies, whereas a narrow-beam, deep-null phased-array pattern lowers the exceedance to about 40% irrespective of strategy, providing an important input for spectrum regulatory considerations.

Signal Processing.title: WaveGen: Truly End-to-End Waveform Generation via Internal Spectral Trajectory Learning
Signal Processing.summary: This work proposes WaveGen, a fully end-to-end diffusion-based text-to-waveform framework based on Spectral Forcing, which jointly learns an internal spectral trajectory and the target waveform trajectory within a single model, enabling direct end-to-end text-to-waveform generation. Unlike recent TTS pipelines, WaveGen does not rely on separately trained or externally decoded intermediate representations, such as neural audio codecs, Mel-spectrogram vocoders, or VAE-based latent models. In addition, WaveGen performs internal text-speech alignment within a single model, eliminating the need for external alignment modules such as duration predictors. To preserve a truly end-to-end formulation, our framework further avoids dependence on self-supervised representations, such as BERT-based text embeddings and Wav2Vec 2.0-based semantic representations, as well as semantic distillation methods for training optimization. To achieve this, we carefully design Spectral Forcing, a model architecture with disentangled diffusion heads, and a training objective based on a multi-scale spectral $v$-loss. We further validate the scalability of end-to-end TTS models by scaling the model size from 0.1B to 0.6B parameters. Using a single architecture, open-source data, and one-stage training, without external modules such as duration predictor or REPA, WaveGen demonstrates fully end-to-end waveform generation achieving state-of-the-art performance on the Emilia training dataset. In particular, WaveGen achieves a WER of 1.47 and a SIM of 0.75 on the Seed-en benchmark. Source code and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/sh-lee-prml/WaveGen
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026

Signal Processing.title: Reference-Dependent Utility Optimization for Goal-Oriented Communication Systems
Signal Processing.summary: Traditional communication resource allocation optimizes operational metrics such as rate, latency, energy efficiency, and reliability. Motivated by goal-oriented semantic communication, we develop a generalized allocation framework that transforms operational rewards through reference-dependent user utilities and evaluates them via expected utility, cumulative prospect theory (CPT), or related decision criteria. The formulation separates operational rewards, user-side valuations, and system-level decision criteria under uncertainty. We characterize utilities incorporating QoS/service reference levels, deficit sensitivity, post-reference saturation, and loss aversion. Weighted sum-reward maximization, proportional fairness, $α$-fairness, and stochastic expected utility maximization emerge as exact special cases, while soft QoS-aware allocation follows from a deficit-penalty generalization. For deterministic orthogonal systems, we derive utility-weighted marginal-reward KKT conditions characterizing global optimality under concave composite objectives. For nonorthogonal and stochastic systems, we develop successive convex approximation (SCA) algorithms and establish stationary-point guarantees under explicit smooth and composite nonsmooth assumptions, including a CPT branch-stationarity result under eventual nondegenerate ordering identification. For globally solved penalized problems, we derive an $O(1/λ)$ bound on excess aggregate soft-QoS deficit, and on the deficit itself whenever a QoS-feasible allocation exists. Additionally, we establish an $O(1/ε^2)$ outer iteration bound for the smooth fixed-step SCA best-response residual. Numerical examples demonstrate how reference points, marginal utility slopes, channel quality, and resource budgets influence active users and allocation policies.
Signal Processing.comment: This paper has been submitted for publication

Signal Processing.title: Grid Design for Near-Field Channel Estimation with Uniform Linear Arrays
Signal Processing.summary: This paper develops deterministic grids for line-of-sight near-field channel estimation with uniform linear arrays (ULAs) and hybrid receivers. A normalized channel approximation squared error (NCASE) criterion leads to geometric covering problems under a constant-amplitude parabolic model and an elliptical approximation of the correlation regions. For a horizontal ULA, transformation and scaling yield a disk-covering problem, addressed by adapting a hexagonal lattice to the mapped ground-plane region. For a vertical ULA, a reciprocal-distance interval cover is solved optimally by a farthest-reaching greedy procedure. Numerical evaluation with exact spherical-wave channels yields empirical maximum approximation errors close to the target and improved P-SOMP estimation relative to the tested polar-domain grids of comparable size.

Signal Processing.title: Neural Multipath Fields for 6G FR3 Digital Twins: Latent Adaptation from Sparse Data
Signal Processing.summary: Wireless digital twins are essential for environment-aware 6G communications, motivating the investigation of frequency range 3 (FR3), an emerging mid-band regime offering a promising balance between bandwidth and propagation characteristics. Neural Radio Frequency (RF) fields provide continuous surrogates for site-specific radio propagation, but adapting a scene-specific field to a new environment can require substantial measurements and retraining. To this end, we propose the Latent-Adaptive Neural Multipath Field (LANMF), a scene-conditioned FR3 model that predicts path-resolved delays, complex channel impulse response (CIR) coefficients, and arrival and departure directions from transmitter-receiver coordinates. LANMF learns shared propagation representations across source environments and adapts to unseen scenes by optimizing only a 16-dimensional scene latent. Evaluated on six ray-traced indoor scenes at 7.5 GHz, latent-only adaptation yields improvements in prediction with just 5-10 target links (0.42-0.83% of available links). Compared with full-network fine-tuning, it updates only 16 persistent target parameters, reducing adaptation time by 28-30% and incremental peak GPU memory by 82-85%. While the proposed solution supports various wireless applications, we demonstrate its utility through beam-candidate reduction using a 64-beam codebook, retaining measurement-based final beam selection.

Signal Processing.title: Deep learning for structural health monitoring: An application to heritage structures
Signal Processing.summary: Thanks to recent advancements in numerical methods, computer power, and monitoring technology, seismic ambient noise provides precious information about the structural behavior of old buildings. The measurement of the vibrations produced by anthropic and environmental sources and their use for dynamic identification and structural health monitoring of buildings initiated an emerging, cross-disciplinary field engaging seismologists, engineers, mathematicians, and computer scientists. In this work, we employ recent deep learning techniques for time-series forecasting to inspect and detect anomalies in the large dataset recorded during a long-term monitoring campaign conducted on the San Frediano bell tower in Lucca. We frame the problem as an unsupervised anomaly detection task and train a Temporal Fusion Transformer to learn the normal dynamics of the structure. We then detect the anomalies by looking at the differences between the predicted and observed frequencies.

Signal Processing.title: VNA-Only Calibration of Waveguide Thermistor Mounts with Self-Consistent Determination of the Thermistor-Port Impedance
Signal Processing.summary: A method is presented for determining the calibration factor and the effective efficiency of waveguide thermistor mounts from vector-network-analyzer reflection data alone, without a microcalorimeter, extending the three reflection-coefficient method of the coaxial case. In waveguide the thermistor is coupled to the line through a matching structure and the reference impedance of the thermistor port, $Z_0$, is not known a priori; it is inferred through a power-consistency relation between pairs of states, under the convention that it is real. The method reproduces the factory certificates (U = 2 %) of four K486A mounts within 1.0 % rms and the PTB-traceable values (U = 0.85 to 0.98 %) of a fifth within 0.34 % rms; its expanded measurement uncertainty is 0.5 to 1.16 % (k = 2) for the best specimen and below 2 % for the five. A mount with its waveguide-to-coaxial adapter is calibrated directly, without characterizing the adapter, from the model factor of the mount and the geometric factor measured through the adapter. The scattering matrix implied by the solution is not passive; a minimum-norm correction of the thermistor impedances along the two directions invisible to the calibration factor - the ratios of the efficiencies of the three states - brings it to the floor of passivity, where the efficiency depends on the load only through its mismatch factor, leaves the result unchanged, and gives the sensitivity of the efficiency to the bias resistance in closed form: below $4\times10^{-5}$ $Ω^{-1}$ in band mean, proportional to the mismatch of the operating state and to the loss of the mount.
Signal Processing.comment: 60 pages, 21 figures. Submitted to Metrologia (IOP Publishing / BIPM), November 2026

Signal Processing.title: A Tutorial on Learning-Based Radio Map Construction: Data, Paradigms, and Physics-Awareness
Signal Processing.summary: Radio maps (RMs) provide the digital representation of the wireless propagation environment, mapping complex geographical and topological boundary conditions to critical spatial-spectral metrics that range from received signal strength to full channel state information matrices. The integration of artificial intelligence into next generation wireless networks further necessitates the accurate construction of RMs as a foundational prerequisite for electromagnetic digital twins. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of learning-based RM construction, systematically addressing three intertwined dimensions: data, paradigms, and physics-awareness. From the data perspective, we review physical measurement campaigns, ray tracing simulation engines, and publicly available benchmark datasets, identifying their respective strengths and fundamental limitations. From the paradigm perspective, we establish a core taxonomy that categorizes RM construction into source-aware forward prediction and \added{source-agnostic} inverse reconstruction, and examine five principal neural architecture families spanning convolutional neural networks, vision transformers, graph neural networks, generative adversarial networks, and diffusion models. We further survey optics-inspired methods adapted from neural radiance fields and 3D Gaussian splatting for continuous wireless radiation field modeling. From the physics-awareness perspective, we introduce a three-level integration framework encompassing data-level feature engineering, loss-level partial differential equation regularization, and \added{architecture-level} structural isomorphism. Open challenges including foundation model development, physical hallucination detection, and amortized inference for real-time deployment are discussed to outline future research directions.

Signal Processing.title: Robust Beamforming and Antenna Position Optimization for Movable Antenna-Assisted Covert Communications
Signal Processing.summary: In this paper, we study a movable antenna (MA)-enhanced covert communication system, where a legitimate transmitter (Alice) serves multiple legitimate users in the presence of multiple non-colluding Willies that attempt to detect the covert transmission from Alice. To ensure data covertness with imperfect knowledge of the Willies' channel state information (CSI), we develop a robust covert transmission framework with a norm-bounded CSI error model. In particular, we aim to jointly optimize the transmit beamforming vectors, artificial noise (AN) covariance matrix, and MA positions to maximize the weighted minimum signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) among all legitimate users subject to worst-case covertness constraints. To tackle this challenging problem, we develop a block coordinate descent (BCD)-based optimization framework, incorporating the S-procedure, semidefinite relaxation (SDR), bisection search, and successive convex approximation (SCA). Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed algorithm in improving the performance of MA-enhanced covert communication systems.

Signal Processing.title: A Scale-Space Theory of Memory
Signal Processing.summary: Scale-space theory has emerged as a central attempt to restrict the {\it general} theory of signal processing with geometric constraints inspired from the animal world. In the mathematical language of operator theory, scale-space theory restricts the Toeplitz operator. The present paper investigates scale-space theory for memory systems. We investigate how scale space theory restricts a memory system encoding past information, that is, restricts the Hankel operator. Our main result is to establish a close correspondence between scale-space theory and the long-studied {\it relaxation} property.

Signal Processing.title: Spectrum Anomaly Detection in OFDMA Systems: Simulation Framework and Benchmark Dataset
Signal Processing.summary: Wireless connectivity underpins modern society and industry, enabling critical applications such as 5G ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) for industrial automation. However, the openness of the wireless medium exposes it to spectrum anomalies, including unintentional interference and malicious jamming, which threaten communication and sensing functionalities in 5G and emerging 6G networks. Despite its importance, spectrum anomaly detection research is hindered by a lack of publicly available datasets reflecting real-world scenarios. To address this, we present a benchmark dataset for spectrum anomaly detection in orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing access (OFDMA) systems, a core technology for 5G and beyond. The dataset includes spectrograms generated across a distributed network of sensing units, covering five distinct jammer types, from simple noise to advanced pilot-aware attacks. These anomalies are simulated in an industrial factory environment using a versatile open-source framework developed and published as part of this work, enabling extensibility to new scenarios and interference types. We provide baseline evaluations for supervised and unsupervised learning methods, demonstrating the challenges posed by different jammers and highlighting areas for further research. The dataset and framework support reproducible studies and serve as a foundation for advancing spectrum anomaly detection, with applications extending to network digital twins. By bridging the gap in open dataset availability, this work empowers the research community to validate and compare advanced detection methods for resilient next-generation wireless systems.
Signal Processing.comment: 15 pages, 9 figures, revised version, submitted for publication to IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society

Signal Processing.title: Deep-Unfolded Accelerated Projected Gradient for Energy-Efficient Cell-Free Massive MIMO
Signal Processing.summary: This paper investigates energy efficiency (EE) maximization for the downlink of cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output systems under quality-of-service and per-access point power constraints. We first derive closed-form gradient expressions of the objective function with respect to the power allocation coefficients, and then propose an accelerated projected gradient (APG) approach to solve this problem. To reduce the computational complexity and runtime of APG, we propose a deep-unfolded APG framework that maps iterative APG updates onto a finite number of neural network layers, where parameters such as step sizes and penalty coefficients are learned from data. The proposed approach produces power allocation solutions through a fixed number of gradient-based updates without the need for line search or manual parameter tuning. Numerical results show that the method achieves EE performance comparable to the iterative APG approach while requiring significantly lower computational cost, with up to a 30-fold reduction in floating-point operations under the considered system settings.

Signal Processing.title: Movable Antenna-Assisted Covert Communications: Robust Beamforming and Antenna Position Optimization
Signal Processing.summary: In this paper, we study a movable antenna (MA)-enhanced covert communication system, where a legitimate transmitter (named Alice) serves multiple legitimate users in the presence of multiple aerial wardens that attempt to detect the transmission from Alice. To ensure data covertness with imperfect knowledge of warden channel state information (CSI), we develop a unified robust covert transmission framework that incorporates bounded and statistical CSI error models. In particular, we aim to jointly optimize the transmit beamforming, the artificial noise (AN) covariance matrix, and MA positions at Alice to maximize the minimum weighted signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) among the legitimate users subject to data covertness constraints. The resulting optimization problem is intractable to solve optimally due to the strong coupling among the optimization variables and the random channel uncertainty. To deal with this issue, we propose a block coordinate descent (BCD)-based algorithm. Specifically, for the norm-bounded CSI error model, we first employ the S-procedure to convert the covertness constraints into a sequence of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Then, a successive convex approximation (SCA) procedure incorporating semidefinite relaxation (SDR) and bisection search techniques is proposed to solve the resulting problem. For the statistical CSI error model, the Bernstein-type inequality is employed to derive deterministic approximations of the probabilistic constraint in terms of LMIs and second-order cone (SOC) constraints that can be efficiently tackled. Numerical results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed algorithm in improving the performance of MA-enhanced covert communication systems.

Signal Processing.title: Mitigating the BICM Loss in MIMO Receivers with Correlation-Informed Logits
Signal Processing.summary: Bit-interleaved coded modulation (BICM) is widely used in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) wireless systems. However, separating MIMO data detection from channel decoding and only exchanging per-bit soft information discards correlation information among the bits within each transmit vector. We show that the resulting information loss limits the performance of practical one-shot receivers. Even though iterative detection and decoding (IDD) can recover most of this loss, IDD significantly increases receiver complexity and latency. In order to reduce this loss, we propose COrrelation-Informed Logits (COIL), a soft-output format that combines per-bit soft information with pairwise coupling logits for correlated bits. We show how to incorporate these coupling logits into a conventional belief-propagation-based channel decoder, which enables correlation-aware decoding in a one-shot receiver without IDD. We evaluate COIL in a MIMO-BICM system with a conventional low-density parity-check code. For a 4x4 MIMO orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) system, a one-shot linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE) receiver with COIL outperforms a conventional one-shot unbiased LMMSE receiver by 1.3dB and operates within 0.8dB of four-iteration IDD, while requiring only a single pass through the data detector.
Signal Processing.comment: Submitted to a journal

Signal Processing.title: Spectral-Domain Information Geometry of Stationary Covariance Models: Gaussian and Elliptical Extensions
Signal Processing.summary:
This paper develops an information-geometric framework for stationary covariance structures. We begin with the infinite-dimensional setting, where stationary covariance structures can be characterized without finite-window boundary effects. By formulating the covariance structure as a bilinear form on a suitable class of test functions, we establish its spectral representation and show how finite-dimensional Toeplitz covariance matrices arise as restrictions to nested observation subspaces. For zero-mean proper complex Gaussian wide-sense stationary (WSS) processes, we show that the normalized finite-dimensional Fisher information converges to a spectral-domain metric. In logarithmic spectral coordinates, this metric becomes the standard $L^2$ inner product, yielding an explicit Fisher--Rao distance that is also recovered as the asymptotic normalized affine-invariant Riemannian distance between Toeplitz covariance matrices.
  We then extend the framework to elliptical observation models by separating global covariance scale from shape. The shape Fisher information is orthogonal to radial nuisance directions and is characterized by a dimension- and radial-model-dependent coefficient. We derive a condition under which this coefficient converges to its Gaussian value as the observation dimension tends to infinity. The resulting limiting spectral-shape geometry is the centered $L^2$ geometry of log-spectra and is invariant to positive rescaling. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical convergence results and the recovery of the Gaussian shape coefficient.
Signal Processing.comment: 26 pages, 7 figures

Signal Processing.title: Joint Power and Adaptive-Constellation Optimization for OFDM-ISAC Systems
Signal Processing.summary: Next-generation wireless systems are expected to support integrated sensing and communications (ISAC). However, sensing imposes different requirements on the power allocation (PA) and the modulation format than communications, leading to a fundamental trade-off in frequency-selective channels. In this paper, we jointly optimize the PA and modulation format for orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM)-based ISAC systems, considering both target detection and tracking. We first derive an upper bound on the mutual information to predict the communication performance for power-constellation allocation. We then use an autoencoder (AE) to learn a family of finite constellations that realizes the allocation under different sensing constraints without retraining. The results show that tracking alleviates the sensing & communications (S&C) tradeoff compared with initial detection, and that the PA and the modulation dominate the S&C trade-off at low and high signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), respectively. At intermediate SNR, the proposed joint optimization significantly outperforms individual optimizations, while the pretrained adaptive constellation family almost fully realizes the predicted allocation gains.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted at 1st IEEE Conference on Integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC), Lisbon, Portugal, Nov. 2026

Signal Processing.title: Prospective Importance-based Cognitive Pilot Design for Semantic Sensing in ISAC Systems
Signal Processing.summary: Semantic sensing enables integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems to acquire environmental information relevant to downstream tasks. However, existing pilot design methods either rely on static pilot configurations or learn end-to-end pilot selection policies, without explicitly evaluating the semantic contribution of candidate pilot locations. In this work, we propose a cognitive semantic sensing framework for human activity recognition in orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM)-ISAC systems. Rather than directly learning a high-dimensional mapping from observations to pilot locations, we introduce a semantic importance weight (SIW) to measure the semantic contribution of each candidate pilot location. Leveraging the information bottleneck (IB) principle and the mutual information-minimum mean-square error (I-MMSE) relationship, SIW assigns high values to future time-frequency (TF) channel coefficients that are both difficult to infer from the preceding observations and valuable for downstream inference. To efficiently obtain the SIW, we further develop a conditional diffusion model that predicts the corresponding uncertainty through denoising covariance estimation. Experiments on a real-world Wi-Fi sensing dataset show that the proposed method consistently outperforms baselines across different signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) and pilot budgets.
Signal Processing.comment: The paper has been submitted to the 2027 WCNC conference

Signal Processing.title: Flexible Piezoelectric Tactile Sensing System for Intelligent Object Recognition
Signal Processing.summary: Tactile sensing provides information about object properties that can improve robotic grasping and manipulation.
