In silico experiments show that DNA-MGC+ supports reliable decoding at error rates up to 24% for a 15-KB file, while separate scalability experiments demonstrate reliable decoding of files up to 200 MB at a 5% error rate. In vitro experiments involving a 24-KB file and electrochemical synthesis show that different DNA-MGC+ configurations achieve minimum sequencing depths below 3x and read costs below 3.5 nts/bit under both Illumina and Nanopore sequencing.

Information Theory.title: A reverse entropy power inequality for i.i.d. log-concave random variables
Information Theory.summary: We show that $h_\infty(X+Y)\leq h_\infty(Z+W)$, where $X, Y$ are independent log-concave random variables, and $Z, W$ are exponential random variables having the same respective $\infty$-Rényi entropies. Analogs for integer-valued monotone log-concave random variables are also obtained. Our main tools are decreasing rearrangement, majorization, and the change of measure.

Information Theory.title: Coding for Multiple Reverse-Complement and Palindromic Duplications
Information Theory.summary: Reverse-complement (RC) and palindromic (PAL) duplications insert a reversed copy of a length-$k$ block immediately after the block; an RC duplication also applies a fixed involutive complement to the inserted symbols. We study $q$-ary codes correcting $t$ such operations applied in sequence, where later operations may copy inserted symbols. For fixed $q\geq2$ and $k,t\geq1$, we prove that every length-$n$ code $C$ for either channel has redundancy $n-\log_q|C|\geq t\log_q n-O_{q,k,t}(1)$; for fixed $q,k$ and $1\leq t=t(n)=o(n)$ the lower bound is $t\log_q(n/t)-O_{q,k}(t)$. For fixed $k$, known codes for one length-$k$ insertion burst attain redundancy $\log_q n+O_{q,k}(1)$ for a single duplication of either type. For every even $k$ and any involutive complement, we show that the two channels are equivalent for every number of errors: the bijection complementing every other coordinate turns each RC duplication into a PAL duplication. This bijection therefore converts any $t$-error-correcting RC code into a PAL code of the same size, and conversely, with linear-time transfer of encoders and decoders. For every even $k$, we also determine the maximum number of descendants of one word under exactly two errors; by the bijection, it is the same for both channels. For fixed even $k$, a direct count using this maximum proves the existence of two-error-correcting PAL and RC codes with redundancy at most $4\log_q n+O_{q,k}(1)$. A known existence bound for two deletion bursts transfers to insertions with the same leading term as ours and a larger additive constant. For two errors, the converse gives $2\log_q n-O_{q,k}(1)$, a factor of two below these existence bounds.

Information Theory.title: Identifiable but Hard to Estimate: Rotation in Equally Spaced Overcomplete ICA
Information Theory.summary: How many observations are needed to estimate a common rotation in two-dimensional overcomplete independent component analysis? We study equally spaced mixing columns with known source count, common source law, and column norm. For a fixed non-Gaussian fourth-order Gram-Charlier source law, the rotation is identifiable modulo the column spacing. Yet the sample size for fixed relative angular accuracy grows exponentially with the source count. We characterize this sample size, up to absolute constants, by the reciprocal of the squared Hellinger distance between two rotations separated by half the column spacing. An explicit radially weighted phase estimator attains this scale uniformly over the rotation family, using the observation radius to prevent cancellation in the mean of an angular harmonic. We also determine the exact exponential decay rate of single-observation total variation for the same pair. This gives bounds on the sample size exponent; its exact value remains open. Finally, a noisy binary-source example shows how an exact zero line of the observed characteristic function can have an exponentially small normal derivative.

Information Theory.title: Joint LSFC and Nakagami-m Estimation From Downlink SINR in GZF-Precoded CF-mMIMO
Information Theory.summary: Accurate characterization of the instantaneous signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) is important for reliability-sensitive cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) systems. This paper proposes a joint estimation method for link-specific large-scale fading coefficients (LSFCs) and a common Nakagami-$m$ shape parameter using power and downlink SINR measurements. A tractable SINR distribution is first derived under global zero-forcing (GZF) precoding, Nakagami-$m$ fading, and link-level fractional power control (FPC). Based on the derived probability density function (PDF), a model-driven neural network (NN) is developed to solve the resulting maximum-likelihood estimation (MLE) problem. Simulations show that the reconstructed SINR distributions obtained with the estimated parameters closely match the empirical distributions. With $2 \times 10^{5}$ samples, the proposed method achieves an LSFC root-mean-square error (RMSE) of approximately 1.0 dB and an $m$ RMSE of approximately 0.085.

Information Theory.title: Fast Rates for Offline Contextual Bandits with Forward-KL Regularization under Single-Policy Concentrability
Information Theory.summary: \emph{Kullback-Leibler} (KL) regularization is ubiquitous in reinforcement learning algorithms in the form of \emph{reverse} or \emph{forward} KL. Recent studies have demonstrated $ε^{-1}$-type fast rates for decision making under reverse KL regularization, in contrast to the standard $ε^{-2}$-type sample complexity. However, for forward-KL-regularized objectives, existing statistical analyses are either not applicable or result in $\tilde{O}(ε^{-2})$ slow rates. We take the first step towards addressing this problem via a streamlined analysis of forward-KL-regularized offline CBs. We give the first $\tilde{O}(ε^{-1})$ upper bounds in tabular and general function approximation settings, both under notions of \emph{single-policy concentrability}. In particular, our convex-analytical pipeline unifies these settings by exploiting the pessimism principle in a novel way and completely bypasses the proof routines in previous works based on the mean value theorem, which might be of independent interest. Moreover, we provide rate-optimal lower bounds, manifesting the tightness of our upper bounds in terms of statistical rates. Our lower bounds also demonstrate that the forward-KL-regularized sample complexity recovers the unregularized slow rate in the low-regularization regime, similarly to the reverse-KL regularization.
Information Theory.comment: 36 pages, camera-ready version, fixed a compilation issue

Information Theory.title: Bounds and Constructions for Optimal Wide-Gap Frequency Hopping Sequences
Information Theory.summary: In a frequency-hopping (FH) system, to reduce interference to the received signal, each user's frequency hopping sequence (FHS) shall have wide-gap property. In this paper, we update the upper bounds on the minimum gaps of optimal uniform wide-gap frequency hopping sequences (WGFHS) with parameters $(v,s,λ;e)$ where $v=ks, k\ge 3, λ=k$ and $s\ge k(k-1)+1$ is odd. We completely prove the existence of such WGFHSs for $k\le 3$.

Information Theory.title: Double circulant LCD codes over $\mathbb{F}_2+u\mathbb{F}_2$ and their related binary LCD codes
Information Theory.summary: Linear complementary dual (LCD) codes are linear codes that intersect their dual trivially. We study double circulant (Euclidean) LCD codes over the finite chain ring $R=\mathbb F_2+u\mathbb F_2$, where $u^2=0$. Using the Chinese Remainder Theorem and the factorization of $x^n-1$, we derive an explicit enumeration formula, with a separate treatment of the constituent corresponding to $x-1$, which is not obtained by a formal specialization of the previously known counting formula over $\mathbb F_q[u]/(u^k)$. Assuming Artin's primitive root conjecture for $2$, we show that the binary Gray images contain an asymptotically good family of rate $1/2$ which attains the asymptotic Gilbert--Varshamov bound, i.e., whose relative distance can approach $H_2^{-1}(1/2)$ from below. More importantly from the constructive viewpoint, by combining Gray images with a known extension construction, we obtain a binary LCD code with previously unknown parameters $[29,15,7]$ and construct two explicit permutation-inequivalent binary LCD codes with parameters $[45,23,9]$ and nine binary LCD codes with the best known parameters.

Information Theory.title: Binary Belief Propagation Fixed Points: Finiteness, Rigidity, and Topological Complexity
Information Theory.summary: A fixed finite binary Ising model has only finitely many admissible complex belief propagation fixed points, even at degenerate parameter values. Families of positive fixed points obtained by varying external fields can nevertheless have nontrivial topology. We study this distinction through the external-field projection. For a fixed field, we prove finiteness by bounding the pole orders of the magnetizations on a hypothetical complex solution curve. The generic degree on the support graph then bounds the total local multiplicity. A graph has a single smooth real line as its full positive response for every choice of positive couplings, base field, and strictly positive sweep direction exactly when it contains no two vertex-disjoint connected subgraphs of cycle rank at least two. Two such subgraphs suffice to create a circular component. For a plane obtained by varying two vertex fields, connected simple bipartite cubic graphs with one uniform coupling and a universal bound on the fixed fields realize every genus. The minimum number of vertices grows logarithmically in the genus, by a matching algebraic upper bound on Betti numbers. Finally, we certify the complete field discriminant of an eighteen-vertex product model and recover its torus component's genus from the counts of distinct roots on all field cells. The three main theorems, including the logarithmic size bounds, are formally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.
Information Theory.comment: 37 pages, 3 figures. Lean 4 formalization and interval certificates at https://github.com/ywatanabex/bp-response-geometry-lean

Probability.title: Moments of Magic Squares: Line-Sum Conditions, a Permutation Threshold, and Random Energies
Probability.summary: Every semi-magic square of order $n$ satisfies the axial moment identities $\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}j^m=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}i^m=M(n)\sum_jj^m$ for all $m\ge1$, where $M(n)=n(n^2+1)/2$. For real matrices the converse requires $1\le m\le n-1$, whereas for arrangements of $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ fewer moments suffice once $n\ge14$. We define the permutation threshold $k^*(n)$ as the least $k$ such that every arrangement satisfying these identities for $1\le m\le k$ is semi-magic. In terms of the column-sum deviations $γ_j$, the degree-$k$ conditions state that $\sum_jγ_jt^j$ is divisible by $(t-1)^{k+1}$, linking $k^*(n)$ to the Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem. While Schur's bound on real zeros gives $k^*(n)\le\sqrt{2(n-1)\log(n^4/4)}$, we prove the converse realisability bound $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt2-o(1))\sqrt n$ (and $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt6-o(1))\sqrt n$ when $4\mid n$) by perturbing semi-magic squares with complementary row pairs via horizontal swaps. We also show that $k^*(n)=n-1$ for $3\le n\le13$, $k^*(n)=n-2$ for $14\le n\le17$, and $k^*(n)\le n-3$ for $n\ge18$, and determine $k^*(n)$ for $18\le n\le40$ with computer assistance. Finally, at the $k=1$ level of the hierarchy, we specialise the Mantel--Hubert quadratic assignment variance formula to obtain exact means, variances, and limit laws under a uniform random arrangement for the full line-sum energy $E_{\mathrm{full}}$, for the four-term energy $E_4$ combining the first moments and the two diagonals, and for Loly's moment of inertia, and find that $|L_4|=14,639,440$ arrangements of order $4$ satisfy $E_4=0$.
Probability.comment: 29 pages, 3 figures, 4 tables; ancillary verification scripts, C enumerators, and exact lattice certificates included

Probability.title: A Tail-Respecting Splitting Numerical Scheme for Lévy-Driven SDEs With Superlinear Drifts
Probability.summary: We present an explicit numerical approximation scheme, denoted by $\{X^n\}$, for the effective simulation of solutions $X$ to a multivariate stochastic differential equation (SDE) with a superlinearly growing $κ$-dissipative drift, where $κ>1$, driven by a multiplicative heavy-tailed Lévy process that has a finite $p$-th moment, with $p>0$. We show that the strong $L^{p_X}$-convergence $\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\mathbf E \|X^n_t-X_t\|^{p_X}=\mathcal O (h_n^γ)$ holds for any $p_X\in (0,p+κ-1)$, which is exactly the range where the $p_X$-moment of the solution is known to be finite. Additionally, for any $p_X\in (0,p)$ we establish strong uniform convergence: $\mathbf E\sup_{t\in[0,T]} \|X^n_t-X_t\|^{p_X}=\mathcal{O} ( h_n^δ )$. In both cases we determine the convergence rates $γ$ and $δ$. In the special case of SDEs driven solely by a Brownian motion, our numerical scheme preserves super-exponential moments of the solution. The scheme $\{X^n\}$ is realized as a combination of a well-known Euler method with a Lie-Trotter type splitting technique.

Probability.title: Minimax Optimal Estimation of Transport-Growth Pairs in Unbalanced Optimal Transport
Probability.summary: Unbalanced optimal transport extends classical optimal transport to measures with different total masses, but statistical guarantees for estimation of the transport map and the growth map remain limited. We study unbalanced optimal transport with quadratic cost and Kullback-Leibler marginal penalties and argue that the natural target of estimation is a transport-growth pair. Consequently, we develop two estimators for the transport-growth pair under two setups: a nearest-neighbor estimator for transporting between general densities, and a kernel-based estimator for transporting between smooth densities. We prove that the kernel-based estimator achieves the minimax optimal rate up to a logarithmic factor by deriving a matching lower bound on the minimax risk. Our main technical contribution is a reduction of estimation to a stability bound on the unbalanced optimal transport value. This bound controls the transport map and growth map risks through the duality gap of the true dual potentials for the estimated measures. These results provide a statistical foundation for estimation of the transport-growth pair in unbalanced optimal transport.

Probability.title: Microscopic derivation of the classical KMS condition for one-dimensional Bose gases
Probability.summary: The Kubo--Martin--Schwinger (KMS) condition provides an intrinsic characterization of thermal equilibrium, both in quantum and classical statistical mechanics. In this work, we establish stability of the KMS condition through the quantum-to-classical limit for one-dimensional defocusing Bose gases. More precisely, we consider scaled quantum KMS states in the (mean-field) semiclassical regime and prove that every associated Wigner measure satisfies the classical KMS condition corresponding to the nonlinear Schrödinger Hamiltonian. This result extends to an infinite-dimensional setting an earlier derivation of the classical KMS condition for finite-dimensional Bose--Hubbard systems. It also provides a complementary perspective on the derivation of nonlinear Gibbs measures from many-body quantum statistical mechanics.

Probability.title: Sharp and explicit Berry--Esseen inequalities over convex sets
Probability.summary:
We establish finite-sample Berry--Esseen bounds over all convex subsets of $\R^{d}$ for sums of independent random vectors. The upper bounds give explicit dependence on the sample size, dimension, and moments of the summands, with numerical constants. They allow arbitrary dependence among coordinates and cover every real moment order from three onward. For i.i.d. summands, we determine the optimal dependence of the worst-case error on the sample size, the dimension, and the prescribed moment bound. We obtain matching lower bounds using bounded distributions that can be chosen independently of the sample size.
  The results reveal a fourth-moment threshold for normal approximation over convex sets. Four is the first moment order for which uniform bounds on the corresponding coordinate moments yield a worst-case error bound linear in the dimension. Bounds on higher moments give the same worst-case rate.
  The proof combines convexity with the addition of independent Gaussian noise to establish a normal approximation bound for Rademacher sums on Parseval frames. Random swaps with independent copies then allow us to apply this bound conditionally to general sums of independent random vectors.

Probability.title: Eigenvector Occupation Statistics and Extremes in the Rosenzweig-Porter Model
Probability.summary: We study the occupation probabilities $p_i=|u_i|^2$ of a normalized bulk eigenvector in the GUE Rosenzweig-Porter model $A_N=B_N+τ_NG_N$, with $τ_N^2=N^{1-γ}$ and $1<γ<2$. Conditioning on an eigenvalue at a regular bulk energy $E$ through the normalized one-eigenpair Kac-Rice law, we derive an exact finite-$N$ projective density and reduce its asymptotic analysis to a Hubbard-Stratonovich integral over $2\times2$ Hermitian matrices, which we evaluate by the saddle-point method. The resulting occupation field is governed by a self-consistent Lorentzian profile with effective resonant size $K_N(E)\asymp N^{2-γ}$ and local exponential fluctuations. We prove the asymptotics of all generalized inverse participation sums and identify a transition at $q=1/2$. We also obtain a two-branch thickened amplitude-counting spectrum. At the two ends of the occupation field we prove marked Poisson point-process limits: the largest components have Gumbel fluctuations, whereas the smallest component has an exponential limit on the scale $N^{-1-γ}$. Finally, for every fixed $q>0$ the largest component contributes an asymptotically vanishing fraction of the inverse participation sum, showing that these fixed-$q$ statistics do not freeze. The statements are quenched, uniformly on a high-probability regularity event for the diagonal disorder, and hence also hold in the annealed setting.

Probability.title: Distributional Limits of Empirical Codegree Processes in Sampled Networks
Probability.summary: We study fluctuations of empirical distributions of normalized codegrees under independent vertex sampling from deterministic or random weighted parent networks. We establish a quantitative multivariate normal approximation for sampled biclique counts. Under additional graph-limit and sparsity assumptions, we establish convergence of the finite-dimensional distributions of the empirical codegree process indexed by smooth test functions. We further establish functional convergence on Hölder balls, with a smoothness threshold depending on network sparsity and vertex sampling probabilities. We verify our assumptions for classes of graphon-generated random graphs and give counterexamples showing that the smoothness conditions cannot in general be weakened.

Probability.title: The Brown measure of a sum of two free nonselfadjoint random variables, one of which is R-diagonal
Probability.summary: Suppose that $X_1$ and $X_2$ are two $*$-free, possibly unbounded, random variables with Brown measures $μ_{X_1}$ and $μ_{X_2}$ respectively. Using properties of classic free additive convolution, we develop a method for calculating $μ_{X_1+X_2}$ when $X_2$ is $R$-diagonal. This method determines a density relative to Lebesgue measure on an open set whose closure equals the support of $μ_{X_{1}+X_{2}}$. We prove that $μ_{X_1+X_2}$ has no singular continuous part, that its density is strictly positive on this open set, and we determine the masses of its atoms. Explicit calculations are possible in several important cases. As an application, we combine our Fuglede--Kadison determinant formula with known subordination convergence results to calculate the limiting logarithmic potentials of free multiplicative random walks. We identify the limit with the Fuglede--Kadison determinant formula for free multiplicative Brownian motion previously proved by some PDE methods.

Probability.title: Sub-Diffusive Black--Scholes Model and Structure-Preserving Girsanov Transform
Probability.summary: We propose a sub-diffusive Black--Scholes model in which stock prices are governed by stochastic differential equations driven by sub-diffusions. The model captures the periods of low trading activity observed in bear markets, and it contains the classical Black--Scholes model as a special case. The sub-diffusive spot market is arbitrage-free but, in general, incomplete. We study the pricing of European contingent claims in this model. To this end, we establish a structure-preserving Girsanov transform for sub-diffusions. We use it to identify the minimal martingale measure of the model. This measure is the unique equivalent martingale measure under which the discounted stock prices are martingales driven by sub-diffusions with the same law as the original ones. Using this measure, we price every contingent claim in $L^p$ with $p>2$. For each such claim, we construct a replicating strategy that is mean self-financing and minimizes the local risk, and whose value process gives the price process of the claim. Finally, we derive an explicit formula for the price of a European call option. We show that this price solves a partial differential equation with a fractional derivative in time, which we call the time-fractional Black--Scholes equation.

Probability.title: Permutations, Pattern Covers, Posets and Positivity, Part II: Regular Pattern Packings and Moment Sequences
Probability.summary:
We prove that broad families of regular pattern packings are enumerated by moments of probability measures on $[0,\infty)$. A packing prescribes occurrences of a consecutive permutation pattern at equally spaced positions, with successive occurrences overlapping and together covering the permutation. This regularity underlies the structure theory for the associated pattern-packing posets that we developed in Part I (arXiv:2610.29846).
  We obtain moment representations for all two-level shifted-grid families of Part I and all overlap-one patterns whose first and last letters differ by one or two. For families whose posets are trees with a unique minimum or maximum and overlap at most half the pattern length, positivity instead holds after finitely many initial terms of the enumerating sequence have been discarded. Our proofs develop further enumeration formulas and combine probabilistic constructions with total nonnegativity and weighted paths, yielding explicit laws or continued fractions in several cases.
  Although a previously conjectured universal moment property fails, our results establish positivity for all packing sequences associated with patterns of length at most four and all but one of the distinct sequences arising from patterns of length five. Extensive numerical evidence suggests that the remaining sequence is also a moment sequence. These results lead us to formulate refined conjectures for all overlap-one patterns and for the shifted-grid families of Part I with arbitrarily many levels.

Probability.title: Control policies for a two-stage queueing system with parallel and single server options
Probability.summary:
We study a two-stage queueing system attended by two flexible servers. Once a server begins to interact with a job, it remains attached to its job throughout both stages of service. After completing the first-stage service, the server chooses between two second-stage options. Option 1 sends the server-job pair to a parallel-service station where both servers may operate simultaneously; therefore, the server immediately begins the second-stage service on its job. Option 2 routes the pair to a single-service station that admits at most one server-job pair into service at a time. While we consider the complete range of parameters, the usual reason for choosing Option 2 is that jobs may receive higher-quality (faster and/or lower expected cost) service. If the single-service station is occupied, the pair must wait together until the station becomes available.
  The decision-making scenario is modeled via a Markov decision process formulation of a clearing system with holding costs at each station. Focusing on cases with a large initial queue, we fully characterize the structural properties of an optimal control policy based on the relationship between the service rates at the downstream stations. A numerical study highlights the significance of understanding the structure of the optimal policy by comparing its performance against several natural heuristic policies.

Probability.title: Brown Measures and Spectral Convergence for Arbitrary GUE Polynomials
Probability.summary:
For arbitrary noncommutative polynomials in independent GUE matrices, we prove that the empirical eigenvalue measure converges weakly in probability to the Brown measure of the corresponding polynomial in free semicircular variables. We also prove convergence of the entire eigenvalue set in Hausdorff distance and convergence of the spectral radius, both in probability. Equivalently, these matrix conclusions hold for arbitrary $*$-polynomials in independent complex Ginibre matrices. Independently, we prove that the support of the Brown measure of every polynomial in free semicircular variables equals its operator spectrum. The proof of weak convergence combines a criterion based on the second moment of the Brown measure with complex Gaussian rotation and convexity. The support theorem uses linearization and rigidity of matrix Dyson equations.
  We also prove absolute continuity for nonconstant polynomials without adjoints in free circular variables. A matrix Dyson equation recovers Brown measures of arbitrary semicircular polynomials through regularized logarithmic potentials. For drift-corrected nondegenerate elliptic free random walks, it yields quantitative convergence of potentials in the interior of the limiting domain and weak convergence of Brown measures to that of free multiplicative Brownian motion.

Probability.title: A Hoare Logic for Continuous-Time Stochastic Processes
Probability.summary:
Programming language researchers have developed a wide array of tools to reason about probabilistic programs, but it remains unclear how to apply these proof techniques to continuous-time stochastic processes. To bridge this gap, we propose a verification method for properties of continuous-time stochastic processes by reasoning about them as standard programs.
  To demonstrate our approach, we define a continuous semantics for a probabilistic imperative language $\mathrm{pWhile}^{\mathrm{dt}}$ by taking the Kuratowski limit of the standard semantics, which collects limit points of the standard program semantics as the time-step approaches zero. Then, we present a Hoare-style logic that uses loop invariants and decreasing functions to verify properties of continuous programs. To establish soundness, we identify a broad class of assertions that are preserved from the standard semantics to the continuous semantics. To demonstrate our approach, we verify properties of ten continuous-time stochastic processes modeled in $\mathrm{pWhile}^{\mathrm{dt}}$, including variants of Brownian motion and a stochastic hybrid system.

Probability.title: Global Asymptotics of a Toda Soliton Condensate with Random Scattering Data
Probability.summary: We study a dense $N$-soliton condensate for the infinite Toda lattice in the limit $N \to \infty$. In contrast to previous mathematical studies of soliton gases where the norming constants are assumed to be deterministic or infinitesimal, we consider initial scattering data where both the discrete eigenvalues and the norming constants are independent random variables. The norming constants $γ_j$ are allowed to be arbitrarily large under a mild moment condition $\mathbb{E}[γ_j^ν] < \infty$ ($ν> 1$). Our main result is divided into two parts. First, we develop a probabilistic Riemann--Hilbert framework to show that the system self-averages: despite large, independent fluctuations in the initial data, the random Toda lattice variables converge deterministically to an effective continuum model at a polynomial rate $\mathcal{O}(N^{-δ})$ for $0 < δ< 1/2$. Second, by performing the Deift--Zhou nonlinear steepest descent analysis of the continuum problem, we obtain the complete leading-order macroscopic description of the lattice across the entire space-time plane. The solution decomposes into five distinct finite-gap regimes, characterized explicitly by modulated elliptic and genus-2 waves with an error of order $\mathcal{O}(1/\ln N)$. In contrast to the straight characteristic rays typical of standard soliton gas limits, the interfaces separating these five macroscopic regimes in the space-time plane are genuinely non-linear curves; in particular, the boundary of the modulated genus-2 region is completely non-linear. Finally, under our assumptions, we establish the Nonlinear Dispersion Relations for the Toda soliton condensate and prove that the macroscopic ensemble averages are determined by the soliton gas density of states.

Probability.title: A Non-Markovian Approach to a Stochastic Rumor Dynamics with Cognitive Deliberation
Probability.summary: We introduce a non-Markovian rumor model on a complete graph of $n$ vertices, integrating the classical interactional framework of Daley and Kendall (1964) with modern cognitive insights into misinformation. Unlike traditional Markovian models, our approach incorporates a deliberation delay -- a decision-making window where individuals evaluate information before committing to dissemination or refutation. We establish a Functional Law of Large Numbers (FLLN) and a Functional Central Limit Theorem (FCLT) to characterize the asymptotic behavior and diffusion-scaled fluctuations of the process.
Probability.comment: Title changed. Model, proofs, and introduction significantly revised and rectified

Probability.title: Staircase phase transitions for the extreme eigenvalues of heavy-tailed sample correlation matrices
Probability.summary: We establish phase transitions in the first-order asymptotics of the largest and smallest nonzero eigenvalues of high-dimensional sample correlation matrices formed from data with i.i.d. centered real entries of finite variance, allowing an infinite fourth moment. Because of self-normalization, spectral outliers are driven by collisions of large entries in distinct rows of a common column rather than by individual large entries. The resulting phase transitions depend jointly on the aspect ratio and the entry tail, producing staircase boundaries in the phase diagram. We prove convergence to the corresponding Marčenko--Pastur edges in subcritical regimes and to deterministic outlier levels in supercritical regimes. In critical regimes, Poisson limits for the point processes of spectral outliers and nondegenerate limiting laws for the extreme eigenvalues are established.
Probability.comment: This version merges the original manuscript with arXiv:2609.15731v1 to give a unified treatment of both spectral edges

Probability.title: Spanning triangulations in random graphs
Probability.summary: In 1991 Bollobás and Frieze found the threshold for the emergence of a spanning triangulation of a triangle in the binomial random graph, up to a logarithmic factor. In this paper, we find the threshold probability for the emergence of a spanning triangulation of a $k$-gon for any $3\leq k\leq n$, up to a constant factor.

Probability.title: Continuum hierarchical Cannings process: I. Construction, duality and dichotomy
Probability.summary: We construct spatial measure-valued Cannings processes on the \emph{continuum} hierarchical group $Ω_N^\infty$ of order $N\in\N$ (an uncountable topological group with an ultrametric distance). These processes arise as the continuum-space limit of spatial Cannings processes on the \emph{discrete} hierarchical group $Ω_N$ of order $N\in\N$ (a countable topological group with an ultrametric distance) analysed in \cite{GHKK14}. On $Ω_N$, each site represents the \emph{geographic location} of a colony of individuals, each carrying a \emph{type} drawn from a compact type space $\K$, and the state in each colony is a probability measure on $\K$ describing the type distribution in that colony in the large-colony-size limit of individual-based models. The continuum-space processes on $Ω_N^\infty$ take values in the set of locally finite measures on $Ω_N^\infty \times \K$ and are to be thought of as describing a population of individuals, each equipped with a geographic location in $Ω_N^\infty$ and a type in $\K$, and each being subjected to \emph{migration} and three mechanisms of \emph{resampling}: (1) Fleming-Viot resampling at single sites; (2) Cannings resampling at single sites; (3) Cannings resampling and uniform reshuffling in balls around single sites (corresponding to consecutive hierarchical levels). The reshuffling adds to the migration, resulting in an \emph{effective migration} that is the superposition of the two relocation mechanisms.

Probability.title: Deterministic Principal Ideals of Dependent Random Operators
Probability.summary: We classify the algebraic principal ideals of alternating quadratic random operators under dimension-free two-sided curvature bounds. For the centered evaluation of a Hilbert two-form, an explicit covariance compensator determines the principal ideal after every fixed compact perturbation. For fixed spectral choices, the compensator is a compact linear function of the full covariance with explicit finite-dimensional approximation bounds; its class modulo the independent Gaussian ideal is intrinsic. For fixed spatial weights of rank at least two and a trace-class kernel, all attainable principal ideals form an exact order interval. Every intermediate ideal is realized by a Gaussian covariance arbitrarily close to the identity while each row retains its standard Gaussian law. For these spatial weights, trace class is also the exact kernel domain for raw evaluation under every law in the curvature class. The proof uses a conditional-residual criterion for linear operators, polarization, and finite-rank approximation. Applications include Wiener area and dependent matrices with doubly monotone variance weights. A logarithmic example separates principal ideals with identical membership in every Schatten class.

Probability.title: Double-Scaling Limits for Monitored Haar Products
Probability.summary: We study products of independent Haar matrices interspersed with a fixed corank-one projection. As the matrix dimension $N$ and product length $L$ grow with $L/N\toτ$, we prove that the empirical distribution of squared singular values converges to the free multiplicative Poisson law with $S$-transform $S(z)=\exp(τ/(1+z))$, for both the unitary and orthogonal ensembles. Lagrange inversion yields its moments explicitly, proving Beenakker's conjectured Erlang formula for every moment order.
Probability.comment: 20 pages. Substantially revised, with a new title and reorganized exposition. Added proofs of convergence of all transmission moments and empirical spectral distributions in the double-scaling regime for both unitary and orthogonal ensembles, establishing the conjectured moment formula for every order

Probability.title: Smallest gaps of the two-dimensional Coulomb gas
Probability.summary: We consider the two-dimensional Coulomb gas with a general potential at the determinantal temperature, or equivalently, the eigenvalues of random normal matrices. We prove that the smallest gaps between particles are typically of order $n^{-3/4}$, and that the associated joint point process of gap locations and gap sizes, after rescaling the gaps by $n^{3/4}$, converges to a Poisson point process. As a consequence, we show that the $k$-th smallest rescaled gap has a limiting density proportional to $x^{4k-1}e^{-\frac{\mathcal{J}}{4}x^{4}}$, where $\mathcal{J}=π^{2}\int ρ(z)^{3}d^{2}z$ and $ρ$ is the density of the equilibrium measure. This generalizes a result of Shi and Jiang beyond the quadratic potential.

Probability.title: Diophantine conditions for absolute continuity of projections for self-similar measures
Probability.summary: We prove that every projection of a planar self-similar measure $μ$ is equivalent to Lebesgue measure on its support if the rotations satisfy a simultaneous Diophantine condition with exponent $τ$ and $μ$ has finite $s$-energy for some $1+2τ\le s<2$. Under strong separation, we prove the fibre measures have exact dimension $\dim_Hμ-1$. For self-similar sets $E$ with $\dim_H E>1+2τ$, the same rotation condition implies uniformly positive projection lengths and fibres of dimension $\dim_H E-1$ at Lebesgue-almost every point of each image without separation assumptions. The absolute continuity and fibre dimension theorems extend to non-coordinate projections of products under a joint Diophantine condition with exponent $τ$ on the logarithmic contraction ratios. These imply for all self-similar sets $K,L\subset\mathbb R$ satisfying this condition and $\dim_HK+\dim_HL>1+2τ$, every sum $uK+L$, $u\ne 0$, has positive length, and $\dim_H(L\cap(y-uK))=\dim_HK+\dim_HL-1$ for Leb. a.e. $y\in uK+L$. The proof combines the $L^1$ Gaussian smoothing approach used in the higher dimensional case with averaging at random stopping scales with a Brownian martingale bound using Itô calculus.

Probability.title: Permutation symmetries and characteristic polynomials
Probability.summary: We compute certain multilinear functionals of permutation-invariant random matrices, following the work of Marcus and Geneson. As an application, we derive formulae for the average characteristic polynomial of the sum and the product of permutation-invariant random matrices.

Probability.title: The Paley--Wiener excess and a local law for the ${\rm Sine}_β$ process
Probability.summary: The main result of this paper is the proof that the Paley--Wiener excess of the ${\rm Sine}_β$ process almost surely equals $\lfloor \sqrt{2/β}\rfloor$ for all $β>0$. We also derive the loop equations for the resolvent of the ${\rm Sine}_β$ point process and use them to obtain accurate bounds on the moments of the associated Stieltjes transform.

Probability.title: The singular Gaussian scaling limit for a tagged particle in the infinite-dimensional Dyson model at $β=2$
Probability.summary: We prove a logarithmic central limit theorem for a tagged particle in infinite-dimensional Dyson Brownian motion at inverse temperature $β=2$, starting from the sine$_2$ point process. The fluctuation is of order $\sqrt{\log t}$, which is subdiffusive and substantially slower than the polynomial fluctuations of classical short-range interacting particle systems, reflecting the rigidity induced by long-range logarithmic repulsion. We further identify the scaling limit as the singular Gaussian field corresponding to the zero-Hurst parameter, which provides a realisation of the singular Gaussian field as a scaling limit of a tagged particle raised by Dürr, Goldstein and Lebowitz (Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 38 (1985)).
Probability.comment: V2: added two references of Dandekar-Krapivsky-Mallick and streamlined minor presentations

Probability.title: A phase transition for the cokernels of random band matrices over the p-adic integers
Probability.summary: Let $\mathbf{B}_n$ be an $n\times n$ Haar-uniform band matrix over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ with band width $w_n$. We prove that $\text{cok}(\mathbf{B}_n)$ has Cohen-Lenstra limiting distribution if and only if \[\lim_{n\to\infty} \left(w_n-\log_p(n)\right)=+\infty.\]

Probability.title: Exponential mixing for the randomized two-vortex model
Probability.summary: This paper investigates the mixing of passive scalars advected by a randomized two-vortex model on $\mathbb{T}^2$, in which the vortices interact through a regularized Biot--Savart kernel and are driven by independent Brownian motions. We establish quenched exponential mixing for the Lagrangian flow, characterized by the exponential correlation decay of mean-zero $H^s$ observables. The proof proceeds by establishing ergodicity of the associated two-point Markov process. We combine a uniform contraction estimate with controllability arguments to verify the Lyapunov drift and minorization conditions, allowing us to apply Harris-type theorem.

Probability.title: Probabilistic counting of labelled trees with prescribed vertical edge profile
Probability.summary: The vertical edge profile of a labelled plane tree $t$ is the collection of integers counting the number of oriented edges from label $i$ to label $j$ for every possible pairs of labels $(i, j)$. In a previous work by the second author, it was shown that a process constructed from the vertical edge profile forms a Markov chain for a wide class of models of random labelled plane trees where edge label increments are constrained to lie in $\{-1, 0, 1\}$. The purpose of this paper is twofold. First, we continue the study of Markov properties of the vertical edge profile. In particular, we derive general formulas for the transition kernel and the initial distribution of a class of Markov chains related to the vertical edge profile. Second, we apply these results to the probabilistic enumeration of trees with a prescribed vertical edge profile. These applications yield a unified probabilistic derivation of several enumeration formulas. In particular, we recover some results established Bousquet-Mélou and Chapuy for binary trees and Cayley trees. These enumeration formulas admit a remarkable factorized form, already noted in previous works. The probabilistic methods developed here explain this phenomenon by showing that these factorizations arise naturally from the Markov structure underlying the vertical edge profile.

Probability.title: Mean-field BSDEs with jumps under quadratic-exponential growth
Probability.summary: This paper studies the well-posedness of mean-field backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs, for short) with Poisson jumps, where the generator has quadratic growth with respect to $Z$ and exponential growth with respect to $U$, where $(Y,Z,U)$ denotes the solution of this BSDE. First, we prove the existence and the uniqueness of local solutions to mean-field backward stochastic differential equations with jumps (BSDEJs, for short) by using a fixed-point argument. Then, based on these local results, we discuss the solvability of global solutions in the following two cases: in the first one, the generator has linear growth with respect to $Y$ and the corresponding marginal distribution $μ_1$; and in the second one, the generator has subquadratic growth with respect to the marginal distribution $μ_2$ and linear growth with respect to the marginal distribution $μ_3$, corresponding to $Z$ and $U$, respectively. Finally, by employing a Girsanov transformation we establish a comparison theorem for mean-field BSDEJs under quadratic-exponential growth conditions.

Probability.title: Phase transition for the smallest eigenvalue of high-dimensional sample correlation matrices
Probability.summary: We study the smallest nonzero eigenvalue of the sample correlation matrix $\mathbf{R}_n$ formed from a $p_n \times n$ data matrix with i.i.d. real entries $ξ$ of mean zero and unit variance, in the high-dimensional regime $p_n / n \to φ\in (0, \infty) \setminus \{1\}$. In the tall regime $φ> 1$, we prove almost-sure convergence of $λ_n (\mathbf{R}_n)$ to the lower Marčenko--Pastur edge $λ_- = (1 - \sqrtφ)^2$ without additional moment assumptions. In the wide regime $φ< 1$, we establish a phase transition at the third-order tail scale. If $t^3 \mathbb{P}\{\lvert ξ\rvert > t\} \to 0$ as $t \to \infty$, the smallest eigenvalue $λ_{p_n} (\mathbf{R}_n)$ converges in probability to $λ_-$. While if $t^3 \mathbb{P}\{\lvert ξ\rvert > t\} \to \infty$, then $λ_{p_n} (\mathbf{R}_n)$ converges in probability to zero. At the critical scale $t^3 \mathbb{P}\{\lvert ξ\rvert > t\} \to κ\in (0, \infty)$, the point process of eigenvalues in the lower gap $(0, λ_-)$ converges in distribution to a Poisson random measure with explicit intensity. In this critical regime, we also identify the nondegenerate limiting distribution of $λ_{p_n} (\mathbf{R}_n)$, which has a continuous density on $(0, λ_-)$ and a positive atom at $λ_-$.
Probability.comment: This manuscript has been merged into the revised version of arXiv:2610.06731.

Probability.title: Sampling Colorings on $G(n, d/n)$ via Glauber Dynamics
Probability.summary:
We study the mixing time of Glauber dynamics for sampling uniformly from the proper $q$-colorings of sparse Erdős-Rényi random graphs $G(n,d/n)$. Our main result establishes that with probability $1-o(1)$ over the draw of $G$, Glauber dynamics is rapidly mixing for every $q\geq d+d^{1/2+\varepsilon}$, given any fixed $0<\varepsilon\leq1/2$ and any sufficiently large fixed $d$. In particular, the surplus of colors above $d$ is sublinear and close to $\sqrt{d}$. The achieved color range therefore approaches the tree uniqueness threshold and improves over the previously best achievable number of colors $q > 1.763 d$ due to Efthymiou, Hayes, Stefankovic, and Vigoda [SODA 2018]. Moreover, our mixing-time bound is $O(n^{2+o_d(1)})$, and hence almost quadratic as $d\rightarrow\infty$.
  Our proof is based on establishing a spectral gap for block dynamics resulting from a suitable decomposition of $G(n,d/n)$ into blocks and singleton vertices, ensuring that every high-degree vertex is encapsulated within a block. Our main technical contribution is a novel way of establishing rapid mixing of block dynamics via an integrated Bochner-Bakry-Émery approach, which we expect to have applications beyond sampling colorings. We further devise a new block decomposition of $G(n,d/n)$ that strengthens and simplifies similar constructions used in previous work. Finally, to compare block and Glauber dynamics, we establish a novel recursive separator decomposition of tree-like blocks, together with a coupling argument that avoids the need for nearly uniform color marginals at vertices adjacent to hubs. This comparison argument might be of independent interest.

Probability.title: Self-organized regime switching in null-recurrent dynamics
Probability.summary: Based on discrete observations $X_0,X_Δ,\dots, X_{nΔ}$ for $Δ=n^{-γ}$ with $γ\in [0,1)$ of the null-recurrent dynamic $dX_t = σ(X_t)dW_t$ with a Brownian motion $W$ and $σ(x)=α\mathbb{1}\{x<ρ\} + β\mathbb{1}\{x\geq ρ\}$, we derive rate of convergence and limiting distribution of the profile MLE for $ρ$. This includes low-frequency asymptotics ($γ=0$) for which the observations form a null-recurrent Markov chain. The derived non-standard limit is the argsup over a doubly stochastic drifted Poisson process explicitly involving the local time of oscillating Brownian motion. Its dependence on $ρ$ as well as the unknown volatility levels $α$ and $β$ is shown to be continuous w.r.t. the topology of weak convergence, enabling statistical inference. Whereas this limit is independent of the sampling frequency, the profile MLE's rate of convergence equals $n^{-(1+γ)/2}$ and is proven to be minimax optimal. The surprising idea of the proof of the limit theorem is to relate the long-term behavior of the null-recurrent Markov chain to the infill asymptotics on a fixed time interval. Indeed, in the very special case that $(X_t)_{t\geq 0}$ is started in the true parameter $X_0=ρ_0$, the process $(X_t-ρ_0)_{t\geq 0}$ is shown to possess a desirable distributional self-similarity. On basis of the strong Markov property, the artificial constellation of starting in $ρ_0$ is finally overcome by a coupling argument.

Probability.title: Large deviations, optimal trajectories and conservation of momenta in generalised Jackson networks
Probability.summary:
We study properties of optimal trajectories for
  the quasipotential that governs large deviations of queue lengths in generalised Jackson networks (GJN). The trajectories are shown to satisfy Hamilton equations. The Hamiltonian is identified. Optimal trajectories and associated costs are found for networks with two and three stations. A conservation law for adjoint variables
  is discovered to the effect that certain components are maintained along an optimal trajectory. A process is proposed for finding optimal trajectories and computing their costs
  in general GJN.

Probability.title: Pathwise solutions of the stochastic Burgers equation driven by a multiplicative Hermite noise
Probability.summary: We study the viscous Burgers equation on the real line perturbed by a multiplicative noise $σ(u)\dot{Z}_t$, where $Z$ is a Hermite process of order $q\ge1$ and Hurst index $H\in(1/2,1)$; the case $q=1$ is fractional Brownian motion and $q=2$ is the Rosenblatt process. The stochastic term is a Young integral and the equation is solved path by path. A transformation of Doss-Sussmann type reduces it to a parabolic equation with random coefficients and quadratic growth in the gradient, for which we prove a maximum principle and a gradient estimate of Bernstein type on short time windows. We obtain global existence and uniqueness, the pathwise bound $|u(t,x)|\le\|u_0\|_\infty+\|σ\|_\infty|Z_t|$, and a Wong-Zakai type result without correction term. All moments are finite and $\mathbb{E}\exp(λ\sup_x|u(t,x)|^{2/q})<\infty$ for small $λ$. For the Rosenblatt process with $σ\geσ_0>0$, $\mathbb{E}\,e^{λu(t,x)}$ is finite for small $λ$ and infinite for $λσ_0t^H\geθ_H$, an explicit spectral constant, while the left tail is sub-Gaussian. We show that the temporal Hölder exponent $H$ is optimal, identify the limits of the power variations of $t\mapsto u(t,x)$, and deduce consistent estimators of $H$ and of the noise intensity from one path observed at one spatial point. For $q=2$ we relate the pathwise solution to a Skorokhod formulation through the forward/Skorokhod correction formula of Čoupek, Duncan and Pasik-Duncan.
Probability.comment: 38 pages. v2: complete rewrite, which corrects errors in v1. The noise is now a Hermite process of arbitrary order, the stochastic integral is a pathwise Young integral, and the solution is global. The results on moments, optimal time regularity, power variations and parameter estimation are new

Probability.title: On transition probabilities for the ASEP on the half-line
Probability.summary: We study the asymmetric simple exclusion process on the half-line with particle insertion and no particle removal at the boundary. We point out that there exist two distinct multiple contour integral formulas for the transition probability between two finite particle configurations containing the same number of particles. We recall one of these formulas from the literature and prove a second, new formula by showing that it satisfies the evolution equation using a coordinate Bethe ansatz calculation and verify that the initial condition is implemented by the contour integrals. As an application we sum this formula over all final configurations and obtain an integral formula for the probability that the number of particles is conserved up to a given time. The proofs use symmetric rational functions and their properties together with contour deformations.

Probability.title: An extension of Stein's method incorporating dependence
Probability.summary: We extend Stein's method to include a prescribed dependence with respect to an auxiliary random variable, for conditional laws for which Stein characterizations do exist. This considerably extends the range of applications of Stein's method. The characterization we derive subsumes the case of independent random variables. Using the Malliavin calculus, we illustrate our extension on the example of a conditionally Gaussian/Beta-distributed random variable.

Probability.title: Local Search with Correlated Randomness
Probability.summary:
The running-time distribution of a randomized algorithm is computed under independent randomness, but independence is rarely what a source guarantees. We study sources $ν$ with $ν[w]\le DP[w]^s$ for every finite prefix $w$ of the tape, where $P$ is an independent reference law, $0<s\le1$, and $D\ge1$; individual choices may be predictable, even determined by the past. The worst-case probability of any closed tape event $E$ is exactly $\min\{1,DC_s(E)\}$, where $C_s(E)$ is the infimum cost of covering $E$ by prefixes of varying depth. This tree max-flow/min-cut identity makes worst-case probabilities exact and optimizable.
  Three applications follow. In scheduling, $n$ tasks on one machine are each retried until the next random symbol lies in its success set; every schedule has the same makespan distribution under independent randomness, yet under our constraint two fixed orders miss a linear deadline with worst-case probabilities $1$ and $\exp[-Θ(n)]$, and a static priority rule is optimal at every deadline. For the standard local walk on a $k$-CNF with an assignment satisfying a majority of each clause, we find the sharp source threshold $s_*$: below it, on some instances one admissible source forces nontermination for every clause selection; at it, with fixed $D$, the expected number of flips is at most cubic in the initial distance, against linear under independence, with matching instances at distances up to a constant fraction of the number of variables; a fixed margin above it restores linear dependence. For noisy predecessor search with prefix-bounded comparison errors, verified backtracking attains any prescribed error probability at or above a source threshold whose sharpness we leave open, with the same cubic-to-linear query bounds. Restarting on the shared tape restores exponential tails exactly when the nontermination event has a prefix cover of cost below one.

Probability.title: On the Concavity of Rényi Entropy and Rényi Entropy Power along Heat Flows on Manifolds
Probability.summary: In this paper, we establish the concavity of Rényi entropy and Rényi entropy power along heat flow on Euclidean space of arbitrary dimension, for Rényi orders $α\in[1,2]$. More generally, we prove the corresponding result along the heat flow generated by the Witten Laplacian on complete Riemannian manifolds under a suitable curvature-dimension condition. Our argument builds on novel functional inequalities that were recently developed for the study of Tsallis entropy concavity along the heat flow. We extend both these inequalities and the resulting concavity theorem from the Euclidean setting to the Riemannian manifold setting. In addition, we establish the complete monotonicity of Tsallis entropy of order $2$ along the heat flow and derive its spectral decomposition.

Probability.title: The Zaporozhets-Tarasov Conjecture on Mean Distances
Probability.summary: For a convex body $K \subset \mathbb R^d$ let $Δ(K)$ be the expected distance between two independent uniform points of $K$, and let $θ(K)$ be the corresponding expectation for normalized surface measure on $\partial K$. The Zaporozhets-Tarasov conjecture asserts $Δ(K) \le θ(K)$. We prove this conjecture in case $d=2$. In addition, we give a six-vertex convex polytope in $\mathbb R^3$ for which the reverse strict inequality holds, and obtain counterexamples in every dimension $d \ge 3$ by taking products with segments.
Probability.comment: Split off Section 5 from previous version to make it a separate manuscript

Probability.title: Noise estimation of SDE from a single data trajectory
Probability.summary: In this paper, we propose a pathwise data-driven framework for model discovery of stochastic differential equations (SDEs) from a single trajectory, without requiring the ergodicity or stationary assumption on the underlying continuous process. By combining (stochastic) Taylor expansions with Girsanov transformations, and using the drift function's initial value as input, we construct drift estimators while simultaneously recovering the model noise. This drift is unique up to the fixed underlying Brownian sample path, in line with pathwise unique Rough-Smooth decomposition. This allows us to recover the underlying $\mathbb P$ Brownian motion increments for the observer path $ω$. Building on these estimators, we introduce the first stochastic Sparse Identification of Stochastic Differential Equation (SSISDE) algorithm, capable of identifying the governing SDE dynamics from a single observed trajectory without requiring ergodicity or stationarity. To validate the proposed approach, we conduct numerical experiments with both linear and quadratic drift-diffusion functions. Among these, the Black-Scholes SDE is included as a representative case of a system that does not satisfy ergodicity or stationarity.

Probability.title: An optimal local theory for reaction-diffusion equations driven by non-trace-class noise
Probability.summary: We study local well-posedness for a class of stochastic reaction-diffusion equations driven by multiplicative, possibly colored, noise. The interaction between rough stochastic forcing and polynomial nonlinearities naturally leads to solutions with low spatial regularity, making the treatment of the nonlinear terms delicate. Our main contribution is a general local existence and uniqueness theory for SPDEs with rough noise and highly irregular initial data. The framework also yields new results in standard noise regimes, including trace-class noise and space-time white noise. We identify the critical initial-data spaces for a wide range of nonlinearities, and we establish instantaneous parabolic regularization, general blow-up criteria, and sufficient conditions for positivity preservation. We apply the abstract theory to several prototypical models, including the stochastic Allen-Cahn, Burgers, Fisher-KPP, and coupled Gray-Scott equations. Finally, in the one-dimensional space-time white-noise setting, we combine our local theory with existing global a priori results in a highly singular regime.
Probability.comment: 50 pages; Corrected some mistakes and typographical errors identified with the assistance of LLM

Probability.title: Blowup for the multiplicative stochastic heat equation with superlinear drift
Probability.summary: We consider the stochastic heat equation with multiplicative white noise: $\partial_t u =\partial_x^2u + b(u) +σ(u) \dot W$, both on $[0,1]$ and $\mathbb R$. In the case of $[0,1]$ we show that the finite Osgood criterion on $b$ is a necessary and sufficient condition for finite-time blowup, under fairly general conditions on $σ$. In the case of $\mathbb R$ we show instantaneous explosion when we start with initial profile $u_0\equiv 1$. Our work introduces a novel approach that not only extends the work of [12] which dealt with bounded $σ$, but also provides an alternate route to proving such results. A key ingredient is a comparison result which shows that the solution on $\mathbb R$ stays above the corresponding solution on $[0,1]$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions.
Probability.comment: Major revision. Added Theorem 1.3(1); some of the calculations wherein are AI-inspired. Improved the exposition in accordance with many comments

Probability.title: Geometry and Stochastic Analysis of Flow and Diffusion Models: A Survey
Probability.summary: Flow-based and diffusion-based models have become the principal means of learning and sampling high-dimensional probability distributions, from images and video to proteins, molecules and physical fields, and increasingly language. Each carries a simple law to the law of the data along a curve of probability measures, and behind the variety of their names lie three geometries, those of the state space on which the data live, of the space of probability measures through which the curve passes, and of the space of paths traced by the generating process. A single analytic idea runs through the subject. Every score identity used to train a diffusion model is an integration by parts, on the noise, on the data or on Wiener space, and Malliavin calculus extends this to nonlinear and infinite-dimensional diffusions. We develop these foundations with full definitions and follow them through normalising flows, flow matching and few-step maps, diffusion models and their convergence theory, conditioning, Schrödinger bridges and stochastic control, and their extension to manifolds, Lie groups, discrete and function spaces and jump processes. We close with statistical physics, renormalisation and, more speculatively, holography, in which the radial direction of anti-de Sitter space can play the role of flow time. A table of the main methods and a collection of open problems complete the survey.

Probability.title: Permutons
Probability.summary: Permutons are limit structures for large permutations. Intrinsically, a permuton is a familiar mathematical object: a probability measure on the unit square with uniform marginals. The compact space of permutons completes the set of permutations of all sizes under a natural topology; each permuton is not only a limit of permutations but also a generator of random permutations. Since their (relatively recent) discovery as a tool for understanding the behavior of large (possibly random) permutations, permutons have proved remarkably fruitful, with dozens of fascinating connections to combinatorics and probability. We review the fundamentals of permutons, sometimes providing new, shorter proofs, and give an account of some of their myriad applications. The survey concludes with a long list of open problems. An extensive -- but not comprehensive -- bibliography is appended.

Probability.title: Limits of Stochastic Semigroups and Block-Triangular Majorisation
Probability.summary: We investigate limits of semigroups of stochastic matrices defined by their invariant distribution. Given probability vectors $q(β)$ depending on a parameter $β$, we introduce a notion of convergence as $β\to\infty$ for the corresponding semigroups of $q(β)$-preserving stochastic matrices and investigate the structure of the resulting limit. In general, the limiting semigroup differs from the semigroup preserving the limiting distribution, showing that these two operations do not commute. We develop a general framework for such limiting semigroups and study in detail the case in which the invariant distributions are Gibbs vectors at inverse temperature $β$. In that case, the limiting semigroup consists of block-upper-triangular stochastic matrices subject to additional substochasticity constraints. We characterise and enumerate their extremal elements and determine the preorder on probability vectors induced by the action of the semigroup. The resulting notion of Block-Triangular majorisation interpolates between ordinary majorisation and upper triangular (also known as unordered) majorisation. We show that it is completely characterised by a finite family of monotones and analyse the corresponding behaviour of R{é}nyi $α$-entropies as $β\to\infty$.
Probability.comment: 19 pages, 1 figure, Major revision with presentation improved and typos fixed; Comments welcome!

Probability.title: Anomalous regularity and scaling limit by rough transport noise for stochastic 2D fluid models on the torus
Probability.summary: We consider the stochastic 2D Euler and mSQG equations on the torus, with $L^2$ initial data and driven by rough Kraichnan transport noise, for which we construct weak solutions enjoying anomalous regularity and dissipation properties. Moreover, we show that weak solutions in this regularity class are pathwise unique, thus establishing probabilistically strong well-posedness. We further obtain the scaling limit from these equations to the deterministic Navier--Stokes/mSQG equations, with respect to positive Sobolev norms. The proofs rest on the analysis of energy spectrum of the vorticity and on a uniform weighted discrete Poincaré inequality on the lattice, the latter being crucial for making the positive norms accessible.

Probability.title: Pairwise correlation bounds for the random-cluster model with cluster weight at most one
Probability.summary: We establish quantitative bounds on pairwise edge correlations for the random-cluster model with cluster weight $q\in[0,1]$ on arbitrary finite connected graphs. We give two explicit bounds that retain the dependence on the activities of the two specified edges and hold uniformly over the activities of all remaining edges. We also obtain a refinement of one of these bounds using connectivity information from the graph with the two specified edges removed. These results sharpen the bound obtained by a direct application of Lorentzian polynomial theory. At $q=0$, the model is supported on connected spanning subgraphs. In particular, for the uniform probability measure on these subgraphs, the joint inclusion probability of two distinct edges is at most $10/9$ times the product of their marginal inclusion probabilities.

Probability.title: On fractal minimizers and potentials of occupation measures
Probability.summary: We highlight two basic types of variational problems and prove the existence of fractal minimizers through the direct method in the calculus of variations. By design these minimizers are Hölder curves or Hölder parametrizations of surfaces whose images generally have a non-integer Hausdorff dimension. Their origin is deterministic, but their regularity properties are roughly similar to those of typical realizations of stochastic processes. As a key tool and our main technical result, we prove novel continuity and boundedness results for potentials of occupation measures of Gaussian random fields. These results complement well-known results for local times, but hold under much less restrictive assumptions. In an auxiliary section, we generalize earlier results on nonlinear compositions of fractional Sobolev functions with $BV$-functions to higher dimensions.

Probability.title: Khintchine's limit theorem for monotone convolutions
Probability.summary: We prove that every weak limit of monotone convolution powers is monotonically infinitely divisible. In contrast, we prove that every probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ can occur as a weak limit of monotone convolutions of an infinitesimal triangular array. We also discuss similar limit theorems for multiplicative monotone convolution on the unit circle.

Probability.title: A reverse entropy power inequality for i.i.d. log-concave random variables
Probability.summary: We show that $h_\infty(X+Y)\leq h_\infty(Z+W)$, where $X, Y$ are independent log-concave random variables, and $Z, W$ are exponential random variables having the same respective $\infty$-Rényi entropies. Analogs for integer-valued monotone log-concave random variables are also obtained. Our main tools are decreasing rearrangement, majorization, and the change of measure.

Probability.title: A Dimension-Free Bound on the Poincaré Constant of Isotropic Log-Concave Measures
Probability.summary: The Kannan--Lovász--Simonovits (KLS) conjecture asserts that isotropic log-concave probability measures have Poincaré constants bounded by a universal constant, independently of dimension. In this work, we provide a deterministic variational proof that the Poincaré constant $C_P(μ)\le25$, where $μ$ is any isotropic log-concave probability measure. The proof centers on mean-zero integration of compatible symmetric tensor fields. Starting from constant tensors, we obtain factorially normalized Appell polynomials by iterating this procedure. Using moment estimates and a quadratic variance inequality, we establish geometric bounds on these iterated primitives through a \emph{joint} variational argument over the measure and test function. At a maximizing pair, stationarity in the test function controls the weighted sum of the two highest-order cumulant terms arising from the measure variation. To extend these bounds to arbitrary compatible fields, we use a weighted Helmholtz--Hodge decomposition of weighted divergence, the formal adjoint of differentiation. Controlling the curl in the decomposition yields a curvature comparison for the integration operators, uniformly in tensor order. Combining this comparison with the Appell bounds gives a bound on the full integration operator and hence the stated Poincaré inequality. The estimate is independent of the auxiliary positive curvature, allowing approximation to general isotropic log-concave measures.

Probability.title: An iterated-logarithm price of anytime validity for log-optimal e-processes
Probability.summary: Log-optimal e-variables at fixed horizons, also called numéraires, have been conjectured to ``almost'' form an e-process for exponential-family null hypotheses. A related open question is whether an e-process can attain the optimal e-power at every horizon up to a bounded loss. Given a final horizon, we study the minimax regret of e-processes relative to the numéraires at all times up to it. For the Gaussian location null and the composite alternative of Gaussian distributions with a smaller variance and an unknown location, we show that the minimax regret in the worst case over the location grows like the iterated logarithm of the final horizon. A single e-process attains this rate at every horizon. This growth answers the question negatively. It also refutes the conjecture if ``almost'' means a regret bounded uniformly over horizons. For this Gaussian location problem, we thus exhibit the frontier precisely: the minimax regret is bounded if and only if the alternatives have at least the variance of the null.
Probability.comment: 9 pages + 18 appendix; AI-generated Lean formalization available at https://adriencorenflos.github.io/formalization/log-optimal-e-processes, with discussion in the appendix

Probability.title: M-estimation for Gaussian processes with time-inhomogeneous drifts from high-frequency data
Probability.summary: We study drift and covariance estimation for a stationary Gaussian process with an integrated deterministic drift, observed at high frequency over an expanding time horizon. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality of an increment least-squares estimator under conditions on drift accumulation and the full covariance of the weighted increments. For directly Riemann integrable drifts, this estimator need not be consistent, as an explicit example shows. Covariance parameters can nevertheless be estimated consistently when the drift decays sufficiently fast. For smooth short-range kernels, we prove a joint central limit theorem for the centered sample variance and the normalized increment second moment, with rate $\sqrt{T_n}$. These statistics require no drift estimate and identify both parameters of the Gaussian kernel. The results clarify how drift accumulation and increment dependence affect the two estimation problems.

Probability.title: Bulk-edge sticking beyond the Perron mode in Gaussian softmax attention
Probability.summary: We study row-softmax self-attention with independent Gaussian query and key weights in the proportional regime, at fixed inverse temperature. Hayase, Collins, and Karakida proved Gaussian equivalence for the empirical squared singular-value distribution after removal of the Perron direction. A global law alone does not exclude finitely many nonleading outliers. We prove that no such outliers persist: the rescaled squared singular value $\ell s_k(A)^2$ converges in probability to the upper edge of their bulk law for every fixed $k\ge 2$. In fact, this convergence is uniform over any deterministic sublinear number of leading non-Perron indices. The proof uses an exact decomposition of the softmax normalization, conditions on the key matrix, identifies the conditional covariance exactly with a diagonally conjugated inner-product kernel, linearizes that kernel in operator norm, and applies the outside-support local law of Fan, Ma, Paquette, and Wang. A separate stability argument identifies the finite conditional deformed Marchenko-Pastur edge with the limiting bulk edge. We also derive a scalar formula for that edge throughout the proportional regime and recover the explicit square-model formula of Hayase, Collins, and Karakida, including its physical branch.

Probability.title: McKean--Vlasov Diffusions from Liouville Spectral Green Response
Probability.summary: For Dirichlet Liouville Brownian motion with $0<γ<2$, the Gaussian response of a finite vector of logarithmic eigenvalues determines a conditional Green energy. We weight this energy by the current spectral density in the fixed reference space. The resulting self-consistent evolution is a porous-medium equation for the canonical spectral form. We construct its positive probability flow, prove an energy identity, and pass from the regularized response forms to the Green limit. The energy identity yields strong convergence of the Gaussian gradients and of the conditional response drifts. A superposition argument then realizes the flow as a McKean--Vlasov weak diffusion.

Probability.title: Continuous-time mean field games: a primal-dual characterization
Probability.summary:
This paper establishes a primal-dual formulation for continuous-time mean field games (MFGs) and provides a complete analytical characterization of the set of all mean field equilibria (MFEs). We reformulate the representative player's control problem as a linear program over occupation measures and derive its dual formulation over smooth subsolutions of the associated Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) equation. This primal-dual formulation yields a verification theorem for MFEs under measurable coefficients and provides necessary and sufficient conditions characterizing all MFEs under a strong duality condition. We establish this strong duality for nondegenerate diffusions with Hölder continuous coefficients through a new global $C^{2,α}$ regularity result for fully nonlinear parabolic HJB equations.
  A key insight is that the dual variable need only coincide with the HJB solution on the support of the mean field flow. Compared with existing approaches, our characterization requires neither convexity of the Hamiltonian nor uniqueness of its optimizer, accommodates relaxed equilibria, and remains applicable when the HJB equation lacks classical solutions.

Differential Geometry.title: VC-Dimension and Generalization in Geometric Machine Learning with Applications to Active Learning
Differential Geometry.summary: We compute the VC-dimension of metric ball classifiers in the model spaces of Riemannian geometry (Euclidean, spherical, hyperbolic) and present upper and lower bounds on the VC-dimension of metric balls in several other situations, including general normed vector spaces (potentially infinite VC-dimension), vector spaces with $\ell^p$-norms (VC-dimension grows at least linearly in the dimension, faster than Euclidean for $p=1$), flat tori, and general Riemannian manifolds (arbitrarily large VC-dimension after a conformal change). In several situations where the VC-dimension is large or even infinite, we prove generalization bounds under additional assumptions on the data distribution using covering arguments. Both in the VC-dimension and covering setting, we consider data on low-dimensional subsets of high-dimensional Euclidean spaces. As an application, we consider coverage-based algorithms in active learning.

Differential Geometry.title: Stacky geometry and logarithmic topology of transversely affine foliations
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the linear monodromy of codimension-one transversely affine foliations through multiplicative quotient stacks and logarithmic boundary topology. When the transverse affine structure admits a global presentation on $U$, a choice of multiplicative developing coordinate induces a morphism to $[\mathbb{C}^*/Γ]$, where $Γ\subset\mathbb{C}^*$ is the image of the linear monodromy. We prove that for infinite $Γ$ every strict semi-equivariant holomorphic self-map of $\mathbb{C}^*$ is a monomial, and classify the nonconstant strict semi-equivariant rational self-maps of $\mathbb{P}^1$ for arbitrary $Γ$. For a logarithmic connection along a simple normal crossings divisor, we describe the meridional characters and angular foliations on the boundary fibres of the Kato--Nakayama space, including the topology and closures of their leaves. We also describe the extension of the linear monodromy local system to this space and the effect of local Kummer base change on finite meridional monodromy.

Differential Geometry.title: Skeletal Homology
Differential Geometry.summary: By ``skeletal homology'' $K_{n}^{\varepsilon}(X)$ we mean the homology of the chain complex $S_{n}^{\varepsilon}(X)$ generated by skeletal $(n,\varepsilon )$-simplices, i.e.\ maps from the $0$-skeleton of the standard simplex into a metric space $X$ whose image has diameter less than $\varepsilon$. Goldfarb showed for finite metric spaces that this homology is isomorphic to the simplicial homology $H_{n}^Δ(VR_{\varepsilon}(X))$ of the Vietoris--Rips complex. We give a new proof of this isomorphism for arbitrary metric spaces. We then develop a metric analogue of methods from singular homology by replacing the topological notion of ``homotopic'' with the metric notion of ``close''. The key tool is a discrete prism construction, which shows that uniformly close functions with a common modulus of continuity induce the same homomorphism on skeletal homology. This leads to stability results for $K_{n}^{\varepsilon}(X)\cong H_{n}^Δ(VR_{\varepsilon}(X))$, including broad extensions of the theorems of Hausmann and Latschev beyond the setting of Riemannian manifolds. Finally, repeated barycentric subdivision and restriction induce a natural homomorphism $ρ_{\varepsilon}:H_{n}% (X)\longrightarrow K_{n}^{\varepsilon}(X). $ We call its image the \emph{real homology} $H_{n}^{\varepsilon}(X)$ at scale and define the corresponding \emph{phantom homology} $P_{n}^{\varepsilon}(X) = K_{n}^{\varepsilon}% (X)/H_{n}^{\varepsilon}(X). $ We show that phantom homology can detect impending topological collapse, as illustrated by collapsing Riemannian manifolds such as Berger spheres.

Differential Geometry.title: On the volume of K-semistable Fano manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that the anti-canonical volume of an $n$-dimensional K-semistable Fano manifold that is not $\mathbb{P}^n$ is at most $2n^n$. Moreover, the volume is equal to $2n^n$ if and only if $X\cong \mathbb{P}^1\times \mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ or $X$ is a smooth quadric hypersurface $Q\subset \mathbb{P}^{n+1}$. Our proof is based on a new connection between K-semistability and minimal rational curves.

Differential Geometry.title: Legendre manifolds generated by the Barenblatt equations
Differential Geometry.summary: The paper is devoted to the construction of exact general solutions of the equations of oil filtration in a porous medium under the action of an active reagent injected into the reservoir. The choice of the reagent solution determines the control process of chemical oil flooding in hard-to-recover fields. The problem is described by a system of two first-order nonlinear partial differential equations (the Barenblatt model).
