We demonstrate how dimensional-analysis and data-scaling can be leveraged to collapse performance data onto scaling functions that are mathematically simple, yet counterintuitive and therefore difficult to predict a priori. These scaling laws reveal success-failure boundaries, including sharp break points which we show can be framed as an ``effective swarm size.'' Additionally, we show how this technique can be used to quantify trade-offs between agent count and platform parameters such as velocity, sensing or weapon range, and attrition rate. Furthermore, we show the benefits of embedding an optimal path planning loop within this framework, which can qualitatively improve the scaling laws that govern the outcome. The methods we demonstrate are highly flexible and would enable rapid, budget-aware sizing and algorithm selection for large autonomous swarms.
Systems and Control.comment: Published in Physical Review E. 16 pages, 12 figures

Systems and Control.title: Equilibria and Consensus in Mixed Weighted-Average and Weighted-Median Opinion Dynamics: The Consensus-Promoting Role of Weighted-Average Individuals
Systems and Control.summary: How individuals respond to their neighbors' opinions shapes whether a networked group reaches consensus. This paper analyzes synchronous discrete-time opinion dynamics on a fixed influence network, where individuals use either weighted-average (WA) or weighted-median (WM) opinion-aggregation mechanisms with individual-specific inertia coefficients. We characterize equilibria through graph-theoretic conditions on opinion level sets and WA balance equations, proving that every solution converges to a Lyapunov-stable equilibrium. We define type-dependent cohesive sets, whose WA members assign all their influence weight to the set and WM members assign at least half. The absence of two disjoint such sets gives a necessary and sufficient graph-theoretic criterion for consensus from any initial condition. Otherwise, an open set of initial conditions leads to persistent dissensus. Converting WM individuals to WA cannot create type-dependent cohesive sets and preserves existing guarantees of consensus from any initial condition. If the conversion eliminates every disjoint pair of these sets, the converted system also guarantees consensus from any initial condition. Four numerical studies examine the locations and proportion of weighted-average individuals, as well as the influence weights, while comparing the consensus criterion with finite-horizon simulation outcomes. In the four network ensembles with 100 individuals, the observed frequency of reaching a prescribed consensus tolerance is nondecreasing with WA proportion at each tested simulation horizon. This trend supports the consensus-promoting role of WA individuals, although individual realizations need not follow it.

Information Theory.title: When are bosonic Gaussian states classical to learn?
Information Theory.summary:
A fundamental question in physics is: When does classical behavior emerge from quantum systems? Bosonic Gaussian states provide a natural setting to explore this quantum-classical boundary, as they capture both the classical field behavior and the intrinsic quantum nature of light. Here, we address this problem from a learning-theoretic perspective by asking: When are bosonic Gaussian states classical to learn? That is, under what conditions (if any) can an n-mode bosonic Gaussian state be learned with as few samples, and with operations as simple, as are needed to learn a classical 2n-variate Gaussian distribution? We establish a smooth crossover in learnability governed by the state's thermal fluctuations:
  - Cold Gaussian states are non-classical to learn: When the covariance matrix satisfies $Σ\le(\frac12+O(\frac1n))I$, i.e. close to the vacuum covariance, tomography under single-copy (i.e., non-entangled) measurements fundamentally requires $Ω(n^3)$ copies, strictly exceeding the sample complexity $Θ(n^2)$ of learning classical Gaussian distributions. We show that this hardness persists even when few-copy entangled measurements are allowed.
  - Warm Gaussian states are classical to learn: When thermal fluctuations exceed the vacuum noise, parameterized by $Σ\ge(\frac12+ν)I$ for any parameter $ν>0$, we prove that single-copy tomography requires $N=Θ\left(n^2\min(n,1+ν^{-1})\right)$ copies. This bound is tight and is achieved by simple, non-adaptive, unentangled heterodyne measurements. Crucially, for $ν=Ω(1)$, the sample complexity drops to $Θ(n^2)$, matching the classical case.
  Our results tightly characterize a quantum-to-classical crossover in the learnability of bosonic Gaussian states, reveal a novel connection between fundamental physics and statistical learning theory, and have implications for real-world sensing experiments.
Information Theory.comment: comments welcome. v2: corrected typos and slightly expanded discussions

Information Theory.title: Karhunen-Loève Transforms of Autoregressive Windows Based on Matched Symmetry Groups
Information Theory.summary: The Karhunen-Loève transform of a window of a stationary autoregressive process of any order $p$ is described through its poles, extending the Algebraic Diversity framework, which selects a transform by the matched group. For simple roots every basis vector is a sum of at most $p$ sinusoids, at the frequencies where the spectrum equals the eigenvalue, plus modes decaying from the ends. The window covariance differs from a member of the class diagonalized by the type-II discrete cosine transform by a closed-form matrix of rank $2p$, exactly when no pole is zero, so the eigenvalues interlace spectrum samples on the cosine grid, and the coding-gain loss of the cosine transform is an exact function of that matrix with computable bounds: for the $8\times8$ Markov block of image coding at pole $0.95$ it is below 1.2 percent. By Kronecker's theorem the rank is at most $2\max(p,q)$ for rational spectra; a moving-average window departs in its Hankel corners, and an integrated (ARIMA) window departs by low rank from the type-VII sine class, exact for the random walk. The exact symmetry is generically the reflection and contains a wreath product for interleaved windows; the dihedral group of the even extension is matched approximately, the dominant pole's sign choosing cosine or sine. The two groups give the transform a fast form: a parity fold, half-length cosine cores and a cascade of at most $p$ first-order Cauchy stages, exactly $p$ for a minimal AR($p$) model. The first-order case recovers results obtained by other means.

Information Theory.title: The optimal information complexity of VC learning
Information Theory.summary: Steinke and Zakynthinou(2020) introduces the Conditional Mutual Information (CMI) framework of analyzing the information complexity of learning algorithms based on algorithm-dependent information-theoretic quantities. We study one of these quantities, the evaluated Conditional Mutual Information (eCMI). It has been an interesting question whether the optimal PAC guarantee for VC classes can be recovered from the algorithm-dependent analyses via CMI. And we show that it is possible to recover this guarantee by constructing a learning algorithm whose eCMI is of order O(d) in the realizable case, where d is the VC-dimension of the concept class. Specially, our algorithm is a randomized Majority-of-5 base learners with optimal in-expectation generalization guarantee.

Information Theory.title: LWM-TF: A Wireless Foundation Model on 5G NR Time-Frequency Resource Grids
Information Theory.summary: Received OFDM grids preserve both pilot and payload observations, yet wireless foundation models are rarely pre-trained on them. We introduce LWM-TF, a 9.58M-parameter factorized masked autoencoder pre-trained on complex 5G NR uplink grids taken after the FFT and before channel estimation. Each block attends first across OFDM symbols and then across resource blocks and receive antennas, and the mask follows the same two axes. Because the payload phase is unpredictable, the model reconstructs the normalized log-power of each masked token and predicts its scale separately; ablations show that the two terms are complementary and that this target outperforms complex-signal reconstruction. The encoder is pre-trained on 850,496 physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) slots from a 10^6-slot dataset simulated with the NR transmit chain under various channel conditions. With the encoder frozen, linear probes classify modulation, predict CRC success, and detect UE mobility. On a separately generated test set, 16 labeled slots per class give 0.85 modulation accuracy, 0.82 CRC area under the ROC curve (AUROC), and 0.73 mobility AUROC, ahead of a supervised CNN on every paired draw. With 10,000 labels the probes reach 0.94, 0.96, and 0.92, well above engineered receiver statistics, and detect mobility where the CNN stays at chance. Without any impairment labels, distances in the frozen feature space flag unseen waveform impairments with 0.78 macro AUROC, against 0.68 for receiver statistics. A single pre-trained encoder thus provides receiver features that transfer across tasks, most strongly when labels are scarce.
Information Theory.comment: Accepted for publication in IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Signal Processing (JSTSP)

Information Theory.title: Sample-Efficient Quantum State Tomography for Structured Quantum States in One Dimension
Information Theory.summary: In this paper, we answer this fundamental question affirmatively by using a class of informationally complete positive operator-valued measures (IC-POVMs), including symmetric IC-POVMs (SIC-POVMs) and spherical $t$-designs, focusing on sample complexity while not accounting for the implementation complexity of the measurement settings. For SIC-POVMs and spherical 2-designs, we show that the number of state copies to guarantee bounded recovery error of an MPO state with a constrained least-squares estimator depends on the probability distribution of the MPO under the POVM but scales only linearly with $n$ when the distribution is approximately uniform. For general spherical $t$-designs with a sufficiently large $t$, we prove that only a number of state copies proportional to the number of independent parameters in the MPO is sufficient for a guaranteed recovery of any state represented by an MPO. In addition, we establish a sample complexity lower bound based on the Cramer-Rao bound, showing that, for strictly positive definite MPO states and unbiased estimators, a number of state copies proportional to the number of independent parameters in the MPO is also necessary, although the upper and lower bounds do not yet match in their dependence on the target accuracy. Furthermore, we propose a spectral method and a projected gradient descent (PGD) algorithm to solve the constrained least-squares problem, both equipped with rigorous recovery error guarantees.

Information Theory.title: Compression of Sources with Memory and Private Random Access
Information Theory.summary: Private local decoding imposes a stringent constraint on compression: the codeword bits used to recover a source symbol must reveal nothing about the remaining symbols beyond what the recovered symbol itself reveals. For memoryless sources, this constraint is known to be compatible with entropy-rate compression. We show that the same holds for any stationary ergodic source over a finite alphabet. Specifically, every rate above the entropy rate is achievable with exact privacy and error-free local decoding on a set of source sequences whose probability tends to one. In contrast, we exhibit non-ergodic sources for which private local decoding incurs a strictly positive rate penalty.

Information Theory.title: Sharp Rates for Optimal Recovery of Bandlimited Functions from Localized Oversampling
Information Theory.summary:
It is well-known that one can recover a function $f$ bandlimited to $[-δ,δ]$ ( $0<δ<π$) from its finite sample data $f(j),-n\le j\le n$, with an approximation error exponentially decaying to zero as $n$ tends to infinity. Various regularized Shannon sampling formula have been proposed to achieve such exponential approximation. So far the best rate has been
  $$
  O\biggl(\frac1{\sqrt{n}}\exp(-(π-δ)n)\biggr).
  $$
  We establish that the optimal recovery algorithm in the worst-case scenario achieves an approximation error $ρ_{n,δ}$ satisfying
  $$
  c_* \frac1{\sqrt{n}}(\tan\fracδ4)^{2n+1/2}\le ρ_{n,δ}\le C^* \frac1{\sqrt{n}}(\tan\fracδ4)^{2n+1/2},
  \quad 0<δ\leqπ,\quad n\geq1,
  $$
  where $c_*,C^*$ are positive constants independent of $n$ and $δ$. This result identifies the best possible exponential rate to reconstruct bandlimited functions from two-sided finite oversampling data. In other words,
  $$
  ρ_{n,δ} \asymp \frac{\tan\fracδ4}{\sqrt{n}}\exp\bigl(-c_δ(π-δ)n\bigr),
  $$
  where $c_δ$ is strictly decreasing on $(0,π]$ and
  $$
  \lim_{δ\toπ^-}c_δ=1,\ \lim_{δ\to 0^+}c_δ=+\infty.
  $$
  We also make the new finding that one can also reconstruct $f$ bandlimited to $[-δ,δ]$ with exponentially decaying error from one-sided sample data $f(j)$, $1\le j\le n$, and the sharp rate of approximation error $ρ_{n,δ}'$ of the optimal algorithm is
  $$
  ρ_{n,δ}' \asymp \sqrt{δ/π}\sin^n(δ/2).
  $$

Information Theory.title: Statistical Physics of Coding for the Integers
Information Theory.summary: We study a paradigm of coding for compression of the natural numbers via the zeta distribution and develop a statistical-mechanical interpretation, both in terms of Hagedorn systems and a Bose gas with energy levels given by logarithms of prime numbers. We also propose a simple coding scheme for the zeta distribution that nearly achieves the ideal code length. For block coding of vectors of natural numbers, we derive the micro-canonical entropy function and demonstrate its asymptotic linearity implying that its behavior is analogous to that of a Hagedorn system. We also derive the large deviations rate function, and provide a formula for the best coding parameter in the large deviations sense. We show that due the Hagedorn-type phase transition there is only partial equivalence of ensembles, due to the degeneration of the domain of the partition function.
Information Theory.comment: 41 pages, 2 figures, accepted to Journal of Statistical Physics Theory and Experiment (JSTAT)

Information Theory.title: CHANNELS4WORLD: An Environment-Scale Dataset for Wireless Foundation Models
Information Theory.summary: Wireless foundation models learn reusable representations across tasks, configurations, and deployment environments. Their pretraining requires environmental breadth, yet wireless datasets often sample few sites densely. We introduce Channels4World, a scene-centered dataset of 100,000 distinct outdoor RF scenes and a procedural method for generating them. Each scene links a generated environment and RF material assignments to 32 base-station (BS) positions, 16,384 UE positions, and aligned variable-length multipath and ordered interaction records at 3.5 and 7~GHz. The corpus comprises 52.43 billion physical BS-UE pairs, 104.86 billion frequency-specific evaluations, and a 29.14-TB packaged payload. Scene identity aligns geometry, placements, channels, and interactions across frequencies, allowing environmental breadth and within-scene observation density to vary independently. The public release offers predefined subsets at multiple scales and separate access to corpus components. A deterministic 90K/10K scene-level train-test split keeps both frequencies and all scene components together. We characterize morphology, RF materials, and transceiver placement across three generation profiles. Controlled propagation and path-retention analyses show that diffraction materially affects retained-link availability and multipath structure, while the retention policy reduces storage substantially with little loss in represented aggregate power. Under matched training exposure, models trained on broader scene collections perform better on held-out scenes, although an equal-episode control shows that scene count alone cannot explain the gain. By making environmental breadth explicit and controllable, Channels4World supports the development and evaluation of wireless foundation models for generalization across deployment environments.

Information Theory.title: Joint Design of Communication and Control in Center-Fed Pinching-Antenna Systems
Information Theory.summary: An analytical and optimization framework for the joint design of communication and control (JDCC) in a center-fed pinching-antenna system (C-PASS) is proposed. Within this framework, the mathematical coupling between data throughput and closed-loop control cost is characterized for JDCC. The analysis captures the mutual interference between concurrently transmitted data and control streams during uplink state uploading and downlink command delivery. Based on this coupling, an achievable communication-control performance region is established for C-PASS. Accordingly, a throughput maximization problem is formulated to jointly optimize digital and pinching beamforming subject to control-cost constraints. To address this problem, an alternating optimization algorithm is developed based on constraint reformulation and resource decomposition. The proposed framework reveals how control requirements shape achievable data throughput, guiding the joint beamforming design. Numerical results demonstrate that 1) the proposed C-PASS design achieves 110.2\% higher frame-average throughput than conventional PASS, and 2) the proposed concurrent data-control transmission protocol increases frame-average throughput by up to 66.7\% over separated transmission.

Information Theory.title: Linear Set Reconciliation with $O(d)$ Additive Redundancy
Information Theory.summary:
In set reconciliation, two parties holding sets $A, B \subseteq [n]$ with $|A \triangle B| \le d$ seek to recover their symmetric difference from short $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear sketches, which is equivalent to recovering a $d$-sparse vector $x = \mathbf{1}_{A \triangle B} \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$ from its syndrome $Hx \in \mathbb{F}_2^m$. While the information-theoretic counting bound requires $L(n,d) := \log \sum_{i=0}^d \binom{n}{i} = d\log(n/d) + Θ(d)$ bits, existing polynomial-time schemes either use at least $d\lceil\log(n+1)\rceil$ bits (algebraic sketches, leaving an $Ω(d\log d)$-bit gap) or incur a multiplicative $(1+δ)L(n,d)$ overhead (peeling-based sketches), raising the question of whether $L(n,d) + O(d)$ bits is achievable with fast updates and decoding.
  We construct a public-coin randomized $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear sketch of length $L(n,d) + O(d) + λ\log^{O(1)} n$ that recovers each fixed input of weight at most $d$ with probability at least $1 - 2^{-λ}$, with $\log^{O(1)} n$ update time and $d\exp(O((\log\log n)^2)) = dn^{o(1)}$ worst-case decoding time. In particular, for $n \le 2^{\operatorname{polylog}(d)}$ and $λ\le d^{1-Ω(1)}$, this achieves $L(n,d) + O(d)$ bits with $\operatorname{polylog}(d)$ update time and $d^{1+o(1)}$ decoding time.
  Our construction encodes $d$ permuted rows via randomly scaled Pinsketch syndromes and sketches the resulting bit array column by column. Decoding columns sequentially from prefix predictions cancels recovered rows and exposes undecided rows as decoder-side hints, reducing each column to a hinted sparse recovery problem that we solve via a recursive sketch, HintSketch.

Information Theory.title: Beating the Probabilistic Bound for Hashing and Improving Lower Bounds for Trifferent Codes
Information Theory.summary: We improve the probabilistic lower bounds on the rates of hash codes and list-recoverable codes. For perfect $q$-hashing, we prove $R_q>B_q$ for every $q\geq 3$. Our main result concerns non-perfect hashing. For every $q\geq 4$, we prove $R_{q,3}>B_{q,3}+\frac{1}{250000}.$ In particular, the case $q=9$, combined with the Tetra code, strictly improves the Körner-Marton lower bound $R_3\geq \frac14\log(9/5)$ for trifferent codes. We also extend the method to $(p,2,3)$-list recovery. For every $q\geq 4$ and $0\leq p<\frac{q-2}{12(q-1)}$, we prove $R_q^{\mathrm{LR}}(p)>B_q^{\mathrm{LR}}(p)$. For every fixed $0\leq p<1/18$, the rate improvement is bounded below by a positive constant independent of $q\geq 4$. The same holds for every fixed $0\le p<1/12$ when $q$ is sufficiently large.

Information Theory.title: A Characterization of $q$-Ary $2$-Designs and a $3$-Design Obstruction for Doubly-Extended Reed-Solomon Codes
Information Theory.summary: Let $\mathcal{C}_k$ be the doubly extended Reed--Solomon code with parameters $[q+1,k,q-k+2]_q$, where $q\ge3$ is a prime power and $2\le k\le q$. We prove a conjecture of Wu and Zhou by showing that the minimum-weight codewords of $\mathcal{C}_k$ do not form a $q$-ary $3$-design when $2\le k\le q-1$. Using shortening, we extend this obstruction to every nonempty weight class with $3\le w<q+1$. We also establish that each individual nonempty positive-weight class of $\mathcal{C}_k$ forms a $q$-ary $2$-design if and only if $\gcd(k-1,q-1)=1$. Consequently, every nonempty positive-weight class below full support has exact $q$-ary design strength $2$ when this coprimality condition holds, and $1$ otherwise.The three-design obstruction follows by applying a classical subset-product character identity to a marginal covering count for three prescribed nonzero symbols. The comparison between weights rests on a covering-count formulation of the classical MDS coset-weight relations. For every linear $[n,k,d]_q$ MDS code with $2\le k\le n-1$, this formulation shows that the $q$-ary $2$-design property at any one nonempty positive weight is equivalent to the same property at every nonempty positive weight.More generally, for $2\le t\le\min\{k,d\}$, we prove that the $q$-ary $t$-design property at any $t-1$ distinct nonempty positive weights forces it at all nonempty positive weights.

Information Theory.title: QoS-Aware Energy-Efficient Sub-THz Near-Field Multiuser Hybrid MIMO Systems Employing Circular Arrays
Information Theory.summary: Near-field communications have emerged as a promising technology for future sixth-generation (6G) networks. However, designing energy-efficient hybrid beamfocusing schemes for multiuser (MU) systems remains challenging due to the non-convex quality-of-service (QoS) constraints and hardware limitations of hybrid architectures. In this paper, we investigate a hybrid massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) architecture for a near-field sub-THz MU downlink system employing a large uniform circular array (UCA) at the base station. A QoS-aware transmit power minimization problem is formulated for energy-efficient beamfocusing and addressed through a two-stage penalty-driven joint optimization (PDJO) framework, where auxiliary variables are introduced to reformulate the QoS constraints into second-order cone (SOC) constraints. Furthermore, a near-field polar-domain codebook is developed via joint angle- and distance-domain sampling. We establish that the fully digital (FD) beamfocuser lies within the column space of the proposed codebook, enabling hybrid precoder design to be formulated as a multiple measurement vector (MMV)-based sparse approximation problem. The formulated problem is then solved using a low-complexity simultaneous orthogonal matching pursuit (SOMP) algorithm under hardware and transmit power constraints. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves spectral- and energy-efficiency performance close to the ideal FD beamfocusing scheme while providing a favorable trade-off between hardware complexity and system performance.

Information Theory.title: Analysis of the Effect of Doppler on Direct-to-Cell: Real-World Performance and Proposed Improvements
Information Theory.summary: Direct-to-cell (DtC) satellites serve unmodified LTE phones today from low Earth orbit, where the satellite's motion creates Doppler shifts of tens of kHz. Since large offsets such as these cannot be compensated adequately by the user equipment (UE), the satellite pre-compensates the Doppler shift of each beam, but it can do so for only one reference point in the beam. A UE elsewhere in the beam still has to compensate a residual offset; previous field studies report residuals of up to 10 kHz, beyond the $\pm$7.5 kHz that the 15 kHz subcarrier spacing can resolve. In this paper we corroborate this effect with our own detailed measurements of Starlink transmissions and further correlate ineffective handover performance to inadequate residual offset compensation. We analyze the Doppler compensation problem with detailed standard-specific simulations and propose a compensation method at the UE, based on the location of the UE with respect to the beam reference point used for the Doppler compensation and the known satellite location, that improves the efficiency of handover. With UE cell-specific pre-compensation, the neighbors are identified, read correctly and handed over to in time rather than lost to radio-link failure.

Information Theory.title: Iterative Interference Cancellation for Near-Field XL-MIMO Networks with LoS Channels
Information Theory.summary: In extra-large multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) systems, near-field users experience spherical wavefront propagation, offering higher spatial resolution than far-field plane-wave models, but complicating signal detection and interference cancellation. Under line-of-sight conditions, we propose a weighted-rate successive interference cancellation (WR-SIC) scheme whose ordering metric exploits the enhanced spatial degrees of freedom of near-field propagation to prioritize users with stronger channels. An iterative detection and decoding (IDD) scheme with LDPC coding is then developed. Simulations in hybrid near- and far-field deployments show that the proposed WR-SIC and IDD schemes improve bit-error and sum rates over existing schemes

Probability.title: Random Configurations and Fourier Decoupling
Probability.summary: We use tools from high dimensional probability to analyze random configurations of balls in the context of Fourier decoupling and we answer a question on the structure of superlevel sets in the setting of decoupling due to Guth.

Probability.title: SDEs with critical general distributional drifts: sharp solvability and blow-ups
Probability.summary:
We develop weak solution theory of SDEs having general distributional drifts that can introduce local blow-up effects. Our assumption on the drift is closely related to the variational theory of the Kolmogorov backward equation in the standard Hilbert triple $W^{1,2} \hookrightarrow L^2 \hookrightarrow W^{-1,2}$. Under suitable smallness assumption on the drift, one has well-posedness of the Cauchy problem in this Hilbert triple. In turn, by a result of Mazya and Verbitsky, boundedness of the drift term from $W^{1,2}$ to $W^{-1,2}$ is equivalent to a decomposition of the drift in the sum of a form-bounded drift (including, for example, Morrey or Chang--Wilson--Wolff drifts) and a divergence-free distributional drift in the ${\rm BMO}^{-1}$ space of Koch and Tataru; such decomposition is our class of drifts.
  We apply our results to finite particle systems with strong attracting interactions immersed in a stationary turbulent flow. This includes particle systems of Keller-Segel type. Crucially, in dimensions $d \geq 3$, we cover almost the entire admissible range of attraction strengths, reaching nearly to the blow-up threshold. As a further application of our results for SDEs and of the theory of Bessel processes, we obtain an improved upper bound on the constant in the many-particle Hardy inequality of Hoffmann-Ostenhof, Hoffmann-Ostenhof, Laptev, and Tidblom.
Probability.comment: Fixed a number of minor errors and typos

Probability.title: Conditional Fluctuations of Mean-Field Systems with Stable Common Noise
Probability.summary: We study conditional fluctuations of smooth mean-field systems on a torus with symmetric stable common jumps of index $0<α<1$. A positive-strip estimate makes empirical Poisson acceptance errors negligible at the sampling scale. Given the full Poisson master, the conditional laws converge in probability to a centered Gaussian kernel in a negative Sobolev path space. In dimension one, quantile coupling preserves this limit for microscopic marks with relative tail remainder $O(x^{-ρ})$, where $ρ>\tfracα{2}$. A second-order tail expansion identifies the response when this condition fails: it shifts the conditional Gaussian mean at criticality and, when nonzero, dominates sampling below criticality. We also identify the transition from a stable to a Brownian rank error. In a translation model, rank and clock couplings give the same microscopic laws but different path fluctuations. Rank coupling gives a functional Gaussian limit. Clock coupling admits no diverging additive path normalization at the limiting center.

Probability.title: Discrete Distributions and Their Limit Theorems in the Surreal Numbers
Probability.summary: We extend the discrete uniform, hypergeometric and binomial distributions to the surreal numbers, allowing infinitely many outcomes, chips and trials. A uniform distribution on $\mathbb{N}$ gives each outcome probability $1/ω$; on the eventually periodic sets we define the needed sizes explicitly, obtaining a probability that is regular and strictly monotone. For an urn with infinitely many chips and finitely many draws, the hypergeometric distribution is within an infinitesimal of the binomial. With infinitely many trials, and under a hypothesis on factorials of omnific integers that we show can be satisfied, we prove a surreal de~Moivre--Laplace theorem, and we show that the hypergeometric distribution with infinitely many draws is locally normal with a finite-population correction. Near its center, it is relatively close to the binomial distribution if and only if the sampling fraction is infinitesimal, an exact form of a familiar rule of thumb. For rare successes we prove, without any hypothesis on factorials, a surreal Poisson limit theorem and describe urns with finitely many red chips, where the binomial approximation fails beyond the first success.

Probability.title: A Pricing and Hedging Framework for Infinite-Dimensional Financial Markets
Probability.summary: In this paper, we provide a comprehensive study of how the classical Black--Scholes-type market framework behaves in an infinite-dimensional setting. The asset prices are modeled by stochastic evolution equations in a separable Hilbert space. The evolution of the risk-free asset and the corresponding discounting operators are governed by a strongly continuous group of bounded linear operators. Accordingly, we consider contingent claims with Hilbert-space-valued payoffs, whose values are discounted through the corresponding operators. Within this framework, we investigate the pricing and hedging of contingent claims, deriving the corresponding Hilbert-space-valued Black--Scholes equations and establishing exact replication results for both strong and mild solutions. We also study the special case where the infinitesimal generator is given by $A=rI$, allowing for real-valued contingent claims. We further investigate no-arbitrage and market completeness, introducing a Hilbert lattice structure to formulate arbitrage and characterizing attainability through operator equations associated with martingale representations. We also establish asymptotic completeness through finite-dimensional noise truncations. We introduce geometric Brownian motions in Hilbert spaces and derive sufficient conditions for the existence and uniqueness of an equivalent risk-neutral measure, together with explicit pricing formulas for some tractable examples. These results extend key aspects of the classical Black--Scholes framework to markets with infinite-dimensional asset-price dynamics. As a concrete application, the model can be interpreted as a segmented market consisting of a sequence of one-dimensional geometric Brownian motions.

Probability.title: Comparability for quadratic forms with space-dependent singular measures
Probability.summary: This paper investigates quadratic forms $\mathcal{E}^Γ$ generated by configurations $Γ$ and families of measures that are parametrized in the space variable and singular with respect to the Lebesgue measure. A first basic result is the construction of corresponding integro-differential operators in divergence form. These operators are obtained by symmetrizing the family of singular measures. The main result is the comparability of the quadratic form $\mathcal{E}^Γ$ with the quadratic form $\mathcal{E}^s$ which is associated with the fractional Laplacian $(-Δ)^s$. Comparability of $\mathcal{E}^Γ$ and $\mathcal{E}^s$ implies Hölder regularity and a weak Harnack inequality for solutions to integro-differential equations involving these operators.

Probability.title: Second-order Wasserstein response for Lévy laws
Probability.summary: Moving an atom and splitting it symmetrically can give the same weak change in a Lévy characteristic, yet produce Wasserstein errors of different orders. We explain this through first- and second-order expansions of the distribution function for infinitely divisible laws with a Gaussian factor. The expansions are uniform over Lipschitz tests and include distributional directions from moving atoms. When the first response is nonzero, analyticity gives the signed second coefficient of the Wasserstein--1 distance. When it vanishes, a finite second displacement moment gives a quadratic response, with a positive coefficient whenever the dispersion is nonzero. For local balanced remeshing, we prove matching bounds in terms of grid-alignment variance and construct a linear program with a controlled optimization gap. We also determine the sharp transition as Gaussian smoothing vanishes. The appendices give proofs, metric speed and length, and multivariate and state-dependent extensions.

Probability.title: Trees in Random Sparse Graphs with a Given Degree Sequence
Probability.summary:
Let $\mathbb{G}^{D}$ be the set of graphs $G(V,\, E)$ with $\left|V\right|=n$, and the degree sequence equal to $D=(d_{1},\, d_{2},\,\dots,\, d_{n})$. In addition, for $\frac{1}{2}<a<1$, we define the set of graphs with an almost given degree sequence $D$ as follows, \[ \mathbb{G}_{a}^{D}:=\cup\,\mathbb{G}^{\bar{D}}, \] where the union is over all degree sequences $\bar{D}$ such that, for $1\leq i\leq n$, we have $\left|d_{i}-\bar{d}_{i}\right|<d_{i}^{a}$.
  Now, if we chose random graphs $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{g}}\left(D\right)$ and $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{a}}\left(D\right)$ uniformly out of the sets $\mathbb{G}^{D}$ and $\mathbb{G}_{a}^{D}$, respectively, what do they look like? This has been studied when $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{g}}\left(D\right)$ is a dense graph, i.e. $\left|E\right|=Θ(n^{2})$, in the sense of graphons, or when $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{g}}\left(D\right)$ is very sparse, i.e. $d_{n}^{2}=o(\left|E\right|)$. In the case of sparse graphs with an almost given degree sequence, we investigate this question, and give the finite tree subgraph structure of $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{a}}\left(D\right)$ under some mild conditions. For the random graph $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{g}}\left(D\right)$ with a given degree sequence, we re-derive the finite tree structure in dense and very sparse cases to give a continuous picture.
  Moreover, for a pair of vectors $\left(D_{1},D_{2}\right)\in\mathbb{Z}^{n_{1}}\times\mathbb{Z}^{n_{2}}$, we let $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{b}}\left(D_{1},D_{2}\right)$ be the random bipartite graph that is chosen uniformly out of the set $\mathbb{G}^{D_{1},D_{2}}$, where $\mathbb{G}^{D_{1},D_{2}}$ is the set of all bipartite graphs with the degree sequence $\left(D_{1},D_{2}\right)$. We are able to show the result for $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{b}}\left(D_{1},D_{2}\right)$ without any further conditions.

Probability.title: Boundary Harnack principle for abstract supersolutions on uniform domains
Probability.summary: We develop an axiomatic approach to the boundary Harnack principle on diameter-uniform domains in proper doubling metric measure spaces. Under critical-density and upper-contraction assumptions, we establish a scale-invariant one-sided boundary comparison between nonnegative supersolutions and positive solutions as well as Hölder continuity of quotients of positive solutions. Our framework does not require linearity or rectifiable curves. Applications include classical elliptic equations with Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions, spectral fractional Laplacians, harmonic functions on fractals, and Pucci operators.

Probability.title: Sitewise Generator Decomposition and Non-Equilibrium Steady States for Generalized Zero-Range Processes
Probability.summary: In this paper we study the generalized zero-range processes considered in [20, 11, 12] with boundary driving. In these processes mass is moved between neighboring sites with rates depending only on the departure site. For a wide class of such models, the equilibrium stationary states are known to be of product form. We show that for such models, the boundary-driven generator can be decomposed into a sum of generators acting on single sites when integrating against (possibly inhomogeneous) products of the equilibrium marginals. We exploit this structure to derive new results for the harmonic models introduced in [15]. In particular, we prove that the propagation of mixture measures in [19] is still valid on graphs with asymmetric edges. On the chain geometry with asymmetric edges, we identify a class of models for which the NESS is given precisely by the NESS of the symmetric harmonic model on the chain. In addition to these results for harmonic models, we also present a new class of asymmetric models on the chain for which the NESS can be found explicitly and exhibits shock behavior. The large deviations for the density profile corresponding to these NESS are stated and proved.

Probability.title: A Log-Star Comparison Between Expectation Threshold and Fractional Expectation Threshold
Probability.summary:
We proved a log-star comparison between the expectation threshold $q(\mathcal F)$ and the fractional
  expectation threshold $q_f(\mathcal F)$ for any nontrivial increasing family $\mathcal F$ on a finite ground set $V$ of size $|V|=N$. Specifically, we show that
  $$q_f(\mathcal F)\le64\log_2^*(N+2)\,q(\mathcal F),$$
  where $\log_2^* x$ is the iterated logarithm of base-2.
  Using similiar methods, one can extend this result to the following stronger form: there exists a universal constant $C>0$ such that
  \[
  q_f(\mathcal F)\le Cq(\mathcal F)\log_2^*(l(\mathcal F)),\quad q_f(\mathcal F)\le Cq(\mathcal F)\log_2^*(\operatorname{VC}(\min\mathcal F)),
  \]
  where $l(\mathcal F):=\max\{2,\max_{S\in\min\mathcal F}|S|\}$ and $\operatorname{VC}(\min\mathcal F)$ denotes the VC-dimension of $\min\mathcal F$.
  On October 7, 2026, OpenAI released a result proving the equivalence of fractional and integral thresholds, which supersedes the findings in this note. The authors are keeping this note for historical reference.

Probability.title: Equivalence of finite and infinite survival and sharpness of the phase transition for additive particle systems
Probability.summary: Krone's two-stage contact process is an interacting particle system in which each site on a grid can be in one of three possible states: 0 (empty), 1 (young individual), and 2 (adult individual). Only adults can multiply, and their offspring is initially young, before growing up after an exponential time. There are two death rates, one for adult trees, and a higher one for young trees. The process is additive and has an additive dual, but unlike the contact process it is not self-dual. Answering a question of Krone, for the process on the $d$-dimensional integer grid, Foxall proved that survival of finite populations is equivalent to nontriviality of the upper invariant law. Using a completely different method, we generalise this result to processes on countable groups and along the way also establish sharpness of the phase transition for a general class of additive interacting particle systems.

Probability.title: Singular parabolic Anderson models - From flat space to geometric contexts
Probability.summary: These notes (which grew out of some lecture notes prepared for the first Aarhus Summer School in Analysis and Probability) are an introduction to the parabolic Anderson model (PAM), or otherwise stated the stochastic heat equation $\partial_{t} u \,=\, \tfrac{1}{2}Δ\, u \,+\, β\, u\,\dot{W}$. In this system, a multiplicative random potential $\dot{W}$ drives the solution away from the smooth spreading of the classical heat flow and toward intermittency. Namely one observes that mass concentrates, as time grows, on a few tall and widely separated peaks. Through the Feynman-Kac representation this analytic phenomenon has an equivalent probabilistic reading as the localization of a directed polymer in a random environment. We first develop this picture on the flat space $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, covering the construction of the driving noise, well-posedness of the equation, and two-sided bounds on the moment Lyapunov exponents that quantify intermittency. We then turn to the more original goal of the monograph: understanding how these phenomena, and the exponents attached to them, change when $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ is replaced by a genuinely geometric background, such as a sub-Riemannian manifold or a fractal set. Throughout, the emphasis is on concepts, main results, and the intuition behind their proofs, rather than on exhaustive technical detail.
Probability.comment: Those lecture notes are still considered as a draft, comments are welcome

Probability.title: The critical Cauchy boundary for Gibbs partitions
Probability.summary: We study critical Gibbs partitions whose component law is in the domain of attraction of a spectrally positive stable law of index one. In the dense phase, we prove a local limit theorem for the number of components and functional limits for their sizes. We also describe convergent and divergent condensation regimes, and a phase transition at a boundary in which the dense and condensation contributions compete.

Probability.title: Fourth-Moment Theorems for Sums of Multiple Wigner Integrals
Probability.summary: We derive quantitative free fourth-moment bounds for sums of two Wigner chaoses of opposite parity under mirror symmetry. The bound contains an explicit remainder consisting of internal contractions of the two kernels. In particular, vanishing of this remainder together with the fourth free cumulant implies convergence to the standard semicircular law. If the higher-order kernel is cyclically symmetric, the internal contractions can be moved to an endpoint and we obtain an explicit fourth-root bound without a remainder. For fully symmetric kernels we obtain a square-root bound under the $W_2$-Wasserstein distance. Using the operator-norm support estimate for Wigner integrals, we also extend these bounds to every $W_p$-Wasserstein distance , where $1\le p<\infty$.

Probability.title: Rate of convergence for the Wiener--Itô chaos in $W_p$ for $1\leq p<\infty$
Probability.summary: Inspired by previous work of Nualart, Ledoux, Peccati, Nourdin, and others, we establish quantitative fourth moment theorems for random variables in a fixed Wiener--Itô chaos and for sums of two Wiener--Itô chaoses in the $W_p$-Wasserstein distance for $1\leq p<\infty$.

Probability.title: Doubly Free-Boundary Rail-Yard Dimers and Annular Gaussian Fluctuations
Probability.summary: We study rail-yard dimer models with free boundaries at both ends. The double free-boundary geometry introduces infinitely many reflected Cauchy factors into partition functions and contour formulas for height Laplace observables. For admissible piecewise periodic weights satisfying the stated separation conditions, we prove a Laplace-transform law of large numbers and obtain a limit shape through weak convergence of slope measures. For $β=1$, under the stated regularity and nonexceptional endpoint conditions, we derive a necessary real double-root condition for the frozen boundary. We also prove Gaussian fluctuations of centered height Laplace observables, with covariance determined by an annular reflected-image kernel expressed through theta functions. Finally, we construct an exact growth-diagram sampler for finite reflected truncations and prove that their laws converge in total variation to the full Gibbs measure on every fixed rail-yard graph with finitely many columns as the truncation level tends to infinity.

Probability.title: Uniform inference for $U$-statistics of exchangeable arrays under degeneracy
Probability.summary: Many $U$-statistics of row-column exchangeable arrays become degenerate at natural null hypotheses: their convergence rates change and their limiting laws may or may not remain Gaussian. We establish conditions under which inference based on the classical unbiased variance estimator is uniformly valid across these changes, without knowledge of the degeneracy order. It is known that $U$-statistics can be decomposed into orthogonal projections indexed by bipartite graphs. Under uniform fourth-moment assumptions, we establish that the standardized statistic is asymptotically Gaussian and the classical unbiased variance estimator is ratio-consistent, as long as a certain measure of concentration for projections indexed by disconnected graphs tends to zero. Under compactness of the normalized projections, both properties hold if and only if the proportion of variance contributed by disconnected graphs tends to zero. The necessity of this condition follows from a general limit theorem for these $U$-statistics, in which each graph contributes to a Wiener chaos of order equal to its number of connected components. We note that the row-column jackknife variance estimator, although nonnegative, does not generally give a studentized statistic with a standard normal limit in degenerate regimes. We illustrate our theory with an application to estimation and testing based on a distance from product form, exhibiting Gaussian and non-Gaussian limits at various rates depending on the model. We also propose a conservative inference procedure that does not require a Gaussian limit, valid under additional moment and projection conditions.

Probability.title: A formula for the edge density $\sqrt{n}$-correction for two-dimensional Coulomb systems
Probability.summary:
In connection with recent work on smallest gaps, C. Charlier proves that the 1-point function of a suitable planar Coulomb system $\{z_j\}_1^n$, in the determinantal case with respect to an external potential $Q(z)$, admits the expansion, as $n\to\infty$, $$R_n\bigg(z_0+\frac t {\sqrt{2n\partial\bar{\partial} Q(z_0)}}ν(z_0)\bigg)=n\partial\bar{\partial} Q(z_0)\frac {\operatorname{erfc} t}2+\sqrt{n\partial\bar{\partial} Q(z_0)}\,C(z_0;t)+\mathcal{O}(\log^6 n).$$ Here $t$ is a real parameter, $z_0$ is a regular boundary point of the (connected) Coulomb droplet and $ν(z_0)$ is the outwards unit normal; the coefficient $C(z_0;t)$ has an apriori structure depending on a number of parameters.
  In this note we identify the parameters and obtain a formula for $C(z_0;t)$ in potential theoretic and geometric terms. Our formula holds for a large class of potentials such that the droplet is connected with smooth boundary. Our derivation uses the well known expectation of fluctuations formula.
Probability.comment: This update contains a few relatively minor clarifications of proofs

Probability.title: Localization Lengths for Two-Dimensional Random Band Matrices: Exponential Lower Bounds
Probability.summary: We consider $N \times N$ random band matrices $H = (H_{xy})$ with centered complex Gaussian entries, indexed by points $x,y$ on the two-dimensional discrete torus $(\mathbb{Z} / \sqrt{N} \mathbb{Z})^2$. The matrix entries $H_{xy}$ vanish whenever the distance between $x$ and $y$ exceeds a constant multiple of the bandwidth parameter $W$. We prove that, for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$, if $W\geq(\log N)^{1+\varepsilon}$, then all bulk eigenvectors are delocalized with high probability. Equivalently, this yields a lower bound of order $\exp(W^{1-\varepsilon})$ on the localization length of two-dimensional random band matrices for arbitrarily small constant $\varepsilon>0$, improving the superpolynomial lower bound $W^C$ for every fixed constant $C>0$ established in arXiv:2503.07606. A key ingredient of our proof is a new strategy that closes the resolvent flow analysis using only loop observables of order at most two, without relying on the higher-order loop hierarchy.
Probability.comment: 79 pages. Extended the main results to smaller bandwidths, down to the scale of $\log N$

Probability.title: Understanding Simulated Annealing: from Weak Poincaré Inequalities to a Discrete Optimal Transport Framework
Probability.summary:
Simulated annealing follows a path of distributions from an easy initial law to a target. Standard analyses require rapid mixing at every fixed temperature, which can fail for multimodal targets even when annealing succeeds. Motivated by the continuous optimal-transport analysis of annealed Langevin dynamics by Guo, Tao, and Chen (ICLR 2025), we develop a discrete optimal-transport framework for finite-state annealing.
  The discrete action of the path integrates the minimum electrical energy needed to route the demand $-\partial_sπ_s$ through the chain's transition capacities. Like a path-dependent inverse conductance, it penalizes a bottleneck only when the path must move mass across it. We also introduce weak action, which leaves an $\varepsilon$ amount of this motion unrouted. Up to initialization error, action $\mathcal A$ gives reverse-KL error at most $\mathcal A/(4T)$ after $T$ expected updates, while weak action gives TV error at most $\varepsilon+\sqrt{\mathcal A^{w}_\varepsilon/(8T)}$.
  Paralleling canonical paths and Poincaré inequalities, we develop flow and spectral bounds, showing that pathwise (weak) Poincaré inequalities imply (weak) action bounds. We also show that a weak Poincaré inequality yields a genuine one after removing a small amount of mass. As a pathwise analogue of chain decomposition, we obtain a componentwise algorithm for mixtures with phase weights supplied at initialization.
  Applications include mean-field Ising and Potts models and bipartite spin systems. For every fixed $δ>0$, we give a polynomial-time single-site annealing sampler for uniform independent sets in $(d,D)$-biregular bipartite graphs with $D/d\geq1+δ$ and large $D$. To our knowledge, this is the first polynomial-time sampler requiring only a fixed multiplicative degree imbalance, strictly extending the $D\geq7d\log d$ regime of Cannon and Perkins (SODA 2020).

Probability.title: Phase Transitions for Random Least Common Multiples with Memory
Probability.summary: We study the least common multiple of a random subset of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ when the selection follows a correlated Bernoulli process with memory. The copying rule preserves the marginal retention probabilities and creates a genealogical forest. At fixed density, the logarithmic least common multiple exhibits a fluctuation phase transition at the memory parameter $a=1/2$. The boundary limits depend on how genealogical families are distributed among the divisibility classes carrying the leading arithmetic weight. Our proofs combine the von Mangoldt representation with a reduction to large primes. At fixed density, an exact expansion separates an innovation martingale from a memory term. An asymptotic projection onto the retained count identifies the contribution of memory. Marked point-process convergence and estimates for rare genealogical families give the boundary limits.

Probability.title: Fingerprints of feedback cycles in stationary diffusions
Probability.summary: When does the stationary density of a $d$-dimensional diffusion process driven by standard Brownian motion uniquely determine its drift? In general, it does not: the $d$ drift components enter the stationary Fokker-Planck equation only through a single scalar divergence. We consider drifts whose component functions only depend on a subset of their input variables, and encode this dependence with a directed graph. We exclude 2-cycles, which admit rotations that leave the stationary density invariant, but otherwise allow arbitrary graphs, including those with feedback cycles. We show that if the stationary density is sufficiently $s$-concave, e.g., strictly log-concave, then the drift is uniquely determined among graph-structured drifts in a weighted Sobolev space. For drifts with linear self-regulation, a single locally strictly convex level set of the stationary density is sufficient to identify the drift in the region it encloses. Both results follow from Raychaudhuri equations. Excluding 2-cycles allows treating nontrivial rotational and symmetric terms simultaneously, extending the scope of the corresponding Bochner- and Reilly-type arguments. We illustrate the results by recovering the Hill-type regulation of a stochastic genetic repressilator from samples of its stationary distribution.

Probability.title: A Markovian SuASR epidemic framework with stochastic external factors
Probability.summary: Epidemic waves are often shaped by uncertain external drivers, such as environmental variability or behavioral and policy changes, that can randomly amplify or dampen transmission. Capturing this randomness requires models whose dynamics evolve under time-varying, stochastic influences. In this paper, we introduce a stochastic Susceptible-Asymptomatic-Symptomatic-Removed (SuASR) framework that embeds random external factors directly into the epidemic mechanism through an extended continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC). The proposed framework is flexible enough to represent epidemic dynamics both with reinfection and with infection-induced immunity, depending on the epidemiological setting under study. Unlike standard Markovian epidemic models, our formulation explicitly tracks two concurrent infectious sources (asymptomatic and symptomatic), yielding coupled infection pathways and substantially richer transient behavior. A key contribution is analytical tractability, where we derive computable expressions for the joint distribution of asymptomatic and symptomatic infection-event counts and develop tools tailored to extreme-outbreak risk, including the distribution of the maximum infectious burden. These results enable probabilistic quantification of epidemic severity beyond mean trajectories, providing direct estimates of the likelihood of rare but consequential surges. We validate the model through extensive sensitivity analysis and an application to the H1N1 influenza epidemic, illustrating how stochastic external influences reshape outbreak profiles, total infections from both sources, and the probability of extreme epidemic scenarios

Probability.title: Tail behaviour of infimum of Gaussian processes
Probability.summary: We investigate the upper tail of $\inf_{t\in\mathcal T}X(t)$, where $X$ is a centred Gaussian process (GP) with continuous sample paths on a nonempty compact metric space $\mathcal T$. As suggested by the findings of [1], the exponential rate is governed by an optimal-measure problem, while the exact prefactor depends on the local geometry of the corresponding contact set. In the full-contact regime, we strengthen the known Gumbel max-domain of attraction property of the distribution of $\inf_{t\in\mathcal T}X(t)$ by establishing the von Mises condition. For fractional Brownian motion on $[a,b]$, $0<a<b$, with Hurst index $H\in(0,1/2)$, we also determine the order of the logarithmic correction to the leading Gaussian exponential. For finite contact sets, we distinguish dominated, smooth-critical, and rough-critical regimes and derive exact asymptotics of $P\{\inf_{t\in\mathcal T}X(t)>u\}$ as $u\to\infty$ under suitable local assumptions. We illustrate our findings with examples including fractional Brownian motion and the fractional Brownian sheet.

Probability.title: Impropriety and resilience of the chromatic number
Probability.summary: We show that, for $p$ bounded away from $1$ and $np\to\infty$, the chromatic number of the binomial random graph $G_{n,p}$ is resilient to removal of a subgraph $H$ with $o(n \log(np))$ edges. It follows that the same assertion holds with $H$ being a subgraph of maximum degree $o(\log(np))$; and both these results are best possible up to a constant factor. We also prove corresponding results for the random $r$-regular graph $G_{n,r}$, when $r\to\infty$ and $r/n$ is bounded away from $1$, where $H$ has $o(n\log r)$ edges or maximum degree $o(\log r)$. Our results rely on a natural connection between chromatic resilience to edge removal and improper graph colouring. This work provides counterpoint to the work of Sudakov and Vu (2008) and Alon and Sudakov (2010), which treated chromatic resilience for $G_{n,p}$ subject to the addition, rather than removal, of edges.

Probability.title: Harmonic and Monogenic Representations of White Noise and its weighted harmonic Bergman estimates
Probability.summary: Continuing Feichtinger's generalized stochastic process theory, we analyze harmonic and monogenic representations of white noise in Euclidean spaces. We define its convolution with square-integrable functions. Using the weighted Sobolev regularity of the white noise, we establish a high-dimensional Sokhotski-Plemelj formula for the white noise density. Furthermore, we embed these representations into new weighted Bergman spaces, proving that the weighted Bergman norms of the harmonic representations are bounded by the white noise's weighted Sobolev norms.

Probability.title: Perron--Wright asymptotics and critical component processes for inhomogeneous random graphs
Probability.summary:
We extend Wright's enumeration of connected labelled graphs with fixed surplus to irreducible critical finite type kernels and continuous compact type kernels satisfying a positivity condition. Let $\mathsf{C}_t(k,r)$ denote the total weight of connected labelled graphs with $k$ vertices and surplus $r$. Let $u>0$ satisfy $Ku=u$ and $\int u dμ=1$, and put $α=\int u^2 dμ$ and $β=\int u^3 dμ$. We prove that the rooted-tree radius $ρ$ is positive and real analytic near $1$, with $ρ(1)=1$ and $\logρ(t)=\frac{α^2}{2β}(t-1)^2+O(|t-1|^3)$, and that, for fixed $r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ and $0\le L<\infty$, $\mathsf{C}_t(k,r)=w_rβ^{(r-1)/2}e^{-k}ρ(t)^{-k}k^{k+3r/2-2}\{1+O_{r,L}(k^{-1/2})\}$, uniformly for $|t-1|\le Lk^{-1/2}$, where $w_r$ is the classical Wright constant. At criticality, the leading constant depends on the kernel only through $β$, under the stated normalization of $u$.
  At $t_n=1+λn^{-1/3}$, exact component identities combine with these asymptotics to give fixed size factorial densities and local size and surplus point-process limits for deterministic finite type models and annealed compact type Bollobás-Janson-Riordan models. With sizes rescaled by $β^{1/3}n^{-2/3}$, the limit is the Aldous process at parameter $αβ^{-2/3}λ$, and the corresponding type profiles concentrate at the Perron law $p(dx)=u(x)μ(dx)$. For every bounded uniformly positive countable critical kernel, we construct graph sequences with growing finite supports and the same local limits, and identify the additive shift of the critical window caused by spectral perturbations of order $n^{-1/3}$.

Probability.title: Infinite dimensional Gaussian limits for the giant component of inhomogeneous random graphs
Probability.summary: We prove Gaussian limits for the type measure of the giant component in sparse inhomogeneous random graphs. Countable types yield convergence in a weighted Hilbert space under boundedness, irreducibility, supercriticality, and a uniform tail condition on the empirical type weights. For types on a finite dimensional closed Riemannian manifold, smooth kernels yield convergence in a negative Sobolev space for any Borel type distribution. We allow deterministic types and first order kernel perturbations; independent type sampling adds an independent Gaussian term. The proof combines a seeded exploration identity, Hilbert space martingale limits, tail estimates, and inversion of the branching operator outside the giant. Finite types with random parameters are covered. A heat kernel example gives explicit variances for all spectral modes.

Probability.title: Heavy tails in Gaussian-process surrogates: process-level profiling degeneracy versus observation-level identifiability
Probability.summary: In this article, we study heavy-tailed alternatives to Gaussian-process surrogates, namely Student-$t$ processes, $α$-stable processes and Gaussian processes with heavy-tailed noise. These are Gaussian scale mixtures, and the position of the mixing variable decides whether the tails can be learned from a single realization. For process-level mixtures with a free amplitude, the profile likelihood of the mixing law is data-free and is maximized by the Gaussian law, the plug-in predictive is a data-free transformation of the Gaussian-process predictive, and no estimator can be consistent for the mixing law over the model along one path. For observation-level mixtures with symmetric $α$-stable noise, the tail index is identifiable. Further, for one-dimensional inputs under fixed-domain asymptotics with $α_0<2$ and compact hyperparameter sets, a cross-fitted plug-in estimator and the Laplace marginal-likelihood estimate computed at the global posterior mode attain the efficiency bound of the model with a known regression function, also for Matérn-$5/2$ sample paths. We also characterize small-sample failures of the Laplace approximation as folds of a posterior-mode branch and give a diagnostic. Finally, in a repeated Bayesian optimization study, observation-level tails reduced regret under gross outliers, as did Student-$t$ noise, and no degradation was detected under Gaussian noise.
Probability.comment: Extended 4 November 2026 version, with supplementary material included

Probability.title: Density estimation for exponential functionals of subordinators
Probability.summary: Exponential functionals of subordinators play a key role in probability theory and arise in numerous applications, yet explicit density formulas have until now been available only in a limited number of special settings. This paper provides a general remedy. First, we obtain a closed-form representation of the density for the entire class of integer-valued subordinators (compound Poisson processes with positive integer jump sizes) in the form of a rapidly converging series whose coefficients obey a simple recurrence; we further extend the construction to include drift by means of an explicit iterative scheme. Second, we propose a general approximation method for arbitrary driftless subordinators, including cases where the Lévy measure has continuous support. By discretizing the Lévy measure, we generate a sequence of explicit, computable densities that is proved to converge to the true density. Together, these results greatly broaden the theory of exponential functionals, transforming a problem previously tractable only in rare instances into one that is either explicitly solvable or can be systematically approximated for the full class of subordinators. The resulting formulas enable fast and accurate computations for financial modelling, insurance risk assessment, and stochastic simulation, while the approximation procedure provides a robust and stable alternative to existing numerical methods. The unified framework --- linking pantograph equations, $q$-calculus, and Poisson approximation --- also opens avenues for analyzing more general decreasing functionals and drifted subordinators with general Lévy measures.
Probability.comment: 34 pages, 2 tables, 6 figures. Retitled (formerly "On certain integral functionals of integer-valued subordinators"), reorganized for clarity, main results unchanged

Probability.title: Edge universality of sparse Erdős-Rényi digraphs
Probability.summary:
Let $\mathcal A$ be the adjacency matrix of the Erdős-Rényi directed graph $\mathscr G(N,p)$. We denote the eigenvalues of $\mathcal A$ by $λ_1^{\cal A},...,λ^{\cal A}_N$, and $|λ_1^{\cal A}|=\max_i|λ_i^{\cal A}|$. For $N^{-1+o(1)}\leq p\leq 1/2$, we show that \[ \max_{i=2,3,...,N} \bigg|\frac{λ_i^{\mathcal A}}{\sqrt{Np(1-p)}}\bigg| =1+O(N^{-1/2+o(1)}) \] with very high probability. In addition, we prove that near the unit circle, the local eigenvalue statistics of ${\mathcal A}/\sqrt{Np(1-p)}$ coincide with those of the real Ginibre ensemble. As a by-product, we also show that all non-trivial eigenvectors of $\mathcal A$ are completely delocalized.
  For Hermitian random matrices, it is known that the edge statistics are sensitive to the sparsity: in the very sparse regime, one needs to remove many noise random variables (which affect both the mean and the fluctuation) to recover the Tracy-Widom distribution. Our results imply that, compared to their analogues in the Hermitian case, the edge statistics of non-Hermitian sparse random matrices are more robust.

Probability.title: Stochastic Parallel Transport along Markov Processes: I. General Theory
Probability.summary: We give a framework for transporting vectors along Markov processes that may have jumps, without assuming a manifold or other specific geometric structure. We prove existence and uniqueness of the resulting transport. In doing so, we develop a theory of vector bundles defined quasi-everywhere, in which the vectors live, and an axiomatic framework for energy forms that determine the bundle and the transport.

Probability.title: On Size-Biased Distributions and the Chainability of Positive Infinitely Divisible Distributions
Probability.summary: Bar-Lev and Letac (2025) introduced the concept of chainability of infinitely divisible distributions on $\mathbb R$. In this note, we show that a simpler notion of chainability can be used for infinitely divisible distributions on $[0,\infty)$. We derive some properties and give a probabilistic interpretation in terms of so-called size-biased distributions. As an application, we discuss simulation from size-biased distributions associated with an important class of tempered stable distributions.

Probability.title: Large-Time Analysis of the Langevin Dynamics for Energies Fulfilling Polyak-Łojasiewicz Conditions
Probability.summary: In this work, we take a step towards understanding overdamped Langevin dynamics for the minimization of a general class of objective functions $\mathcal{L}$. We establish well-posedness and regularity of the law $ρ_t$ of the process through novel a priori estimates, and, very importantly, we characterize the large-time behavior of $ρ_t$ under truly minimal assumptions on $\mathcal{L}$. In the case of integrable Gibbs density, the law converges to the normalized Gibbs measure. In the non-integrable case, we prove that the law diffuses. The rate of convergence, in terms of relative Dirichlet energy with respect to the Gibbs measure, is $\mathcal O(1/(σt))$, where $σ$ is the diffusion parameter. Under a Polyak-Lojasiewicz (PL) condition on $\mathcal{L}$, we also derive sharp exponential contractivity results toward the set of global minimizers. Combining these results we provide the first systematic convergence analysis of Langevin dynamics under PL conditions in non-integrable Gibbs settings: a first phase of exponential in time contraction toward the set of minimizers and then a large-time exploration over it with rate $\mathcal O(1/(σt))$ in terms of the relative Dirichlet energy.

Probability.title: Holomorphic Cauchy Networks for Efficient Stationary Tail Computation in High-Dimensional Reflected Brownian Motions
Probability.summary: Stationary tail computation for high-dimensional reflected Brownian motions (RBMs) remains computationally challenging. Building on NN4MGF's shared-coordinate basic-adjoint-relationship (BAR) framework, we develop Holomorphic Cauchy Networks (HCNs). Native complex-valued rational Cauchy subnetworks enforce holomorphicity on pole-free domains, removing sampled Cauchy-Riemann penalties and their input-derivative graphs. Exact origin anchoring and boundary-coordinate exclusion enforce structural identities, while anchored interactions represent dependent transforms. Under holomorphic-log assumptions, we establish simultaneous value and first-derivative approximation for the constrained architectures and a mixed-derivative lower bound for coordinate-only representations under nonzero cross-covariance. Closed-form real-axis derivatives and sequential backpropagation further control memory. On the same NVIDIA H100 NVL, the tested 30D HCN configuration uses approximately tenfold less peak allocated memory and has 9.7-fold lower mean update time than NN4MGF; extrapolation to the respective scheduled update counts gives a projected full-schedule update-time ratio of 58.2. With 64 million sampled base inputs per high-dimensional run, HCN reaches 50 dimensions on a laptop GPU with 6.367% mean relative error over thresholds 1 through 8. Degree-matched comparisons yield lower reported mean relative errors over the primary evaluation ranges, including 1.422% versus 6.684% on the 2D Harrison non-product benchmark. On a 10D correlated RBM benchmark, HCN achieves 3.829% mean relative error over thresholds 1 through 8 against a simulation reference, compared with 19.386% for an independent-marginal baseline.
Probability.comment: 28 pages, 3 figures, 14 tables. Updated the 10D simulation reference and revised the exposition. Code available at https://github.com/KehanWang126/holomorphic-cauchy-networks-rbm

Probability.title: Mean-level arithmetic computation via stochastic reaction networks
Probability.summary: Reaction networks provide a natural model for analog computation in which inputs and outputs are encoded by molecular abundances. Much of the work on analog computation with chemical reaction networks (CRNs) has focused on deterministic mass-action systems. In DNA- and protein-based circuits, however, low copy numbers can make intrinsic fluctuations significant, motivating the use of stochastic models. In this paper, we develop a framework for computation with stochastic CRNs at the level of stationary means. Specifically, we construct elementary arithmetic modules for identification, addition, and multiplication, and analyze their mean-level correctness and convergence rates. We focus on these three modules because they are simple enough to analyze explicitly while already exhibiting the new issues raised by stochastic mean-level computation. Unlike in deterministic systems, the computed value cannot be read from a single output measurement. Instead, readout requires Monte Carlo estimation, with error arising from transient bias as the system approaches stationarity and intrinsic sampling noise that persists even at stationarity. We therefore study the convergence rates of output means, variances, and autocovariances to their stationary values, as well as the stationary fluctuations governing sampling error. We also show that this readout cost can depend strongly, and sometimes unexpectedly, on the architecture of the computation. In particular, comparing linear-chain and binary-tree implementations reveals that binary trees can greatly reduce stationary variance for addition, but can instead produce exponentially larger variance for multiplication.

Differential Geometry.title: Complete gradient Yamabe solitons
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, all complete gradient Yamabe solitons of dimension at least three are classified. More precisely, we show that complete steady gradient Yamabe solitons are either rotationally symmetric manifolds or scalar-flat manifolds. We also classify nontrivial complete shrinking and expanding gradient Yamabe solitons.

Differential Geometry.title: Collapsing flat manifolds with totally geodesic boundary
Differential Geometry.summary: We study volume collapse of compact connected flat manifolds with nonempty totally geodesic boundary and uniformly bounded diameter. We prove subsequential Gromov--Hausdorff convergence to compact flat orbifolds, allowing reflector loci, and describe the limit using the canonical involutions of the doubles. We distinguish the cases in which the maximal distance to the boundary tends to zero or to a positive limit, and classify all possible limits in dimension three.

Differential Geometry.title: Polar foliations on the Cayley plane
Differential Geometry.summary: We classify polar foliations on the Cayley projective plane, completing the classification of polar foliations on compact rank one symmetric spaces.

Differential Geometry.title: Geometric Endpoints, Global Trajectories, and Teichmüller Projection for the Möbius-Invariant Willmore Flow
Differential Geometry.summary: We study endpoints and conformal projection of the Möbius-invariant Willmore flow in the round three-sphere. Under uniform nonumbilicity or an integrable weighted condition, image-measure transport yields a unique finite-time integral-varifold limit. Reduced Hopf trajectories have unique anchored finite-time profile and marked conformal endpoints at arbitrary energy. Every smooth global reduced trajectory converges smoothly modulo reparametrization to an elastic profile, with quantitative rates and finite dissipation length. We compute the differential of the conformal-class projection along reduced trajectories and prove that its maximal rank persists at every finite time when it holds initially. Near the Clifford torus, Hopf tori with the same marked conformal type can have noncollinear projected velocities, ruling out a common autonomous Teichmüller equation even after positive time recalibrations.

Differential Geometry.title: Uniqueness of Finite-Time Varifold Limits for the Möbius-Invariant Willmore Flow
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove uniqueness of finite-time geometric endpoints for the Möbius-invariant Willmore flow in $\mathbb{S}^3$ under uniform quantitative nonumbilicity. The multiplicity-counting varifolds converge, without reparametrization or Möbius renormalization, to a unique integral two-varifold. An intrinsic transport estimate gives quantitative total-variation convergence of the induced area measures on the fixed domain and bounded-Lipschitz Cauchy control of their pushforwards. Together with Allard compactness and rectifiability, this upgrades subsequential compactness to full-trajectory varifold convergence. The limit has generalized Euclidean mean curvature in $L^2$ with the natural endpoint lower-semicontinuity bound. For finite maximal trajectories with initial energy at most $8π$, Jakob's subsequential alternative becomes sequence independent: the limit is zero, or it has unit density and embedded Lipschitz support of genus zero or one. For Hopf-torus trajectories under the same energy bound, nonumbilicity is automatic and the anchored constant-speed profiles converge weakly in $W^{2,2}$ and strongly in $W^{1,2}$ and $C^{1,α}$ for every $α<\frac{1}{2}$. At infinite time, the same method yields a unique limit under an additional finite-dissipation-length condition.

Differential Geometry.title: Index and nullity of critical spherical catenoids in hyperbolic three-space
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that every critical spherical catenoid in a geodesic ball of hyperbolic three-space has Morse index four and nullity two. This resolves Medvedev's index conjecture throughout the parameter range of the catenoid family. The kernel consists precisely of the normal components of rotations that preserve the center of the ball and tilt the axis of the catenoid. As consequences, the radius of the supporting ball increases strictly along the family, and each critical spherical catenoid admits a smooth family of free boundary constant mean curvature deformations in its supporting ball. The proof combines a global boundary inequality obtained from a Wronskian, a positive Dirichlet eigenfunction supplied by the time component of the unit normal, and a Riccati comparison for the angular mode $k=2$. A ground-state identity then yields positivity of every angular mode $k\ge2$. We also show that the energy index of every critical spherical catenoid in $\mathbb{H^3}$, that is, the index of the second variation of its energy, equals four; hence the inequality between the energy index and the spectral index conjectured by Medvedev for geodesic balls of $\mathbb{H^n}$ fails.
Differential Geometry.comment: 18 pages. v3: added Theorem 2 and Section 9: the energy index of every critical spherical catenoid in $\mathbb{H^3}$ is four, disproving the inequality in Medvedev [10, Remark 7]

Differential Geometry.title: Pluriclosed flow on Kähler manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove the maximal existence conjecture for pluriclosed flow on Kähler backgrounds. This leads to a priori generalizations of the Aubin-Yau and Calabi-Yau theorems, and resolves the question of connectedness of generalized Kähler structures on Calabi-Yau backgrounds.

Differential Geometry.title: Critical-point-free energy for fractional-Toledo representations
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $S_g$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g\ge2$. For a reductive representation $ρ:π_1(S_g)\to\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$, let $E_ρ$ be the energy function on Teichmüller space associated to equivariant harmonic maps into $\mathrm{CH}^2$. For every positive integer $d$ with $3\nmid d$, all sufficiently large $h$, and every $g>h$, we construct an irreducible reductive representation \[ ρ_{g,h,d}:π_1(S_g)\to\mathrm{PU}(2,1) \] with \[ τ(ρ_{g,h,d})=2h-2-\frac{2d}{3}\notin\mathbb Z, \qquad \mathrm{Crit}(E_{ρ_{g,h,d}})=\varnothing. \] Consequently, the associated branched-minimal-surface forgetful map is not surjective in these nonintegral Toledo components.
Differential Geometry.comment: Improved typesetting. Mathematics and content remain unchanged

Differential Geometry.title: Smooth Rigidity Near Extremal Horizons
Differential Geometry.summary: The Einstein equations constrain the transverse Taylor series at a degenerate Killing horizon, but even complete knowledge of that series need not determine a smooth spacetime: a nonzero difference can vanish to every order at the horizon. We show that this ambiguity disappears when the limiting metric on the space of Killing orbits admits a spacelike graph over a compact horizon section. In dimensions $d\geq4$, smooth vacuum Einstein germs with the same marked transverse jets are then locally isometric on a two-sided neighborhood of the whole section. The proof combines a terminal wave-map gauge with energy estimates on the orbit cylinder and yields a finite weighted matching criterion. For unwarped horizons with positive-Einstein sections, a condition on the full Lichnerowicz spectrum reduces the smooth classification to parallel first transverse data. All such data have convergent multiwarped Einstein realizations, including examples whose sections have negative sectional-curvature directions. We also obtain a finite-regularity version for round sections. The continuation argument extends to four-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell theory and gives smooth charged-Nariai rigidity.
