Code is available at: https://github.com/Sachithx/ConceptTime.git.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026, Main Track, Poster

Signal Processing.title: Partially Decentralized Multi-Agent Q-Learning via Digital Cousins for Wireless Networks
Signal Processing.summary: Q-learning is a widely used reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm for optimizing wireless networks, but faces challenges with large state-spaces. Recently proposed multi-environment mixed Q-learning (MEMQ) algorithm addresses these challenges by employing multiple Q-learning algorithms across multiple synthetically generated, distinct but structurally related environments, so-called digital cousins. In this paper, we propose a novel multi-agent MEMQ (M-MEMQ) for cooperative decentralized wireless networks with multiple networked transmitters (TXs) and base stations (BSs). TXs do not have access to global information (joint state and actions). The new concept of coordinated and uncoordinated states is introduced. In uncoordinated states, TXs act independently to minimize their individual costs and update local Q-functions. In coordinated states, TXs use a Bayesian approach to estimate the joint state and update the joint Q-functions. The cost of information-sharing scales linearly with the number of TXs and is independent of the joint state-action space size. Several theoretical guarantees, including deterministic and probabilistic convergence, bounds on estimation error variance, and the probability of misdetecting the joint states, are given. Numerical simulations show that M-MEMQ outperforms several decentralized and centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE) multi-agent RL algorithms by achieving 60% lower average policy error (APE), 40% faster convergence, 45% reduced runtime complexity, and 40% less sample complexity. Furthermore, M-MEMQ achieves comparable APE with significantly lower complexity than centralized methods. Simulations validate the theoretical analyses.
Signal Processing.comment: This work has been accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing

Signal Processing.title: Soft-then-Hard: Joint Link Association and Precoding Optimization for LEO Satellite Networks
Signal Processing.summary: Spatial multiplexing in dense low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite downlinks is hindered by two bottlenecks. First, line-of-sight (LoS)-dominant propagation from a high orbital altitude places the users in a narrow angular region, which limits the spatial resolution achievable by a single satellite. Second, the visible satellites cause severe inter-satellite interference. Both effects call for joint link association and precoding, because the association decides which users are served together and which streams interfere. However, conventional block coordinate descent with hard association updates suffers from premature turning-off, where an inactive link loses precoder power and cannot be reactivated in subsequent iterations. To overcome this limitation, we propose a soft-then-hard update scheme that relaxes the association into continuous weights via iterative scaling, keeping candidate links active. Annealing progressively concentrates the association weights as the precoders are updated, after which a single hard matching determines the serving links. We further extend this framework to the LEO space-time channel, where distinct Doppler shifts provide user separability beyond angular geometry. Numerical results show that, over the space-time channel, the proposed design outperforms the baselines while effectively exploiting this separability.
Signal Processing.comment: 13 pages, 8 figures

Signal Processing.title: Coexistence of LEO Satellite Communication Systems under Regulatory Protection Constraints
Signal Processing.summary: This paper investigates the coexistence of two low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communication systems sharing the same frequency band: a primary system with regulatory precedence over the spectrum and a secondary system that must not cause excessive interference to the primary system's ground users. This spectrum sharing paradigm was recently formalized by the United States Federal Communications Commission (FCC) through short-term and long-term protection criteria that limit primary-link unavailability and throughput degradation due to interference inflicted by the secondary system. To facilitate coexistence, we propose a satellite selection mechanism that associates the secondary system's satellites with clusters of ground cells at each handover to maximize secondary-user throughput while abiding by these regulatory constraints. Our mechanism enforces both constraints through a cumulative assessment that combines past primary-link performance with predicted performance over the upcoming handover interval. Simulation results show that our proposed method achieves up to 31% higher secondary-user throughput than prior work that imposes interference-to-noise ratio (INR) constraints, even when its constraints are tuned to satisfy the FCC's throughput-based protection criteria.

Signal Processing.title: Mechanistic Interpretability with Sparse Autoencoder Neural Operators
Signal Processing.summary: We introduce sparse autoencoder neural operators (SAE-NOs), a new class of sparse autoencoders that operate in function spaces rather than fixed-dimensional Euclidean representations. We formalize the functional representation hypothesis, where data are explained through sparse compositions of structured functions. Unlike standard SAEs that represent concepts with scalar activations, SAE-NOs parameterize concepts as functions, enabling representations that capture not only a concept's presence, but also how and where it is expressed across the input domain. We achieve this through joint sparsity: concept sparsity selects active concepts, while domain sparsity governs where they are expressed. We instantiate this framework using Fourier neural operators (SAE-FNOs), parameterizing concepts as integral operators in the Fourier domain. This functional and spectral parameterization is particularly advantageous when data exhibit spatial structure across scales or when concepts are frequency-structured. We characterize SAE-FNO on vision data and demonstrate that it learns localized patterns, uses concepts more efficiently, and exhibits stable concept characteristics across sparsity levels. We further show that SAE-FNO adapts to changes in domain size and generalizes across discretizations, operating at resolutions beyond those seen during training, where standard SAEs fail. We also introduce lifting into SAEs and show theoretically and empirically that it acts as a preconditioner that accelerates optimization. Overall, our results show that moving from vector-valued to functional parameterizations, with concept and domain sparsity, extends SAEs from representing concept presence to modeling structured concept expression, highlighting the importance of parameterization.
Signal Processing.comment: Tolooshams and Shen has equal contribution. Preprint. Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. Earlier version was presented as Oral and Extended Abstract at the Workshop on Unifying Representations in Neural Models (UniReps) at NeurIPS 2025

Signal Processing.title: From Winding-Fault Geometry to Reliability: Estimation and Prognosis of Stator Inter-Turn Faults
Signal Processing.summary: This paper develops an integrated framework for estimation, prognosis, and reliability assessment of stator inter-turn faults in induction motors. The fault is characterized by its severity, defined as the fraction of short-circuited turns, and its spatial orientation. A geometric fault model shows that the resulting output signature is affine in the fault severity and exhibits a fundamental spatial periodicity. Exploiting this structure, an augmented-state particle filter jointly estimates the nonlinear electromechanical state and the unknown fault severity while quantifying posterior uncertainty. The estimated degradation is then propagated using four prognostic models: linear trend, Holt exponential smoothing, Bayesian degradation, and particle-based forecasting. Their predictions are connected to threshold-crossing remaining useful life (RUL), first-passage reliability, degradation-dependent hazard reliability, and a Weibull lifetime benchmark, thereby providing both deterministic and probabilistic health assessments. Numerical results demonstrate accurate online fault estimation and output reconstruction, characterize the effects of degradation pattern and prediction horizon on prognosis, and show consistent reliability and threshold-crossing predictions. Moreover, estimation accuracy remains comparable across the distinct fault orientations induced by the spatial periodicity. The resulting framework provides a unified connection from physics-based inter-turn fault modeling to online diagnosis, degradation prognosis, and reliability assessment.

Information Theory.title: Optimal Sampling and Transmission Policy for Information Freshness in Gossip Networks
Information Theory.summary: We study the optimal sampling and transmission policies for a transmitter communicating with n gossiping receivers with the objective of tracking a source's status over time using a semantic freshness metric: Version Age of Information (VAoI). The transmitter observes the version changes in the source, and can acquire a new information version by paying a sampling cost. The receivers gossip, allowing information exchange among each other without direct transmission. Gossiping can save on transmission cost, but it may propagate stale version information, necessitating transmitter intervention. With imperfect communication links, we formulate an infinite horizon average cost Markov Decision Process (MDP) in order to jointly optimize receivers' VAoIs, sampling and transmission costs in a time slotted fully connected (FC) gossip network. We first solve the MDP using Relative Value Iteration (RVI) algorithm. Then, we prove that the sampling decision has a threshold structure in the transmitter VAoI. Further, under reliable gossiping links, we show that transmission and idling has an VAoI-difference threshold structure with minimum VAoI activation. Numerical results obtained using RVI show that the optimal policy consistently outperforms natural baselines. These results characterize how source sampling, direct transmission, and receiver gossip should be jointly coordinated for cost-aware semantic freshness in gossip networks.

Information Theory.title: CL-SEC: Cross-Layer Semantic Error Correction Empowered by Language Models
Information Theory.summary: Achieving reliable communication has long been a fundamental challenge in networked systems. Semantic Error Correction (SEC) leverages the semantic understanding capabilities of language models (LMs) to perform application-layer error correction, complementing conventional channel decoding. While promising, existing SEC approaches rely solely on context captured by LMs at the application layer, ignoring the rich information available at the physical layer. To address this limitation, this paper introduces Cross-Layer SEC (CL-SEC), an LM-empowered error correction framework that integrates cross-layer information from both the physical and application layers to jointly correct corrupted words in text communication. Using a Bayesian combination in product form tailored to this framework, CL-SEC achieves significantly improved performance over methods that process information in isolated layers. CL-SEC shows substantial gains across multiple error-correction metrics, including bit-error rate, word-error rate, and semantic fidelity scores. Importantly, unlike most semantic communication systems that focus solely on recovering the semantic meaning of transmitted messages, CL-SEC aims to reconstruct the original transmitted message verbatim, leveraging the semantic understanding capabilities of LMs for precise reconstruction.

Information Theory.title: Quantum synchronizable codes, polynomial and quasi-polynomial shifts
Information Theory.summary: Quantum synchronizable codes protect quantum information against Pauli errors and against misalignments of the block boundaries. Almost all known constructions use cyclic codes, because the channel shifts the transmitted block cyclically. We study what happens when the algebraic shift of the code differs from the physical one. When one uses a twisted padding, constacyclic codes synchronize at no cost, and they are the only polycyclic codes with this property for a linear padding. For the other polycyclic codes, we measure the cost of each misaligned position, and we show that the phase damage it causes can be corrected as erasures. Using annihilator duality, we extend the construction to quasi-polycyclic codes, in which the cost is confined to a single block. We prove that the usual quasi-cyclic families have a distance bound that does not grow with the length, and show that quasi-polycyclic codes over repeated-root trinomials overcome it, giving synchronizable codes with larger dimension and distance than the known synchronizable codes of the same length.
authors: Miguel de los Ríos de Antonio

Information Theory.title: A Spectral Representation Of The Simple Hypothesis Testing Problem
Information Theory.summary: The minimum Type II error probability (or volume) of simple hypothesis tests with randomized detectors is expressed as a Riemann integral of the (cumulative) distribution function of the likelihood ratio for all non-negative Type I error probability (or volume) values: $β(\varepsilon)=\int_{0}^{\infty}|F(1/τ)-\varepsilon|^{+}dτ$ for all $\varepsilon\geq0$. The derivation relies on convex conjugation (the Legendre transform) and level set integration, and is sufficiently general to extend to tests between $σ$-finite measures. Measure change identities relating the $β(\cdot)$ functions of different hypothesis testing problems are established. Approximations for Type II and Type I volumes are derived under two different hypotheses concerning the Kolmogorov distance to normality for the log-likelihood ratio distributions. In both the Central Limit Theorem and the large deviations regimes, the resulting non-asymptotic expressions recover and extend state-of-the-art characterizations of optimal performance in the memoryless case, and improve and generalize them in the Markovian case. Finally, The distinction between the implications of the Central Limit Theorem and the Berry--Esseen Theorem for the asymptotic simple hypothesis testing problem is clarified.
Information Theory.comment: 30 pages. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Information Theory

Information Theory.title: Efficient Soft-Output Guessing for Enhanced Quantum Tanner Code Decoding
Information Theory.summary: We introduce a generalized low-density parity-check decoding framework for quantum Tanner codes utilizing soft-output guessing random additive noise decoding (SOGRAND). By soft-output decoding entire component codes rather than individual parity checks, we mitigate the effects of trapping sets and cycles, resulting in improved convergence. Because our decoder preserves the message passing structure of standard belief propagation (BP), it is compatible with many BP enhancements. We demonstrate this with OSD postprocessing, quaternary BP, and RelayBP, each yielding further gains. Standalone SOGRAND outperforms the standard BP+OSD baseline by over two orders of magnitude in logical error rate. In combination with the Relay principle, SOGRAND outperforms RelayBP by over one order of magnitude, providing a way forward for scalable decoding of the emerging class of Tanner-code-based quantum codes.

Information Theory.title: Efficient SC-Flip Decoding for Polar Codes through Decision-Boundary Normalization
Information Theory.summary: Accurate first erroneous position (FEP) identification is key to improving the error-correction performance of successive cancellation flip (SCF) decoding. However, FEP identification remains challenging with a limited number of re-decoding attempts. To address this issue, we propose decision-boundary normalization (DBN) to improve FEP identification and develop a novel DBN-SCF decoding algorithm. DBN normalizes the magnitude of each decision log-likelihood ratio (LLR) by the standard deviation predicted by the Gaussian approximation (GA) for the corresponding bit-channel. This allows a single normalized threshold to be shared across bit-channels within each code configuration, giving it a consistent statistical meaning and avoiding per-channel calibration. DBN-SCF decoding selects candidate flip positions from the information set in the natural successive cancellation (SC) decoding order using a threshold, without sorting. Moreover, DBN-SCF decoding achieves better error-correction performance with a limited number of re-decoding attempts. It also requires lower average decoding complexity than existing SCF decoding methods at a comparable level of error-correction performance.

Information Theory.title: Quantum channel bounds for constant-composition codes
Information Theory.summary:
We extend the quantum-channel optimization of Alrabiah and Guruswami to $q$-ary constant-composition codes. We study explicit channel and flag constructions that recover selected classical asymptotic upper bounds, including the Ben-Haim--Litsyn, moving-subspace and Horn-channel bounds. We give two equivalent formulations, Gram and flag, and prove stability of the obtained upper bounds under permutation transport and generalized shortening. A hierarchy defined by bounding the output-state ranks within each flag improves strictly between consecutive levels at every composition and every positive distance below the Plotkin threshold.
  We provide finite matrix parametrizations of these bounds (i.e., the number of variables does not depend on the length of codes under consideration). Numerical optimization rapidly produces improvements over the known asymptotic upper bounds throughout all tested nonbinary parameter ranges. For rational input data, each finite level admits near-optimal feasible rational descriptions of polynomial length. Their feasibility can be checked exactly and their objective values computed to any prescribed accuracy in polynomial time; the associated threshold problem with a prescribed gap belongs to $\mathsf{PromiseNP}$.

Information Theory.title: The Resurrection of Spectrum Spreading for 6G and Beyond: From Sinusoids to Chirps
Information Theory.summary: Orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) and its sinusoidal subcarriers have underpinned the 4G and 5G eras, delivering high spectral efficiency and resilience to multipath fading through an efficient multicarrier architecture. However, as future systems move toward doubly dispersive environments driven by high-mobility applications and migration to mmWave/sub-THz bands, the time-invariance assumption underlying OFDM becomes increasingly difficult to maintain, and Doppler-induced degradation becomes prominent. While enhancements such as MIMO, advanced coding, and scheduling provide incremental remedies, they introduce additional overhead, because the sinusoidal subcarrier itself offers no inherent waveform-level robustness to Doppler impairments. Accordingly, two time-frequency spreading philosophies have emerged to improve Doppler resilience by distributing each symbol's energy across both dimensions of the time-frequency plane: (i) 2D isotropic spreading via the delay-Doppler (DD) domain, exemplified by the orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) family, and (ii) sheared spreading via parameterizable chirps, exemplified by the affine frequency-division multiplexing (AFDM) family. In this article, we examine key considerations for future waveform design across these paradigms and argue that transitioning from the sinusoidal subcarriers of OFDM to the chirp-based subcarriers offers a viable design direction for improving Doppler robustness while retaining much of the mature OFDM infrastructure. This perspective also highlights the suitability of chirp-based waveforms for integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) and their extensibility to emerging physical-layer techniques. Overall, we argue that the transition from sinusoids to chirps is a technically motivated, compelling evolutionary direction for future wireless physical layer design.

Information Theory.title: BP-based qLDPC Decoding under Long-range Correlated Noise: Trapping Configurations and Prior Mismatch
Information Theory.summary: We study the robustness of two state-of-the-art BP-based qLDPC decoders, Relay-BP and beam search, designed for independent noise when applied to spatially correlated noise with unchanged single-mechanism error probabilities. We generate correlated errors with a hidden Gaussian Markov random field, which lets us control the strength and range of the correlation while keeping every marginal error probability exact. This setting complements correlation-aware decoding: it asks how existing decoders perform when their assumed joint error model is mismatched. Across multiple tested circuits and code instances that we simulated, we observe that correlations can change logical error rates by orders of magnitude, reduce the finite-size distance advantage, and alter the relative ranking of Relay-BP, beam search, and BP-OSD. On one of the two tested circuits, Relay-BP and beam search become worse than BP-OSD, and increasing relay memory or beam width does not compensate for the degradation. Configuration analysis indicates that correlation primarily increases the probability of trapping configurations that are known to challenge these decoders; at matched error weight, correlated errors still cause decoding failures several times more often than i.i.d. errors. Finally, supplying the decoders with the marginals conditioned on the hidden field recovers most of the lost performance in the tested settings identifying prior mismatch as a major contributor to performance degradation under correlation.

Information Theory.title: New Classes of CCZ-Inequivalent APN Functions with Boomerang Uniformity One in Odd Characteristic: Differential and Boomerang Spectra
Information Theory.summary: Let $q=p^n>3$ be an odd prime power and let $g:\F_q\to\F_q$ be an even perfect nonlinear (PN) function with $g(0)=0$. We construct almost perfect nonlinear (APN) functions $G_{λ,M}(x)=g(x)+M(x)+λ(x^{q-1}-1)$, where $λ\in\F_q^*$, $-λ\notin g(\F_q)$, and $M$ is an $\F_p$-linearized permutation polynomial. These one-point modifications of $g+M$ have boomerang uniformity one, the smallest possible value for APN functions in odd characteristic. We give complete differential and boomerang spectrum formulas and obtain closed-form evaluations for selected constructions based on Coulter--Matthews monomials and Dembowski--Ostrom polynomials. For $q>7$, comparison of differential spectra establishes CCZ-inequivalence to all APN monomial families listed in the paper and every APN binomial in the original Ness--Helleseth family or its extension by Zeng et al. We characterize CCZ-equivalence within our construction, showing that any two linearly inequivalent even PN functions over the same field yield CCZ-inequivalent APN functions. We obtain three pairwise CCZ-inequivalent APN functions with boomerang uniformity one over $\F_{p^{15\ell}}$ for every $\ell\ge1$, six over $\F_{p^{120r}}$ for every $r\ge1$, and unbounded numbers of such classes in characteristic three. We further prove that CCZ-equivalence and EA-equivalence coincide for functions at Hamming distance at most $m$ from a PN function, provided that $m(m+1)<q-q/p$. We also show that all our APN functions have the maximal possible algebraic degree $n(p-1)$. Finally, we exhibit both CCZ-equivalent and CCZ-inequivalent APN pairs with boomerang uniformity one at Hamming distance one.

Information Theory.title: Performance Analysis of Entanglement Swapping DV-QKD over MIMO FSO Channels
Information Theory.summary: This paper studies multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) free-space optical (FSO) quantum communication systems employing polarization-encoded discrete-variable quantum key distribution (DV-QKD), based on entanglement swapping, with the goal of extending secure communications beyond the reach of a direct link. The FSO channels are subject to atmospheric absorption, diffraction, beam wander, pointing errors, and turbulence-induced fading, while background noise and detector imperfections degrade the performance. An eavesdropper controlling the channels and the relay is also considered. To analyze the performance of the considered system, both hops MIMO channels are decomposed into parallel spatial eigenchannels via singular value decomposition (SVD), photon loss is modeled using Kraus operators, and a threshold-detector model is developed for the relay. Based on these models, closed-form per-eigenchannel expressions for the relay gain are derived, which are then used to obtain expressions for the quantum bit error rate (QBER) and the secret key rate (SKR). Numerical results demonstrate that entanglement swapping maintains a low QBER over longer distances than direct transmission, extending the communication range beyond the noise-limited cutoff of the direct link, at the cost of a lower SKR at short distances. The crossover distance beyond which entanglement swapping prevails is determined mainly by the background noise and the detector technology, and it is demonstrated to increase with MIMO configurations. Moreover, the reach gain is shown to be maximized for a midpoint relay. Finally, since each swapping event requires a single-pair emission from both sources, a near-deterministic entangled-photon source is required, which spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources do not provide at practical key rates, whereas MIMO substantially relaxes this requirement.

Information Theory.title: Constructions of locally repairable codes via concatenated codes
Information Theory.summary: Locally repairable codes (LRCs) have attracted considerable attention owing to their pivotal role in distributed storage systems. Since binary linear LRCs can significantly reduce the complexity of both encoding and decoding, the construction of binary LRCs has drawn extensive research interest. In this paper, we construct binary LRCs with locality $r=2$ and disjoint local repair groups via classical concatenation, where the outer codes are linear codes over $\mathbb{F}_4$ and the inner code is the binary $[3,2,2]$ linear code. We present a systematic approach for selecting outer codes to obtain LRCs attaining specified bounds, and show that the weight distributions of the resulting binary LRCs are determined by those of the selected outer codes. Under certain sufficient conditions, we construct several classes of optimal binary LRCs, including those attaining Griesmer-type bounds and binary perfect LRCs. Furthermore, we sharpen the Johnson-like bounds of Ma and Ge for binary LRCs with locality $r=2$ and disjoint local repair groups, and define nearly perfect binary LRCs and $k$-optimal binary LRCs with respect to the improved bounds. We show that nearly perfect binary LRCs can be constructed via concatenation when the outer codes are nearly perfect linear codes over $\mathbb{F}_4$. Finally, we present several examples of such nearly perfect and $k$-optimal binary LRCs.
Information Theory.comment: Revised several proofs and added two examples attaining the refined dimension bound at parameters where it is strictly tighter than the Ma-Ge bound

Information Theory.title: Regret Equals Integrated Covariance: Exact Identities for the Value of Information in Stochastic Optimization
Information Theory.summary: For a stochastic program $\min_{z\in Z} c^T z + h(z)$ with a random cost vector $c$, regret, or the expected value of perfect information, is usually computed by re-solving the problem scenario by scenario. We show that regret is determined by the covariance between the cost vector and the optimal decision $π^s(c)$. The identity is exact and holds without regularity assumptions once the covariance is integrated along the path from the mean to each scenario. With $c_s=E[c]+s(c-E[c])$, $Reg=-\int_0^1 s^{-1} Cov(c_s,π^s(c_s))\,ds$. Three consequences follow. First, the plain covariance is always an upper bound: $0\le Reg\le-Cov(c,π^s(c))$. Second, when the optimal decision rule is affine, as in unconstrained and equality-constrained (e.g., budget-constrained Markowitz) quadratic programs, regret equals exactly one half of the covariance. For purely linear objectives, an affine rule forces zero regret. Third, the ratio of regret to covariance lies in $[0,1]$ and is governed by the shape of the covariance profile along the path. The noise level at which this profile first becomes positive is a decision-stability margin that tightens the bound. The identity also holds scenario by scenario for any predicted cost, so it applies to linear and combinatorial programs with discontinuous decision rules. We give dimension-free concentration bounds and a central limit theorem for the plug-in estimator. Across 7 problem classes, 8 cost distributions, and the shortest-path benchmark of Elmachtoub and Grigas (2022) with $10^6$ draws per configuration, the identities hold to within quadrature error, and the covariance bound holds in every scenario.

Information Theory.title: Learning-Assisted Beamforming Optimization for Hybrid XL-RIS-Aided Communication
Information Theory.summary: Hybrid active-passive extremely large-scale reconfigurable intelligent surface (XL-RIS) architectures mitigate the double-hop path loss of passive RIS while enabling near-field spatial energy focusing, but impose a computationally intensive mixed discrete-continuous beamforming design problem under strict radio-frequency (RF) power constraints. This paper investigates a hybrid XL-RIS-assisted downlink multi-user multiple-input single-output (MU-MISO) system in the near-field regime. The joint optimization of the base station (BS) precoder, discrete XL-RIS phase shifts, and active-element amplification gains is addressed via a discrete coordinate ascent (DCA)-based alternating optimization (AO) framework, in which discrete variables are updated through local index-domain searches and the BS precoder is derived in closed form via a noise-aware minimum mean-square error (MMSE) criterion. To reduce the per-sample computational cost for XL-RIS apertures, a deep unfolding (DU) framework is proposed as a low-complexity alternative, unrolling a fixed number of Riemannian gradient ascent steps on the sum-rate objective and recovering the discrete phase configuration via quantized phasor projection, with one learnable step size per layer trained in a self-supervised manner. Numerical results under near-field spherical-wave channel models confirm that the DU framework achieves sum-rate performance close to the AO scheme with substantially lower and nearly constant runtime, and that both schemes consistently outperform manifold optimization under discrete hardware constraints.

Information Theory.title: On Relative Greedy Weights
Information Theory.summary: Relative greedy weights were introduced by Li and Liu in [19] as a measure of information leakage in coordinated two-party wire-tap channels of type II when the adversary follows a greedy strategy. Their definition can be viewed as a relative version of the CEZ greedy weights, which are only locally greedy. In this paper, we revisit the concept of greediness and relative greediness introducing new measures, and we discuss other perhaps more relevant applications of relative greedy weights than the coordinated two-party wire-tap channel of type II. We pay special attention to bottom-up greedy weights, which correspond to an adversary with an ultimate greedy approach, and we present families of nested codes for which such weights are larger than the relative CEZ greedy weights.

Information Theory.title: Separation Is a Riesz Energy: How Many Environments Does ICA Need?
Information Theory.summary: How many environments and samples does it take to separate $d$ Gaussian sources whose variances change across environments? Each source has a signature, its vector of variances. The Riesz $2$-energy $E_j$ of source $j$ sums the inverse Fisher informations for rotating it towards other sources. With known whitening, we prove a worst-case squared-angle risk lower bound of order $E_j/(n+E_j)$ for orthogonal estimators at every $n$ and $d$. A quadratic pencil given the signatures attains $E_j/n$ up to a constant above a separation-dependent sample threshold, even with estimated whitening. For well-spread signatures at fixed $K$, the energy grows as $d^2$, $d\log d$ and $d$ for $K=2$, $3$ and $K\ge4$, respectively. A design with $K\asymp\log d$ and pairwise Fisher information bounded below by a constant makes $d\log d$ samples sufficient. The eigenvectors of a single fixed linear combination have an average first-order error coefficient of at least order $d^2$. Simulations up to $d=1000$ support the first-order predictions, and on task fMRI the energy helps rank split-half instability.

Information Theory.title: Monitoring One Channel Is Not Communication Control: Causal Evidence for Adaptive Reallocation of Joint Message--Route Codes
Information Theory.summary: Monitoring a visible channel can change how learned agents communicate without removing why communication is useful. We test this distinction in an end-to-end game where a sender and receiver learn a discrete protocol and route policy without communication supervision. In two independent 20-seed batches, 20/20 and 19/20 protocols form. Online partial coverage increases shadow-route share over no monitoring by .701 [.574,.826] and .575 [.412,.737], while task accuracy remains .905/.913 and signed frozen message contribution remains .592/.563. Complete coverage removes most selective migration without removing communication. Frozen interventions, including a fresh pre-outcome confirmation, show that route is semantic: joint message--route shuffling changes .668 of receiver predictions and route alone retains .388 accuracy versus .25 chance. A corrected explicit-silence cost makes 18/20 policies fully silent and lowers mean sending to .050, but its strict complete-suppression gate fails because two seeds retain communication. Failed semantic-evasion and operational gates further bound the result. The evidence supports adaptive reallocation of a joint message--route code under partial monitoring, not open-world route discovery, emergent encryption, or a universal defense.
Information Theory.comment: 23 pages total: 8-page main paper plus 15-page supplementary material; 1 main-paper figure and 3 main-paper tables. Equal contribution. Code available at: https://github.com/SummerRainET2008/DRCB

Information Theory.title: Neural Window Decoding of Spatially Coupled LDPC Codes: Exploiting Window Structure for Learning and Adaptation
Information Theory.summary: We propose a neural window decoder (NWD) for spatially coupled low-density parity-check (SC-LDPC) codes. The proposed methods adapt neural min-sum decoding to the structure and sequential operation of window decoding. First, target-oriented training restricts the loss to the variable nodes whose decisions are required at each window stage. Second, learned damping factors identify check-node updates that can reuse messages from the preceding iteration. Finally, adaptive weight switching selects weights trained for unreliable inherited information when a previous-window failure is detected. For a length-$20{,}000$ $(3,6)$-regular SC-LDPC code, the target-oriented NWD achieves performance comparable to sum-product window decoding while using min-sum updates. On the reduced target graph, scheduling based on regularized damping factors yields an estimated computational cost 48\% lower than that of full-graph weighted min-sum decoding, while maintaining comparable decoding performance. Adaptive weight switching improves decoding performance by 35\% at 3.0 dB relative to plain weights. These learning methods exploit the properties of window decoding to improve the reliability and computational efficiency of SC-LDPC convolutional codes.

Information Theory.title: Amortized Vine Copulas for High-Dimensional Density and Information Estimation
Information Theory.summary: Modeling high-dimensional dependencies while keeping likelihoods tractable re- mains challenging. Classical vine copulas provide an explicit dependence structure but require repeated, costly bivariate fitting. We propose Vine Denoising Copula (VDC)1, an amortized estimator for simplified vines on continuous data. VDC trains a single bivariate denoising network on simulated copulas and reuses it across all vine edges. For each edge, the network maps an empirical histogram to a density grid, and iterative proportional fitting approximately enforces uniform grid marginals. The predicted densities and cached conditional transforms support stan- dard vine recursion, likelihood evaluation, sampling, and information estimation. This retains the classical vine factorization while replacing repeated per-edge fitting with reusable neural inference. Across synthetic and real-data benchmarks, VDC combines accurate bivariate density estimation, competitive information estimates, and faster high-dimensional vine fitting after pretraining. Performance varies across datasets; finite grid resolution and conditional prediction remain limitations. The explicit fitted structure supports edge- and tree-level information decomposition, making repeated dependence analysis more practical.

Information Theory.title: Smoothed Score Queries and the Complexity of Sampling
Information Theory.summary: We study the query complexity of sampling from high-dimensional Gaussian distributions using gradient information. In the standard oracle model, exact gradients expose only matrix-vector products with the precision matrix, leading to polynomial approximation barriers and a characteristic $\sqrtκ$ dependence on the known spectral range. We show that this barrier disappears when the sampler is allowed to query smoothed scores, namely gradients of the logarithms of the Gaussian-convolved densities. For a centered Gaussian target with precision matrix $Λ$, a smoothed-score query at noise level $τ$ gives access to the resolvent $(Λ+τ^{-1}I)^{-1}$. Combining geometrically spaced noise levels with sinc-quadrature rational approximation, we obtain a sampler with $q=O((\logκ+\log(e\sqrt d/δ_{\rm TV}))\log(e\sqrt d/δ_{\rm TV}))$ smoothed-score queries for total variation error $δ_{\rm TV}$, improving the condition-number dependence from $\sqrtκ$ to logarithmic. We also study finite-bit gradient oracles. Using coordinatewise quantization of the transformed smoothed-score answers and a final dithering step, we obtain a sampling scheme whose total communicated gradient information is polylogarithmic in $κ$; in particular, for fixed dimension and accuracy, the bit complexity is $O(\log^2κ)$. To complement these upper bounds, we introduce a channel-synthesis, or reverse-Shannon, converse technique for sampling lower bounds. This converts total-variation simulation guarantees into communication requirements and yields an $Ω(d\logκ)$ bit lower bound for $d\ge2$ and fixed total variation error below one, as $κ\to\infty$. Together, these results identify smoothed scores as a provably more informative oracle for sampling and give nearly matching upper and lower bounds for its finite-bit complexity.

Information Theory.title: A Communication-Theoretic Framework for LLM Agents: Cost-Aware Adaptive Reliability
Information Theory.summary: Agents built on large language models (LLMs) rely on reliability techniques such as retry, majority voting, and self-consistency developed in parallel rather than within a common analytical framework. We observe that an LLM sampled at temperature $T$ is a discrete stochastic channel $p(y \mid x)$ in the sense of Shannon's coding theory, and use this identity as the entry point for such a framework. Each of these techniques is a special case of one of six classical reliability operators: diversity combining, hybrid retransmission, iterative generator-critic decoding, rateless sampling, structured redundant verification, and difficulty-adaptive routing. Within the framework we give two closed-form results, a noise-variance threshold above which uniform averaging beats quality-weighted averaging and a contractivity criterion for generator-critic refinement, and turn each into a design rule checkable before committing compute. We further introduce a cost-aware semantic-nearest-neighbor router whose single Lagrangian knob traverses the quality-cost frontier without retraining. Across six local and cloud channel configurations, no fixed model-technique-budget choice dominates. On a 300-item hard split of MMLU, GSM8K, and HumanEval, the router occupies the empirical Pareto frontier: at matched quality its normalized cost is $\approx$56% lower than the best fixed technique, and at matched cost it improves quality by $\approx$7% (26% over single-shot decoding). Judge-free grading of 6,900 outputs confirms that the judge tracks correctness at the item level and that the router's advantage over a fixed policy persists at most cost settings; with internal reasoning enabled, the gain of external refinement shrinks but remains significant for our incremental-redundancy operator. These results argue for consolidating reliability techniques into a single tunable layer informed by channel coding.
Information Theory.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (camera-ready version). 76 pages, 39 figures, 23 tables

Information Theory.title: Reliability Analysis for Ground-Air Cooperative Wireless-Powered Internet-of-Things
Information Theory.summary: Battery-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) devices face significant challenges in maintaining long-term uplink data collection, especially in network-limited scenarios. This paper investigates a Ground-Air cooperative Wireless-Powered IoT network (GA-WPIoT), where ground power beacons (GPBs) provide radio-frequency energy supply and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) serve as flexible aerial access points for IoT data collection. Unlike conventional UAV-enabled wireless-powered solutions, GA-WPIoT decouples energy transfer and data collection, reducing the hardware and energy burden of UAVs. To capture the device-level performance variations among IoT devices, we develop a stochastic geometry-based analytical framework, where UAVs are modeled by a Matérn hard-core point process, IoT devices by a Poisson point process, and GPBs by a finite annular binomial point process. The conditional success probabilities of the GPB-device link (for energy transfer) and the device-UAV link (for data collection) are characterized, and device-level reliability distributions are obtained through the Meta-Distribution based analysis. Numerical results under suburban and urban environments reveal the impacts of UAV altitude and annular GPB deployment on reliability distributions, providing useful guidelines for GA-WPIoT.

Information Theory.title: List Recovery for Random Low-Rate Linear Codes
Information Theory.summary:
We show that random linear codes of fixed dimension $d$ over sufficiently large prime fields have nearly optimal output list size for list recovery. Fix an error fraction $0<α<1$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$. For all sufficiently large block lengths $n$, with probability at least $1-\varepsilon$, the following holds simultaneously for every input list size $\ell\le 2^{δn/\log n}$, where $δ>0$ depends only on $α,\varepsilon$, and $d$. Given any list of $\ell$ symbols at each coordinate, at most $(1+\varepsilon)\ell/(1-α)$ codewords agree with the lists in at least $(1-α)n$ coordinates.
  Our proof adapts the colored-graph and determinant arguments of Matousek, Privetivy, and Skovron for reconstructing planar point sets from their projections. We also prove that the range of input list sizes is nearly optimal. There is a constant $c=c(α,\varepsilon)>0$ such that, for every linear code of dimension at least two over a sufficiently large prime field $\mathbb{F}_p$ and every $2^{cn}\le\ell\le p$, there are lists of size $\ell$ and a set of more than $(1+\varepsilon)\ell/(1-α)$ codewords, each of which agrees with those lists in every coordinate.
  The main results of this paper were discovered by ChatGPT 5.5 Sol using harness components from the UCLA Moonshot Harness Project, in response to a less optimal result found by the authors. See the end of the introduction for a discussion.

Probability.title: Quantitative QSD convergence in 1-Wasserstein distance via the Föllmer drift
Probability.summary: We develop a novel pathwise approach to study the convergence of the law of killed diffusion processes conditioned on non-absorption, towards a quasi-stationary distribution (QSD) as time goes to infinity. We start from the general observation that the dynamics of an absorbed Markov process conditioned upon survival up to time $T>0$ is the minimizer of the pathwise relative entropy with respect to its unconditioned dynamics, under a simple distributional constraint at that time; in other words, a Föllmer process. We then show how this result applies to a Brownian diffusion process softly-killed at a state-dependent regular rate, and characterize the minimizer and its drift change. In the case when the diffusion process is moreover reversible, we leverage these ideas and recent results on the propagation of weak log-concavity of HJB semigroups to prove that, under strict asymptotic convexity of the potential, the conditioned dynamics satisfies a contractivity property in $1$-Wasserstein distance, uniformly in $T>0$. We then establish the existence of a QSD with a large domain of attraction and deduce the exponentially fast convergence to it of the conditioned semigroup in the $1$-Wasserstein distance as $T$ goes to infinity. Finally, we deduce the exponentially fast convergence, also in $1$-Wasserstein distance, of the law of the corresponding Q-process towards its equilibrium.

Probability.title: The stochastic phase field crystal equation with conservative space-time white noise: well-posedness, regularity and existence of a density
Probability.summary: We study the phase field crystal equation $\partial_tu=Δ[(1+Δ)^2u+u^3-\varepsilon u]+σ\partial_x\dot W$ on $[0,π]$ with the boundary conditions $\partial_xu=\partial_x^3u=\partial_x^5u=0$ at $x=0,π$, perturbed by a conservative space-time white noise. This sixth order equation is the standard model for crystal growth at atomic length scales and diffusive time scales, and the conservative noise is the form of thermal fluctuations used in the physics literature. We prove that for every initial condition in $H^1$ there exists a unique global mild solution, continuous in space and time, which preserves the mean and whose supremum has finite moments of all orders. We determine its Hölder regularity: away from $t=0$, it is Hölder continuous in time with any exponent smaller than $1/4$, and $C^1$ in space with a spatial derivative which is Hölder continuous with any exponent smaller than $1/2$. Finally, using Malliavin calculus and a localization argument, we prove that for $σ\neq0$ the law of $u(t,x)$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure for every $t>0$ and every $x$. A specific feature of the model is a second neutral mode of the linear operator, besides the constant mode, which requires a separate treatment in the a priori estimates.

Probability.title: Spectral gaps and mixing rates of primitive matrices
Probability.summary: We obtain lower bounds on spectral gap/upper bounds for mixing rate for arbitrary $n$-state (not necessarily reversible) primitive Markov chains which have exponent $-O(n)$ rather than $-O(n^2)$, a significant improvement on the order obtained from classical arguments. Our improvements come from using the irreducibility distance and chainable index (which are at most linear in $n$) rather than the primitivity index (which can be near $n^2$). This also yields corresponding bounds for arbitrary nonnegative primitive matrices.

Probability.title: An Introduction to Applied Probability and Stochastic Processes: Open Lecture Notes
Probability.summary: These open lecture notes provide a broad introduction to measure-theoretic probability and stochastic processes, with a focus on applications. Topics include probability spaces, conditional expectation, generating and characteristic functions, Markov chains in discrete and continuous time, convergence of random variables, Brownian motion, stochastic calculus, stochastic differential equations and their connection to partial differential equations, jump diffusions, stochastic control, optimal stopping, and Monte Carlo methods. Most chapters include exercises, and solutions are provided. The notes were written for a two-quarter course for first-year PhD students in applied mathematics, and should also be useful to graduate students in statistics, engineering, economics and finance. The LaTeX source is freely available on GitHub under a CC BY-SA 4.0 license, and readers are encouraged to fork the notes and contribute corrections, improvements, and new material.
Probability.comment: Lecture notes, approx. 320 pages. LaTeX source: https://github.com/mattlorig/intro-probability-stochastic-processes

Probability.title: An Exact Poisson Mixture Representation of Siler Remaining Life Expectancy
Probability.summary: The Siler model describes mortality from birth to old age as the sum of a declining immaturity hazard, a constant background hazard, and an increasing senescence hazard. Its remaining life expectancy has no known closed form, and numerical evaluation alone does not reveal how the immaturity hazard enters it. We show that the remaining-lifetime distribution at age $x$ is Gompertz--Makeham with a Poisson-distributed Makeham term. Successive Makeham terms differ by the rate at which immaturity mortality declines, and the Poisson mean is the cumulative immaturity hazard remaining after age $x$. In a latent-clock construction, individuals carry a Poisson number of constant-rate clocks, and selection removes those carrying more clocks first. Integrating the mixture yields an exact series for remaining life expectancy with a closed-form truncation bound. The life expectancy lost to immaturity mortality is close to the probability of carrying a clock times life expectancy with that hazard removed, with a closed-form error bound. In annual fits to Swedish female mortality, this loss at birth fell from 4.3 years in 1900 to less than 0.01 years in 2020, a decline equal to 15\% of the gain in life expectancy at birth, and the approximation was always within 0.06 years.
Probability.comment: 17 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Code and data: https://github.com/scpatricio/siler-poisson-mixture

Probability.title: The Right Wing of the SABR Smile with an Absorbing Boundary: Resolution of Conjectures of Henry-Labordère
Probability.summary: We determine the fixed-maturity right tail of the SABR model with $β\in(0,1)$ absorbed at zero, for every correlation $ρ$: the probability $P(k)$ that the forward ends above $f_0e^k$ satisfies $-k^{-2}\ln P(k)\to(1-β)^2/(2ν^2T(1-(ρ\wedge0)^2))$. The implied volatility therefore tends to $ν\sqrt{1-(ρ\wedge0)^2}/(1-β)$. Henry-Labordère's conjectured limit $ν/(1-β)$, which Hagan's leading-order formula also gives, holds for $ρ\ge0$ and fails for $ρ<0$, where survival keeps the noise orthogonal to volatility above a moving square-root barrier. The Gaussian estimate behind his second conjecture does not hold for $ρ<0$; the rate is instead given by the intrinsic distance within the survival domain.
Probability.comment: v2: adds a comparison with Hagan's formula and shorter proofs for nonnegative correlation; states the saddle-point value of the potential (Section 6.4) as a large-strike limit rather than a constant; minor corrections; revised exposition. 38 pages, 4 figures

Differential Geometry.title: Taylor Formulas for H-structures
Differential Geometry.summary: We give a uniform second-order Taylor formula for tensorial Riemannian $H$-structures in Riemannian normal coordinates whose initial frame is $H$-adapted. For a defining multi-tensor $ξ$ with intrinsic torsion $T$, the linear coefficient is $T_q\diamondξ$, and the quadratic coefficient features the covariant derivative of $T$, its iterated diamond action, and curvature. The formula applies componentwise to tensors of arbitrary type and recovers the known $G_2$ and $\operatorname{Spin}(7)$ expansions. We also give the almost Hermitian specialisation and prove that vanishing of the complete second-order torsion contribution forces the intrinsic torsion to vanish at the centre of the coordinates.

Differential Geometry.title: A note on Positivity and Rigidity for an Expanding Quasi-Local Energy
Differential Geometry.summary: We study positivity and rigidity for an expanding quasi-local energy $E_λ$ associated with constantly umbilic initial data $(Ω,g,k=λg)$, introduced in earlier work [ALP26] as an analogue of the Brown-York energy adapted to an expanding flat de Sitter background. Under nonnegative scalar curvature and suitable boundary assumptions, our previous results established positivity for $λ$ below a geometrically determined threshold $α$, while vanishing $E_λ$ at $λ=α$ forced the boundary to be round. In this paper, we strengthen this endpoint rigidity statement by showing that, if $E_λ=0$ when $λ=α$, then $(Ω,g)$ is isometric to a closed Euclidean 3-ball of radius at most $1/λ$. The proof combines the rigidity theorem of Shi-Tam for the Brown-York energy with a strict concavity argument. We also construct an explicit counterexample to the positivity and rigidity conjecture formulated in [ALP26], showing that the energy can become negative beyond this threshold and that vanishing energy need not imply rigidity.

Differential Geometry.title: Eaton Triples, Polar Representations, and Lie Triple Systems
Differential Geometry.summary: An Eaton triple consists of a finite dimensional real inner product space, a closed subgroup of its orthogonal group, and a closed convex cone that meets every orbit and satisfies an extremal inner product inequality. In the literature on group majorization and invariant norms it is a standing hypothesis that the triple admits a reduced triple, obtained by restriction to the span of the cone. We prove that this is always the case: the axioms force the span of the cone to be a section of a polar representation, and Gichev's orbit intersection theorem applies. The reduced group is a finite reflection group, crystallographic when the group is connected; Eaton cones are its closed chambers, unique up to the group action; and a compact linear group admits an Eaton cone if and only if its representation is polar with a finite reflection group as Weyl group. For connected groups we construct a Lie triple system on the space, determined by the inner product and the orbits alone, for which the cone is a Weyl chamber; unlike Dadok's orbit equivalence with a symmetric space, it involves no choices.

Differential Geometry.title: Controlled Riemannian rigidity
Differential Geometry.summary: Given a compact Lie group acting smoothly and freely on a compact connected manifold, we prove that the space of invariant Riemannian metrics whose symmetry group is precisely the group in question is open dense in that of all invariant metrics provided the orbit space is sufficiently large. This strengthens the author's prior results and recovers Ebin's to the effect that trivial-symmetry Riemannian metrics constitute an open dense set. In the process, the discussion also addresses a number of apparent gaps in said sources, pertaining to the rigidity results in question.

Differential Geometry.title: Parallel domains in $SL_3(\mathbb{R})$ and the ideal triangle reflection group
Differential Geometry.summary:
For a given positive triple of flags, we associate an open set, called a parallel domain, in the symmetric space of $SL_3 (\mathbb{R})$ whose boundary is parametrized by three spacelike geodesics of the pseudo-Riemannian symmetric space $SL_3 (\mathbb{R})/GL_2 (\mathbb{R})$. This construction is a higher-rank analog of how three points in the ideal boundary of the hyperbolic plane have an associated ideal triangle.
  As an application, using the fact that positive triples determine a representation of the ideal triangle reflection group into $SL_3(\mathbb{R})$, we show that these parallel domains are fundamental domains for the group action in the symmetric space. Moreover, using the explicit construction and combinatorial properties of the Farey tessellation, we compute the asymptotics for the critical exponent in the symmetric space and the Hilbert critical exponent as the triple ratio of the triple of flags goes to infinity.

Differential Geometry.title: An upper bound on the growth of minimal graphs
Differential Geometry.summary: Graphs of solutions to the minimal surface equation over simply connected domains with boundary values 0 can have at most exponential growth.

Differential Geometry.title: The J-twist of the Dirac operator, spectral Einstein functionals and the noncommutative residue
Differential Geometry.summary: We study spectral Einstein functionals associated with the $J$-twist of the Dirac operator on almost product Riemannian spin manifolds. On closed even-dimensional manifolds, we compute the corresponding noncommutative residue in terms of the Einstein tensor, the curvature of the connection determined by $D_J^2$, and its zero-order endomorphism. For four-dimensional compact manifolds with boundary, we consider two boundary residue functionals obtained by inserting two covariant derivatives in the first factor of the compositions $π^+(D_J^{-2})\circπ^+(D_J^{-2})$ and $π^+(D_J^{-1})\circπ^+(D_J^{-3})$. Under the stated collar and almost product structure assumptions, we calculate their interior and boundary contributions and obtain Dąbrowski--Sitarz--Zalecki type formulas. We also present applications of these results in physics and noncommutative geometry, focusing on spectral actions, spectral distance, and mean-curvature boundary contributions.

Differential Geometry.title: Statistical Inference for Rates of Change in Spatial Processes over Riemannian Manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: Statistical inference for spatial processes from partially realized or scattered data has seen voluminous developments in diverse areas ranging from environmental sciences to business and economics. Inference on the associated rates of change has seen some recent developments. The literature has been restricted to Euclidean domains, where inference is sought on directional derivatives, rates along a chosen direction of interest, at arbitrary locations. Inference for higher order rates, particularly directional curvature has also proved useful in these settings. Modern spatial data often arise from non-Euclidean domains. This manuscript particularly considers spatial processes defined over compact Riemannian manifolds. We develop a comprehensive inferential framework for spatial rates of change for such processes over vector fields. In doing so, we formalize smoothness of process realizations and construct differential processes -- the derivative and curvature processes. We derive conditions for kernels that ensure the existence of these processes and establish validity of the joint multivariate process consisting of the ``parent'' Gaussian process (GP) over the manifold and the associated differential processes. Predictive inference on these rates is devised conditioned on the realized process over the manifold. Manifolds arise as polyhedral meshes in practice. The success of our simulation experiments for assessing derivatives for processes observed over such meshes validate our theoretical findings. By enhancing our understanding of GPs on manifolds, this manuscript unlocks a variety of potential applications in machine learning and statistics where GPs have seen wide usage. We propose a fully model-based approach to inference on the differential processes arising from a spatial process from partially observed or realized data across scattered location on a manifold.

Differential Geometry.title: Optimal rational spherical designs on the circle
Differential Geometry.summary: The minimum numbers of points in rational equal-weight spherical designs on the circle are $2304$, $4608$, $9216$, and $9216$ at strengths $4$, $5$, $6$, and $7$, respectively. We construct two nonisometric optimal designs at each strength. At arbitrary strength $t$, we obtain an explicit cardinality divisor $D_t$ with $\log D_t=(1/2+o(1))t\log t$. Applied to the antipodal pairs of a $4608$-point design, Gromov's torus construction gives a flat minimal immersion of $\mathbb{T}^2$ into $S^{4607}$ with $2304$ distinct integral frequencies, attaining Petrunin's sharp Euclidean normal-curvature bound.
Differential Geometry.comment: 35 pages. Includes exact verification algorithms and construction certificates

Differential Geometry.title: Geometry-aware similarity metrics for neural representations on Riemannian and statistical manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: Similarity measures such as centred kernel alignment (CKA) or representational similarity analysis (RSA) are widely used to compare the representational geometries employed by different neural networks to solve the same task. Yet, because existing methods compare the extrinsic geometry of representations in state space, rather than their intrinsic geometry, they may fail to capture subtle yet crucial distinctions between fundamentally different computations. Here, we introduce metric similarity analysis (MSA), a novel method which leverages tools from Riemannian geometry to compare the intrinsic geometry of neural representations under the manifold hypothesis. We show that MSA can be used to (i) disentangle neural computations of deep networks in rich vs. lazy learning regimes, (ii) compare the dynamics of recurrent neural networks and state-space models, and (iii) investigate the statistical manifolds of diffusion models. Overall, we introduce a mathematically grounded and broadly applicable framework to understand the mechanisms behind neural computations by contrasting their intrinsic geometries.

Differential Geometry.title: Almost paracontact metric Walker 3-manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: On a Walker 3-manifold $(M,g)$, we construct and study almost paracontact metric structures $(\varphi ,ξ,η,g)$, only by means of coordinate functions of a unit space-like vector field $ξ$ and the metric $g$. Necessary and sufficient conditions are established for $M$, endowed with these structures, to belong to one of the classes of almost paracontact metric 3-manifolds, according to the classification of S. Zamkovoy and G. Nakova. We find some classes to which the studied manifolds do not belong. The almost paracontact metric structure on a Walker 3-manifold examined in \cite{GC2} is obtained here as a particular case. Special attention we pay to an $η$-Einstein manifold, whose $ξ$-sectional, $\varphi $-sectional and scalar curvatures are investigated. Some local and global examples are constructed throughout.

Differential Geometry.title: Smooth local isometric embeddings in dimension four
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that every smooth four-dimensional Riemannian metric admits, near each point, a local isometric embedding into $\mathbb{R}^{10}$, and that this universal dimension is optimal. A Gram criterion constructs a regular analytic embedding of the Euclidean metric from a rational positive semidefinite tensor obtained by signed evaluations. A specified finite-field minor certifies characteristic regularity. The real-principal-type construction of Nakamura and Maeda gives openness of the metric map on a fixed ball. Rescaling then applies it to arbitrary smooth metrics.
Differential Geometry.comment: 8 pages, with ancillary Python scripts for verifying the algebraic certificates

Differential Geometry.title: Curvature estimates for stable hypersurfaces of the Euler-Dierkes-Huisken functional
Differential Geometry.summary: A hypersurface $Σ\subset\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ is called EDH-stable if it is a critical point of the Euler-Dierkes-Huisken functional $\mathcal{E}_α(Σ)=\int_Σ|x|^α\, d\mathcal{H}^n$ with nonnegative second variation, which was introduced by Dierkes and Huisken in \cite{[DH-24]}. In this paper, we first establish a Bellettini-type $ε$-regularity theorem and use it, together with tangent cone analysis, to derive curvature estimates for EDH-stable hypersurfaces with $2\leq n \leq 6$.

Differential Geometry.title: Rigidity of Five-dimensional Shrinking Gradient Ricci Solitons with Constant Scalar Curvature I
Differential Geometry.summary: We investigate five-dimensional shrinking gradient Ricci solion $(M^5, g,f)$ satisfying $Ric+\nabla^2f= \frac{1}{2} g$ with constant scalar curvature. Fernández-López and Garc\'ıa-R\'ıo \cite{FR16} proved that the possible values of scalar curvature are $\{0,1,\frac{3}{2}, 2, \frac{5}{2}\}$. If $R=0$, the soliton is isometric to $\mathbb{R}^5$; if $R=2$, the soliton is a finite quotient of ${N}^{4}\times\mathbb{R}$ \cite{FR16}, where ${N}^4$ is a four-dimensional Einstein manifold; if $R=\frac{5}{2}$, the soliton is Einstein \cite{Petersen-Wylie2}. The most difficult cases are $R=\frac{3}{2}$ or $R=1$. In \cite{Li-Ou-Qu-Wu} we proved that it is a finite quotient of $\mathbb{R}^3\times \mathbb{S}^2$ if $R=1$. In this paper, we prove that five-dimensional shrinking gradient Ricci soliton with $R=\frac{3}{2}$ is isometric to a finite quotient of $\mathbb{R}^2\times \mathbb{S}^3$.

Differential Geometry.title: Positive sectional curvature on all smooth 13-spheres
Differential Geometry.summary: Every smooth homotopy $13$-sphere admits a Riemannian metric of strictly positive sectional curvature. We construct a special $S^3$--$S^3$ bundle over $S^{13}$ whose star quotient represents the nonzero class $\pmα_1β_1\inΘ_{13}\cong\mathbb Z/3$. The defining equivariant map factors through the Blakers--Massey map by a smooth Hopf construction representing an unstable $J$-generator. This factorisation retains the prescribed base representation and makes Schultz's plumbing composition formula applicable; a normal-invariant computation in smoothing theory then identifies the smooth structure. On the quotient we implement the compatible-disk strategy with complete curvature estimates on arbitrary two-planes, matching boundary metrics, and a strictly positive sum of outward second fundamental forms. A direct smoothing argument completes the metric construction. Orientation reversal gives the remaining nonzero class in $Θ_{13}$.

Differential Geometry.title: Local regularity and p-harmonic approximation for weak inverse mean curvature flow
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove local Lipschitz regularity for locally bounded $BV$ solutions of the calibration equations for inverse mean curvature flow. We also approximate every prescribed variational weak flow locally by Moser's logarithmic transforms of positive $p$-harmonic functions. On a fixed smooth domain, with the trace of a calibrated Lipschitz solution prescribed, both the uniform error and the absolute difference of total variations are $O((p-1)^{1/3})$ as $p\downarrow1$. In particular, the approximations converge strictly in $BV$.

Differential Geometry.title: Rigidity of Five-dimensional Shrinking Gradient Ricci Solitons with Constant Scalar Curvature II
Differential Geometry.summary: We investigate 5-dimensional shrinking gradient Ricci soliton $(M^5, g,f)$ satisfying $Ric+\nabla^2f= \frac{1}{2} g$ with constant scalar curvature. Fernández-López and Garc\'ıa-R\'ıo \cite{FR16} proved that the possible values of scalar curvature are $\{0,1,\frac{3}{2}, 2, \frac{5}{2}\}$. If $R=0$, the soliton is isometric to $\mathbb{R}^5$; if $R=2$, the soliton is a finite quotient of ${N}^{4}\times\mathbb{R}$ \cite{FR16}, where ${N}^4$ is a four-dimensional Einstein manifold; if $R=\frac{5}{2}$, the soliton is Einstein \cite{Petersen-Wylie2}. The most difficult cases are $R=\frac{3}{2}$ or $R=1$. In \cite{Li-Ou-Qu-Wu} we proved that it is a finite quotient of $\mathbb{R}^2\times \mathbb{S}^3$ if $R=\frac{3}{2}$. In this paper, we prove that every five-dimensional shrinking gradient Ricci soliton with $R=1$ is isometric to a finite quotient of $\mathbb{R}^3\times\mathbb{S}^2(\sqrt2)$. Thus every complete connected five-dimensional shrinking gradient Ricci soliton with constant scalar curvature is rigid, so Cao's conjecture holds in dimension five.

Differential Geometry.title: An exact Kähler form on $(\mathbb C^*)^2$ without a global SYZ fibration
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct an explicit exact Kähler form on \((\mathbb C^*)^2\) admitting no almost-toric fibration and hence no smooth Lagrangian torus fibration. For the logarithmic holomorphic volume form, we also rule out any special Lagrangian fibrations with compact fibers and dense regular locus, even when arbitrary compact connected singular fibers are allowed. For higher dimensions, taking products also yields explicit exact Kähler forms on \((\mathbb C^*)^n\), for every \(n\ge2\), admitting no smooth proper Lagrangian torus fibration.

Differential Geometry.title: The principle of relativity in classical nonholonomic mechanics and $G$-Chaplygin systems with affine time-dependent constraints
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the principle of relativity in classical time-dependent nonholonomic Lagrangian mechanics from the perspective of moving global reference frames. We also introduce time-dependent $G$-Chaplygin systems with affine constraints, which are natural objects for the invariant formulation of nonholonomic systems with symmetries. As far as the author is aware, the Hamiltonization problem for time-dependent constraints has not yet been studied. As a first step in this direction, we consider a rolling without sliding of a balanced disc of radius $r$ over a vertical circle of a given variable radius $R(t)$. We modify the Chaplygin multiplier method and prove that the reduced system becomes Hamiltonian with respect to the new time.
Differential Geometry.comment: 29 pages, 4 figures, to appear in Journal of Geometry and Physics

Differential Geometry.title: The Fast Tree Transform
Differential Geometry.summary: The Fast Tree Transform is a locally-aggregated transform defined for arbitrary graph geometries that generalizes both the Hadamard frequency transform and the Haar wavelet transform on the circle. The pure frequency part of the transform approximately diagonalizes the graph Laplacian; this fact makes it useful as a preconditioner in geometric optimization problems. The full transform provides an only slightly-redundant representation of signals on the graph that allows sparse representation of signals that include both edges and textures.

Differential Geometry.title: Uniqueness and stability of Appleton's solitons
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that Appleton's noncollapsed steady gradient Ricci solitons on complex line bundles over positive Kähler--Einstein manifolds are the unique such solitons arising from his metric ansatz. We then show that the four-dimensional examples on $O_{\mathbb{CP}^1}(-k)$, $k \geq 3$, are strictly linearly stable. By a result of Deruelle, this implies dynamical stability under the Ricci flow.
Differential Geometry.comment: 56 pages. A Wolfram Mathematica notebook containing computational checks is included in the submission source

Differential Geometry.title: On cylindrical directions of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ derived from contact with spherical cylinders
Differential Geometry.summary: We investigate the contact of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with spherical cylinders $S^2(r) \times \mathbb{R}$. We introduce cylindrical directions of these surfaces, defined by the axes of spherical cylinders having degenerate contact with the surfaces, and show that these directions capture the ridge condition of projected regular surfaces under orthogonal projection along these directions.

Differential Geometry.title: The $L^p$ spectrum of the Stokes operator on hyperbolic 3-space and exponential decay for the Navier-Stokes equations
Differential Geometry.summary: We determine the $L^p$ spectrum, $1<p<\infty$, of the Stokes operator $A=-\PP\LD$ on divergence-free vector fields of hyperbolic 3-space of curvature $-a^2$, where $\LD=Δ_B+\Ric$ is the Ebin-Marsden deformation Laplacian and $\PP$ is the Leray projector. The spectrum is the parabolic region $a^2\{4+z^2:\ z\in\C,\ |\im z|\le|1-2/p|\}$. For $p>2$ every interior point is an eigenvalue, realized by an explicit family of divergence-free swirl fields which leave $L^p$ exactly at the boundary of the region. It follows that the Stokes semigroup on $\Lp$ has exponential type exactly $-μ_p$ with $μ_p=a^2\bigl(4-(1-2/p)^2\bigr)$. At $p=3$ this is $35a^2/9$, which lies strictly above the rates $26a^2/9$ and $10a^2/3$ that follow from pointwise domination by the scalar heat semigroup and from interpolation, and strictly below the $L^2$ gap $4a^2$. For the Navier-Stokes equations with small data in $L^3$, whose global solvability on $\HH^3$ is due to Pierfelice, the solutions decay in $L^3$ and in $L^6$ at every rate below $μ\cdot35a^2/9$, where $μ$ is the viscosity, and no faster rate holds for the linearized flow. The exponent $3$ is the usual scaling threshold. Curvature fixes the time scale of the decay and introduces no new threshold.

Geometric Topology.title: Absolute mod-two gradings on framed real monopole Floer homology
Geometric Topology.summary: We construct absolute mod-two gradings on framed real monopole Floer homology, for real 3-manifolds such that the image of the fixed point set in the quotient is nullhomologous. This allows us to fix the sign of Miyazawa's degree invariant. Our construction uses a mod-two index-theoretic correction term, the Arf invariant.

Geometric Topology.title: The Gorsky-Oblomkov-Rasmussen conjecture over $\mathbb{Q}$
Geometric Topology.summary: We prove a generation theorem for the homology of certain Koszul complexes which naturally arise as the $E^1$ pages of the stable Rasmussen spectral sequence of torus links. Combining this theorem with recent work of Ballinger, Gorsky, Hogancamp, and Wang, we compute the stable Khovanov-Rozansky $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ homology of torus links and determine its Poincaré series, resolving conjectures of Gorsky, Oblomkov, and Rasmussen and their $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ analogs, over $\mathbb{Q}$. Using these results, we determine the Khovanov homology of $T(n,n-1)$ and $T(n,n)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, confirming conjectures of Shumakovitch and Turner and of the first author, which in turn allows us to compute the Khovanov skein lasagna module of $\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ over $\mathbb{Q}$.

Geometric Topology.title: $(t,q)$-Series Invariants of Seifert Manifolds
Geometric Topology.summary: Gukov, Pei, Putrov, and Vafa developed a $q$-series invariant of negative definite plumbed $3$-manifolds with spin$^{c}$ structures, building on earlier work of Lawrence and Zagier. This was recently generalized to an an infinite family of two-variable $(t,q)$-series invariants by Akhmechet, Johnson, and Krushkal (AJK). We calculate one such series for all Seifert manifolds with $b_{1}=0.$ These results extend a previous theorem of Liles and McSpirit to any number of exceptional fibers and the Reduction Theorem of Gukov, Svoboda, and Katzarkov to the two-variable case. As a consequence, a previous result of Liles and McSpirit on modularity properties and radial limits is enhanced to a larger family of manifolds. We also calculate the infinite collection of $(t,q)$-series invariants for three infinite families of manifolds, finding mixed modularity properties for one such family.

Geometric Topology.title: The flip symmetry on Khovanov-Rozansky homology
Geometric Topology.summary: The flip symmetry on link diagrams induces an involution on Khovanov-Rozansky ${\frak{gl}}_{N}$ homology. We prove that this involution is the identity over the integers, generalizing a previous result of Chen and the author. The key ingredients of the proof are (1) a homotopy perturbation argument from a detailed study of the fork twist, which allows us to reduce the computation to planar ${\frak{gl}}_{N}$ webs, and (2) the computation of the flip map for planar ${\frak{gl}}_{N}$ webs via diagrammatics of Soergel bimodules. The latter computation can also be interpreted as a naturality result for the half twist action on type $A$ Soergel bimodules, which might be of independent interest.
Geometric Topology.comment: 42 pages, many figures. v2: major revision, main result improved

Geometric Topology.title: Parallel domains in $SL_3(\mathbb{R})$ and the ideal triangle reflection group
Geometric Topology.summary:
For a given positive triple of flags, we associate an open set, called a parallel domain, in the symmetric space of $SL_3 (\mathbb{R})$ whose boundary is parametrized by three spacelike geodesics of the pseudo-Riemannian symmetric space $SL_3 (\mathbb{R})/GL_2 (\mathbb{R})$. This construction is a higher-rank analog of how three points in the ideal boundary of the hyperbolic plane have an associated ideal triangle.
  As an application, using the fact that positive triples determine a representation of the ideal triangle reflection group into $SL_3(\mathbb{R})$, we show that these parallel domains are fundamental domains for the group action in the symmetric space. Moreover, using the explicit construction and combinatorial properties of the Farey tessellation, we compute the asymptotics for the critical exponent in the symmetric space and the Hilbert critical exponent as the triple ratio of the triple of flags goes to infinity.

Geometric Topology.title: Triangulation of orbifolds with corners
Geometric Topology.summary: We prove that every compact orbifold with corners admits a triangulation compatible with all its corners: for every $k\ge1$, each connected component of the $k$-corners maps onto the image of a subcomplex, and every open simplex lies in the set of points of a single depth. Faces need not be embedded, and the local groups may permute boundary components. The proof turns the boundary hyperplanes of linear charts into mirrors by means of the squaring map, which, unlike the folding $y\mapsto|y|$, is compatible with smooth changes of charts, and then applies the triangulation theorem for orbit spaces of proper Lie groupoids.

Geometric Topology.title: Discontinuous actions of rational special linear groups on manifolds
Geometric Topology.summary: For every $n\geq 1$, we construct continuum-many pairwise non-conjugate actions of $\operatorname{SL}(n+1,\mathbb{Q})$ by homeomorphisms on the $n$-sphere. None of these actions extend to a continuous action of $\operatorname{SL}(n+1,\mathbb{R})$. Our construction refines a blow-up procedure of Bowden and Mann, allowing the stabiliser action inside each blown-up disc to be prescribed. We motivate studying these actions and record some related observations.
Geometric Topology.comment: Minor changes and expanded references. Comments welcome!
