Information Theory.title: A Class of Self-Orthogonal, NMDS, or LCD MDS $(\mathcal{L}, \mathcal{P})$-Twisted Generalized Reed-Solomon Codes
Information Theory.summary: Maximum distance separable (in short, MDS), near MDS (in short, NMDS), linear complementary dual codes (in short, LCD) and self-orthogonal codes play a pivotal role in algebraic coding theory, particularly in applications such as quantum communications and secret sharing schemes. Recently, the construction of non-generalized Reed-Solomon (in short, non-GRS) codes has emerged as a significant research frontier. This paper focuses on a class of $(\mathcal{L}, \mathcal{P})$-twisted generalized Reed-Solomon (TGRS) codes $\mathcal{C}_{k-1}\left(\boldsymbolα,\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbolη\right)$ characterized by $\ell+1$ twists. By considering a special class of parity-check matrices derived from existing results, we derive the corresponding necessary and sufficient conditions or sufficient conditions for $\mathcal{C}_{k-1}\left(\boldsymbolα,\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbolη\right)$ to be self-orthogonal, and then generalize the corresponding results given by Liu et al. (2021), Sui et al. (2021), and Zhang et al. (2025). As applications, leveraging these self-orthogonal structures, we can obtain several families of LCD MDS codes. Secondly, we provide a characterization of the NMDS property for the codes $\mathcal{C}_{k-1}\left(\boldsymbolα,\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbolη\right)$, offering a partial solution to the open problem concerning general $(\mathcal{L}, \mathcal{P})$-TGRS codes posed by Hu et al. (2025). Finally, we rigorously prove that the codes $\mathcal{C}_{k-1}\left(\boldsymbolα,\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbolη\right)$ are of non-GRS type when $2k > n>k+\ell+2$.

Information Theory.title: On a class of generalized Roth-Lempel codes
Information Theory.summary: Maximum distance separable (MDS), almost MDS (AMDS), and self-dual codes have applications in communications, data storage, and quantum coding. The construction and structural study of MDS codes that are not equivalent to generalized Reed-Solomon (GRS) codes are important problems in coding theory and finite geometry. In this paper, we investigate the generalized Roth-Lempel (GRL) codes \(GRL_k(α, v, A_{3\times 3})\) introduced by Li et al. [28] in the case of a \(3\times 3\) appended matrix. Using the Cauchy matrix method of Roth and Lempel, we derive a sufficient condition under which these codes are not equivalent to GRS codes. We also establish necessary and sufficient conditions for their duals to be AMDS and for the codes to be self-dual. The self-duality criterion extends the corresponding result in [28], and we provide examples illustrating our results. Under suitable parameter assumptions and an explicit rank condition, we show that the Schur square of an \([n, k]_q\) GRL code \(GRL_k(α, v, A_{3\times 3})\) has dimension \(2k + 2\). Using this invariant, we show that, under certain conditions, these GRL codes are not equivalent to codes from several known non-GRS families.

Information Theory.title: Concatenated Codes with One Inner Code: Low-Rate Gilbert-Varshamov Asymptotics from Algebraic-Geometric Codes
Information Theory.summary: Constructing codes that attain the Gilbert-Varshamov (GV) bound while admitting efficient encoding and decoding is a fundamental problem in coding theory. We study concatenated codes that reuse a single binary inner code across all outer coordinates. To exploit existing encoding and decoding algorithms, we restrict the outer codes to random subcodes of scaled copies of prescribed algebraic codes and investigate their minimum distance. Our first contribution is a general upper bound on the minimum-distance failure probability that separates two terms controlled by the inner code's bias moments and the dual weight distribution of the prescribed code, together with sufficient conditions for exponential decay. Our second contribution is a concrete construction satisfying these conditions using algebraic-geometric codes from the Garcia-Stichtenoth tower. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, we construct a family of random binary codes $C_m$ whose rates approach $\varepsilon^2$ and satisfy \[ \Pr\left[δ(C_m)\geq\frac12-\sqrt{\frac{\ln 2}{2}}\left(\varepsilon+\frac{\varepsilon^3}{2}\right)\right]\geq 1-2^{-c\varepsilon^4N_m}, \] for all sufficiently large $m$, where $N_m$ is the block length and $c>0$ is independent of $\varepsilon$ and $m$. Thus, the distance guarantee matches the leading coefficient of the GV bound at low rates. For each fixed $\varepsilon$, the construction uses a single inner encoding map throughout the family and admits polynomial-time encoding and unique decoding within a guaranteed radius. This answers the question of Doron, Mosheiff, and Wootters for subcodes of scaled algebraic geometry codes at low rates.

Information Theory.title: Exact Transport-Information Correspondence for Distribution-Adaptive Discretization
Information Theory.summary: Discretization of continuous probability distributions is an operation on the sample space, and the structure induced by this operation cannot generally be determined solely from information geometry. In our recent work on unavoidable canonical nonlinearity (UCN), we established a non-arbitrary connection between the transport cost associated with discretization and the information-geometric indistinguishability of continuous probability distributions. Through this transport-information correspondence, UCN quantifies the information-theoretic cost associated with discretization in terms of the expected Kullback-Leibler divergence between nearby continuous distributions characterized by the discretization geometry. In the original UCN construction, discretization is implemented by transporting the probability mass within each cell to its geometric centroid. The resulting transport-information correspondence, however, is derived under specific conditions involving the cell geometry, spatial coverage, and the vanishing-cell-scale limit. In this work, we generalize the local-map discretization framework by allowing an arbitrary representative point for each cell and establish an exact decomposition of the associated transport cost into contributions from the conditional covariance of the probability distribution and the displacement of the representative point from its probability-weighted centroid. Consequently, the resulting transport cost is exactly represented by the expectation of the associated Fisher-induced quadratic form, without requiring uniform cell geometry, complete coverage of the sample space, or an infinitesimal cell-scale limit. The proposed construction thus establishes an exact transport-information correspondence for finite-scale discretization using arbitrary collections of non-overlapping bounded sets.
Information Theory.comment: 6 pages. The framework is extended to discretization to arbitrary representative points from the previous version. The choice of the Fisher metric for the case of discrete distributions is modified

Information Theory.title: ISAC with Backscattering RFID Tags: Beamforming and Codebook Design
Information Theory.summary: This paper explores an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system with backscattering radio frequency identification (RFID) tags. In this setup, an access point employs communication beams to serve communication users while leveraging a sensing beam to interrogate RFID tags. Under the total transmit power constraint of the system, our objective is to design a joint sensing and communication beamforming codebook by considering the tag interrogation and communication requirements. To lay a foundation for the codebook design problem, we first study the beamforming design problem in the single-tag scenario and investigate two approaches: a two-stage zero-forcing-based design with optimized power allocation and a joint beamforming design that minimizes the total transmit power. Extending our study to the multi-tag scenario, we propose a site-specific beamforming codebook design. The proposed approach partitions the region of interest into angular sectors and jointly optimizes the sensing and communication beams for each sector. The simulation results show that the proposed beamforming designs can effectively mitigate the mutual interference between sensing and communication functionalities, thus enhancing the interrogation range of the tags while minimizing transmit power. Also, the efficacy of the proposed site-specific codebook design has been demonstrated in terms of interrogation success rate, offering a promising approach for ISAC backscattering systems.
Information Theory.comment: 16 pages, 10 figures. Accepted in IEEE Transactions on Communications

Information Theory.title: Two-Stage Secret Sharing
Information Theory.summary: We give an information-theoretic formulation of two-stage secret sharing for situations in which secret information becomes available progressively. In the proposed model, shares for an initial part of the secret are distributed before the remaining part becomes available, and additional shares are distributed to new participants after the remaining part becomes available, without updating the shares already distributed and without using any additional information other than shares. To characterize this setting, we propose the notion of a two-stage access structure and provide its characterization. We further quantify the amount of information about the first-stage secret that the dealer must retain between the two distribution stages, derive a universal lower bound, and present a construction that achieves this bound for every two-stage access structure. We also position advance sharing as a special case of the proposed model and give its characterization and a related construction in classical information-theoretic secret sharing.

Probability.title: Harper's beyond square-root conjecture for random matrices
Probability.summary: For a Haar unitary matrix $U_N$ of size $N$, we prove that the first absolute moment of $\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{Sym}^k U_N)$ tends to zero as $\min(N,k)\to\infty$. This settles the random matrix version of Harper's beyond square-root conjecture formulated by Wang and Xu, with no restriction on $k/N$. The proof is elementary and self-contained, combining exact weighted trace moments with a Gaussian change of measure. It also connects the result to the critical chaos model studied by Soundararajan and Zaman, also known as holomorphic multiplicative chaos.
Probability.comment: 8 pages. Minor corrections and reformulations, some remarks added or corrected

Probability.title: On $L^p$ density of self-similar measures and Bernoulli convolutions
Probability.summary: We prove that an absolutely continuous self-similar measure has an $L^p$ density for some $p>1$. Moreover, explicit examples of Bernoulli convolutions with a continuous density are established.

Probability.title: Niche construction as an emerging phenomenon from fast ecological and slow evolutionary-environmental timescales in individual-based models
Probability.summary: We consider an individual-based model of niche construction built upon birth-death processes of d interacting biological entities (e.g., species, subpopulations or mutant strains in the same species) immersed in a slowly-varying environment which is influenced by the population state. In this setting, extinction and/or emergence of entities with negligible size or rarity, on long time scales can be observed. We prove that the joint dynamics of the environment and the species sizes on a logarithmic scale undergo a piecewise deterministic Markov process in a large time regime, which can be approximated by an explicit dynamical system in the limit of large populations. This convergence result holds true under the assumption that no "bad event" occurs during the population dynamics, corresponding to situations where several species become dominant or go extinct simultaneously. We also prove that no such bad event occurs for Baire-almost all initial conditions of the population sizes and the environmental resources. We apply this framework to study the long term coexistence of two specialist species consuming two resources, with a "joint" niche construction where each species constructs the niche of the other while depleting its resources. We also study an example of immune escape in cancer, where the environmental variable is associated with the state of the immune system and the species are associated with three types of tumor cells.

Probability.title: Price-impact Martingale optimal transport
Probability.summary: Martingale optimal transport (MOT) provides model-independent bounds for option prices calibrated to vanilla options, assuming frictionless trading in the underlying. In this work, we consider the case where dynamic trading incurs quadratic temporary price impact. First, we prove a duality result for the superhedging price. In particular, the primal of the duality relaxes the strict martingale constraint by penalizing the deviation from a specific martingale. Second, for one asset and one trading period, we interpret this price-impact martingale optimal transport (PIMOT) as a weak optimal transport (WOT) problem, and provide a characterization in the spirit of Wasserstein projection. Finally, we justify that PIMOT is an interpolation between MOT and classical optimal transport (OT), and derive the convergence rate to both sides. Numerical examples with SPX option data show how the price bounds per claim depend on the order size.

Probability.title: On the maximum of Poissonian log-correlated fields
Probability.summary:
We consider stationary log-correlated random fields of the form
  \[
  X_n(t):= \sum_{j\le n} f(e^{τ_j} t+ v_{j})\,,\quad t\in \mathbb{R}
  \]
  for a centered 1-periodic analytic function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, where $(τ_j)_{j\ge1}$ are the arrival times of a rate-1 Poisson process on $\mathbb{R}_+$ and $(v_j)_{j\ge1}$ are iid uniform random variables in $[0,1)$.
  We show that with high probability,
  \[
  \max_{t\in[-1,1]}X_n(t) = c_1 n + c_2 τ_n- (c_3+o(1))\log n
  \]
  where $c_1,c_2,c_3$ are positive constants depending on $f$.
  In particular, the random frequency $τ_n$ produces a central limit fluctuation of order $\sqrt{n}$, together with a logarithmic correction different from the ubiquitous Bramson correction for models with strong comparisons to Gaussian fields, such as homogeneous branching random walks and log-characteristic polynomials of C$β$E matrices.
  Our proof makes a connection with branching random walks in random time-environment, where coarse-scale fluctuations of the arrival times $τ_j$ play the role of a quenched random environment, and fine-scale fluctuations are leveraged to establish a branching decorrelation structure.
  We conjecture analogous asymptotics for the characteristic polynomials of random permutation matrices, and expect the same mechanism to arise in other Poissonian fields such as characteristic polynomials of sparse random matrices.

Probability.title: Mean-field Fluctuations for First-Passage Percolation with Symmetric Kernels
Probability.summary: We study first-passage percolation on finite weighted graphs whose normalized Weibull edge hazards form a symmetric Markov kernel on $N$ vertices. We prove that a uniform absolute spectral gap and an $O(N^{-1})$ bound on a fixed even-step return probability imply the stochastic mean-field passage-time limit and an independent Gaussian hopcount limit. Jointly with these quantities, the entire geodesic from an arbitrary source to an independent uniform target is approximated in total variation by an independent Markov chain stopped at the hopcount. This comparison yields laws of large numbers for fixed-length path segments and joint central limit theorems for bounded additive observables. The results extend to edge laws with a uniform relative hazard error $o(1/\log N)$, including common noise distributions with a power-law hazard and a positive-power error near zero. Applications include integrable singular torus kernels, macroscopic spread-out graphs, non-transitive regular graphs, finite groups, and discretizations of symmetric continuum kernels.

Probability.title: Laguerre tessellations in spaces of constant curvature and their sectional distributions
Probability.summary: We determine the sectional distributions of Poisson--Laguerre tessellations in spaces of non-zero constant curvature, proving closure under totally geodesic sections and deriving explicit weight intensity measures. This includes sections of Poisson--Voronoi tessellations. We construct the generalised polar region, a new geometric object which extends existing polar constructions for both positive and negative curvature and provides an alternative representation of Laguerre tessellations. We also give deterministic conditions for tessellation existence and establish sharp integrability criteria for Poisson--Laguerre tessellations.

Probability.title: Combinatorial Bernoulli Factories with Polynomially Many Coins
Probability.summary: We provide an efficient implementation of combinatorial Bernoulli factories. Such a factory turns coins of unknown biases $x$ into a random vertex of a polytope $P$ whose mean is exactly $x$. For every affine slice of the cube (the class of polytopes that admit a factory), we give a single algorithm whose expected number of coin flips and running time at every interior $x$ are polynomial in the dimension and in $1/{δ_*}$, where ${δ_*}=\min_i\{x_i,1-x_i\}$ is never supplied to the algorithm. For perfect matchings this gives $O(n^{8}{δ_*}^{-2}\log(n/{δ_*}))$ flips, while the factory of Niazadeh, Paes Leme, and Schneider [STOC 2021] spends at least $n^{2n-1}$ flips in expectation at the uniform doubly stochastic matrix. For other polytopes, our method rounds exactly given a point deep inside $P$ and the promise that $x$ is far from the boundary of $P$.

Probability.title: Particle systems and the supercooled Stefan problem: Long time behaviour and fluctuations
Probability.summary: We consider an infinite system of particles on the positive real line, initiated from a Poisson point process, which move according to Brownian motion up until the hitting time of a barrier. The barrier increases when it is hit, allowing for the possibility of sequences of successive jumps to occur instantaneously. The scaling limit gives a representation for the supercooled Stefan problem and its free boundary, from which we can determine the asymptotic limit for the barrier movement. We establish also a functional central limit theorem describing the fluctuations about this limit, from which we can determine the rate of convergence for particle system approximations to the supercooled Stefan problem under ``weak feedback" assumptions introduced in arXiv:1811.12356. We finally show that these fluctuations are identical to the fluctuations of a continuous analogue to 1D-MDLA.

Probability.title: Radius decay and boundary polymers: cluster expansion for long-range many-body tilts
Probability.summary: We consider a nearest-neighbor Gibbs measure on a region in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ (e.g., the Ising model) tilted by $\sum_{x,r} g_{x,r}$, where $g_{x,r}$ is an arbitrary function of the spins in the ball of radius $r$ about $x$, with $\|g_{x,r}\|_\infty\leq \exp(-C r)$: an exponential decay in the radius of the ball rather than in its volume. Standard cluster expansions fail for such many-body tilts, as a ball of radius $r$ carries $\exp(c r^2)$ configurations. We show that the partition function can be resummed into a polymer model whose polymers are outer boundaries of connected unions of balls, decorated by the spins along them, with weights decaying exponentially in the boundary length. The proof uses only the domain Markov property of the base measure; it develops a version of this resummation argument that appeared in a recent work of the authors in the context of RG analysis of Grassmann variables. As applications, we show convergent cluster expansions for many-body tilts of Ising models at high and low temperatures; existence of infinite-volume limits; and exponential decay of correlations.

Probability.title: Signature representations of certain BSDEs
Probability.summary: We link the solvability of backward stochastic differential equations with time-augmented Brownian signature data to the solvability of a differential equation on the tensor algebra of signature coefficients. We show that in certain cases the solutions are of closed form and remain within the class of linear functionals of the signature. Lastly, we derive a closed-form solution to a pricing and hedging problem in terms of the time-augmented Brownian signature.

Probability.title: Existence of a fluid phase for the two-dimensional one-component plasma
Probability.summary: The two-dimensional one-component plasma is a system of point charges that repel each other logarithmically, in a uniform neutralizing background. When the inverse temperature $β$ is at most $2$, we prove that its correlations decay exponentially, and that its Gibbs state is unique among point processes whose fluctuations are controlled. This constitutes part of the fluid phase predicted by physicists. As a consequence, we obtain the existence of an infinite-volume limit, extending the Ginibre point process, which we call $\mathrm{Gin}_β$. We show that its truncated two-point function, at the scale of the Debye length, is given to first order in $β$ by the Debye-Hückel approximation.

Probability.title: Mass gap for the fractional $Φ^4_2$ model
Probability.summary: We present a new, simple and self-contained technique for proving a mass gap for Euclidean quantum field theories in the high-temperature regime using the stochastic quantisation approach. As an application, we establish exponential decay of spatial correlations for the fractional $Φ^4$ model on the plane in the Wick-ordering regime. The key idea is to analyse the propagation of perturbations using the linearised stochastic quantisation equation. Spatial propagation is controlled by an auxiliary random walk, while the potentially destabilising effect of the renormalised nonlinearity is controlled by combining dissipative energy estimates for the nonlinear dynamic with the Boué-Dupuis variational formula.

Probability.title: Universal sampling rules for the signed friendship paradox
Probability.summary: The friendship paradox describes a bias in mean degree induced by neighbour sampling. We study signed weighted networks, with transitions proportional to edge magnitudes and signed strength as the vertex score. We characterize all positive initial weights, depending on total strength and score, that guarantee a nonnegative one-step mean change on every connected graph. Without regularity assumptions, the same condition yields stochastic dominance at every fixed time. Continuous admissible rules are precisely total strength multiplied by a positive continuous nonincreasing function of the score. It is enough to test connected graphs with at most five vertices and two vertex types. The bound of five is optimal even for continuous rules; the proof uses a sharp four-vertex energy inequality. The complete score vector alone cannot determine a universally valid initial law with full support. Under marked local convergence and suitable integrability assumptions, we also obtain joint limits for local conditional mean score increments and compute an explicit limiting law and mean for independently signed random regular graphs. Under joint cut-norm convergence of the magnitude and signed kernels and uniformly bounded normalized strengths, we also obtain Wasserstein convergence of the sampling-weighted distributions of normalized local biases and convergence of their means.

Probability.title: Parabolic stochastic quantisation of the fractional $Φ^4_3$ model in the full subcritical regime
Probability.summary: We present a construction of the measure of the fractional $Φ^4$ Euclidean quantum field theory on $\mathbb{R}^3$ in the full subcritical regime via parabolic stochastic quantisation. Our approach is based on a truncated flow equation for the effective description of the model at sufficiently small scales and on coercive estimates for the nonlinear stochastic partial differential equation describing the interacting field. The constructed measure is translation invariant, reflection positive, and has quartic exponential tails.

Probability.title: Hydrodynamic Limit of the Directed Exclusion Process
Probability.summary: We derive the Euler (hyperbolic) hydrodynamic limit for the directed exclusion process (DEP), a one-dimensional conservative interacting particle system that preserves particle--hole symmetry while breaking left--right symmetry. The proof relies on an explicit multi-process coupling, which guarantees a strong form of attractiveness and macroscopic stability for the particle system. Further open questions about DEP are briefly discussed.

Probability.title: A posteriori error estimates for fully coupled McKean-Vlasov FBSDEs with jumps
Probability.summary: We prove a two-sided a posteriori error estimate for numerical approximations of fully coupled McKean-Vlasov forward-backward SDEs with jumps under full-tuple law dependence. The coefficients may depend on the joint law of $(X,Y,Z,U)$, and we allow infinite jump activity. We construct a computable estimator ${\mathcal{E}_π}$ for the squared full-tuple error ${\mathcal{D}_π}$ relative to the exact Euler solution. The estimator uses the boundary and cumulative residuals of any admissible grid approximation. Under monotonicity and on sufficiently fine grids, $c\,{\mathcal{E}_π} \le {\mathcal{D}_π} \le C\,{\mathcal{E}_π}$. The efficiency bound holds without monotonicity or a mesh restriction. Analogous two-sided bounds hold for the continuous-time error up to a discretisation remainder that vanishes under coefficient time regularity. Closed-form and state-nonlinear benchmarks cover full-tuple law dependence, mark-dependent jump integrands, nonzero orthogonal martingales and infinite jump activity. In our experiments, the estimator tracks the discrete error during neural training and across Picard iterations. In a mean-field inventory model, we use the estimator and a computable discretisation term to bound the excess cost of the computed control over the discrete optimum.

Probability.title: Averaging Dynamics and Wong-Zakai approximations for a Fast-Slow Navier-Stokes System Driven by fractional Brownian Motion
Probability.summary: We study a Fast-Slow system of coupled two- and three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations in which the fast component is perturbed by an additive fractional Brownian noise with Hurst parameter $\H>\frac{1}{3}$. Using rough path theory, we establish subsequential convergence in law of the slow component, with limiting dynamics depending on the Hurst parameter and the noise scaling. For $\H<\frac12$, an averaging regime yields a deterministic Navier-Stokes equation with an additional Itô-Stokes drift. Under a stronger noise scaling, corresponding to a Wong-Zakai approximation, and a centering condition on the quadratic fast dynamics, we obtain a Navier-Stokes equation driven by fractional transport noise. For $\H>\frac12$, the transport-noise limit holds in the Wong-Zakai regime without this centering condition, with integration understood in the Young sense.
Probability.comment: This version includes an improved Wong-Zakai result for the case H<1/2. Comments are welcome

Probability.title: Quantitative characterization of Gaussian small ball probabilities
Probability.summary: The quantitative study of the Gaussian measure of symmetric convex sets is a central theme at the interface of probability theory and convex geometry. From a probabilistic perspective, it amounts to analyzing the tail behavior of suprema of Gaussian processes. The typical magnitude and upper tail of Gaussian processes are well-understood, thanks to Talagrand's celebrated Majorizing Measures theorem and to Gaussian concentration. In contrast, despite fundamental connections with metric entropy established by Kuelbs and Li, no general sharp characterization of the lower tail is available. In this work, we close this gap by establishing a sharp two-sided characterization of Gaussian small ball probabilities, involving both metric entropy and local widths of the underlying convex body. This yields an explicit chaining-type description of lower quantiles of Gaussian processes in terms of the metric structure of the convexified index set, as well as a general comparison inequality for convex sets. We further obtain analogous quantitative characterizations of two important geometric quantities associated with symmetric convex sets, namely intrinsic volumes (quermassintegrals) and the radii of random sections beyond the classical Dvoretzky range. A unifying theme of these results is the central role of convexity in the quantitative understanding of small ball probabilities.

Probability.title: Asymptotic transportation cost of the optimal matching subject to different boundary conditions
Probability.summary:
We establish equality between several asymptotic limits of the transportation cost between stationary random measures, with respect to the Euclidean distance cost raised to the $p$-th power, with different boundary conditions.
  Our approach relies on a comparison with the optimizer of the mean transportation cost between the two random measures, which is defined on the whole space. In particular we do not use any PDE techniques related to the regularity theory for optimal transport maps.

Probability.title: Spectrum of non-Hermitian self-normalized random matrices with heavy tails
Probability.summary: We study non-Hermitian matrices $Y_n$ obtained by normalizing each row of an $n\times n$ matrix with i.i.d. entries to Euclidean norm one. We consider regularly varying radial tails of index $α\in[0,2]$, with $α=0$ denoting slowly varying tails, and the broader normal domain of attraction. For $0<α<2$, assuming angular tail convergence, we prove convergence in probability of the empirical singular value measures of every shift $Y_n-zI$ to deterministic laws characterized by the root resolvent of a column-normalized directed Poisson weighted infinite tree, extending the framework of Bordenave, Caputo and Chafai (arXiv:1006.1713). Under a bounded density assumption, the empirical eigenvalue distribution converges in probability to a deterministic law $μ_α^{\mathrm{SN}}$ on $\mathbb{C}$. This law is rotationally invariant, is supported in the closed unit disk with outer radius one, and has neither point atoms nor mass on the unit circle. The laws interpolate between $δ_0$ as $α\downarrow0$ and the circular law as $α\uparrow2$. These also describe the limiting eigenvalue distributions of $Y_n$ for real entries with slowly varying tails and for centered entries with bounded density in the normal domain of attraction, respectively. For real symmetric entries with bounded density, the spectral radius converges to one in probability for $0<α\le2$, using the upper bound of Francois, Heiny and Hu (arXiv:2608.28169). We also give a general criterion identifying the outer support radius of rotationally invariant laws from fractional moments of fresh cavity weights, under explicit trace and radial-recovery assumptions.

Probability.title: Learning controls in mean field games: the fictitious play and related gradient descent
Probability.summary: We investigate two learning procedures and their relationship to the formation of equilibrium in potential mean field games (MFGs). The first one is a version of the fictitious play in which players observe directly the actions (controls) of other players and learn the distribution of the MFG through an update rules on controls. This leads to a new iterative procedure which converges for a wide class of potential MFGs of controls, even in the presence of common noise. On the other hand we also consider the learning procedure of a principal agent trying to solve a mean field control problem with only local gradient information. We prove that under very general assumption, the gradient descent of such agent converges to a solution of the associated potential MFG.

Probability.title: Continuum space hierarchical Cannings process: II. Genealogies and ancestral web
Probability.summary:
The present paper is the second in a series of three papers in which we consider a \emph{spatial multi-type population model} arising as the many-individuals-per-site limit of individual-based models. The evolution mechanisms in this model are: migration, Fleming-Viot resampling, $Λ_0$-Cannings resampling, and $(Λ_k)_{k \in \N}$-Cannings block-resampling. This evolution leads to a collection of \emph{measure-valued} processes indexed by a continuum geographic space $Ω_N^\infty$, called the \emph{continuum hierarchical group}, obtained as the limit of a discrete hierarchical group $Ω_N^L$ as $L\to\infty$, where $Ω_N^L = \oplus_{k \geq -L} Z_N$ with $Z_N$ the cyclical group of order $N$. On this geographic space, each component is a probability measure on a type space $\K$.
  In the first paper \cite{gh1}, we \emph{constructed} the measure-valued process on $Ω_N^\infty$ describing the type frequencies in the population and identified its main properties. We found a \emph{dichotomy} between this process being \emph{stochastic} (= locally monotype) or \emph{deterministic} (= locally multitype). In the present paper we turn to the \emph{genealogies} of the population on $Ω_N^\infty$.

Probability.title: Hausdorff measures of planar Brownian level sets
Probability.summary: For any Hausdorff gauge \(h\), we prove that all level sets of planar Brownian motion have zero \(h\)-measure almost surely if and only if \(\liminf_{r\to0^+}h(r)\log(1/r)=0\). This resolves Taylor's question for arbitrary Hausdorff gauges. The proof yields \(0<\HH^{h_0}(L_x)<\infty\) for some \(x\) almost surely, where \(h_0(r)=1/\log(1/r)\). The Hausdorff dimensions of the spatial mass superlevel sets form a deterministic, strictly decreasing bi-Lipschitz spectrum. For each fixed positive mass below the supremum, the exact-mass set almost surely has the same dimension as the corresponding superlevel set.

Probability.title: Entire sig-jump-diffusions, their expected signature and applications to score-based generative modeling
Probability.summary:
We develop score-based generative models for time series and standard finite-dimensional data, building on the analytical computation of the expected signature of a new class of jump-diffusions, called entire sig-jump-diffusions. These are semimartingales whose characteristics are given by linear combinations of potentially infinitely many components of their own signature. We show that their expected signature can be computed by solving linear ODEs in the extended tensor algebra, providing a tractable foundation for learning procedures. Specifically, the learning of a generalized score function for jump diffusions, a key ingredient of our generative modeling framework, can be reduced to solving linear ODEs and a deterministic optimization problem.
  We further prove that polynomial jump-diffusions can be embedded into this framework, and that their expected signature reduces to a finite-dimensional system of linear ODEs. Building on this result, we develop an alternative approach for finite-dimensional data, based on inverse signature matching, a method that learns the score by matching the expected signature of the reverse process with that of the inverse forward signature.

Probability.title: Lin--Lu--Yau Curvature and Edge-Connectivity of Hypergraphs
Probability.summary:
We give a local geometric criterion ensuring that the edge-connectivity of a hypergraph equals its minimum incidence degree: every locally finite connected simple $r$-uniform linear hypergraph with $r\ge3$ and nonnegative Lin--Lu--Yau curvature has this property. Among the various extensions of Ollivier--Ricci curvature to hypergraphs, we work with the equal-edges random walk on hypergraphs \cite{CoupetteEtAl2023}. Moreover, we show that both uniformity and linearity are essential: if either assumption is removed, there exist positively curved hypergraphs for which the gap between minimum incidence degree and edge-connectivity is arbitrarily large.
  For adjacent vertices in any locally finite simple hypergraph, the Ollivier--Ricci idleness function is concave and piecewise affine with at most three affine pieces, and is affine on $[1/2,1]$. In particular, $κ_{\LLY}=2κ_{1/2}$, which we use to verify positive curvature in the two families of examples.

Probability.title: On the Uniqueness of Fréchet Means for Polytope Norms
Probability.summary: Fréchet means are a popular type of average for non-Euclidean datasets, defined as those points that minimise the average squared distance to a set of data points. We consider the behaviour of sample Fréchet means on normed spaces whose unit ball is a polytope; this setting is particularly important for semi-discrete data, but is rarely covered by existing literature on Fréchet means, which focuses primarily on manifolds and spaces with bounded Alexandrov curvature. We study the geometry of the set of Fréchet means over polytope normed spaces, with a focus on dimension and probabilistic conditions for uniqueness. In particular, we provide a geometric characterisation of the threshold sample size at which Fréchet means have a positive probability of being unique, and we prove that this threshold is at most one more than the dimension of our space. This geometric characterisation presents a novel framework for computing the unique Fréchet mean sample threshold, which we demonstrate in the case of the $\ell_1$, $\ell_{\infty}$ and tropical norms. In particular, we show that the $\ell_1$ sample threshold is always 3, but the $\ell_{\infty}$ and tropical sample thresholds grow at different rates with the dimension of our space.

Probability.title: Off-diagonal decay of capacitance matrices via Brownian motion
Probability.summary: We establish upper and lower bounds for the off-diagonal entries of the capacitance matrix of infinite systems of spherical resonators in chain, screen and crystal geometries. Let $d$ denote the distance between two resonator centres. For chains contained in a cylinder of bounded radius and with bounded axial gaps, the decay is of order $d^{-1}\log^{-2}(2+d)$. For screens contained in a slab and relatively dense in the tangential directions, it is of order $d^{-3}$. For relatively dense three-dimensional configurations, we obtain exponential upper and lower bounds. No periodicity is assumed. Our proofs are based on the classical connection between the Dirichlet problem and Brownian motion, which enables us to relate the decay estimates to hitting probabilities of Brownian motion.

Probability.title: A perturbation theory for Feynman-Kac models and their particle interpretations
Probability.summary: We develop a perturbation analysis of Feynman--Kac models, describing how local errors introduced at each step of the Feynman--Kac recursion propagate over time. Under general conditions on the potential functions and the Markov transitions, which are shown to hold for a large class of state-space models, we prove that the global error for any time horizon $T\geq 1$ is bounded by $C\,Δ_T\log(1+Δ_T^{-1})$, where $Δ_T$ is the largest local error; this bound holds both for the prediction and the updated models. These conditions require no Lyapunov function and no stability of the Markov transitions, and allow for non-compact state spaces: confinement is provided by the potential functions. Our perturbation bounds hold in total variation and in the Kolmogorov norm; for the latter, we extend the Hardy--Krause variation and the Koksma--Hlawka inequality to unbounded domains. Our perturbation theory is applied to derive time-uniform bounds for linearized Kalman filters, Euler schemes for partially observed diffusions and nudged state-space models, as well as high-probability error bounds, uniform over whole trajectories, for particle filters and, more generally, for mean field particle methods such as sequential Monte Carlo and diffusion Monte Carlo algorithms.

Probability.title: GFF for 3D Ising interfaces in three moves of Tetris
Probability.summary: We show that at sufficiently large inverse-temperature $β>0$, the 3D Ising model on the torus, under boundary conditions that have a positive slope $θ_1,θ_2>0$, has a GFF scaling limit for its interface. The proof goes through three steps of a Tetris map, which lets cubes drop according to gravity in each of the three axes, yielding Solid-On-Solid (SOS), Half-Monotone SOS (HMSOS) and monotone surfaces (dimers). We establish GFF limits sequentially, in particular resolving the analogous problem for the $(2+1)$D SOS. A crucial ingredient is an improved RG analysis for interacting dimers, which is of independent interest: it relaxes the assumptions on interactions from being uniformly bounded in $L^\infty$ to only being typically small.

Probability.title: Strong Approximation of Stochastic Burgers Equations with Space-Time White Noise
Probability.summary: In this paper, we establish algebraic strong convergence rates for spectral Galerkin and fully discrete approximations of the stochastic Burgers equation driven by additive space--time white noise. For deterministic initial data in $H^1$, the spectral approximation is shown to be convergent in the spatial supremum norm, uniformly in time and in every finite probability moment, with order arbitrarily close to $1/2$. Furthermore, we prove that an accelerated fully tamed exponential method possesses spatial and temporal strong convergence orders arbitrarily close to $1/2$ and $1/4$ under a CFL condition. The key to our analysis is a polynomial stability estimate for the conservative Burgers flux, which allows us to control the nonlinear error using polynomial moment bounds for the exact and numerical solutions. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first algebraic strong convergence rates on the whole probability space for this equation with additive space--time white noise.

Probability.title: Intermittent Cauchy walks enable optimal 3D search across target shapes and sizes
Probability.summary: Efficiently locating rare targets requires balancing the exploration of novel space with the exploitation of local vicinities. While this tradeoff is well-documented in simplified environments, its behavior in realistic three-dimensional environments remains unclear. Here we analyze intermittent Lévy walks in three dimensions and show that search efficiency becomes strongly dependent on target geometry, with volume, surface area, and elongation governing performance across the Lévy spectrum. Against this geometric complexity, the Cauchy walk ($μ= 2$) emerges as a robust, near-optimal solution across a wide range of target geometries. Specifically, we prove that for convex targets of surface area $Δ$ in a domain of volume $n$, the optimal expected detection time scales as $n/Δ$, and that the Cauchy walk achieves this scaling up to polylogarithmic factors, while other Lévy strategies are suboptimal in different geometric regimes. Our findings provide a theoretical framework for biological movement patterns, including marine predator foraging and immune surveillance, and inform the design of efficient search algorithms for engineered systems such as autonomous nanoscale explorers.
Probability.comment: Published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS). Published version: https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2614625123

Probability.title: A zero-one law for swap-invariant events in uniform spanning forests
Probability.summary: We prove that every event invariant under swaps has probability zero or one for either the free or the wired spanning forest on any connected, locally finite, infinite network. Applications include the constancy of the number of components and of the total number of excessive ends. For the free forest, these results resolve longstanding questions of Benjamini, Lyons, Peres, and Schramm [Ann. Probab. (2001), Question 15.7] on constancy of the component count and of Lyons, Morris, and Schramm [Electron. J. Probab. (2008), Question 7.7] on the zero-one law for one-endedness. In the latter case, we obtain the stronger conclusion that the total number of excessive ends is deterministic.

Probability.title: An FBSDE Approach to the Two-Dimensional Abelian-Higgs Model
Probability.summary: We develop an iterated forward-backward stochastic differential equation (FBSDE) approach to the two-dimensional infinite-volume Abelian-Higgs model in Coulomb gauge. We prove tightness of the joint renormalized lattice gauge-Higgs laws, after continuum extension, as the lattice spacing tends to zero and the volume tends to infinity. We represent the lattice measure as the joint terminal law of the FBSDEs and establish uniform moment bounds for the corresponding terminal shifts. For the Higgs field, we combine a low-high frequency decomposition with covariant energy estimates to obtain bounds with sufficiently mild dependence on the gauge shift. For the gauge field, we establish high-frequency estimates for the effective force and combine them with quantitative diamagnetic control in the infrared.

Probability.title: Exact Wasserstein Convergence Rate for Conditional Empirical Measures of Killed Diffusion Processes
Probability.summary: Let $M$ be a $d$-dimensional compact connected Riemannian manifold $M$ with boundary $\pp M$, and let $X_t$ be the diffusion process generated by $L:=\DD+\nn V$ for some $V\in C^2(M)$ which is killed on the boundary. For any initial distribution $ν$ which is not fully supported on $\pp M$, let $μ_t^ν$ be the conditional empirical measure for the diffusion process under the condition that the process is not yet killed at time $t$, and let $μ_0$ be the associated quasi-stationary distribution. We derive the sharp convergence rate of $μ_t^ν$ to $μ_0$ in the quadratic Wasserstein distance $\W_2$ as $t\to\infty$. In particular, if $ν(B(x,r))\asymp r^k$ for some $k\in [0,d]$ and all $r\in [0,1]$ uniformly in $x\in {\rm supp}ν$, then for large $t>0$ $$ \W_2(μ_t^ν,μ_0)\asymp_ν\begin{cases} t^{-1},&d-k<6,\\ t^{-1}\sqrt{\log t},&d-k=6,\\ t^{-\ff{d-k+2}{2(d-k-2)}},&d-k>6. \end{cases} $$ Moreover, letting $\rr_\pp(x)$ be the distance of $x$ to $\pp M$, for large $t>0$ we have $$ \W_2(μ_t^{\dd_x},μ_0)\asymp \begin{cases} t^{-1},&d\le 3,\\ t^{-1}\log (1+\rr_\pp(x)^{-1}), & d=4,\\ t^{-1} \rr_\pp(x)^{-1}, & d=5,\\ t^{-1}\sqrt{\log t} \rr_\pp(x)^{-1},&d=6,\\ t^{-\ff{d+2}{2(d-2)}}\rr_\pp(x)^{-\ff 4{d-2}},&d\ge 7. \end{cases} $$

Probability.title: Infinite-variation Lévy processes are either strongly eroded or abrupt
Probability.summary: We prove that every real Lévy process of infinite variation is either abrupt or strongly eroded, resolving the conjectured geometric dichotomy on the smoothness of the convex hull of the graph of a Lévy path [Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré Probab. Stat. 60(4) (2024), 2352-2381]. We give counterexamples to the stronger point-hitting conjecture of Vigon. As applications, we classify convex-hull smoothness, Lipschitz-minorant contact sets and Burgers shock geometry.

Probability.title: On the randomized lattice-point count problem
Probability.summary: Counting (integer) lattice points in a convex body $K$ has a rich history, beginning with the famous circle problem imposed by Gauss in 1834. Clearly, the number of covered lattice points depends on the position, orientation, size, and shape of $K$ in a delicate way. In 1947, Kendall was the first to consider a randomized version of this problem by allowing random translations of $K$. In this survey, we aim to provide an overview of the current state of research on the \emph{randomized lattice-point count problem}, i.e.\ on the distribution of the lattice-point count under random rotations and translations of $K$. As it turns out, even the variance is far from being well-understood, leaving multiple open questions for future research. The motivation for the present work grew out of the author's research interest in a related combinatorial problem, dealing with the convex hull of all covered lattice points.

Probability.title: Averaging Principle and Uniform Large Deviations for Time-Dependent Slow-Fast Systems via Young-Rough Integration
Probability.summary: The main aim of this work is to investigate the limiting behavior and asymptotic properties of time-dependent slow-fast stochastic dynamical systems. The slow component is driven by a stochastic process with Hölder-continuous paths of regularity greater than 1/2, while the fast component is driven by a Brownian rough path. We introduce a novel Young-rough integration framework tailored to such systems and establish well-posedness results, providing the analytical foundation for further asymptotic analysis. Building on this framework, we employ Khasminskii's time-discretization method to establish the strong convergence of the slow component to the solution of the corresponding averaged equation in the L^p-sense. Furthermore, when the driving noise in the slow equation is specified as a fractional Brownian motion, we apply the weak convergence approach to establish a uniform large deviation principle for the slow component, uniformly over compact sets of initial conditions, in the Hölder topology.

Probability.title: Fluctuations of sample eigenvalues in a spiked covariance model with Haar-rotated spikes: a transition at $p^2 \asymp n$
Probability.summary: We study the outlying eigenvalues of a sample covariance matrix whose population covariance is itself random. The population covariance is $Σ_p=A_p+O_pB_pO_p^*+σ^2I_p$, where $A_p$ and $B_p$ are deterministic positive semidefinite matrices of fixed ranks $r$ and $s$, and where $O_p$ is Haar distributed on the orthogonal group in the real case, and on the unitary group in the complex case. Conditionally on $O_p$, we observe $n$ independent centered Gaussian vectors with covariance $Σ_p$, and we build the sample covariance matrix $\widehatΣ_p$ from these vectors. The fluctuations of the spike eigenvalues of $\widehatΣ_p$ come from two different sources: the Haar matrix $O_p$, which displaces the population spikes at the scale $1/p$, and the sampling, which acts at the scale $n^{-1/2}$. Comparing these two scales amounts to comparing $p^2$ with $n$, so the ratio which governs the fluctuations is $p^2/n$, while in the classical spiked model it is the aspect ratio $p/n$. We give the limiting law of each spike in four regimes where $n,p\to \infty$. When $p/n\to c>0$, and when $p/n\to0$ with $p^2/n\to\infty$, the sampling term dominates, the limit does not depend on $O_p$ and is Gaussian, as in the classical spiked model. When $p^2/n\to0$, the Haar randomness dominates, and the limit is a weighted sum of independent $χ^2_1$ variables in the real case, and of independent exponential variables in the complex case. When $p^2/n\toτ\in(0,\infty)$, the two terms are of the same order, and the limit is the convolution of Gaussian and $χ^2_1$ or Exponential variables. We then apply these results to a linear mixed model with a continuous batch effect, in which the Haar assumption is what makes the separation of the signal and of the batch possible, and we build a test for the value of a single spike.

Probability.title: Parabolic equations with large long-range random potentials of arbitrary Hermite rank: convergence to Hermite-driven Feynman-Kac limits
Probability.summary: We consider the one-dimensional heat equation with a large, rapidly oscillating random potential, obtained by applying a polynomial of arbitrary Hermite rank to a stationary Gaussian process with long-range dependence. When the correlations decay slowly enough, the solution does not homogenise to a deterministic limit. We prove that it converges in law, as a random field, to a Feynman-Kac functional driven by a Hermite process, which is fractional Brownian motion for Hermite rank one and the Rosenblatt process for Hermite rank two. The proof rests on an identity which expresses the exponent of the Feynman-Kac formula as a continuous functional of the integrated potential, so that neither local times of fractional processes nor exponential moments with respect to the potential are needed. We also show that the limit has moments of every order for Hermite rank one, and for Hermite rank two with a negative second Hermite coefficient, whereas for a positive coefficient its mean is infinite, although it is finite almost surely. A numerical experiment illustrates the convergence of the integrated potential to the Rosenblatt law.
Probability.comment: v2: complete revision; extends the results to Hermite rank m >= 2; the results of v1 on rates of convergence, fluctuations and superdiffusion are withdrawn. 29 pages, 1 figure

Probability.title: Exponentially Fading Memory Signature
Probability.summary: We introduce the exponentially fading memory (EFM) signature, a time-invariant transformation of an infinite (possibly rough) path that serves as a mean-reverting analogue of the classical path signature. We construct the EFM-signature via rough path theory, carefully adapted to accommodate improper integration from minus infinity. The EFM-signature retains many of the key algebraic and analytical properties of classical signatures, including a suitably modified Chen identity, the linearization property, path-determinacy, and the universal approximation property. From the probabilistic perspective, the EFM-signature provides a "stationarized" representation, making it particularly well-suited for time-series analysis and signal processing overcoming the shortcomings of the standard signature. In particular, the EFM-signature of time-augmented Brownian motion evolves as a group-valued Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. We establish its stationarity, Markov property, and exponential ergodicity in the Wasserstein distance, and we derive an explicit formula à la Fawcett for its expected value in terms of Magnus expansions. We also study linear combinations of EFM-signature elements and the computation of associated characteristic functions in terms of a mean-reverting infinite dimensional Riccati equation.

Probability.title: Time-changed Compound Poisson Process
Probability.summary: In this paper, we introduce a time-changed compound Poisson process (TCCPP) obtained by subordinating the classical compound Poisson process (CPP) with a subordinator and an inverse subordinator, which are defined via distinct Bernstein functions. We study the governing equations and distributional properties of a TCCPP including its moments, dependence structure and limiting behaviour. We derive distributions of the integrated CPP and a linear combination of TCCPPs. We also obtain the law of iterated logarithm, the central limit theorem and weighted sum representation for a TCCPP. Finally, we provide some characterizations of a TCCPP in terms of martingales, a univariate multinomial process, a triangular array process and waiting time distribution. The proposed framework generalizes several existing fractional stochastic processes and offers greater flexibility for modelling complex count data.

Probability.title: The External Path Length and Terminal Wiener Index in Random Trees
Probability.summary: We consider two distance-based concepts in rooted trees and compare them to their leaf-restricted counterparts. The path length is the sum of all distances from the root to the vertices of the tree, while the external path length is the sum of all distances from the root to the leaves of the tree. Upon dividing by the number of vertices and leaves respectively, we obtain the average distance to the root. The Wiener index is the sum of all distances between pairs of vertices, and the terminal Wiener index is the sum of all distances between pairs of leaves. Dividing by the number of pairs of vertices and pairs of leaves respectively, we obtain the average distance between vertices and average distance between leaves. For two important classes of random trees, we show that the average distance of the root to a random leaf is almost the same as the average distance to a random vertex and that the average distance between vertices is almost the same as the average distance between leaves. For Bienaymé--Galton--Watson trees, each of these differences is bounded in probability. For three varieties of increasing trees (recursive trees, $d$-ary increasing trees, generalised plane-oriented recursive trees), on the other hand, the differences converge to constants in probability. This allows the transfer of convergence results for the path length to the external path length, and results for the Wiener index to be transferred to the terminal Wiener index.

Probability.title: Cutoff profile for the coupon collector with many collections
Probability.summary: We consider the problem posed by Erdős and Rényi in $1961$ about the limiting distribution of the number of draws $T_{n,m}$ that a coupon collector needs to complete $m$ collections of $n$ distinct types of coupons, when $m$ increases with $n$. Although the limiting distribution was studied in earlier works, we give a simple and self-contained proof that relates it to the cutoff phenomenon for an absorbing Markov chain. We also provide an alternative expression for the cutoff window in terms of the Lambert $W$ function.

Probability.title: Nonsense nonlinear correlations between independent random walks
Probability.summary: Sample distance correlation can remain large between independent random walks. For centred walks with independent, identically distributed increments of finite, positive variance, we prove convergence in distribution to the distance correlation of the joint occupation measure of two independent Brownian paths. This universal limit lies strictly between zero and one almost surely and has full support on the unit interval. We calculate the expected squared distance covariance of the limiting measure and show that ordinary permutation calibration rejects independence with probability tending to one at every fixed nominal level. Gaussian simulations illustrate the persistent dispersion of random-walk correlations and the failure of permutation calibration.

Probability.title: Quenched Growth of Normal Matrices and Harmonic Measure
Probability.summary: The eigenvalues of a large normal random matrix form a two-dimensional Coulomb gas. At fixed weight, the spectral droplet grows with the matrix rank, and its semiclassical density increment is harmonic measure. We freeze an $N$-eigenvalue configuration and sample $M$ further eigenvalues using the projection onto polynomials of degree less than $N+M$ that vanish at the frozen points. Their conditional law is an exact polynomial ensemble in the potential of the frozen charges. For a regular analytic droplet, we prove that the spatial distribution of the new eigenvalues converges to harmonic measure on the old boundary when $M/\log N\to\infty$ and $M/N\to0$. This convergence holds conditionally on the frozen spectrum, outside a set of frozen configurations whose probability tends to zero. The equilibrium process formed from orthogonal polynomials of degrees $N,\ldots,N+M-1$ has the same limit. An exact finite-rank identity relates polynomial moments of the conditional mean to fluctuations of the frozen spectrum, with a remainder from polynomial modes of degree $N+M$ and above.

Probability.title: Uniqueness of generalized conformal restriction measures
Probability.summary: In this note, we give a new proof of the uniqueness of generalized chordal and radial conformal restriction measures for $c\le 1$, where the $c<-2$ case is unproved before. Our approach (called the SLE arc test) is inspired by the completely conformally invariant (CCI) measure introduced by Lawler and Werner (2000), and also by Cai's recent Green's function test for the Brownian loop catcher (2026).
Probability.comment: 18 pages. Minor changes on the last version

Probability.title: The dynamical Seppäläinen-Johansson model and the Brownian web landscape
Probability.summary: The dynamical Seppäläinen-Johansson first passage percolation defines a random directed metric on $\mathbb Z^2$ where the environment is updated according to a Poisson process. We show that its finite dimensional distributions converge after $0:1:2$ scaling to those of the Brownian web landscape defined on the finite dimensional marginals of the dynamical Brownian web. We prove non-uniqueness of geodesics in the Brownian web landscape and we relate it to exact formulas on one-sided reflected Brownian motions. We prove a locally uniform law of large numbers and uniform deviation bounds, and identify Poisson increment-stationary laws for the associated height evolution.

Probability.title: Resolvent convergence under heterogeneous second-moment profiles and quadratic-form control
Probability.summary:
Let $X=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}$ have independent real columns with finite second moments, not necessarily centered or identically distributed. For $z\in\mathbb C\setminus[0,\infty)$, we compare \[ G^z=\left(\frac1nXX^\top-zI_p\right)^{-1} \] with a deterministic matrix $\tilde G^z$ defined by the second-moment profile $(Σ_i)_{i\in[n]}$, where $Σ_i=\mathbb E[x_ix_i^\top]$.
  For deterministic matrices \(A\), we prove finite-dimensional \(L^q\) bounds for $\tr(A(G^z-\tilde G^z))$ in terms of moments of centered quadratic forms, without assuming independence among the coordinates of a column. Operator-test bounds impose no trace-growth or aspect-ratio restriction and display explicitly the effect of the sizes and repetitions of the second-moment matrices $(Σ_i)_{i\in[n]}$. Under $\sqrt p\sup_{i\in[n]}|Σ_i|_{\hs}=O(n)$, the Hilbert-Schmidt bounds involve approximation of the profile by commuting positive-semidefinite matrices, with explicit dependence on the approximation error and the dimension of their span. We also obtain corresponding bounds for \(\tr(A G^z B G^z)\), with deterministic \(A,B\). All bounds are locally uniform in $z\in\mathbb C\setminus[0,\infty)$.

Probability.title: A Finite Markov Chain Analysis of the Simplified Swarm Optimisation Update Rule
Probability.summary: Simplified swarm optimisation (SSO) updates each variable by one draw that copies the global or personal best, keeps the current value or redraws uniformly, with probabilities $c_g$, $c_p$, $c_w$ and $c_r$. As a finite Markov chain under frozen memory, its coordinate kernel $c_w I + (1 - c_w)Π$ has an explicit stationary law and exact convergence rate $c_w^t$. The elitist chain has a geometric hitting-time bound, from a non-optimal start a fixed $c_r$ needs at least $\exp(nc_r/2)$ expected evaluations to reach a unique optimum, and a coupling under changing memories gives $O(n\log n)$ and $O(n^2)$ expected generations on OneMax and LeadingOnes for every population size with redraw share of order $1/n$ and no inertia, and within a $\log n$ factor for fixed inertia. With a frozen memory, inertia cannot speed up first entry into any set from stationary positions, though it can from others. Where the three reference values agree, only $c_r$ acts; where they disagree, copy branches recombine the memories, forcing a redraw only where no active branch holds the target value. Branch logging and checkpoint replay show inertia slowed the tested OneMax and LeadingOnes runs and suggest memory-mediated gains on wider gaps. On Jump functions SSO needed 3.8--8.9 times fewer evaluations than the (1+1) evolutionary algorithm with rate $1/n$, but no consistent advantage over rate-adjusted mutation or a $(μ+1)$ genetic algorithm with uniform crossover was established. The analytical redraw rule improved six of eight benchmark--setting pairs and redundancy allocation, but was slower than $c_r = 0.1$ on Jump$_2$.
Probability.comment: 29 pages, 7 figures, 17 tables. Submitted to Swarm and Evolutionary Computation. Code, per-run records and a one-command reproduction workflow: Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.24153497

Probability.title: Banach-Valued Carré du Champ Operators and Functional Gaussian Approximation
Probability.summary: We develop a projective-tensor-valued carré du champ for Malliavin-differentiable Banach-valued random elements and establish an associated integration-by-parts formula. The resulting dimension-free comparison principle bounds Gaussian approximation against twice Fréchet-differentiable test functions by the expected projective norm of a random covariance discrepancy. For processes on Skorokhod space equipped with the uniform norm, a smoothing argument converts this comparison into a quantitative bound in the bounded-Lipschitz metric, subject to explicit regularization errors. On Banach-valued Wiener chaos we express the carré du champ through contractions and obtain quantitative estimates in terms of contracted kernels. As a concrete application, we establish a quantitative functional Breuer--Major bound for the canonical polygonally interpolated partial-sum process, together with a corollary for the original Skorokhod step process. The estimate applies to the entire path in the uniform topology under explicit covariance conditions. We also record the trace-class specialization of the contraction bounds in Hilbert spaces.

Probability.title: Numerical approximation of nonlinear fourth-order SPDEs with additive space-time white noise
Probability.summary: We consider the strong numerical approximation for a fourth-order stochastic nonlinear SPDE driven by space-time white noise on {$d=1,2,3$}-dimensional torus. We consider its full discretisation with a spectral Galerkin scheme in space and Euler scheme in time. We show the convergence with almost spatial rate $2-\frac{d}{2}$ and $\frac{6-d}{4} \wedge 1$-temporal rate obtained mainly via \it{Stochastic Sewing} technique.

Probability.title: Gaussian processes with random pointwise regularity
Probability.summary: Using wavelet series, we construct Gaussian stochastic processes whose pointwise Hölder exponent is random along a typical sample path, although at every fixed point the exponent is deterministic almost surely. We first give a local non-sparsity condition under which the Hölder exponent almost surely is a deterministic function. In the opposite direction, a lacunary construction shows that the exceptional set on which the exponent is modified can have full Hausdorff dimension. For this model we determine the marginal multifractal spectra and the bivariate spectrum of the deterministic series and its Gaussian randomization.

Probability.title: Almost sure asymptotics of numerical errors for SDEs with additive noise
Probability.summary: In this paper, we characterize the sharp almost sure asymptotics for the numerical error of the Euler--Maruyama method applied to stochastic differential equations with additive noise. Specifically, we establish, to our knowledge, the first sharp laws of the iterated logarithm for Euler--Maruyama errors in this setting along geometric mesh refinements $(N_i)_{i\in\mathbb N^+}=(α^i)_{i\in\mathbb N^+}$ for any integer $α\geq 2$. These results identify $(N_i)^{-1}\sqrt{\log\log N_i}$ as the sharp almost sure error scale and provide an explicit expression for the path-dependent constants governing the asymptotic error envelopes. The LIL constants also admit a natural interpretation through the asymptotic error distribution, specifically through the conditional covariance matrix of the stable limit of the rescaled error given the driving Wiener process. A central challenge in establishing these results is to characterize the almost sure fluctuations of Skorohod integrals arising in the error expansion, which are generally anticipating, non-Gaussian, and dependent across refinement levels. The analysis also provides a framework for studying analogous asymptotics for other numerical methods.

Probability.title: Polarity of the First Dirichlet Liouville Spectral Gap
Probability.summary: We prove zero $1$-capacity of first-gap collisions for the minimal Liouville spectral Green-response form and its canonical extension. The minimal-form diffusion avoids collisions for every initial law absolutely continuous with respect to the spectral law.

Probability.title: On the continuity of martingale optimal transport in higher dimensions
Probability.summary: We investigate qualitative and quantitative continuity of martingale optimal transport under perturbations of both marginals in dimensions $d\geq2$. We assume that each pair of marginals admits a reference martingale coupling whose density relative to the product of its marginals is bounded above and away from zero, uniformly along the sequence. If the limiting target measure is not carried by a hyperplane, we prove continuity under $W_1$-convergence for continuous costs of at most linear growth, assuming only finite first moments. For Lipschitz costs, a uniform $p$-moment bound on the targets, $p>1$, yields an explicit stability estimate with exponent $(1-1/p)/2$; uniformly bounded target supports give exponent $1/2$. The proof constructs a correction of couplings with small martingale bias while preserving both marginals. Truncated moment corrections allow the target measure to have unbounded support. The construction also shows that every martingale coupling of the limiting marginals can be approximated in $W_1$ by martingale couplings of the approximating marginals. We also discuss counterexamples showing that neither the uniform density condition nor non-degeneracy of the limiting target measure can be omitted in general.

Probability.title: Macroscopic diffusive fluctuations for generalized hard rods dynamics
Probability.summary: We study the fluctuations in equilibrium for a dynamics of rods with random length. This includes the classical hard rod elastic collisions, when rod lengths are constant and equal to a positive value. We prove that in the diffusive space-time scaling, an initial fluctuation of density of particles of velocity $v$, after recentering on its Euler evolution, evolve randomly shifted by a Brownian motion of variance $\mathcal D(v)$.
Probability.comment: In the published version the linearized Euler equation was missing a term. This has been corrected in section 2. The main result, contained in Section 3, is not affected. AN erratum will appear in AAP

Probability.title: Strong Well-Posedness and Path-by-Path Uniqueness for Fractional SDEs with Integrable Drifts
Probability.summary: In dimension $d$, we consider stochastic differential equations driven by additive fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H<1/2$ and with a time-dependent drift that is $p$-integrable in space and $q$-integrable in time. Under the subcriticality condition $\frac{Hd}{p}+\frac1q<1-H$, complemented by two integrability conditions needed for Girsanov's theorem, we prove strong existence and path-by-path uniqueness of solutions. We also establish stability with respect to the initial data and the drift, both pathwise and in moment norms, and construct a Hölder continuous semiflow. When $H$ approaches $1/2$, our conditions reduce, up to an endpoint case, to the condition of Krylov and Röckner (2005) for Brownian motion, and in dimension one they complement the results of Nualart and Ouknine (2003), which rely on comparison arguments. Our methods combine the stochastic sewing lemma, Lyons' rough path theory, and the quantitative John--Nirenberg inequality for stochastic processes of vanishing mean oscillation.

Probability.title: Discrete Isoperimetric Inequalities via Curvature
Probability.summary: Isoperimetric inequalities on the Boolean hypercube play a fundamental role in the analysis of Boolean functions. These inequalities have been established primarily for the uniform measure and for biased product measures, often through Fourier-analytic or inductive arguments. We develop a curvature-based semigroup framework to establish isoperimetric inequalities for measures with weakly dependent coordinates. In particular, we show that a Dobrushin-type condition, together with marginal boundedness of the distribution, implies the local Bobkov inequality, Talagrand's $L^1$--$L^2$ and variance--surface-area inequalities, the Kahn--Kalai--Linial inequality, and the Eldan--Gross inequality. Our results apply to zero-field Ising models with interaction matrix $J$ throughout the Dobrushin uniqueness regime $\|J\|_1<1$. The framework builds on discrete Bakry--Émery theory and gradient estimates and can also be extended to measures on Hamming slices or hypergrids.

Probability.title: Strong error estimates for finite element approximations of the stochastic Burgers--Huxley equation with multiplicative noise
Probability.summary: This paper is concerned with strong error estimates for fully discrete finite element approximations of the stochastic Burgers--Huxley equation with multiplicative noise. We use the implicit Euler--Maruyama scheme for time discretization and continuous piecewise linear finite elements for spatial discretization. Moment bounds and exponential integrability estimates are established and used with the discrete stochastic Gronwall inequality to derive error estimates in full expectation. Sub-second-moment error estimates are first obtained in the discrete maximum-in-time $L^2$-norm and the discrete $L^2$-in-time $H^1$-norm. Second-moment error estimates in the discrete maximum-in-time $L^2$-norm are then established using a higher-moment argument. The convergence rates are of order $k^{1/2}$ in time and $h$ in space, with the spatial rate being optimal in the $H^1$-norm. Finally, numerical experiments are provided to examine the convergence rates and the influence of multiplicative noise on the solution.

Probability.title: Sharp Bounds for Near-Maximizers of Gaussian Processes
Probability.summary: For a centered Gaussian process $G$ with continuous sample paths on a compact metric space $T$, a continuous drift $f: T \mapsto \mathbb{R}$, a noise level $σ>0$, and $ε\ge 0$, let $A_ε$ be the set of points at which $f+σG$ is within $ε$ of its maximum. Writing $\mathbb{E}\sup_TG$ for the expected supremum of $G$, we prove that the expected squared diameter of $A_ε$ in the canonical pseudometric of $G$ is at most $8ε\mathbb{E}\sup_TG/σ$ and that the expected maximal squared distance from a point of $A_ε$ to an exact maximizer is at most $4ε\mathbb{E}\sup_TG/σ$. The constants cannot be improved uniformly over index sets, processes, and drifts, and no logarithmic factor in $ε$ appears, unlike in bounds integrated from tail estimates. At $ε=0$ the bounds give the almost sure uniqueness of the maximizer in the canonical pseudometric without nondegeneracy assumptions. Given this uniqueness, both bounds follow from a bound with constant $2$ on the mean square of the largest increment of an independent copy of $G$ from an exact maximizer to a point of $A_ε$. The proof rests on an identity for the mean squared support function of the $ε$-subdifferentials of a smooth convex function at a standard Gaussian vector, obtained from two Gaussian integrations by parts.

Probability.title: Asymptotic analysis of infinite-server queues driven by a Cox process with squared Bessel arrival intensity
Probability.summary: This paper introduces a model for infinite-server queues driven by a Cox process with stochastic intensity given by a squared Bessel (BESQ) process. Exploiting the affine structure of the underlying dynamics, we derive a closed-form expression for the joint moment-generating function (MGF) of the arrival intensity, the number of customers in the system, and the integral of the number of customers in the system over a time interval. The asymptotic properties of the model are also analysed. We establish laws of large numbers, central limit theorems, large deviation principles, and moderate deviation principles for several quantities of interest. More precisely, these results are obtained for three important settings: cumulative occupancy over a finite time interval, system occupancy under a diverging long-run mean arrival intensity, and the superposition of independent infinite-server queues with Cox-BESQ arrival intensities. Numerical experiments illustrate the associated rate functions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the resulting rare-event approximations.

Probability.title: Universal concentration for sums under arbitrary dependence
Probability.summary: We present a universal concentration bound for sums of random variables under arbitrary dependence, and we prove that it is asymptotically optimal for broad families of marginals admitting a uniform integrable tail-quantile envelope. The bound follows directly from the subadditivity of expected shortfall, a property well known in the risk-measure literature. Our sharpness result relies on an explicit construction of asymptotically extremal couplings. We furthermore provide practical sufficient conditions -- based on convex transformation order comparisons with exponential and power-law envelopes -- under which the bound admits simple, explicit tail profiles.
