We further give a mixing time bound on the Markov chain induced by our localization process, which holds if our target distribution satisfies a functional Poincaré inequality. Finally, we apply our framework to differentially private convex optimization in $\ell_p$ norms for $p \in [1, 2)$, where we improve state-of-the-art query complexities in a zeroth-order model.

Probability.title: Swapping and Switching for Markov Processes: Symmetrisation and Fast-Exchange Limits
Probability.summary: In parallel tempering, exchanging the positions of the replicas (swapping) and exchanging the assignment of dynamics to the replicas (switching) are often used interchangeably. We study the two descriptions as stochastic processes, for Markov species (the dynamics that are exchanged) and bounded measurable exchange rates. To guarantee the Markovianity of each process under the exchanges, switching records both the positions and the label that tracks which species each replica carries; swapping records only the positions. Driving both with one exchange clock places them on a common probability space and lets us write swapping as switching with the label forgotten. This relation holds pathwise at every time and, once decomposed over the label, yields an exact identity between their transition kernels. This characterisation lets us relate, in a precise way, where the two processes agree and where they differ. We describe mainly the relation between their decay rates at finite exchange rate, and between their distributions and observables at finite and infinite exchange rate. The relation between the Markovianity of the two is particularly interesting. At finite rate, switching needs the label to be Markov, while swapping is Markov on its own. In the infinite-rate limit this reverses: swapping becomes non-tight, while switching becomes Markov on the physical coordinates alone. We illustrate all these relations on a solvable benchmark of two Brownian motions with drift under a constant exchange rate. The rich behaviour already visible in this simple case, and developed throughout the paper, suggests that the swapping mechanism is of interest in its own right, beyond the balance conditions needed in parallel tempering.

Probability.title: Well-posedness of kinetic McKean-Vlasov equations
Probability.summary: We consider the McKean-Vlasov equation $dX_t = b(t, X_t, [X_t])dt + σ(t, X_t, [X_t])dW_t$ where $[X_t]$ is the law of $X_t$. We specifically consider the kinetic case, where the equation is degenerate because the dimension of the Brownian motion $W$ is strictly smaller than that of the solution $X$, as commonly required in classical models of collisional kinetic theory. Assuming Hölder continuous coefficients and a weak Hörmander condition, we prove the well-posedness of the equation. This result advances the existing literature by filling a crucial gap: it addresses the previously unexplored case where the diffusion coefficient $σ$ depends on the law $[X_t]$. Notably, our proof employs a simplified and direct argument eliminating the need for PDEs involving derivatives with respect to the measure argument. A critical ingredient is the sub-Riemannian metric structure induced by the corresponding Fokker-Planck operator.

Probability.title: A CIR-Type Diffusion Driven by Hermite Processes: Well-Posedness, Positivity and Malliavin Analysis
Probability.summary: We study the stochastic differential equation \[ dX_t=a\bigl(b(t)-X_t\bigr)\,dt+\bigl(σ_0+σ_1\sqrt{φ_\eps(X_t)}\bigr)\,dZ_t^{(q,H)}, \qquad X_0=x_0, \] where $Z^{(q,H)}$ is a Hermite process of order $q\geq1$ and Hurst parameter $H\in(1/2,1)$, $b$ is a periodic target, $σ_0>0$, and $φ_\eps$ is a smooth positive function equal to $x+\eps$ on $[0,\infty)$. The equation is understood pathwise, in the sense of Young. We prove that it has a unique solution. We give lower bounds on the probability that the solution stays positive on $[0,T]$, for every $σ_1\geq0$: after a Lamperti-type change of variables, which makes the noise additive, a last-passage argument shows that the probability of reaching $0$ before $T$ is at most of order $\exp(-c\,Λ(m_0)^{2/q}/T^{2H/q})$, where $m_0$ is the smaller of the initial level and the minimum of the target and $Λ$ is the natural scale of the diffusion coefficient. For $q\le2$ and $σ_1=0$ we show that the solution reaches negative values with positive probability, so that no almost-sure positivity holds in that case. Finally, the solution at each time belongs to $\D^{1,\infty}$, with an explicit representation of its Malliavin derivative, and its law is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure. The proofs of these two results are self-contained and rely on the additive form of the equation. Numerical experiments based on a wavelet-type simulation of Hermite processes illustrate the results.
Probability.comment: 32 pages, 4 figures. v2: substantially revised. New result on the failure of almost-sure positivity for q <= 2; self-contained proof of Malliavin differentiability and absolute continuity; simplified moment bounds; simulations redone with a corrected normalisation of the simulated Hermite processes; references updated

Probability.title: A high-order recombination algorithm with adaptive scale selection for weak approximation of stochastic differential equations
Probability.summary:
High-order recombination keeps weak approximation trees of diffusions small
  by a moment-preserving reduction of the measure on each patch of nodes.
  The weighted Litterer--Lyons (WLL) test of Ninomiya and Shinozaki
  sets the patch scale using a scalar \(λ>0\) chosen
  beforehand, whose appropriate value depends on coordinate units.
  First, the anisotropically weighted Litterer--Lyons (AWLL) rule
  selects the scale during recombination within a bounded factor of
  the measured increment amplitude. On a fixed set of nodes, expanding
  coordinate units leaves the AWLL patch-count bound unchanged but raises
  the WLL lower bound as a power until saturation. In Heston and shifted Stochastic-Alpha-Beta-Rho (sSABR)
  systems with initial price or forward rate 100, AWLL reduces
  the terminal supports of WLL with \(λ=1\) by factors of 137 and
  1488 at comparable errors, but enlarges them at smaller Heston initial
  prices. Second, \(λ\) is extended to a positive definite matrix
  with a joint error bound for prices and sensitivities, a bound on
  the gain of its shape, and patch-count bounds. Third, the elimination stage of batched basis
  exchange requires \(O(J)\)
  arithmetic operations for \(J\) nodes at fixed moment rank and panel width, against
  \(Θ(J^{3})\) for the direct kernel update of Ninomiya and Shinozaki.

Probability.title: Controlling avalanche sizes in the Abelian sandpile model
Probability.summary: The Abelian sandpile model is a classical framework for studying large cascading events, such as those arising in models of forest fires and earthquakes. This work studies the control of such avalanches through the targeted removal of sand grains. We formulate this sequential control problem as an average-cost Markov decision process in which, before each grain addition, a controller may remove a sand grain from a selected vertex. The objective is to balance the long-run expected avalanche size against the cost of intervention. We analyze local intervention policies, which remove grains from a prescribed set of vertices whenever possible, and establish structural results for the recurrent classes and stationary distributions of the induced Markov chains. When the intervention set satisfies a property called topple-freeness, we sharpen these results, derive expressions for the gain and bias functions, and give necessary and sufficient conditions for optimality on general finite graphs. Finally, we apply the general theory to several specific graph classes and obtain a complete characterization of optimal policies on the one-dimensional lattice, the complete graph and the star graph for every value of the intervention cost.

Probability.title: Slicing a Doughnut at Random
Probability.summary: Choose a random plane that hits a solid torus. How likely is the slice to be a single disk, and how fat should the doughnut be to make this as likely as possible? Answering requires saying precisely what a "random plane" is. We explain this from scratch, first for random lines in the plane and then for random planes in space, and then solve the problem with nothing more than calculus. Along the way we meet a two-dimensional cousin of the problem (the doughnut's shadow) and two tempting wrong turns. One wrong turn appeared in print; it turns out to be a correct solution of the two-dimensional cousin. The other was the author's own first attempt, which luckily stayed in a drawer.

Probability.title: Ignoring Blow-Ups for Approximations
Probability.summary: It is well known that for SDEs with non-Lipschitz coefficients, the Euler scheme can fail to converge in an Lp sense. It is also widely observed that convergence fails only due to rare explosive trajectories, that distort the expectation. In this work we demonstrate that almost any method of removing these rare explosive trajectories leads to convergence in a suitable strong and weak sense. We apply this framework to coefficients that grow faster than linearly at infinity and Lennard-Jones type coefficients that explode like a reciprocal power on a compact set.

Probability.title: The second reconstruction transition for random graphs from 2-neighborhoods
Probability.summary: We prove that, with high probability, the Erdős--Rényi random graph $G(n,p)$ is reconstructible up to isomorphism from the multiset of its rooted induced 2-neighborhoods whenever $p\geq n^{-3/4}(\log n)^3$. Together with the non-reconstructibility result of Johnston, Kronenberg, Roberts and Scott, our result locates the second reconstruction transition at the scale $p=n^{-3/4}$ up to polylogarithmic factors, resolving a question they posed. Our proof relies on a global rigidity argument exploiting 5-cycle constraints.

Probability.title: Sharp Gaussian approximation for Polyak--Ruppert averaged linear stochastic approximation
Probability.summary: We study how quickly the normalized Polyak--Ruppert average approaches its Gaussian limit in linear stochastic approximation with bounded i.i.d.\ coefficients. For step sizes decaying as $k^{-γ}$, with $1/2\leγ<1$, we prove an upper bound of order $n^{γ-1}$ on the approximation error over convex sets in fixed dimension. A matching lower bound holds for every fixed model. The fastest rate in this range is $n^{-1/2}$, attained at $γ=1/2$. We also obtain an $O(n^{-1/2})$ bound on the error of the recursive multiplier bootstrap procedure.

Probability.title: Optimal linear filtering of partially observed polynomial processes in discrete and continuous time
Probability.summary: This paper is devoted to filtering, smoothing, and prediction of polynomial processes that are partially observed. These problems are known to allow for an explicit solution in the simpler case of linear Gaussian state space models. The key insight underlying the present piece of research is that in linear filtering applications polynomial processes and their discrete-time counterpart are indistinguishable from Gaussian processes sharing their first two moments. We describe the construction of these Gaussian equivalents of polynomial processes and explicitly compute optimal linear filters, predictors and smoothers for polynomial processes in discrete and continuous time. The consideration of Gaussian equivalents also opens the door to parameter estimation and linear-quadratic optimal control in the context of polynomial processes.

Probability.title: A Computer-Assisted Proof of Speed Monotonicity for the Biased Random Walk on a Galton-Watson Tree Beyond the Known Range
Probability.summary: The speed $v(λ)$ of the $λ$-biased random walk on a supercritical Galton--Watson tree without leaves is conjectured to be nonincreasing on $[0,m)$, where $m$ is the mean offspring. For non-constant offspring, monotonicity is known only for small bias: $λ\le 1/1160$, $λ\le 1/2$, and, when every vertex has at least $m_1\ge 2$ children, $λ\le m_1/(1+\sqrt{1-1/m_1})$. For offspring uniform on $\{2,3\}$ ($m=2.5$) the last bound is $2/(1+\sqrt{1/2})\approx1.1716$. We prove, with computer assistance, that $v$ is strictly decreasing on $[0,1.755]$ for this law. The proof has three parts. Aïdékon's speed formula gives $v=(R-λ)/(R+λ)$ for an explicit functional $R$, so $v$ decreases exactly when $R/λ$ does; we compare $R/λ$ at two biases directly, which avoids differentiating the conductance. A pathwise Lipschitz bound on the conductance in $λ$ turns that comparison into an inequality between expectations of explicit functions. A monotone sandwich of discretised laws gives two-sided bounds on the conductance law, and each $λ$-cell is checked in exact rational arithmetic over bounded floating-point error, with five cells re-checked in interval arithmetic; all reduction lemmas and an exact-integer certificate across $[1.17,1.755]$ are also formally verified in Lean 4. The method stops where the crude Lipschitz bound becomes too weak; sharper control of the derivative of the conductance is what the full range needs. Code and certificates are public.
Probability.comment: 9 pages, 1 figure. v3 adds a Lean 4 + mathlib formalisation of all reduction lemmas and an exact-integer certificate covering [1.17, 1.755]. Code: https://github.com/samyama-ai/gw-speed-certificate

Probability.title: Duality and hidden symmetries for time-inhomogeneous Markov processes
Probability.summary: We study the notion of duality in the setting of time-inhomogeneous Markov processes. We define duality with time-dependent duality functions. We establish the connection between duality and time-dependent symmetries and intertwinings. We illustrate the abstract results with examples from interacting particle systems and diffusion processes.

Probability.title: On ergodicity of the SAGA-LD algorithm
Probability.summary: The so-called SAGA-LD algorithm is used for efficient sampling from high-dimensional distributions in machine learning. Its intricate dynamics resists standard approaches of Markov chain theory. We prove, using a model-specific method, that SAGA-LD converges to a limiting distribution and a law of large numbers holds.

Probability.title: On shared responsibility, fish, and the strong law of large numbers
Probability.summary: We give a new, short, and intuitive proof of the strong law of large numbers for i.i.d. random variables.

Probability.title: Discontinuous transition in 2D Potts: II. Wetting and Brownian watermelon
Probability.summary:
The $q$-state Potts model is an archetypical model for various types of phase transitions. We consider it on the square grid and focus on the regime where it undergoes a discontinuous transition, that is $q>4$. At the transition point $T_c(q)$, there are exactly $q+1$ extremal Gibbs measures (pure phases): $q$ ordered (monochromatic) and one disordered (free). This work establishes for the first time the wetting phenomenon in a precise geometric form and in the entire regime of discontinuity $q>4$: at $T_c(q)$, between two ordered phases a disordered layer emerges and, in the diffusive scaling, its boundaries converge to a pair of Brownian motions conditioned not to intersect. This is starkly different from the subcritical ($T<T_c(q)$) behaviour. At $T_c(q)$, previous results (Bricmont--Lebowitz '87, Messager--Miracle-Sole--Ruiz--Shlosman '91) were limited to the construction and properties of the surface tension for large enough $q$.
  In a companion work, arXiv:2502.04129, we provide a detailed study of the Potts model under order-disorder Dobrushin conditions. That work also develops a ``renewal picture'' à la Ornstein-Zernike for a suitable percolation model, which plays a central part in our study of the Potts interfaces. The latter is the random-cluster representation of an Ashkin--Teller model (ATRC), and is related to the Potts model via a chain of couplings going through the six-vertex model.
  In the current work, we extend the analysis to a pair of interacting order-disorder interfaces forming the separation between the two ordered phases, and couple them to a pair of well-behaved random walks conditioned not to intersect. The construction of the coupling is based on rigorously deriving entropic repulsion between the two interfaces. We also prove convergence of interfaces in the FK-percolation model at $p_c(q)$ when $q>4$.
Probability.comment: 58 pages, 18 figures. v2: typo fixing, cosmetic improvement. Comments welcome!

Probability.title: Discontinuous transition in 2D Potts: I. Order-Disorder Interface convergence
Probability.summary:
We study a $q$-state Potts model on the square grid when $q>4$ at the point $T_c(q)$ of its (discontinous) transition. This model exhibits exactly $q+1$ extremal Gibbs measures: $q$ ordered (monochromatic) and one disordered (free). The current work deals with the Dobrushin order--disorder boundary conditions on a finite $N\times N$ box. Our main result is that this interface is a well-defined object, has $\sqrt{N}$ fluctuations, and converges to a Brownian bridge under diffusive scaling. The same holds also for the corresponding FK-percolation model for all $q>4$.
  Our proofs rely on a coupling between FK-percolation, the six-vertex model, and the random-cluster representation of an Ashkin--Teller model (ATRC), and on a detailed study of the latter. The coupling relates the interface in FK-percolation to a long subcritical cluster in the ATRC model. For this cluster we develop a ``renewal picture'' à la Ornstein-Zernike. This is based on fine mixing properties of the ATRC model that we establish using the link to the six-vertex model and its height function. Along the way, we derive various properties of the Ashkin-Teller model, such as Ornstein-Zernike asymptotics for its two-point function.
  In a companion work, we provide a detailed study of the Potts model under order-order Dobrushin conditions. We show emergence of a free layer of width $\sqrt{N}$ between the two ordered phases (wetting) and establish convergence of its boundaries to two Brownian bridges conditioned not to intersect.
Probability.comment: 82 pages, 29 figures. v2: improved presentation, adaptations to fit with companion work. v3: cosmetic improvements. Comments still welcome!

Probability.title: Homogenization theory of random walks in degenerate random environment
Probability.summary: Recent progress on the understanding of the Random Conductance Model is reviewed. A particular emphasis is on homogenization results such as functional central limit theorems, local limit theorems and heat kernel estimates for almost every realization of the environment, established for random walks among stationary ergodic conductances that are possibly unbounded but satisfy certain moment conditions.
Probability.comment: 36 pages, 2 figures; accepted version, to appear in Fractal Geometry and Stochastics VII, Progress in Probability

Probability.title: Higher order convergence rate in probability for approximations of the stochastic Burgers and Cahn-Hilliard equation
Probability.summary: We consider temporal approximations of stochastic PDEs driven by additive space-time white noise, with nonlinearities that may lose both integrability and regularity. Our key examples are the stochastic Burgers equation in dimension 1 and the stochastic Cahn-Hilliard equation in dimensions $\leq 3$. We show that the accelerated exponential Euler scheme achieves a rate of convergence in probability that is well beyond the state of the art: arbitrarily close to $3/4$ in the case of Burgers and $1-d/8$ in the case of Cahn-Hilliard.

Probability.title: The loop-ensemble scaling limits of near-critical percolation in the plane
Probability.summary: We prove that the collection of all cluster boundaries of near-critical site percolation (with a fixed parameter) on the triangular lattice has a unique scaling limit in the loop-ensemble space, as the mesh size tends to 0. This answers a problem proposed by Camia, Fontes and Newman (2006). Using this, we also prove that near-critical percolation exploration path in a disk converges in distribution to a continuous path as the mesh size goes to 0. The main idea of our proof is to construct the cut-off loop ensembles under the near-critical coupling, based on the enhanced networks and the quad-crossing scaling limits of near-critical percolation constructed by Garban, Pete and Schramm (2018); the proof also relies on the study of the geometry of cluster chains. Some properties of the limiting loop ensemble, including rotation invariance, scale covariance and finite chaining, are established. Moreover, a few applications of our scaling-limit result and proof strategy are discussed.

Probability.title: Moving Cut Loci and Gaussian Fluctuations of Intrinsic Huber Means on Compact Riemannian Manifolds
Probability.summary: Moving cut loci can change the limiting covariance of sample Huber means even when the cut locus of the population mean has probability zero. On a closed connected Riemannian manifold, we prove that the averaged logarithm field is $C^1$ near a point $m$ whenever the sampling law has a continuous density near its cut locus. The result holds for every continuous weight depending only on the observation, and the covariant derivative includes an explicit integral over the regular cut locus. When $m$ is a Huber mean for a fixed positive threshold, assume that the distance to $m$ has no atom at that threshold. The Hessian of the population risk then equals the expected pointwise Hessian minus a positive semidefinite cut locus correction. If $m$ is unique and this Hessian is positive definite, every measurable selection of global minimizers for i.i.d. samples satisfies a tangent-space central limit theorem. The cut loci of points in a ball of radius $δ$ sweep out a region of volume $O(δ)$, uniformly in the centre. These results establish the volume and integrability conditions previously assumed in a central limit theorem for intrinsic Fréchet means. At each fixed centre, the volume measure on this region, divided by $δ$, converges weakly to an explicit measure on the regular cut locus. The Huber correction vanishes exactly when the region swept out about $m$ has probability $o(δ)$.

Probability.title: Forward BFKL evolution at fixed coupling as a random walk, and the loss of its probability law at fixed next-to-leading order
Probability.summary: The BFKL equation describes how the density of gluons in a hadron grows with the collision energy. This evolution is often treated as a random walk in the logarithm of the gluon transverse momentum, but it has not been established that one set of positive step probabilities describes this walk in the size and the direction of the momentum, or that such probabilities exist beyond leading order. We show that one positive step density describes the evolution in the size and the direction of the momentum with no approximation at leading order, fixed coupling and zero momentum transfer, once the gluon density is rescaled by the size of its transverse momentum and its growth is divided out. The displacements of the resulting walk over separate, equal intervals of rapidity, the logarithm of the energy in units of a reference energy, are then independent and identically distributed, which makes the walk a Levy process. We also show that this description fails when the series in the coupling is cut at next-to-leading order, with the reference energy and the scale of the coupling both set by the product of the transverse momenta before and after an emission. The evolution averaged over directions then has no probability law at any fixed positive coupling and rapidity, because a negative correction growing as the squared logarithm of the momentum ratio outweighs the leading term when one momentum is much larger than the other. A positive step density for the averaged walk agrees with this truncated evolution to next-to-leading order and defines a random walk for every value of the strong coupling below one, so the failure comes from the truncation. The main message is that agreement with perturbation theory does not guarantee positive step probabilities, so an evolution equation summed to all orders and meant to describe a random walk must be tested for them.
Probability.comment: 38 pages, 2 figures. v2: revised and restructured version. The ancillary reproduction archive is unchanged from v1, and its checksum list refers to the v1 source

Probability.title: Secular Dynamics and the LFL for $β$ Corner Process
Probability.summary: In this paper, we consider the Gaussian $β$ corner process, whose edge particles are known to converge to the Tracy-Widom $β$ law. We study the almost sure behaviour of the extrema of the whole trajectory of the edge particles and establish a law of fractional logarithm (LFL) for the corner process for every fixed $β>0$, extending the previous known results in the case $β=1,2$. Our proof relies on the upward Gamma and downward Dirichlet secular equations, which can be regarded as two discrete dynamics to form the corner processes. The secular dynamics are used in both the correlation estimate and the decorrelation estimate, which are known as two key steps of proving LFL in \cite{BCEHK-LFL} for the Wigner minor process. Especially, in the decorrelation part, they are used as discrete analogues of the continuous Dyson Brownian motion.

Probability.title: Quantum unique ergodicity and the critical crossover for 1-d Gaussian band matrices
Probability.summary: We consider an $N\times N$ complex Gaussian random band matrix in one dimension with band width of order $W$, in the periodic block form of Yau and Yin. The $N$ sites are split into $n=N/W$ blocks of size $W$ on a ring, and the entries are nonzero only within a block and between adjacent blocks. The conjectured localization--delocalization transition occurs at $W\sim\sqrt N$. We prove quantum unique ergodicity for bulk eigenvectors at every deterministic rank whenever $W^2/N\to\infty$, with no power or logarithmic separation between $W^2$ and $N$. At the threshold $N/W^2\toτ\in(0,\infty)$, we show that the rescaled bulk eigenvalues and the block-mass profiles of their eigenvectors (the probability measures on the circle placing at $k/n$ the squared norm of the eigenvector on block $k$) converge jointly to a unique law. This law is encoded by a random entire function whose zeros give the limiting eigenvalues, and its derivatives there give the limiting profile integrals. The law of this function is determined by the Dorokhov--Mello--Pereyra--Kumar (DMPK) diffusion of the unitary class. In the critical law, the profiles have strictly positive variance against every nonconstant smooth test function, so they are not concentrated on the uniform profile. As $τ\to0$ this variance vanishes and the local spectrum tends to the sine process. As $τ\to\infty$ it tends to a Poisson process where both limits taken after the critical one. The critical family thus interpolates between the delocalized and localized regimes, confirming for this model the prediction of Fyodorov and Mirlin that at $W^2\asymp N$ the joint law of eigenvalues and eigenvectors depends only on $N/W^2$. The full content of this work has been autoformalized in Lean4 by AxiomProver.

Probability.title: Time-optimal problem in the space of probability measures
Probability.summary: This paper focuses on the value function in the time-optimal problem for a continuity equation in the space of probability measures. We derive the dynamic programming principle for this problem. Using this principle, we prove that the Kruzhkov transform of the value function is a unique discontinuous viscosity solution to the corresponding Dirichlet problem for the Hamilton-Jacobi equation. Finally, we establish the $Γ$-convergence of the value function in a perturbed problem to the value function in the unperturbed problem.

Probability.title: Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for the Kuramoto model on the sphere
Probability.summary: We establish quantitative uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for a generalization of the classical Kuramoto model on spheres of arbitrary dimension. For $n$ particles that are initialized independently from a probability measure with an $L^p$ density, $p>1$, and a nonzero mean vector, we obtain an explicit high-probability bound for the supremum over all times of the Wasserstein distance between the empirical and mean-field distributions. In sufficiently high dimension, this bound has the same order as the standard empirical sampling rate on the sphere and is therefore optimal. The proof combines a finite-time propagation of chaos estimate, a quantitative synchronization result for the mean-field model, and a late-time stability estimate of the system.

Probability.title: Heat kernel estimates for Markov processes with blowing-up jump kernels
Probability.summary: In this paper, we establish sharp two-sided heat kernel estimates for a large class of purely discontinuous symmetric Markov processes on closed subsets $F$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$, whose jump kernels blow up on a Borel subset $Σ$ of $F$. We assume that $F\setminus Σ$ is a $κ$-fat set and is dense in $F$, and additionally, in case of unbounded $F$, that the Assouad dimension of $F$ is strictly less than $d$. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work establishing sharp two-sided heat kernel estimates for jump processes whose jump kernels blow up on part of the state space. The jump kernels under consideration take the form $J(x,y)=|x-y|^{-d-α}{\mathcal B}(x,y)$, where $α\in (0,2)$ and the function ${\mathcal B}(x,y)$ blows up at a subset $Σ$ of $F$. A fundamental obstacle is that the tails of the jump measures are not uniformly bounded, and hence standard techniques in heat kernel analysis do not provide a priori off-diagonal estimates. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a new approach based on weighted integral estimates for the heat kernel that are sensitive to both the blow-up behavior of the jump kernel and the geometry of $F\setminus Σ$. Examples of processes falling within our general framework include traces of isotropic $α$-stable processes in some unbounded $C^{1,\rm Dini}$ sets, processes in Lipschitz sets arising in connection with the nonlocal Neumann problem, and a large class of resurrected self-similar processes in the closed upper half-space.

Probability.title: Hotelling's $T^2$ and the generalized domain of attraction of the normal law
Probability.summary: Let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be independent copies of a full random vector in $\mathbb R^p$, where $p$ is fixed. We prove that Hotelling's $T^2$-statistic at a prescribed location converges to $χ_p^2$ if and only if the underlying distribution belongs to the generalized domain of attraction of the normal law and has that location as its mean. Our proof of necessity combines moment bounds with matrix comparisons for self-normalized sums. It yields a sharp moment inequality for the squared norm of the uncentered self-normalized sum. Convergence of the first two moments of this squared norm to the chi-square values implies generalized normal attraction and identifies the mean. The necessity part of the multivariate Student normal-limit theorem follows as a corollary. Its sufficiency is the established result of Sepanski and of Vu, Maller and Klass.

Probability.title: Sharp partition function bound for the attractive logarithmic gas
Probability.summary: For the attractive logarithmic potential, we prove that the partition function is bounded uniformly in the number of particles on every compact inverse-temperature interval $[0,\be_0]$ with $\be_0<B$, where $B\in(0,2\d]$ is the sharp constant in the logarithmic Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev inequality. The proof separates a smooth bulk, which inherits the entropy inequality, from a short-range singular interaction. The singular contribution is controlled on the event that each box of a fixed grid contains few particles. The complementary overcrowding event has exponentially small probability, which compensates a crude linear-in-$N$ bound on the log partition function. The resulting estimate supplies the partition bound that can be used recycled in a few different results. A separate Lean formalization verifies the conditional partition-bound theorem under the log-HLS assumption.

Probability.title: Testing the number of common factors by bootstrapped sample covariance matrix in high-dimensional factor models and errata
Probability.summary: This paper studies the impact of bootstrap procedure on the eigenvalue distributions of the sample covariance matrix under a high-dimensional factor structure. We provide asymptotic distributions for the top eigenvalues of bootstrapped sample covariance matrix under mild conditions. After bootstrap, the spiked eigenvalues which are driven by common factors will converge weakly to Gaussian limits after proper scaling and centralization. However, the largest non-spiked eigenvalue is mainly determined by the order statistics of the bootstrap resampling weights, and follows extreme value distribution. Based on the disparate behavior of the spiked and non-spiked eigenvalues, we propose innovative methods to test the number of common factors. Indicated by extensive numerical and empirical studies, the proposed methods perform reliably and convincingly under the existence of both weak factors and cross-sectionally correlated errors. Our technical details contribute to random matrix theory on spiked covariance model with convexly decaying density and unbounded support, or with general elliptical distributions.

Probability.title: Upper deviations of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick free energy: the fifth-order law and the onset of constrained Parisi measures
Probability.summary: Let $Z_N$ be the partition function of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at inverse temperature $β>1$. Replica theory (Kondor near the critical temperature, Parisi and Rizzo at all temperatures) predicts that the probability that $N^{-1}\log Z_N$ exceeds its typical value by $δ$ decays like $\exp(-Naδ^{6/5})$ with an explicit $a$; Aronow and Lopatto recently proved bounds of this order. The exponent is the Legendre transform of the Parisi problem constrained to carry an atom $θ$ at zero. We show that the constrained minimum exceeds the equilibrium free energy by $c_βθ^5(1+o(1))$, where $c_β=\frac{9}{640}β^3ρ_β(0)^{-3}$ and $ρ_β(0)>0$ is the density at zero of the Parisi measure. With the fractional-moment formula this gives the exponent $\frac56(6c_β)^{-1/5}δ^{6/5}(1+o(1))$ as $N\to\infty$ and then $δ\to0$. The constrained minimizer has a marginal first positive contact, to leading order at $3θ/(2ρ_β(0))$ with an atom $θ/2$. This plateau calculus applies to every mixture with $ξ'''(0)=0$ whose Parisi measure accumulates at zero; a small field $h$ opens a gap of order $|h|^{2/3}$, and an atom of the Parisi measure at zero, present in every pure $p$-spin model with $p\ge3$, makes the rate leave zero linearly. Near criticality the constant tends to Kondor's value $9/5120$ and the marginal regime ends at a de Almeida-Thouless threshold. For the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at every $β>1$, a finite-step curvature inequality from an unrefereed preprint shows that every constrained minimizer either has an interval of positive contacts, all marginal, or has exactly two atoms, and that the marginal regime ends at a unique de Almeida-Thouless threshold $θ_c(β)$. The laws at every $β>1$ use that the Parisi measure accumulates at zero, a theorem of Lopatto also proved in earlier work of the author.
Probability.comment: v3: replaces v2, whose source files were those of v1; 112 pages, 4 figures, 1 table

Probability.title: The massive phase of the two-dimensional Heisenberg model is stable under small anisotropy
Probability.summary: Polyakov predicted that the classical Heisenberg model on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ has exponentially decaying correlations at every temperature, and proofs of this have recently been posted. We show that the massive phase survives small anisotropy. For every inverse temperature $β$ there is $δ(β)>0$ such that the $S^2$-valued model with couplings $\sum_iJ^iσ_x^iσ_y^i$ has exponentially decaying spin two-point functions, uniformly in finite subgraphs with free boundary conditions and in edge strengths up to $β$, whenever all $|J^i-1|\leδ(β)$. The same holds for aligned single-ion anisotropy and for nearly isotropic $O(n)$ models with $n\ge3$. Consequently, for the easy-plane model with couplings $σ^xσ^x+σ^yσ^y+λσ^zσ^z$, the onset of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless phase, proved by Garban and de Montgolfier for every $λ\in(-1,1)$, moves to zero temperature as $λ\uparrow1$. These results rest on the annulus crossing bound of Ding, Huang and Yang, used on one finite annulus where the anisotropy is a bounded perturbation, and on a sign-cluster argument with Ginibre's inequality for anisotropic planar energies. Explicit constants of another isotropic proof give decay for $β\le c |\log(1-λ)|^{1/2}$. For $n\ge4$ and $|J^i-1|\leδ$ with $δ$ small, at $β\le(1-\varepsilon)|\logδ|/(2π)$ spin one-point functions decay exponentially away from the boundary under every boundary condition, and two-point functions decay, both on the scale $e^{πβ+O(\sqrt{β\logβ})}$. This is the $O(4)$ threshold: for $n=4$ it matches the renormalization-group crossover to leading order; for $n\ge5$ it lies below the prediction. This part is conditional on estimates of a recent manuscript on the $O(4)$ model, which the proof transfers to anisotropic couplings at one scale; only odd observables transfer.

Probability.title: Talagrand's Convolution Bound for Tensor Powers of Finite-State Markov Semigroups
Probability.summary:
Talagrand's convolution conjecture, recently proven by J. Lu, S. Guo, and E. Fang, concerns the smoothing properties of the heat semigroup on $\{-1,1\}^N$. We follow their perturbed coupled reverse-heat approach to generalize the theorem to tensor powers of irreducible continuous-time Markov semigroups on finite state spaces. Specifically, let $(S_t)_{t\geq0}$ be the semigroup of an irreducible continuous-time Markov chain on a finite state space $G_0$ with stationary distribution $π$. Then, for every $τ>0$, there exists a finite constant $C_{τ,S,π}<\infty$ such that, for every $N\geq1$, every nonnegative function $f:G_0^N\to[0,\infty)$, and every $η>1$, \begin{align*}
  π^{\otimes N}\left(S_τ^{\otimes N}f>η\int_{G_0^N}f\,dπ^{\otimes N}\right)\leq\frac{C_{τ,S,π}}{η\sqrt{\logη}}, \end{align*} where the constant is independent of $N$, $f$, and $η$. Most of the machinery developed by Lu, Guo, and Fang transfers cleanly, but since probability distributions on $|G_0|$ elements are not determined by their mean for $|G_0|>2$, we must use explicit terminal bridge laws to find a dimension-independent bound for the terminal-discrepancy estimate. We have formalized our result in Lean 4. The formalization is publicly available.

Differential Geometry.title: Beyond Brown's radial tests: admissibility, parabolicity, and a doubling-Poincaré prior that neither test decides
Differential Geometry.summary: For the estimation of a normal mean in $\mathbb{R}^m$ under quadratic loss, Brown (1971) proved that a generalized Bayes estimator $δ_F$ with bounded drift is admissible if and only if a diffusion attached to the marginal $f^*$ of the prior $F$ is recurrent, and gave two radial tests: a sphere-average test for recurrence and a ray test for transience. He observed that both tests can be silent. We read his theory as the potential theory of the weighted Euclidean space $(\mathbb{R}^m,f^*\,dx)$ and ask what the modern theory of recurrence on weighted manifolds adds inside the zone where neither test applies. Three results. (A) If $f^*\,dx$ is doubling and supports a scale-invariant Poincaré inequality, the sphere test is already complete: recurrence, Brown's sphere test and the ball-volume test are equivalent, so geometric criteria can add decidable cases only on the inadmissible side. (B) They do add one. An explicit prior on $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose marginal is small along a lattice of circles at dyadic scales with spacing equal to the square root of the scale is doubling and Poincaré, silences both of Brown's tests, and is transient by the ball-volume test; its generalized Bayes estimator is inadmissible. (C) Outside the doubling-Poincaré class the zone is two-sided: similar circles placed on one surface per scale give an admissible estimator, decided by a flux bound along a non-spherical exhaustion, and a logarithmic product prior gives an inadmissible one, decided by product heat kernels. A comparison lemma shows that any positive weight with Lipschitz logarithm is, up to constants, the marginal of a prior, so that explicit weights may be used throughout.
Differential Geometry.comment: 26 pages, 8 figures, 6 tables. v3: statements and proofs made precise after a Lean 4 formalization of part of the arguments; Section 2.4 now cites Sturm; new Appendix B on the formal verification; Lean sources in the repository

Differential Geometry.title: Almost-splitting of spacetimes under timelike sectional curvature bounds
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish an almost-splitting theorem for spacetimes under timelike sectional curvature bounds in the spirit of the celebrated Riemannian result due to Cheeger and Colding. More concretely, we show that if a globally hyperbolic spacetime with timelike sectional curvature bounded below by a nonpositive constant close to zero contains a long maximizing timelike segment, then causal diamonds along that segment are close in the Lorentzian Gromov--Hausdorff sense of Minguzzi--Suhr to those in a product metric spacetime. Our result can be interpreted as a quantitative analogue of the Lorentzian splitting theorem for spacetimes with nonnegative timelike sectional curvature by Beem--Ehrlich--Markvorsen--Galloway. In contrast to the Riemannian setting, the timelike sectional curvature bound cannot be replaced by Ricci-flatness, as the small mass limit of the Schwarzschild exterior geometry shows.
Differential Geometry.comment: 47 pages, 1 figure, incl. Appendix A discussing the small mass limit of exterior Schwarzschild

Differential Geometry.title: Addendum to "Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds"
Differential Geometry.summary: In the paper ``Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds'', the same authors introduced a geometric object called Pontryagin-type $C^0$-Finsler structures, which includes Finsler structures on a smooth manifold $M$. Such a structure is defined locally by a control system of $C^1$ unit vector fields on an open subset $U$ of $M$, such that Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) is applicable. As a result of PMP, we obtain the extended geodesic field $\mathcal{E}$, which is a multivalued vector field on the slit cotangent bundle $T^{\ast}U\backslash 0 = \{(x,α): x\in U, α\in T^{\ast}_x U\}$, such that every minimizing path $x(t)$ on $(U,F)$ is an extremal (projection of a Pontryagin extremal $(x(t),α(t))$). Some time after its introduction, its use and external comments, it is useful to provide remarks that clarify the applicability and limitations of this theory. In addition, we point out two errors contained in that work which, although discernible from the context, we believe should be pointed out. Finally, we prove some cases where the property that a minimizing path is the projection of a Pontryagin extremal can be extended beyond a coordinate system, sometimes to $M$. We also work on the problem of determining when $\mathcal{E}$ does not depend on the control system chosen to represent $F$. In particular, $\mathcal{E}$ satisfies these two properties globally for left-invariant $C^0$-Finsler structures on Lie groups, and for $C^1$-Finsler structures (without the condition of strong convexity).

Differential Geometry.title: Flotation Rigidity for Convex Polytopes
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that the oriented liquid-level function determines a full-dimensional convex polytope $P\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, and its relative density $δ\in(0,1)\setminus\{\tfrac12\}$. Uniqueness also follows from buoyancy surfaces at distinct densities accumulating at a non-half interior value. For polygons, fixed-density buoyancy data determine the normalized difference body, yielding uniqueness among centrally symmetric polygons at every density.

Differential Geometry.title: On the atomic decomposition of complete intersections in toric varieties
Differential Geometry.summary:
Building on Liu's and Liu--Sheshmani's systematized description of Kontsevich's localization methods in toric varieties, we develop a computational framework for genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants of smooth projective toric varieties and their smooth complete intersections. This is grounded in equivariant localization and the combinatorial structure of toric fans. We describe how the geometric data required by the localization formulas can be recovered directly from the fan and extend the existing software for flag varieties to compute the small quantum multiplication by the first Chern class. The implementation also incorporates cyclic determinants and regularized-exponent multisets, providing computational tools for investigating the atomic decomposition of quantum cohomology.
  Using this framework, we obtain the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^5$. Also applying new methods to study Hodge atoms in Fano fivefolds, we recover the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^7$, due to Cavenaghi--Katzarkov--Kontsevich, and we prove the nonrationality of every smooth quartic double fivefold and every smooth quartic fivefold.

Differential Geometry.title: The anisotropic Weyl law and Grassmannian equidistribution
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish a Weyl law for the codimension-one anisotropic volume spectrum on compact Riemannian manifolds. We then use this law to obtain equidistribution in the full Grassmannian bundle while keeping the ambient metric fixed. More precisely, on every closed connected smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension three through six, we construct smooth, embedded hypersurfaces stationary for anisotropies smoothly converging to area. The cumulative sum of their area measures, when lifted to the Grassmannian bundle, converges to the uniform measure.

Differential Geometry.title: Entire boosted hypersurfaces of vanishing mean curvature in Schwarzschild spacetime
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove the existence of entire maximal hypersurfaces, asymptotic to suitable coordinate-dependent boosts in the two asymptotically flat ends of maximally extended Schwarzschild spacetime. As a corollary, this generates a foliation of maximal hypersurfaces in exterior Schwarzschild, which corresponds to a geometric choice of time function associated with any boost parameter. As a crucial step in the proof, we introduce a novel rotationally symmetric time function in maximally extended Schwarzschild, which is Cauchy and has properties of independent interest.

Differential Geometry.title: Generic equivariant simplicity of the spectrum of Laplace-type operators with finite symmetry
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that for generic elements in three natural families of Laplace-type differential operators on smooth manifolds, which are equivariant with respect to a finite symmetry group, all the eigenspaces are irreducible representations. In other words, the spectrum of these operators is generically equivariantly simple. The three families of operators with symmetry are Schrödinger operators parametrized by the potential, going back to the work of Wigner, Laplace-Beltrami operators parametrized by invariant Riemannian metrics and conformal Laplacians parametrized by invariant metrics in a given conformal class. The latter two results extend prior work of Zelditch for certain free group actions and resolve, for finite group actions, a well-known open question raised by Guillemin and Yau. Our approach stems from methods developed by Wendl and Doan-Walpuski to address equivariant transversality in symplectic topology.

Differential Geometry.title: Poisson and Jacobi structures on quadratic Lie algebras
Differential Geometry.summary: We study Poisson and Jacobi structures compatible with quadratic structures on finite-dimensional Lie algebras, mostly over fields of characteristic zero. Building on the theory of generalized double extensions, we give necessary and sufficient reconstruction criteria for the skew operators preserving a marked isotropic ideal, allowing degenerate operators, a nonabelian quadratic quotient, and the full generalized extension data. Recalling the characterization of quadratic Poisson structures in terms of skew-symmetric solutions of the classical Yang--Baxter equation, we combine the ambient bracket reconstruction of Kostant and Meyer with prescribed symplectic leaf data to reconstruct Poisson structures whose characteristic subalgebra is nondegenerate for the quadratic form. We express the standard algebraic Jacobi equations through the invariant form and obtain analogous reconstruction results for nondegenerate characteristic subalgebras. Particular attention is given to the contact and locally conformally symplectic cases. A common cochain framework identifies the remaining scalar obstruction in third cohomology in the Poisson case and in the Jacobi branch whose Euler element belongs to the marked ideal, with coefficients in a one dimensional module in the latter case. Our reconstruction results yield systematic procedures for constructing quadratic Poisson structures in dimension $n+2k$ from those in dimension $n$, and recover the earlier quadratic symplectic extension formulas when the Poisson operator is invertible. Explicit examples illustrate the applicability of the theory, including oscillator algebras, the five-dimensional Lie algebra $A_{5,3}$, and Poisson structures associated with the curvature tensor of a bi-invariant metric.

Differential Geometry.title: Entropic Ricci bounds at conic singularities and boundaries
Differential Geometry.summary: We study synthetic Ricci bounds and related rigidity phenomena in conic and boundary neighborhoods through the behavior of entropy along optimal transports. For cones over manifolds, we show that two-sided entropic Ricci bounds at the vertex force the fiber to have constant sectional curvature 1, while non-trivial quotient singularities, such as Euclidean cones over spherical space forms, remain admissible. An analogous rigidity holds for Riemannian manifolds with conic singularities. We also give a local characterization of boundary convexity in terms of entropic lower Ricci bounds, based on a direct optimal transport argument.

Differential Geometry.title: Eigenvalue estimates of the drifted Cheng-Yau operator on bounded domains in pinched Cartan-Hadamard manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish universal eigenvalue inequalities for a drifted Cheng--Yau operator on bounded domains in pinched Cartan--Hadamard manifolds with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Our approach combines a universal quadratic eigenvalue inequality for operators in divergence form with a Rauch-type comparison theorem and a Bochner-type formula. We evaluate the geometric terms in this quadratic inequality under suitable assumptions on the radial behavior of the coefficient tensor and the drifting function, together with curvature pinching conditions. In the general setting, we establish a Rauch-type comparison theorem for the Cheng--Yau operator and derive two auxiliary estimates from its Bochner-type formula. We then prove integral estimates of independent interest and apply them to obtain the desired eigenvalue inequalities for both the Cheng--Yau operator and the drifted Laplacian, recovering known inequalities for the Laplacian. We also establish a rigidity result for the Cheng--Yau operator on a class of bounded annular domains in pinched Cartan--Hadamard manifolds. In Euclidean space, this result can be applied, for instance, with the potential function of the Gaussian shrinking soliton. The hyperbolic space is treated separately in two settings, one exploiting the conformal relation between its metric and the Euclidean metric, and the other via its warped product structure, reducing the problem to one dimension. We extend the hyperbolic construction of the fundamental gap for the Laplacian to a class of operators in divergence form. Examples are provided to illustrate the scope and applicability of our results.
Differential Geometry.comment: This is the final version, published in Annali di Matematica Pura ed Applicata

Differential Geometry.title: Simplifying 2-Bundle Descriptions of Invariants and Local Dynamics
Differential Geometry.summary: A string couples to a 2-form gauge potential whose local descriptions need not fit together as a single global form. Principal 2-bundles provide a geometric description of this gluing. However, we recover surface amplitudes and quantum partition functions, as well as local classical field dynamics, without the 2-bundle formalism. For surface amplitudes, differential characters preserve curvature and flat phases. Ordinary fake-flat crossed-module connections with a fixed flat quotient and a reference lift lead to abelian differential cocycles with local coefficients. In three-dimensional finite gauge theories with cohomological actions, Fourier transformation evaluates the 2-form field sum and gives a sum of ordinary finite-group gauge partition functions. A four-dimensional quadratic example gives a signature response that admits direct cochain evaluation although replacement by an ordinary finite-group gauge theory fails. Established bundle, operator, and module descriptions provide further comparisons for topological and index invariants and twisted-sheaf moduli. For finite-dimensional smoothly separable central crossed modules, an invertible local substitution removes a pure gauge 1-form from invariant classical actions for any adjustment, leaving an ordinary quotient connection and two tensor fields. One of these tensor fields can be separated globally from the remaining lift data after fixing the quotient connection and choosing a smooth bundle splitting. For compact or semisimple quotients, an equivariant splitting makes this separation compatible with the full gauge symmetry without changing the adjustment.

Differential Geometry.title: HKT-Einstein metrics on circle bundles
Differential Geometry.summary: We consider a construction of hyper-Hermitian structures on total spaces of circle bundles over 3-quasi-Sasakian manifolds. We study the HKT-Einstein equation in this setting, proving that a large family of non-homogeneous hyper-complex manifolds admit compatible HKT-Einstein metrics with positive Einstein factor. We also show that the hyper-Hermitian structures on such circle bundles are quaternionic balanced or quaternionic Gauduchon if and only if they are HKT. Finally, the HKT-Einstein condition is investigated under the twist construction.

Differential Geometry.title: On Spherically Symmetric Sprays
Differential Geometry.summary: This paper studies spherically symmetric sprays, i.e., sprays that are invariant under orthogonal transformations. We first establish a canonical form for such sprays, showing that their geodesic coefficients can be expressed as \(G^i = |y|α(r,s) y^i + |y|^2β(r,s) x^i\), where \(r = |x|^2\) and \(s = \langle x,y\rangle/|y|\). For projectively flat spherically symmetric sprays -- which are directly related to Hilbert's fourth problem on characterizing metrics whose geodesics are straight lines -- we derive a complete classification of those with isotropic curvature, and in particular, we obtain the explicit form of those with zero curvature. Furthermore, we characterize sprays of weakly isotropic curvature in this class by a system of partial differential equations. These results may provide a unified framework for understanding symmetry and curvature in spray geometry and may offer new insights into the metrizability problem in Finsler geometry.

Differential Geometry.title: Scalar curvature integrals on geodesic balls
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove bounds for scalar curvature integrals over geodesic balls on complete noncompact manifolds with nonnegative sectional curvature. In every dimension $n\ge3$, when the asymptotic volume ratio is close to one, we obtain upper and lower estimates with the sharp first-order coefficient and a quadratic remainder. The leading terms involve the asymptotic and local volume deficits, respectively. Rotationally symmetric examples show that both first-order coefficients are optimal and that a quadratic remainder is necessary in the upper bound. For dimensions three, four, and five we give estimates for any positive asymptotic volume ratio. When the center is a pole, we give an estimate in dimension three under nonnegative Ricci curvature and in every dimension $n\ge4$ under nonnegative sectional curvature. This estimate is sharp when the asymptotic volume ratio is at most $2^{-(n-1)}$.
Differential Geometry.comment: 47 pages, improve the main results to arbitrary dimension $n\ge3$ compare to v1

Differential Geometry.title: Determinant Identities and Branch Selection in the Stationary Multi-Horizon Balance Problem
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the Hennig-Neugebauer family of stationary and axisymmetric vacuum multi-horizon candidates. The regularity conditions on the symmetry axis lead to quadratic determinant relations which leave an apparent ambiguity between two sign branches. Under explicit non-degeneracy assumptions, we prove that one of these branches is impossible. This branch selection yields a system of explicit determinant equations characterizing equilibrium within the family.

Differential Geometry.title: Conformal boundary rigidity from null geodesic travel times
Differential Geometry.summary: The gravitational field of a distant, isolated system is manifested by the conformally invariant Weyl tensor. Thus the conformal structure far from the system encodes the system's gravitational mass. It also encodes the causal structure, thereby linking it to the mass. For asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetimes, this link led to a novel positive mass theorem of Page, Surya, and the second author \cite{PSW} which did not rely on any traditional energy condition. Here we ask whether that theorem has a rigidity case. Specifically, we consider all null geodesics in an asymptotically AdS spacetime that depart from the Penrose conformal infinity, travel through spacetime, and return to conformal infinity. If all such geodesics from a given point refocus at an antipodal point at infinity, is the spacetime conformal to anti-de Sitter space? It is easy to answer the question if the asymptotically AdS spacetime either (i) obeys the null energy condition in 3 or 4 spacetime dimensions, or (ii) is static (in any dimension), and we give simple proofs in those cases. We then answer the question in the case of globally stationary, asymptotically AdS spacetimes, by applying the theory of magnetic geodesics on the Riemannian manifold-with-boundary obtained by quotienting by the stationary Killing vector field. The question has an analogue for asymptotically flat spacetimes, which we also discuss.
Differential Geometry.comment: Typos fixed, other minor revisions, assumptions in Theorems 3.1 and 4.4 clarified

Differential Geometry.title: Classification of Certain Rational Isoparametric Functions on Damek-Ricci Spaces
Differential Geometry.summary: We classify isoparametric functions on Damek-Ricci spaces which can be written in terms of the standard coordinates $(v,z,t)$ on the half-space model as a polynomial function divided by $t$. Regular level sets of the functions in our classification encompass almost all previously known examples of isoparametric hypersufaces in Damek-Ricci space and also yield new ones. For the new examples, the focal varieties are determined and the mean curvatures of the regular level sets are expressed as a function of the distance from the focal variety. We also study the exceptional case of tubes about $\mathbb R\mathbf H^k$ in $\mathbb C\mathbf H^k$, which are isoparametric, but cannot be obtained as the level sets of any function in our classification. We show that these tubes are level sets of a polynomial function divided by $t^2$, and that analogous functions on Damek-Ricci spaces can be isoparametric only in the case of $\mathbb C\mathbf H^k$.
Differential Geometry.comment: We corrected the statement and proof of Lemma 3.4 appearing in version 2, which necessitated a slight modification of part (i) of the Main Theorem. We also added a new lemma (Lemma 3.2) to establish the revised statement of part (i) of the Main Theorem

Differential Geometry.title: Weighted minimal surfaces in H2 x R invariant under hyperbolic translations
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we consider weighted minimal surfaces in H2xR, namely, surfaces that arise as critical points of a weighted area functional, where the corresponding weight depends only on the height function associated with the second factor R. We refer to these surfaces as φ-minimal surfaces. For a class of increasing and concave weight potential functions φ, we focus our attention on height-weighted minimal surfaces that are invariant under isometries of H2xR that act trivially on R and act by hyperbolic translations in H2. Through a detailed analysis of the corresponding three-dimensional system of ordinary differential equations, we present families of entire graphs, graphs over half-spaces of H2 that are asymptotic to vertical planes, winglike surfaces, and surfaces whose height function has no minimum. These families show that the hyperbolic-invariant setting is considerably richer than the rotational and parabolic settings. For the class of potential functions φ we consider, they also allow us to classify all weighted minimal surfaces in H2xR that are invariant under hyperbolic translations.

Differential Geometry.title: A note on equivariant twisted holomorphic analytic torsion
Differential Geometry.summary: In this note, we introduce an equivariant version of twisted holomorphic analytic torsion for the twisted Dolbeault complex on a complex manifold equipped with an action of a compact Lie group. Our construction is motivated by Ray and Singer's holomorphic analytic torsion, by the equivariant analytic torsion developed for elliptic complexes with group actions, notably in the work of Donnelly and later in the holomorphic setting by Bismut, and by Mathai and Wu's twisted analytic torsion for the twisted de Rham complex. Using pseudodifferential operators and the equivariant noncommutative residue, we define the equivariant twisted holomorphic analytic torsion. We also state its variation formulas under changes of the metric and of the twisting element, and present its functorial properties.
Differential Geometry.comment: 16 pages; this note presents the core material of the author's master's degree thesis. It was completed between late May and early June 2026

Differential Geometry.title: Timelike surfaces of constant mean and constant Gaussian curvature in anti-de Sitter 3-space via loop groups
Differential Geometry.summary: The loop group description of surfaces whose Gauss map is Lorentz harmonic is known for timelike surfaces of constant mean curvature in the flat Lorentzian 3-space, and for surfaces of constant Gaussian curvature in the 3-sphere. We carry out the corresponding construction for timelike surfaces in anti-de Sitter 3-space $\mathbb{H}^3_1\cong SL(2,\mathbb{R})$: those of constant mean curvature, whose Gauss map is harmonic for the conformal structure of the first fundamental form, and those of constant Gaussian curvature $K>-1$, $K\neq0$, whose Gauss map is then an immersion and is harmonic for the second fundamental form. For both classes we prove the harmonicity characterization, recover the surfaces from extended frames by Sym-Bobenko-type formulas, and solve the geometric Cauchy problem by the generalized DPW method, with potentials written explicitly in terms of the data and no normalization of the Gauss map. We then show that the two constructions differ only by a normalization: after the substitution $λ=ζ^2$ and a constant gauge, a constant mean curvature extended frame $\hat F$ is an extended frame of its Gauss map, and the maps $\hat F|_{λ=e^{4θ}}\exp(θe_3)\hat F|_{λ=1}^{-1}$ and $e_3\hat F|_{λ=e^{4θ}}e_3\exp(θe_3)\hat F|_{λ=1}^{-1}$, with $e_3=\mathrm{diag}(-1,1)$, are timelike surfaces of constant Gaussian curvature $1/\sinh^2θ$ and $-1/\cosh^2θ$ wherever the constant mean curvature surface is not flat. The first is the classical parallel surface, the second its polar surface. Explicit families, with extended frames and surfaces in closed form, illustrate the constructions.

Differential Geometry.title: Dirac eigenvalue comparison
Differential Geometry.summary: We study how curvature bounds control the Dirac eigenvalues of closed spin manifolds, comparing the positive and negative eigenvalues separately. Within a fixed conformal class and spin structure, pointwise ordering of scalar curvature relative to a metric of negative scalar curvature implies comparison at every nonzero index. On the two-sphere, a holomorphic ladder on the half-canonical bundle proves the corresponding comparison in both directions under a Gaussian curvature bound. On surfaces of higher genus, the same bundle identities propagate comparison from the scalar and spinor levels to higher canonical powers. In the round conformal class on the higher dimensional sphere, a prescribed scalar curvature bound yields an upper bound in absolute value for the first $2^{[n/2]}$ Dirac eigenvalues. When the conformal class varies, we can show that the corresponding comparisons on hyperbolic surfaces and odd-dimensional spheres no longer hold; while on even-dimensional spheres, the first gap and all sufficiently high-index eigenvalues of either sign satisfy a one-direction comparison.

Differential Geometry.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for $m$-positive and generalized $m$-positive forms
Differential Geometry.summary: We study strong positivity and Hodge--Riemann relations for real $(1,1)$-forms satisfying generalized $m$-positivity conditions. We prove that every good prefix, defined by the hyperbolicity cones of successive directional derivatives of the determinant, has a strictly strongly positive product and satisfies the Hodge--Riemann relations in every bidegree. Allowing factors on the boundaries of these cones, we show that the hyperbolicity cone of every nonzero prefix product equals the polarizing component of its natural exterior-algebra quotient. This gives the full mixed Hodge--Riemann relations for ordinary $m$-positive forms without a semipositivity assumption. We also prove the relations for weakly $(m,l)$-positive forms, defined by $(m-l)$-positivity on every codimension-$l$ subspace, when $p+q\le m$ and $\max\{p,q\}\ge l$. For $l=1$ and $m\ge2$, the associated $(m-1)$-th power map is a diffeomorphism from the weak $(m,1)$-positive cone onto the positive $(d-1,d-1)$-cone. For smooth closed forms satisfying the ordinary, weak $(m,l)$-positive, or good-prefix hypotheses pointwise, Dinh--Nguyên's method gives the corresponding hard Lefschetz theorems and Hodge--Riemann relations on the cohomology of compact Kähler manifolds. We also discuss numerical criteria, generalized Hessian equations, and intersection inequalities for generalized $m$-positive forms.

Differential Geometry.title: Hyperbolicity Notions on Complete Non-Compact Complex Manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: Gromov's Kähler hyperbolicity, extended by McMullen to complete manifolds of finite volume and bounded geometry, has non-Kähler analogues (balanced, SKT, Gauduchon and divisorial hyperbolicity) that have so far been studied only on compact manifolds. We define these notions for complete Hermitian manifolds and prove the following. A manifold carrying a balanced metric and a Hermitian metric with bounded $(\partial+\bar\partial)$-potentials satisfies a Cheeger inequality, so its fundamental group is non-amenable in the compact case. Kähler and SKT hyperbolic manifolds are Brody hyperbolic, and balanced and Gauduchon hyperbolic manifolds are divisorially hyperbolic, without any compactness assumption. Products give complete non-compact non-Kähler examples. A non-compact surface may be divisorially hyperbolic without being Brody hyperbolic. Finally, no functorial pseudo-distance characterises divisorial hyperbolicity.}

Differential Geometry.title: Harmonic functions and the topology of 3-manifolds under nonnegative scalar curvature
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we establish and recover some results about noncompact 3-manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature and some topological assumptions. Firstly, we apply the work in Oronzio \cite{Oro1,Oro2} to obtain a nonexistence result of the harmonic function. Secondly, we use the argument in Yan-Zhu \cite{YZ} to establish a rigidity result, which states that such manifold is isometric to the warped product of a flat tours and a half line. Finally, we recover a topological result in Yan-Zhu \cite{YZ} via a different argument.

Differential Geometry.title: Classification of G-g.o. metrics on compact homogeneous spaces G/H with G simple
Differential Geometry.summary: We classify the $G$-g.o. metrics on compact homogeneous spaces $G/H$, where $G$ is a compact connected simple Lie group and $H$ is an arbitrary closed subgroup. We give the complete list of nonnormal metrics, including their parameter conditions and the possible mixing between equivalent isotropy summands. The proof uses rigidity criteria for arbitrary cometric operators, reductions through centralizers, and the stabilizers of the relevant representations. For every fixed pair $(G,H)$, the space spanned by the $G$-g.o. cometrics has dimension at most three, and we determine the equality cases. We also compare the classification with the compact weakly symmetric pairs and explain why the choice of the transitive group is essential.

Differential Geometry.title: Homotopies in Batalin-Vilkovisky Formalism
Differential Geometry.summary: We review the notion of homotopy of quantum master actions in geometric Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism. Then we construct new examples of such homotopies, coming from renormalization group flow and non-infinitesimal changes of gauge fixing. Finally, we use the field redefinitions given by these homotopies to construct spans of quantum master actions with isomorphic effective actions.
Differential Geometry.comment: 45 pages; v2 - version published in Journal of Geometry and Physics. Corrected some typos and minor sign inconsistencies, clarified connection to the literature in Sections 4.2.3 and 6.1, added some missing references

Differential Geometry.title: Polynomial approximations to Calabi--Yau metrics on quartic K3 surfaces and quintic threefolds
Differential Geometry.summary: On the Fermat quartic K3 surface and the Fermat quintic threefold, we construct Kähler metrics from explicit rational polynomial potentials and bound their differences from the Ricci-flat metrics in integral tensor norms. For specified compact families of smooth quartic and quintic hypersurfaces near the Fermat hypersurfaces, we give a terminating algorithm that constructs polynomial Kähler metrics with prescribed pointwise bounds on their differences from the Ricci-flat metrics and on their Ricci forms. The resulting metrics converge to the Ricci-flat metrics in every $C^r$ norm, uniformly in the parameter.

Differential Geometry.title: Finite-Time Singularities of Lagrangian Mean Curvature Flow with Quantitatively Precise Dynamics
Differential Geometry.summary:
For each integer $K\geq2$ when $n\geq4$, and for $K=2,3,4$ when $n=3$, we construct an almost-calibrated Lagrangian mean curvature flow $L_K(t)$ in $\mathbb{C}^{n}$, starting from initial data arbitrarily close to being special Lagrangian, which develops a finite-time Type II singularity at time $T$ with the explicit curvature blow up rate \[
  \sup_{L_{K}(t)} |\mathbf{A}_{L_{K}(t)}| \sim (T-t)^{-K/2}
  \qquad \text{as } t\nearrow T . \] The tangent flow at the singularity is a transverse pair of cohomogeneity-one special Lagrangian cones, while the Type II blow-up limit is a smooth cohomogeneity-one special Lagrangian desingularization.
  This gives a quantitative construction of Type II blow-up for a fully nonlinear parabolic PDE arising from cohomogeneity-one Lagrangian mean curvature flow. Our construction is based on a modulation analysis around a shrinking family of cohomogeneity-one special Lagrangian desingularizations, using the perturbative spectral theory developed in the companion paper.
Differential Geometry.comment: 114 pages, 1 figure. Comments welcome. Corrected minor errors and added Appendix B

Differential Geometry.title: Variation of Hodge structures for non-Kähler manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we discuss unpolarized, complex variation of Hodge structures for non-Kähler manifolds. In particular, consider a holomorphic family of compact complex manifolds with central fiber $X$. Suppose that the inclusion of complexes $(F^pA^\bullet(X),d)\hookrightarrow (A^\bullet(X),d)$ induces injective maps \[ H^j(F^pA^\bullet(X),d)\longrightarrow H^j(A^\bullet(X),d),\qquad j=k,\ k+1. \] Under this condition, we show that the period map is holomorphic and transversal. An essential ingredient for the proof is a deformation theory of filtered $(p,q)$-forms. We prove a jumping formula for filtered de Rham cohomology and obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for its dimension to be invariant under deformation of complex structures.

Differential Geometry.title: Prescribed inverse-weight Lin-Lu-Yau curvature flow on finite trees
Differential Geometry.summary: We characterize the image of the inverse-weight Lin-Lu-Yau curvature map on finite edge-weighted trees. We prove that the prescribed curvature flow converges if and only if the target curvature is attainable, and that the convergence is exponential whenever it occurs. The key ingredient in the proof is a formulation of the prescribed curvature flow as the gradient flow of a convex functional.

Differential Geometry.title: Liouville type results for super-$p$-biharmonic immersions and $p$-biharmonic submanifolds
Differential Geometry.summary:
We introduce a weak notion of $\varepsilon$-super-$p$-biharmonic immersion into Euclidean space, formulated through a divergence inequality for the mean curvature vector. This class naturally extends the $\varepsilon$-superbiharmonic immersions previously introduced by the third author while remaining well-defined for all $p>1$, including the singular range $1<p<2$. We prove a Liouville-type rigidity theorem showing that every proper $\varepsilon$-super-$p$-biharmonic immersion is minimal provided
  \[
  \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac1{r^{2}} \int_{f^{-1}(B_r)} |\vec{H}| ^{q}\,dμ=0
  \]
  for some $q>p-\varepsilon$. This extends the corresponding superbiharmonic rigidity theorem to the $p$-biharmonic setting under a natural growth hypothesis.
  We also establish a minimality theorem for complete $p$-biharmonic immersions into Riemannian manifolds of non-positive sectional curvature under a polynomial growth assumption on the mean curvature. More precisely, if
  \[
  \int_{B_r(x_0)} | \vec{H} | ^{\,q}\,dμ= O(r^d)
  \]
  for some $q\ge0$ and $d>0$, then the immersion is minimal. For $q=0$ this recovers the polynomial volume-growth theorem of Cao--Luo \cite{CL16}, while for $q>0$ it provides a polynomial-growth analogue of Han's $L^q$-integrability rigidity theorem \cite{H15}.

Differential Geometry.title: A Chord-Arc Estimate for Graphical Hypersurfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove an interior chord-arc estimate for graphical hypersurfaces without an a priori gradient bound, which is not restricted to balls on the scale of their curvature. As a main application we derive an in-radius lower bound depending on the curvature which then also implies Heinz-type estimates for minimal graphs and uniform area bounds for graphical hypersurfaces.

Differential Geometry.title: The cross quadratic bisectional curvature of Kähler $C$-spaces of classical type
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we show that any Kähler $C$-space of classical type has nonnegative cross quadratic bisectional curvature and positive dual cross quadratic bisectional curvature. As a consequence, such manifolds are Fano. This confirms a substantial part of a conjecture of Ni-Zheng (Conjecture 1.5 in \cite{NZ}).
Differential Geometry.comment: 68 pages; a note is added; a minor modification of Lemma A.3 is made

Differential Geometry.title: K-unstable Toric Varieties and Secondary Polytopes
Differential Geometry.summary: For a K-unstable toric variety, Székelyhidi's optimal test-function $Θ_{P}$ is a mysterious concave function over the moment polytope $P$, which gives the maximal destabilizer for K-stability, and encodes the limiting behavior of the divergent Calabi flow. As balanced norms quantize cscK metrics, we show that $Θ_{P}$ can be quantized by the maximal destabilizers for Chow-stability, which are given by the shortest GKZ vectors, i.e., the least norm point on the secondary polytope associated to the set $P\cap k^{-1}\mathbb{Z}^{n}$. The proof is via the $Γ$-convergence method. Properties and algorithms for general sGKZ vectors are given. It may provide a new method to detect the K-instability of Delzant polytopes.

Differential Geometry.title: Topological 5d $\mathcal{N} = 2$ Gauge Theories: Mirror Symmetry and Langlands Duality of $A_\infty$-categories of Floer Homologies
Differential Geometry.summary: We explain why on certain five-manifolds, topological 5d $\mathcal{N} = 2$ gauge theory of Haydys-Witten twist with gauge group $G$, is dual to that of Geyer-Mülsch twist with gauge group $^LG$, where $G$ is a real, compact Lie group with Langlands dual $^LG$. In turn, via their 2d and 3d gauged A/B-twisted Landau-Ginzburg model interpretations, we can show that (i) a Fukaya-Seidel-type $A_\infty$-1-category of an HW$_4$-instanton Floer homology of three-manifolds and (ii) a Fueter-type $A_\infty$-2-category of an HW$_3$-instanton Floer homology of two-manifolds, are dual to (i) an Orlov-type $A_\infty$-1-category of a novel holomorphic $^LG_{\mathbb{H}}$-flat Floer homology of three-manifolds and (ii) a Rozansky-Witten-type $A_\infty$-2-category of a novel holomorphic $^LG_{\mathbb{O}}$-flat Floer homology of two-manifolds, respectively. We also derive their Atiyah-Floer-type correspondences to symplectic categories. Our work, which demonstrates a mirror symmetry and Langlands duality of (higher) $A_\infty$-categories of Floer homologies, therefore furnishes purely physical proofs and gauge-theoretic generalizations of the mathematical conjectures by Bousseau [1] and Doan-Rezchikov [2], and more.
